mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals are distributed with a higher share in the first half than the second half (first-half goals FOR above second-half goals FOR), while Team B's goals AGAINST are distributed with a higher share in the second half than the first half (second-half goals AGAINST above first-half goals AGAINST). This cross-team, cross-half asymmetry in goal-timing profiles — where one team scores early and the other concedes late — may condition the half-level goal distribution differently from what either team's half-split alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism requires jointly conditioning on two distinct half-level splits across two different teams and two different perspectives (home team's goals FOR by half vs. away team's goals AGAINST by half), which is a within-match state dependence combined with a cross-team asymmetry. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on a joint state where one team (Team B) holds structurally high possession (all-prior mean ~61%) while the opponent (Team A) is near 50/50, then jointly examine each team's shots-to-shots-on-target ratio. This requires simultaneously conditioning on possession imbalance AND the joint shot/on-target relationship for both sides — not reducible to a single observable with one band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The high-possession team's shots-on-target as a share of total shots is suppressed relative to the lower-possession team's equivalent ratio when possession imbalance is large; i.e., volume of shots rises with possession dominance but on-target conversion rate does not rise proportionally.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When a large possession imbalance exists between two teams (Team B structurally dominates possession while Team A is near-parity), the relationship between each team's shots and shots-on-target diverges asymmetrically: the high-possession team's shot volume does not proportionally translate into on-target accuracy, while the lower-possession team's on-target rate relative to total shots may be comparatively higher.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint three-variable relationship (possession, shots, shots_on_target) across two sides simultaneously, with an asymmetric cross-team comparison. It cannot be reduced to any single observable mirror, a single observable with one band, or a simple home/away split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on each team's possession level and corner production. Team B holds ~61% possession all-prior but generates ~5.2 corners (near competition mean of ~5.0), while Team A holds ~49% possession but also generates ~4.9 corners. Measure whether, across historical matches, teams with possession levels as high as Team B's generate corners at a rate proportionally above competition baseline, or whether the relationship saturates.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner production saturates or decouples from possession share beyond a threshold level of possession dominance; teams with very high possession do not generate proportionally more corners than near-parity teams.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's structurally high possession does not translate into a proportionally high corner-kick yield, while Team A generates corners near the competition average despite lower possession. The joint relationship between possession dominance and corner production differs across the two teams, suggesting that corner generation is not simply a function of possession share.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a threshold/saturation non-linear relationship between a continuous possession variable and corner output — not a simple single-observable mirror or coarse band split. It requires jointly examining two observables across both teams against a competition baseline.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on each team's foul-committed rate and second-half card rate, comparing the cross-team asymmetry: Team A commits fewer fouls (10.0) than it receives (12.6), while Team B commits more fouls (11.8) than it receives (13.6 against). Measure whether the team that commits more fouls in a matchup accumulates more second-half cards, and whether the direction of the foul imbalance predicts which side's cards_2h is elevated.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The team with the higher foul-commit rate relative to its opponent's foul-commit rate accumulates more second-half cards; the cross-team foul asymmetry rises with second-half card asymmetry.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The relationship between a team's foul rate and its second-half card accumulation is asymmetric across the two sides: Team A concedes more fouls against it (opponent fouls on Team A) than it commits, while Team B concedes more fouls against it than it commits in recent matches. The joint cross-team pattern of who commits fouls versus who receives second-half cards differs structurally, and this asymmetry is measurable as a joint two-observable, two-team relationship.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable (fouls, cards_2h), two-team asymmetric relationship. It requires simultaneously conditioning on both teams' foul rates and comparing the directional cross-team imbalance against second-half card outcomes — not reducible to a single observable mirror or one-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state of a team's recent-window foul rate versus all-prior foul rate, and simultaneously examine whether the cards_2h rate diverges from what the full-match yellow card rate implies. For Team B, recent fouls (9.8) are notably below all-prior (11.8), while cards_2h against Team B (1.8) remains elevated. Measure whether the gap between recent and all-prior foul rates predicts a divergence between full-match yellow cards and second-half card concentration.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent foul rate drops below its all-prior rate, second-half card concentration (cards_2h relative to yellow_cards) rises rather than falls, suggesting disciplinary pressure accumulates in the second half independently of first-half foul volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The relationship between a team's full-match foul rate and its yellow card accumulation differs between first and second halves. Specifically, when a team's recent foul rate diverges from its all-prior foul rate, the second-half card rate (cards_2h) may be disproportionately affected relative to what the full-match yellow card rate would suggest, indicating a within-match state-dependent accumulation pattern.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves three observables jointly (fouls, yellow_cards, cards_2h) with a within-match half-level split and a recent-vs-all-prior regime comparison simultaneously — structurally richer than any single-observable recent-vs-long-run comparison or a single half-level split alone.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on each team's possession level and offside rate (both all-prior and recent), then examine second-half goal rates. Team A: recent offsides FOR dropped to 1.0 (from 1.8 all-prior) while possession rose to 57.2% (from 49.3%); Team B: offsides FOR at 2.1 all-prior, rising to 3.0 recent, with possession at ~61%. Measure whether the combination of high possession AND high offsides (aggressive line-breaking) is associated with elevated second-half goals, versus high possession with low offsides.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goal production rises when a team jointly exhibits high possession and high offside rate (indicating aggressive forward runs against a high defensive line), compared to teams with high possession but low offside rates; the joint possession-offside interaction predicts second-half goal rate above what either variable alone would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between a team's possession level, its offside rate, and its second-half goal production captures a structural attacking pattern: teams that hold high possession and generate high offsides (indicating high defensive lines and aggressive forward runs) may show a different second-half goal rate than teams with similar possession but lower offsides. Team A's recent offside rate has dropped sharply while possession has risen, and Team B maintains elevated offsides with high possession — this joint pattern across both teams relates to second-half goal production.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint three-variable relationship (possession, offsides, goals) with a within-match half-level split, combining a recent-vs-all-prior regime shift in one variable (offsides) with a simultaneous possession level — not reducible to any single-observable comparison or one-band conditioning.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where both shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR are simultaneously above their respective all-prior means for the same team; measure corner kicks FOR in those matches versus matches where only one or neither is elevated.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kick production rises when both shots and shots-on-target are jointly elevated above baseline, more than when only one is elevated — a super-additive joint relationship.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot volume (shots FOR) and shots-on-target jointly condition corner kick generation: when a team produces high shot volume alongside a high shots-on-target rate, corner kick production rises disproportionately relative to what either observable alone would predict. Team B's recent surge in both shots (17.0 recent vs 12.4 all-prior) and shots-on-target (6.4 recent vs 5.8 all-prior) should be jointly tested against their corner kick production (6.2 recent vs 4.8 all-prior) to determine whether the joint elevation of both shooting observables predicts corner kick output beyond what each observable predicts independently.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint conditioning on two distinct observables simultaneously (shots AND shots_on_target both elevated), which cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band. The engine's covered class handles each observable independently against one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For Team A, condition on matches where shots_on_target FOR is below the all-prior mean while shots FOR is also below the all-prior mean, versus matches where only one is below. Measure goals FOR in each regime.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals FOR are more suppressed when both shot volume and shot accuracy are jointly below baseline than when only one is depressed — the joint deficit is a stronger suppressor than either alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots-on-target FOR has dropped sharply in recent matches (2.8 recent vs 4.6 all-prior) while their shots FOR has also declined (9.4 recent vs 10.7 all-prior), but the ratio of shots-on-target to shots (conversion accuracy) may have changed non-proportionally. The joint relationship between shot volume and shot accuracy (shots_on_target / shots ratio) should be tested against goal output to determine whether accuracy decline is a stronger suppressor of goals than volume decline alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires simultaneous conditioning on two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) to capture the joint accuracy-volume interaction on goals. Not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Cross-condition Team B's goals FOR by half (first vs second) against Team A's goals AGAINST by half (first vs second). Measure whether the combination of Team B's second-half attacking strength and Team A's second-half defensive weakness produces a joint elevation in second-half goals beyond what each team's individual half-split would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goals in the match rise when the attacking team has a back-loaded goal production profile and the defending team has a back-loaded goals-conceded profile — the asymmetric half-split interaction amplifies second-half scoring.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B exhibits a pronounced first-half vs second-half goal asymmetry (1.084 goals FOR in first half vs 1.337 in second half all-prior), while Team A's goal production is more evenly split (0.764 first half vs 0.742 second half). The within-match half-level split of goals FOR for each team should be jointly tested against the opponent's half-level goals AGAINST split to determine whether Team B's second-half goal surge is amplified or suppressed when facing a team (Team A) whose defensive vulnerability is also back-loaded (0.640 goals AGAINST first half vs 0.719 second half).
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) split that simultaneously conditions on two teams' asymmetric half-level profiles for different observables (goals FOR for one team, goals AGAINST for the other). It is not a single observable with one band, and it requires half-resolution data.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For Team B, condition on matches where fouls FOR exceeds a threshold (e.g., above the all-prior mean of 11.6) and measure cards_2h FOR in those matches versus matches below the threshold. Test whether the relationship is non-linear (cards_2h rises sharply only above the foul threshold).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half card accumulation (cards_2h) rises non-linearly with foul volume — suppressed at low foul counts but surging beyond a threshold foul level, rather than increasing proportionally across the full range.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's cards_2h FOR (1.684 per second half) is notably higher than their cards_2h AGAINST (1.211), and both exceed the competition context mean (1.378). The within-match second-half card accumulation for Team B should be jointly tested against their fouls FOR (which has risen recently to 12.8 vs 11.6 all-prior) to determine whether high foul volume in a match is a threshold predictor of elevated second-half card accumulation — i.e., whether there is a non-linear relationship where second-half cards surge once foul volume crosses a threshold.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This tests a threshold/non-linear dependence of one observable (cards_2h) on a continuous second observable (fouls), conditioned within a specific match period (second half). It is not a single observable with one coarse band, and it requires half-resolution data for cards_2h.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B's possession FOR exceeds a threshold (above competition mean of 50%) AND the opponent's corner_kicks AGAINST is above the competition mean (5.0 per match). Measure Team B's corner_kicks FOR in those jointly-conditioned matches versus matches where only one condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kick production for the possession-dominant team rises when both possession dominance and opponent corner-concession propensity are jointly present, more than when either condition holds alone — an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B holds dominant possession (55.9% all-prior, 54.0% recent) while Team A is near-neutral (50.2% all-prior, 54.2% recent). The asymmetric possession relationship between the two teams should be jointly tested against corner kick differential: when one team holds structurally higher possession AND the opponent allows above-average corners (Team A allows 4.0 corners per match all-prior), the possession-dominant team's corner production should be elevated beyond what possession alone or corner-allowed alone would predict. This tests whether possession dominance and opponent corner-concession jointly amplify corner generation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric relationship across different observables for the two sides (Team B's possession FOR jointly with Team A's corner_kicks AGAINST), which cannot be reduced to a single observable mirror or a single observable with one band. It requires conditioning on two distinct observables from two different teams simultaneously.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's possession is below a threshold (e.g. below 45%) AND shots produced is below season average; measure whether shots_on_target FOR as a fraction of shots FOR is suppressed relative to matches where possession is at or above average.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's shots-on-target-to-shots ratio falls as possession drops below average, with the suppression amplified when shots volume is also below average — a joint non-linear relationship rather than either observable in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's joint possession-deficit and shot-volume divergence: when Team A operates with below-average possession (recent form shows a sharp drop to 41.6% vs season average 47.2%) while simultaneously experiencing a decline in shots produced (recent 10.2 vs season 12.7), the ratio of shots-on-target produced to shots produced may compress relative to matches where possession is closer to parity. This joint relationship between possession level and shot-quality conversion (shots-on-target / shots) is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession AND shots) simultaneously to detect an interaction effect on a derived ratio; not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For Team B as the defending side, condition on matches where shots allowed exceeds a threshold (e.g. above 18); measure whether shots_on_target AGAINST and goals AGAINST both rise disproportionately relative to the shot-volume increase, indicating a joint amplification rather than a linear scaling.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shots allowed by Team B exceeds a high threshold, goals allowed rises faster than the linear extrapolation from average shot-to-goal ratios would predict — a saturation/threshold interaction between shot volume allowed and defensive quality.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's recent defensive deterioration is asymmetric across shots allowed vs shots-on-target allowed: shots against have surged dramatically in recent matches (23.4 recent vs 12.5 season average) while goals against have also risen (3.0 recent vs 1.7 season), suggesting a joint relationship where the ratio of shots-on-target allowed to shots allowed (opponent shot quality) may be rising simultaneously with shot volume allowed. The interaction between opponent shot volume and opponent shot accuracy against Team B is a joint two-observable mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Involves a threshold/non-linear dependence on shots allowed jointly with shots-on-target allowed and goals allowed — three observables in a non-linear joint structure, not a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition simultaneously on venue (home) AND possession above a threshold (e.g. above 48%); measure whether corner_kicks FOR is elevated beyond what either the home split alone or the possession split alone would predict, testing for a super-additive joint effect.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's corner-kick production rises with possession, and this relationship is steeper at home than away — a joint venue × possession interaction rather than either dimension independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production exhibits a strong home/away asymmetry (7.0 home vs 4.5 away, season averages) that interacts with its possession level: at home Team A generates substantially more corners and holds more possession (50.5% home vs 44.1% away). The joint relationship between venue-driven possession advantage and corner-kick production — where corners rise with possession but the venue effect on possession itself is large — creates a two-dimensional conditioning structure (venue × possession level) that predicts corner output beyond either dimension alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires two distinct conditioning dimensions simultaneously (venue AND a continuous possession threshold), not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band or the standard venue split alone.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team separately, condition on matches where fouls committed exceeds a threshold; measure whether yellow_cards FOR rises disproportionately (non-linearly) beyond the average card-per-foul rate, and test whether this threshold effect differs between Team A and Team B given their divergent recent yellow card trajectories.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's yellow cards per foul rises as fouls committed increases beyond a threshold, and this non-linear relationship is steeper for Team A than Team B — an asymmetric threshold effect across the two teams on the same joint observable pair.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetric relationship between Team A's foul-committing rate and Team B's foul-committing rate, jointly with yellow cards produced, may reveal a differential card-per-foul conversion: Team A commits more fouls (11.3 season, 11.0 recent) and accumulates more yellow cards (2.24 season, 3.0 recent) while Team B commits fewer fouls (10.0 season) with similar yellow cards (2.06 season). The joint relationship between fouls committed and yellow cards received — the card-per-foul rate — differs across the two teams and may interact with the opponent's foul rate allowed, creating an asymmetric cross-team mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Involves a non-linear (threshold) relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) measured asymmetrically across both teams simultaneously — not a single observable with one band, and not a simple mirror comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on half (first vs second) jointly for both Team A and Team B; measure whether the combined second-half goal rate (Team A FOR + Team B FOR in H2) exceeds the combined first-half rate by more than the competition baseline half-split would predict, testing for a joint amplification when both teams share the same directional half-level bias.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams independently exhibit a second-half scoring uplift, the combined second-half goal rate in their head-to-head context rises above what the competition-level half-split baseline predicts — a joint two-team within-match state mechanism.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The within-match half-level split of goals reveals a structural asymmetry for Team A: Team A concedes more in the second half (1.048 per match) than the first half (0.831), while scoring more in the second half (0.880) than the first half (0.747). This half-level scoring/conceding pattern, when jointly considered with Team B's analogous half-level split (Team B scores 0.764 in H1 and 0.921 in H2; concedes 0.787 in H1 and 0.899 in H2), creates a joint within-match state structure: both teams are second-half-weighted in both attack and defence, suggesting the second half of this specific matchup may be disproportionately goal-rich relative to the first half, beyond what either team's half-split alone would indicate.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on half-level splits for both teams simultaneously and comparing against the competition baseline half-split — a within-match state structure involving two teams' directional biases at once, not a single team's observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Examine Team A's FOR perspective: compare the ratio of shots_on_target:shots (accuracy) and shots_on_target:goals (conversion) across ALL_PRIOR vs RECENT_5 windows simultaneously. The mechanism is the joint two-observable relationship (shots volume × conversion rate) rather than either observable alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shots volume rises sharply in recent matches without a proportional rise in goals, shots-on-target conversion rate is suppressed relative to the season baseline, suggesting volume and conversion move asymmetrically in the recent regime.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent surge in shots (and shots on target) relative to its season-long average co-occurs with a persistent deficit in shot-to-goal conversion: despite the recent shots spike, goals scored have not risen proportionally. The joint relationship between shots volume and shots-on-target volume (both FOR) against the resulting goals FOR reveals whether Team A's recent volume increase is converting or is being suppressed by low conversion efficiency.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly tracking two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) against a third (goals) across two time windows simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band; it tests a cross-observable ratio relationship and its divergence across temporal regimes.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Examine Team B's FOR perspective: jointly compare shots, shots_on_target, and goals across ALL_PRIOR vs RECENT_5 windows. The mechanism tests whether the cross-observable conversion chain (shots → shots_on_target → goals) holds or breaks in the recent regime for Team B.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shots and shots_on_target rise in recent matches but goals remain flat, the shots-to-goal conversion chain is suppressed in the recent regime relative to the season baseline, indicating a non-linear (saturating or decoupled) relationship between volume and output.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots and shots_on_target have both risen in recent matches relative to its season average, yet goals FOR have not risen (remaining flat at 1.2 vs 1.207 season average). The joint relationship between Team B's shot volume, shot accuracy, and goal output tests whether Team B's recent volume increase is structurally decoupled from scoring output.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly tracking three observables (shots, shots_on_target, goals) across two temporal windows. Not reducible to any single observable with one band; the mechanism is the cross-observable conversion chain and its regime-level breakdown.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on second-half period for cards_2h and compare jointly with full-match fouls FOR (both ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5) for Team B versus Team A and competition context. The mechanism is the asymmetric cross-observable relationship between fouls committed and second-half card accumulation across the two teams.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's second-half cards FOR rises relative to its fouls FOR rate (and relative to Team A's equivalent ratio), indicating that Team B accumulates second-half cards at a disproportionately high rate per foul committed compared to Team A and the competition baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's cards_2h (second-half cards FOR) is markedly elevated relative to both Team A's cards_2h and the competition context average, while Team B's fouls FOR have recently declined. The joint relationship between fouls committed and second-half cards received tests whether Team B's card accumulation in the second half is disproportionate to its foul rate — i.e., whether cards are being earned at a higher rate per foul in the second half.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team, cross-observable relationship (fouls FOR vs cards_2h FOR) that also involves a within-match period split (second half). It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one band; it requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables and a half-level split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Examine Team A's FOR perspective jointly across offsides, possession, and goals across ALL_PRIOR vs RECENT_5 windows. The mechanism tests whether the recent offsides surge co-varies with possession changes and whether it translates into goal output — a three-way cross-observable joint relationship.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When offsides FOR spike sharply in recent matches alongside modest possession gains, but goals FOR do not rise proportionally, the relationship between possession-driven attacking aggression (proxied by offsides) and goal output is non-linear or saturating in the recent regime.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides FOR have spiked sharply in recent matches (3.4 recent vs 1.823 season average) while its possession FOR has also risen slightly in recent matches. The joint relationship between possession share and offsides generated tests whether higher possession is associated with a more aggressive, line-breaking attacking posture (more offsides) or whether the offsides spike is independent of possession changes.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly tracking three distinct observables (offsides, possession, goals) across two temporal windows. The mechanism is a three-way cross-observable relationship that cannot be reduced to any single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on second-half vs first-half period splits simultaneously for both teams: Team A goals AGAINST by half, Team B goals FOR by half, and cross-reference with corner_kicks and shots_on_target half splits for both teams. The mechanism is the joint two-team, two-half asymmetry across attacking and defensive observables.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second half exhibits a structurally higher combined goal rate than the first half, driven by the joint pattern of Team A's defensive deterioration and Team B's attacking improvement in the second half — a relationship that is stronger than either team's half-split considered in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A concedes goals at a higher rate in the second half than the first half (1.024 vs 0.867), while Team B scores goals at a higher rate in the second half than the first half (0.793 vs 0.415). The joint within-match half-level asymmetry across both teams — Team A's defensive vulnerability rising in the second half coinciding with Team B's attacking output rising in the second half — tests whether the second half creates a structurally elevated combined goal environment beyond what full-match averages suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism requires jointly conditioning on two teams' half-level splits across both attacking and defensive perspectives simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one band; it is a two-team, two-half, cross-perspective joint relationship involving multiple observables.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's shots FOR (RECENT_5) is materially below its ALL_PRIOR mean AND Team A's shots AGAINST (RECENT_5) is materially above its ALL_PRIOR mean simultaneously. Measure whether the joint regime predicts a different total-shots and shots-on-target distribution than either single-observable drift alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both Team A's attacking shot output falls and its defensive shot allowance rises jointly, the combined shots-on-target total for the match is suppressed relative to what either single-observable trend would imply independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume collapse in recent matches (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) co-occurs with a simultaneous surge in shots conceded, suggesting a joint deterioration in both attacking and defensive shot-generation balance. The joint direction of these two observables — shots FOR falling while shots AGAINST rises — may predict a compressed total-shots environment differently than either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots FOR and shots AGAINST) both shifting in the same adverse direction simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band; it requires measuring the intersection of two observable drift signals.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the possession-holding team (Team A, historically ~52%) faces an opponent (Team B) whose shots-FOR rate is well below competition average but whose shots-AGAINST rate is well above it. Measure whether corner-kick volume for the possession-dominant side rises with this asymmetric shot-generation imbalance across the two teams.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kicks for the possession-dominant team rise when the opponent's defensive shot-allowance rate is high relative to its own attacking shot rate — i.e., the asymmetry between Team B's shots FOR and shots AGAINST amplifies corner generation for Team A beyond what possession alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession share is structurally higher than Team B's (both all-prior and venue-split), yet Team A's shots FOR are only marginally above competition average while Team B allows far more shots than it generates. The asymmetric relationship between possession dominance (Team A) and shot-generation efficiency (Team B's low shots FOR vs high shots AGAINST) may jointly determine corner-kick volume differently than possession or shots alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a cross-team asymmetric relationship between two distinct observables (possession for one team, shots-FOR vs shots-AGAINST imbalance for the other). It cannot be reduced to a single observable mirror or a single conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A's corner-kicks FOR RECENT_5 being materially below its ALL_PRIOR mean, AND (b) Team B's corner-kicks AGAINST ALL_PRIOR being above competition average. Measure whether the combination of attacker drought plus permissive-opponent context predicts a reversion in corner volume or sustained suppression, compared to either condition alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's recent corner output is suppressed but the opponent historically concedes above-average corners, the joint regime tests whether corner volume reverts toward the opponent's concession baseline or remains anchored to the attacker's recent form — i.e., which dimension dominates in the joint conditioning.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production has collapsed in RECENT_5 (2.6) relative to its ALL_PRIOR mean (5.57), while Team B concedes corners at a rate (5.64 ALL_PRIOR, 4.4 RECENT_5) that is above competition average. The joint condition of Team A's corner-generation drought AND Team B's corner-concession profile creates a two-dimensional regime that may predict whether corner totals revert or remain suppressed, beyond what either team's single-observable trend implies.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct temporal windows (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) for the same observable across two different teams, testing which regime dominates. It is not a single observable with one band; it is a two-team, two-window joint conditioning.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where a team's fouls FOR (RECENT_5) is materially below its ALL_PRIOR mean while its cards_2h FOR (ALL_PRIOR) remains above competition average. Measure whether second-half card volume is better predicted by the joint relationship between foul rate and card rate than by either observable alone — specifically testing whether a low-foul, high-card regime exists as a distinct pattern.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half cards remain elevated even as foul volume declines, suggesting a non-linear (threshold) relationship where card issuance per foul rises when foul volume falls — i.e., cards_2h does not scale linearly with fouls in this regime.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half cards rate (cards_2h FOR: 1.663) is the highest among both teams and above competition average (1.403), while Team B's fouls FOR have dropped sharply in RECENT_5 (9.6) versus ALL_PRIOR (12.337). This divergence between a structurally elevated second-half card rate and a recent foul-rate decline creates a joint observable pattern: whether second-half cards are driven by foul volume or by a threshold effect where fewer but more dangerous fouls yield disproportionate cards.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This tests a non-linear / threshold relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and cards_2h) rather than treating either in isolation. It also involves a cross-window divergence (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) on one observable while the other remains structurally elevated — a joint two-observable, two-window conditioning not covered by any single-observable baseline.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A's goals FOR being back-loaded (second-half mean exceeds first-half mean), AND (b) Team B's goals AGAINST being back-loaded (second-half concession mean exceeds first-half concession mean). Measure whether the alignment of both teams' second-half goal tendencies predicts elevated second-half goal volume beyond what either team's half-split alone would imply.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the attacking team's scoring is back-loaded AND the defending team's concession is also back-loaded, second-half goal volume rises above what either team's individual half-split would predict independently — the two asymmetries reinforce each other.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals FOR split between first half (0.688) and second half (0.806) shows a back-loaded scoring pattern, while Team B's goals AGAINST split shows the opposite asymmetry — conceding more in the second half (0.910) than the first (0.629). The joint within-match half-level asymmetry across both teams' goal profiles (Team A scores more in H2; Team B concedes more in H2) may predict second-half goal volume differently than full-match averages or either team's half-split in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint conditioning on two distinct teams' within-match half-level splits for the same observable, testing whether the alignment of both asymmetries produces a compounding effect. It is not a single observable with one band, nor a simple home/away or recent/prior split — it is a two-team, within-match period interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Measure the ratio of shots_on_target FOR to shots FOR for each team across all prior matches, then cross-condition on the opponent's shots_on_target AGAINST rate. The mechanism is active when one team's conversion ratio diverges from the competition norm while the opponent's defensive shots_on_target rate also diverges, creating an asymmetric joint signal.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's shots-to-shots-on-target ratio is suppressed relative to competition baseline while the opponent allows shots_on_target at or above baseline, the on-target threat differential rises in favour of the opponent; the joint cross-product of these two ratios tracks the directional imbalance better than either ratio alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR) interacts with Team B's shots-on-target allowed rate to jointly determine the on-target threat differential in this match. Team A produces shots at a near-competition-average rate but converts them to on-target attempts at a below-average rate, while Team B allows shots_on_target at a near-average rate; the joint relationship between one team's shot quality (shots_on_target / shots) and the opponent's shots_on_target conceded rate is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for both teams simultaneously, computing a ratio and cross-multiplying with the opponent's defensive rate. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band, nor to a simple home/away or recent/long-run split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where a team's own offsides FOR (recent vs long-run) diverges sharply downward while its offsides AGAINST (recent vs long-run) diverges sharply upward. Both dimensions must move in opposite directions simultaneously for the mechanism to be active.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent offsides FOR rate collapses relative to its long-run rate while its offsides AGAINST rate simultaneously spikes, the team's attacking line is operating in a qualitatively different regime; corner and shot volume generated by that team's attacks is expected to be suppressed relative to its long-run average.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B exhibits a pronounced asymmetry between its recent (last 5) and long-run offsides FOR rate (recent mean 0.6 vs long-run 1.758) while simultaneously its offsides AGAINST rate has spiked recently (recent 4.6 vs long-run 2.084). This joint within-team divergence across two distinct dimensions of the same observable (own offsides produced vs opponent offsides drawn) signals a structural shift in Team B's attacking line behaviour that is not captured by either dimension alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single observable with one band. It requires jointly conditioning on two distinct perspectives of the same observable (FOR and AGAINST) and comparing recent vs long-run windows for both simultaneously — a two-dimensional within-team regime signal.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Measure the cross-product of Team B's fouls AGAINST rate (fouls drawn) and Team A's fouls FOR rate (fouls committed), then condition on whether the resulting differential exceeds the competition baseline. Separately track how yellow_cards FOR and cards_2h FOR/AGAINST behave when this foul-rate asymmetry is present.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the foul-drawing rate of one team substantially exceeds the competition mean while the opponent's foul-committing rate is near or below average, yellow card volume and second-half card accumulation are expected to rise above competition baseline, with the foul-drawing team's opponent accumulating more cards.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between Team A's foul production (FOR) and Team B's foul concession rate (AGAINST) creates an asymmetric disciplinary pressure context. Team B concedes fouls at a rate well above the competition mean (12.598 vs 11.742) while Team A commits fouls at a rate close to competition average (10.833). This asymmetry — one team drawing fouls at an elevated rate while the opponent commits at a moderate rate — jointly conditions the expected yellow card and second-half card volume in a way neither foul rate alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct observables (fouls and cards) across two teams simultaneously, using an asymmetric cross-team comparison rather than a single observable mirror or a single band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on both teams' first-half and second-half goal FOR and AGAINST rates simultaneously. The mechanism is active when one team is a pronounced second-half scorer while the opponent is a more balanced or first-half-leaning scorer, creating a non-symmetric within-match goal timing profile.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's goals are concentrated in the second half and Team B scores more evenly across halves, the combined first-half goal rate for the match is expected to be suppressed relative to competition baseline, while second-half goal volume rises; the half-level imbalance is directional and asymmetric across the two teams.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals are heavily skewed toward the second half (0.781 FOR second half vs 0.458 FOR first half) while Team B's goals are more evenly distributed across halves (0.742 FOR first half vs 0.959 FOR second half). The joint half-level goal distribution profiles of both teams — not just one team's split — interact to shape the within-match scoring sequence. This cross-team, within-match half-level asymmetry is a structurally richer signal than either team's half split in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on half-level splits for both teams simultaneously (four observables: Team A goals FOR 1H, Team A goals FOR 2H, Team B goals FOR 1H, Team B goals FOR 2H), which is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band or a simple venue split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on the cross-team possession regime divergence (recent vs long-run for both teams simultaneously) and each team's corner kick production rate split by venue. The mechanism tests whether a team gaining possession momentum recently also gains corner volume, and whether the opponent's corner concession rate responds correspondingly — requiring both observables and both teams' recent-vs-long-run windows together.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent possession share rises above its long-run average while the opponent's recent possession falls or stays flat, corner kick volume for the possession-gaining team is expected to rise above its venue-adjusted baseline; the relationship between possession regime shift and corner production is expected to be positive and detectable only when both dimensions are conditioned jointly.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's recent possession share has shifted substantially upward (recent 54.6 vs long-run 49.268) while Team A's recent possession share has drifted slightly downward (recent 49.0 vs long-run 49.656). Jointly, this creates a possession-regime divergence between the two teams' recent form. When one team's recent possession rises while the opponent's falls, and this is cross-conditioned with corner kick production rates (Team A corners FOR home 5.609 vs away 4.24; Team B corners FOR away 4.532), the joint possession-corners relationship tests whether possession regime shifts translate into corner volume changes in a non-linear or threshold manner.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks), uses a recent-vs-long-run regime shift for both teams simultaneously, and cross-conditions on venue — combining three dimensions that individually are already covered but whose joint interaction is not.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compare the joint ratio of goals-FOR to shots-FOR (and goals-FOR to shots_on_target-FOR) in the ALL_PRIOR window versus the RECENT_5 window for Team A. The mechanism tests whether a recent spike in shots is accompanied by a commensurate rise in goals, or whether the two observables diverge — a non-linear / saturation relationship not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's recent shots spike is expected to show diminishing returns in goals relative to the all-prior baseline, i.e. goals-per-shot ratio falls as shot volume rises
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has surged in recent matches while its conversion rate (goals per shot) has not kept pace, suggesting a divergence between shot production and scoring efficiency. Jointly measuring shots FOR and goals FOR across the all-prior versus recent-5 windows reveals whether elevated shot counts translate into proportionally elevated goals, or whether the relationship saturates/decouples.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and goals) across two time windows simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band; the engine would need to evaluate the ratio of two observables and whether that ratio changes across windows.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For Team B, compute the joint relationship between shots_on_target AGAINST and goals AGAINST in the ALL_PRIOR window versus the RECENT_5 window. The mechanism tests whether the recent rise in shots conceded is accompanied by a disproportionate rise in goals conceded (implying a quality/conversion shift) or a proportionate one (implying a volume shift only).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: In Team B's recent matches, goals conceded rises faster than shots_on_target conceded relative to the all-prior baseline, indicating a worsening shot-to-goal conversion rate against them beyond what shot volume alone explains
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's defensive solidity (shots conceded) has deteriorated sharply in recent matches while its goals-against has also risen, but the two observables move at different rates. Jointly tracking shots_on_target AGAINST and goals AGAINST across all-prior versus recent-5 windows tests whether Team B's recent defensive breakdown is driven by volume of shots allowed, quality of shots allowed, or both simultaneously.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires joint evaluation of two distinct defensive observables (shots_on_target AGAINST and goals AGAINST) and their ratio across two time windows — not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's corners FOR (all-prior and recent-5) and Team B's corners AGAINST (all-prior and recent-5) simultaneously, testing whether the combination of a stable attacker and a recently-leaky defender produces a corner total that diverges from what either team's individual baseline would suggest. This is an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The joint pairing of Team A's stable corner production with Team B's sharply elevated recent corners-conceded rate is associated with a higher corner total than either team's own all-prior average would predict in isolation

This asymmetric divergence between Team B's recent corners-against and Team A's corners-for suggests a structural mismatch: the joint combination of Team A's corner production rate and Team B's corner-concession rate in recent form may predict a corner total that neither observable alone would indicate.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship: it pairs one team's FOR observable with the opponent's AGAINST observable and explicitly tests whether the recent-form divergence between the two (one stable, one spiking) creates a non-additive signal. The engine's mirror covers same-observable FOR vs AGAINST symmetrically; this tests the asymmetric divergence in recent-form trajectories jointly.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For both teams, jointly compare cards_2h (second-half period) FOR and AGAINST against full-match yellow_cards FOR and AGAINST, and against the competition cards_2h baseline. The mechanism tests whether the within-match temporal distribution of cards (first half vs second half) is consistent with a uniform distribution or whether cards concentrate in the second half — a within-match state dependence requiring half-level resolution.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Cards concentrate disproportionately in the second half relative to a uniform within-match distribution, and this concentration is more pronounced when both teams have elevated second-half card rates relative to their full-match averages
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half cards rate and Team B's second-half cards rate differ from their respective full-match yellow card rates in ways that suggest the second half of this fixture may have a distinct disciplinary profile. Jointly measuring each team's cards_2h (second-half cards FOR and AGAINST) against their full-match yellow_cards and the competition's cards_2h baseline tests whether the second half concentrates disciplinary events beyond what the full-match rate implies.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires within-match half-level resolution (cards_2h vs full-match yellow_cards) and a joint cross-team comparison of second-half disciplinary rates against the competition baseline — not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's offsides AGAINST (recent-5 vs all-prior) and Team B's offsides FOR (recent-5 vs all-prior), further conditioning on possession to assess whether the offside pattern is consistent with Team B's possession profile. The mechanism tests whether the two observables move in opposite directions simultaneously — an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship — and whether possession mediates this divergence.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's offsides-against rate spikes while Team B's offsides-for rate drops simultaneously, the joint signal diverges from what either team's individual baseline predicts, suggesting a structural mismatch in attacking depth versus defensive line positioning that is not captured by either observable alone
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides conceded (AGAINST) have spiked sharply in recent matches (4.2 recent vs 2.0 all-prior) while Team B's offsides FOR have dropped (0.8 recent vs 1.9 all-prior). This creates a cross-team asymmetric divergence in the offsides dimension: one team is suddenly generating far more offsides traps while the opponent is running fewer offside-risk attacking movements. Jointly measuring Team A's offsides AGAINST and Team B's offsides FOR across all-prior and recent-5 windows tests whether this divergence reflects a structural tactical shift in how the two teams interact.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly evaluating two distinct observables (offsides and possession) across two teams in opposite directions simultaneously — an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship across two observable dimensions, not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's recent-window possession FOR is below its long-run mean AND recent-window shots FOR is below its long-run mean simultaneously (joint below-baseline state). Measure goals FOR and goals AGAINST in those matches versus matches where only one or neither observable is below baseline.

The joint deterioration across possession AND shots FOR AND shots AGAINST in the recent window — relative to long-run baselines — is a richer signal than any single observable's recent-vs-long-run split alone. The mechanism tests whether matches where a team simultaneously loses possession share AND shot dominance (both flipping below long-run mean in the same recent window) are associated with suppressed goals FOR and elevated goals AGAINST, beyond what either observable's individual drift would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint condition on two distinct observables (possession AND shots) simultaneously departing from baseline — not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band. The engine's covered class handles each observable's recent-vs-long-run split independently, not their intersection.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B's recent shots FOR is above its long-run mean AND recent goals FOR is below its long-run mean simultaneously (high volume, low conversion joint state). Measure shots_on_target FOR and corner_kicks FOR in those matches versus the complementary state.

This divergence between shot volume and goal output implies a recent deterioration in shot conversion efficiency. The mechanism tests whether the joint state of high shots FOR combined with low goals FOR (i.e., low implicit conversion rate) in the recent window is associated with a different corner-kick and shots-on-target profile than when shots and goals move together — capturing a non-linear, two-observable interaction rather than either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires joint conditioning on two distinct observables (shots FOR and goals FOR) moving in opposite directions relative to their baselines — not reducible to a single observable's recent-vs-long-run split or a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's cards_2h FOR exceeds cards_2h AGAINST (Team A is the higher second-half card earner) AND Team B's cards_2h AGAINST exceeds cards_2h FOR (Team B concedes more second-half cards than it earns). Measure the directional split of second-half cards (Team A cards vs Team B cards in second half) in such matchups versus symmetric matchups.

When these two asymmetric profiles are placed in opposition — Team A's high second-half card rate FOR facing Team B's high second-half card rate AGAINST — the mechanism tests whether the combined second-half card total is elevated relative to competition context (1.394 per team per second half), and specifically whether the asymmetry between the two teams' second-half card directions predicts a skewed distribution of second-half cards (more cards on one side than the other) rather than a symmetric total.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team relationship between two different observables' directional profiles (cards_2h FOR vs AGAINST for each team), requiring joint conditioning on both teams' asymmetry directions simultaneously — not reducible to a single observable for one team with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's goals FOR rate is higher in the first half than the second half (first-half scorer profile) AND Team B's goals FOR rate is higher in the second half than the first half (second-half scorer profile). Measure the ratio of first-half to second-half goals FOR for each team in such matchups.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A has a first-half goal-scoring advantage and Team B has a second-half goal-scoring advantage, Team A's share of total goals is concentrated in the first half and Team B's share is concentrated in the second half, producing a non-uniform within-match goal distribution

Team B shows the opposite: first-half goals FOR (0.857) is lower than second-half goals FOR (0.939), and first-half goals AGAINST (0.531) is lower than second-half goals AGAINST (0.643). The mechanism tests whether, when a team with a first-half goal-scoring advantage faces a team with a second-half goal-scoring advantage, the within-match goal distribution is non-uniform across halves in a predictable directional way — specifically whether the first half is more likely to be dominated by Team A and the second half by Team B.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires joint conditioning on within-match half-level splits for two different teams simultaneously, comparing first-half vs second-half goal rates across both sides — not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band or a simple home/away split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the opposing team's red_cards AGAINST rate is above competition context AND the focal team's fouls FOR rate is above competition context simultaneously. Measure red_cards AGAINST in those matches versus matches where only one condition holds, to test whether the joint condition (high fouls FOR meeting high red-cards-AGAINST opponent) produces a non-additive elevation in red cards.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The joint condition of high fouls FOR by Team A and high red-cards-AGAINST rate by Team B produces a higher red-card rate than either condition alone, suggesting a threshold interaction rather than additive effects
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's red cards AGAINST rate (0.184 per match, RECENT_5 = 0.4) is substantially above competition context (0.094) and above Team A's red cards FOR rate (0.098). This creates an asymmetric red-card exposure profile: Team B concedes red cards at roughly double the competition rate, while Team A earns them at the competition rate. The mechanism tests whether, when a team with a high red-cards-AGAINST rate (Team B) faces a team with a normal red-cards-FOR rate (Team A), the joint fouls profile — specifically Team A's fouls FOR combined with Team B's fouls AGAINST — predicts whether the elevated red-card-AGAINST rate for Team B is associated with a threshold in Team A's foul-earning rate, i.e., whether Team A's fouls FOR must exceed a certain level for Team B's red-card-AGAINST rate to manifest, or whether it occurs independently of Team A's foul pressure.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires joint conditioning on two distinct observables from two different teams (Team A fouls FOR and Team B red_cards AGAINST) simultaneously, testing a threshold/non-linear interaction — not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band or a simple mirror comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where one team (Team A) structurally dominates possession but shows a recent downward drift in shots and shots_on_target (ALL_PRIOR vs RECENT_5), while the opposing team (Team B) operates with low possession but has a large home/away split in shots (15.3 home vs 9.75 away FOR). Measure the ratio of shots_on_target to possession for each side jointly, not each observable independently.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a possession-dominant team's shot efficiency (shots_on_target per unit possession) declines in recent matches while the low-possession opponent's shot volume rises, the corner kick differential narrows or reverses relative to the season-long possession gap
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A holds a structural possession dominance over Team B (Team A averages ~57% possession FOR vs Team B averaging ~39% possession FOR, and Team B concedes ~61% possession AGAINST), yet Team A's shot volume has declined in recent matches while Team B's shot volume has risen recently. The joint relationship between possession dominance and shot conversion efficiency (shots and shots_on_target per unit possession) differs asymmetrically between the two sides, and this cross-observable ratio may predict corner and shot outcomes better than either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly relating two distinct observables (possession and shots_on_target) as a ratio for each side, then comparing the two sides' ratios asymmetrically — not a single observable against one band. It also incorporates the recent-vs-season drift of a derived cross-observable ratio, which is not a single observable's recent level.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's first-half vs second-half corner production FOR and Team B's first-half vs second-half corner concession AGAINST. The mechanism requires both half-level splits simultaneously — the compounding effect only emerges when both sides' half-level profiles are considered together, not when either is read against a single band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second-half corner total rises above the first-half corner total in matches where Team A's second-half corner production advantage coincides with Team B's elevated second-half corner concession rate
