The joint within-match half-level split of corner production FOR Team A and corner concession AGAINST Team B creates a compounding second-half corner surplus that is not captured by full-match corner averages alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) split that simultaneously conditions on two distinct team-role perspectives (Team A FOR and Team B AGAINST) for the same observable. It is not a single observable with one coarse band — it requires the joint half-level profiles of both sides.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's first-half vs second-half goal production FOR and Team B's first-half vs second-half goal concession AGAINST. The mechanism requires both half-level splits to be evaluated simultaneously to identify whether the second-half goal surplus is structurally reinforced from both sides.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goal totals are elevated relative to first-half goal totals when Team A's second-half scoring rate advantage coincides with Team B's elevated second-half concession rate
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A scores more goals in the second half than the first (0.68 FOR first half vs 0.92 FOR second half) while Team B concedes more goals in the second half than the first (0.708 AGAINST first half vs 0.917 AGAINST second half). Jointly, both sides' half-level goal profiles align to amplify second-half goal production, a relationship not visible from full-match goal averages alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct team-role perspectives (Team A FOR and Team B AGAINST) at the half level for the same observable. It is not a single observable with one coarse band — it requires the simultaneous half-level profiles of both sides to identify the compounding structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state of Team B's foul production FOR (especially its recent upward drift) alongside Team A's yellow cards AGAINST (fouls drawn leading to cards for the fouling side). Measure whether elevated foul production by one side predicts elevated yellow card accumulation for that same side, conditioned on the opponent's foul-drawing tendency.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Yellow card totals for Team B rise with Team B's foul production rate, and this relationship is amplified when Team A's foul-drawing rate (fouls AGAINST) is also elevated, creating a joint cross-observable surplus in total match yellow cards
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B commits substantially more fouls than Team A (12.54 FOR vs 11.04 FOR), and Team B's foul rate has risen further in recent matches (14.0 RECENT_5). Meanwhile, Team A concedes more fouls than it commits (12.08 AGAINST vs 11.04 FOR). The joint relationship between Team B's foul production and Team A's yellow card accumulation (and vice versa) — where one team's fouling rate drives the other team's card exposure — is an asymmetric cross-observable relationship between different observables for the two sides.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) across two sides asymmetrically — Team B's foul production driving card outcomes, conditioned on Team A's foul-drawing profile. It is not a single observable against one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on the second-half card accumulation FOR each team and each team's full-match foul production rate. The mechanism requires both the within-match half-level card split and the cross-observable foul rate to be evaluated together — the second-half card asymmetry is only interpretable in the context of which team is the higher fouler.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second-half card total is elevated and asymmetrically distributed toward Team B when Team B's foul production rate is above the competition baseline, and this asymmetry is amplified in the second half relative to what full-match card averages would suggest
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B accumulates more second-half cards FOR (1.417) than Team A (1.12), while Team A accumulates more second-half cards AGAINST (1.76) than Team B AGAINST (0.667). This asymmetric second-half card profile, when jointly conditioned on each team's foul production rate (Team B's fouls rising in recent matches), suggests a structural second-half disciplinary imbalance that is not captured by full-match card or foul averages alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This combines a within-match half-level split (cards_2h, a second-half-only observable) with a cross-observable conditioning on foul production, and evaluates the asymmetry across both sides simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's shots FOR is well below competition average AND Team B's shots FOR is well above competition average, then examine whether Team A's corners FOR (and corners AGAINST) diverge from competition-context corner baseline in a directionally consistent way across historical matches sharing this joint profile.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's shots FOR is suppressed relative to competition average while its opponent's shots FOR is elevated, that team's corners FOR falls below competition-context corner average, and the relationship is stronger than either shots or corners alone would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume deficit (low shots FOR, high shots AGAINST) combined with Team B's high shot-to-shots-on-target conversion efficiency jointly predict a suppressed corner-kick total for Team A relative to the competition baseline, because a team that rarely generates attacking sequences also rarely forces corners, while a dominant opponent's shot volume does not necessarily translate into corners allowed.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and corner_kicks) across two sides simultaneously; it cannot be reduced to a single observable compared against one opponent-descriptor band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's shots_on_target FOR is substantially below Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST (i.e., Team A underperforms what Team B typically concedes) AND Team B's shots_on_target FOR substantially exceeds Team A's shots_on_target AGAINST. Measure the joint cross-team shots-on-target differential against competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's shots-on-target FOR is below Team B's shots-on-target AGAINST, and simultaneously Team B's shots-on-target FOR exceeds Team A's shots-on-target AGAINST, the combined match shots-on-target total is skewed toward Team B, and this skew is larger than either team's own mirror relationship would predict independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetry between Team A's shots-on-target FOR and Team B's shots-on-target AGAINST (i.e., Team A generates far fewer shots on target than Team B concedes) jointly with Team B's shots-on-target FOR versus Team A's shots-on-target AGAINST creates a cross-observable asymmetric profile that predicts a skewed total-shots-on-target distribution in the match, distinct from what either team's own mirror would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team relationship involving two distinct observables (shots_on_target FOR for one team vs. shots_on_target AGAINST for the other) evaluated jointly; it is not reducible to a single observable's own-vs-allowed mirror.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint within-match state: Team A's goals FOR in the first half versus second half (half-level split), and Team B's goals FOR in the first half versus second half. Measure whether the cross-team half-level goal distribution diverges from a uniform within-match distribution, and whether this divergence is consistent across historical matches.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's goals FOR are concentrated in the second half relative to the first half, while Team B's goals FOR are concentrated in the first half relative to the second half; this creates a within-match temporal asymmetry where the two halves have systematically different goal-scoring profiles for each team, and the joint pattern is more predictive of half-level goal distribution than either team's full-match average.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half goal-scoring rate relative to its first-half rate, combined with Team B's first-half goal-scoring rate relative to its second-half rate, jointly characterise a within-match temporal goal-distribution asymmetry: Team A scores more in the second half while Team B scores more in the first half, suggesting the match's goal timing profile is non-uniform and asymmetric across halves in a way that neither team's full-match goal average alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split applied jointly to both teams' goal-scoring timing, comparing first-half vs. second-half rates across both sides simultaneously — not a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B holds above-average possession (consistent with its season profile) AND Team A's fouls FOR are at or above their own season average. Within this joint state, examine whether Team A's yellow_cards FOR and cards_2h FOR are elevated relative to their unconditional averages, and whether Team B's cards_2h AGAINST is correspondingly elevated.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's possession is high and Team A's foul rate is simultaneously elevated, Team A's yellow cards and second-half cards rise above their unconditional averages; the joint conditioning on both possession and fouls is more discriminating than either variable alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between Team B's possession dominance and Team A's foul rate reveals whether Team A's fouling behaviour rises as a function of being out-possessed — i.e., whether the combination of high opponent possession and elevated own-foul rate co-occurs more than either variable's marginal distribution would predict, and whether this joint state is associated with elevated second-half card accumulation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship among three distinct observables (possession, fouls, cards_2h/yellow_cards) across two sides; it cannot be reduced to a single observable with one opponent-descriptor band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint within-match half-level state: Team A's corners FOR in first half vs. second half, and Team B's corners FOR in first half vs. second half. Measure whether the combined half-level corner distribution across both teams diverges from a uniform within-match split, and whether the two teams' half-level profiles are systematically offset (one front-loaded, one back-loaded) or aligned.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's corners FOR are more concentrated in the second half (second-half average exceeds first-half average), while Team B's corners FOR are more evenly distributed or front-loaded; this joint half-level asymmetry means the second half is expected to have a higher combined corner total than the first half, a relationship not visible from full-match corner averages alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick half-level split (first-half vs. second-half corners FOR) combined with Team B's corner-kick half-level split (first-half vs. second-half corners FOR) jointly characterise whether the within-match corner distribution is front-loaded or back-loaded for each side, and whether the two teams' half-level corner profiles are complementary or reinforcing — a joint within-match state that the full-match corner totals alone cannot capture.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split applied jointly to both teams' corner production, comparing the two halves across both sides simultaneously — not a single observable with one coarse band, and not a simple recent-vs-long-run comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning on Team A's possession FOR (home and all-venue) and Team B's shots FOR split by venue (HOME vs AWAY). The mechanism requires simultaneously observing that Team A holds dominant possession AND that Team B's away shot rate is substantially below their home shot rate — two distinct observables across two distinct venue dimensions for different sides.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's possession FOR is elevated and Team B's shots FOR AWAY is markedly lower than Team B's shots FOR HOME, Team B's total shot count in the fixture is suppressed relative to Team B's all-venue average.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot volume exhibits a strong home/away asymmetry that, when combined with Team A's possession dominance, creates a joint suppression of Team B's shot production in away contexts: Team B generates substantially fewer shots away than at home, while Team A consistently holds high possession both home and away, suggesting that when a high-possession Team A hosts a Team B whose away shot volume is markedly lower than their home volume, Team B's shots are jointly suppressed beyond what either observable alone would indicate.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single-observable mirror or a single observable with one coarse band. It requires a joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession for one team, shots for the other) and two distinct venue-dimension splits simultaneously — one for each team — which cannot be reduced to any single-observable comparison or single-band conditioning.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning on Team A's shots_on_target AGAINST (all-venue) relative to competition context, and Team B's shots_on_target FOR split by venue (HOME vs AWAY). The mechanism fires when Team A suppresses opponent shots-on-target below league average AND Team B's away shots-on-target is substantially below their home rate.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's shots_on_target AGAINST is below competition context AND Team B's shots_on_target FOR AWAY is below Team B's shots_on_target FOR HOME, Team B's shots-on-target in the fixture is doubly suppressed relative to Team B's all-venue average.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-on-target production shows a pronounced home/away split, while Team A's shots-on-target allowed is consistently below the competition average. The joint relationship between Team A's defensive shots-on-target suppression and Team B's away-specific reduction in shots-on-target creates a compounding effect on Team B's on-target output that is not captured by either observable in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires a joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots_on_target allowed by Team A, shots_on_target produced by Team B) each conditioned on a different dimension (competition baseline for one, venue split for the other). This is an asymmetric cross-team, cross-observable joint relationship not reducible to any single-observable or single-band covered case.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning on Team B's fouls FOR split by venue (AWAY vs HOME) and Team A's fouls AGAINST (i.e., fouls drawn by Team A's opponents, which reflects how many fouls Team A draws). The mechanism requires simultaneously observing Team B's elevated away foul rate and Team A's above-average fouls-against rate — two distinct observables for two different sides.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's fouls FOR AWAY exceeds Team B's fouls FOR HOME, and Team A's fouls AGAINST exceeds the competition context fouls average, yellow cards FOR Team B in the fixture rise above Team B's all-venue yellow card average.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B accumulates yellow cards at a rate substantially above the competition average, and this elevated foul/card rate is further amplified in away matches where Team B commits more fouls than at home. When Team B plays away against a team (Team A) that draws fouls at above-average rates, the joint interaction of Team B's away foul tendency and Team A's foul-drawing rate predicts elevated yellow card volume beyond what either team's individual card average suggests.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and yellow cards) across two teams, conditioned simultaneously on venue split for one team and opponent foul-drawing rate for the other. It is not a single-observable mirror or a single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning on Team A's cards_2h AGAINST (second half) and Team B's cards_2h FOR (second half), both relative to the competition context cards_2h baseline. The mechanism requires simultaneously observing that Team A allows above-average second-half cards AND Team B produces above-average second-half cards — a joint cross-team relationship within a specific within-match period.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's cards_2h AGAINST exceeds the competition context cards_2h baseline AND Team B's cards_2h FOR also exceeds that baseline, total second-half cards in the fixture rise above the competition average in a compounding (super-additive) manner.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Second-half card accumulation (cards_2h) is jointly shaped by both teams' second-half card tendencies in an asymmetric way: Team A concedes more cards in the second half than it earns, while Team B earns more second-half cards than it concedes. The interaction of Team B's elevated second-half card production and Team A's elevated second-half card concession creates a compounding second-half card environment that is not captured by either team's individual second-half card rate alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism requires a joint relationship between two distinct team-role perspectives on the same within-match-period observable (cards_2h FOR for one team, cards_2h AGAINST for the other), conditioned on a competition baseline. It is not a single-observable mirror (which would compare one team's FOR against the opponent's AGAINST for the same observable without the joint interaction logic) and it exploits the within-match half-level resolution.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning on Team B's goals FOR split by half (FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF) and Team A's goals AGAINST split by half (FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF). The mechanism requires simultaneously observing that Team B scores disproportionately in the second half AND that Team A concedes disproportionately in the second half — a joint within-match temporal interaction across two teams.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's goals FOR SECOND_HALF substantially exceeds Team B's goals FOR FIRST_HALF, and Team A's goals AGAINST SECOND_HALF substantially exceeds Team A's goals AGAINST FIRST_HALF, second-half goal volume in the fixture rises above what the full-match averages and competition context would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's goal-scoring shows a pronounced first-half versus second-half asymmetry (markedly more goals in the second half than the first), while Team A's goals conceded are also back-loaded (more conceded in the second half). The joint within-match temporal structure — Team B's second-half goal surge combined with Team A's second-half defensive vulnerability — creates a compounding late-match goal environment that is not captured by either team's full-match goal averages alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship between two distinct team-role perspectives on the same observable (goals) each split by within-match half, for two different teams simultaneously. It is not a single-observable with one coarse band — it combines a half-level split for one team's offensive output with a half-level split for the other team's defensive output, requiring both dimensions to be active at once.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR (to derive its conversion ratio) alongside Team B's shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST (to derive its defensive filtering ratio). The mechanism fires when one side has high shot volume but low on-target ratio while the opponent suppresses shots allowed to a low absolute level.

mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume is high but its shots-on-target conversion rate (shots_on_target / shots) is low relative to Team B's, while Team B concedes very few shots against. The joint relationship between Team A's shot-to-on-target ratio and Team B's shots-allowed suppression determines whether Team A's volume translates into meaningful on-target threat, or is neutralised by Team B's defensive structure.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly relating two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for both sides simultaneously — a four-variable joint relationship. It cannot be reduced to a single observable compared against one opponent-descriptor band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's possession FOR and Team A's shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST. Measure whether matches where Team B holds possession above a threshold co-occur with Team A facing shots-against volumes that exceed what Team A's defensive shots-allowed average alone would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's shots-against volume rises with Team B's possession share in a non-linear fashion — the relationship steepens once possession crosses a saturation threshold rather than scaling linearly.

The joint relationship between Team B's possession share and Team A's shots-against volume tests whether possession dominance by Team B translates into a disproportionate shots-against burden for Team A beyond what each observable predicts independently.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable relationship (possession and shots/shots_on_target) across asymmetric sides, with a threshold/saturation test on a continuous possession variable. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's fouls FOR (committed) and Team B's corner_kicks FOR. In matches where Team A's foul rate is elevated above its own season average, measure whether Team B's corner count also rises above Team B's baseline corner production — testing a cross-observable interaction between one team's disciplinary output and the opponent's set-piece volume.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's corner-kick volume rises with Team A's foul rate — the relationship is positive and potentially non-linear, with corner counts increasing more steeply once Team A's fouls exceed a threshold above the competition mean.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A commits fouls at a high rate (especially in recent matches) while Team B earns corners at a moderate rate. The joint relationship between Team A's foul rate and Team B's corner-kick production tests whether Team A's foul-heavy style inflates Team B's set-piece opportunities (corners) beyond what Team B's corner production average alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team, cross-observable relationship (Team A fouls → Team B corners). It cannot be reduced to either observable alone against a single opponent-descriptor band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's yellow_cards FOR trend (recent vs. all-prior) and Team B's cards_2h FOR (second-half cards earned). Measure whether the co-occurrence of Team A's elevated recent yellow-card rate and Team B's above-average second-half card rate produces a second-half total-cards environment above competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half card volume is elevated when Team A's yellow-card rate is trending upward (recent > season average) and Team B's cards_2h rate is simultaneously above competition average — the joint condition produces a super-additive disciplinary environment in the second half.

The joint relationship between Team A's escalating yellow-card trend and Team B's second-half card-earning pattern tests whether the combination of a foul-prone Team A and a card-drawing Team B produces a second-half disciplinary environment that exceeds what either team's card rate alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly relating three observables (yellow_cards, cards_2h, fouls) across both teams with a within-match period split (second half) and a trend dimension (recent vs. all-prior). It is not reducible to any single observable with one conditioning band.

Measure whether the combination of Team B's first-half scoring tendency and Team A's first-half defensive vulnerability produces a first-half goals environment that exceeds the competition's half-level baseline more than either team's individual half-split would suggest.

The joint first-half vs. second-half goal-timing asymmetry across both teams — where Team B's first-half goal rate is high and Team A's first-half goals-against rate is also high — tests whether the two teams' half-level goal distributions interact to concentrate match goals in the first half beyond what either team's half-split alone would predict.

It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band or a simple home/away split.

Measure whether the joint state of high possession by one side AND high shots-against by the other side is associated with a divergence between total shots and shots-on-target conversion rate, compared to either variable alone.

It requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables from two different sides simultaneously (Team A possession FOR vs Team B shots AGAINST) and examining a derived ratio (shots-on-target / shots), which is a non-linear relationship not captured by any single-observable comparison.

The joint interaction between Team B's venue-conditioned shot output and Team A's shots-conceded rate — both dimensions simultaneously — determines whether Team B's away shot suppression is further compounded or partially offset by Team A's defensive shot-allowing profile.

The engine covers venue alone or one opponent-descriptor band alone, but not their joint interaction on a cross-team asymmetric observable.

The within-match temporal interaction between Team A's half-level corner production and Team B's half-level corner-conceding rate — both measured at half resolution — jointly determines whether second-half corner volume is elevated beyond what full-match averages suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) dependence requiring half-resolution data for both teams simultaneously, and it conditions on a joint cross-team observable at half level — not reducible to a single observable's recent vs long-run level or a single coarse band.

Measure whether the asymmetric foul-rate divergence (Team A declining, Team B stable/rising) is associated with a shift in the cards distribution — specifically whether yellow cards and second-half cards skew toward the higher-fouling side beyond what each team's individual foul rate alone predicts.

The asymmetric divergence between one team's recent foul-rate trajectory and the other team's stable foul-rate — measured as a cross-team directional divergence rather than each team's own recent-vs-season split — jointly determines the total foul environment and the resulting cards exposure.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint cross-team asymmetric relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and cards) across two sides simultaneously, conditioned on the directional divergence between recent and season-level trends for each team — not a single observable's recent vs long-run comparison for one team.

Measure whether the cross-team half-level interaction produces a non-uniform within-match goal distribution — specifically whether the first half and second half goal rates for this matchup diverge from what the full-match averages and each team's individual half-split alone would predict.

The cross-team half-level goal-scoring asymmetry — Team A front-loaded, Team B defensively back-loaded — creates a joint within-match state where the half in which goals are most likely differs between the two teams' profiles, and this divergence is not captured by full-match goal averages alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on half-level splits for two distinct teams on the same observable (goals), examining the cross-team interaction of their respective half-level asymmetries — not a single team's half-split in isolation, which is already covered.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on both Team B's recent-5 shots (16.2) being substantially above its all-prior average (12.539) AND Team B's recent-5 shots_on_target (5.4) being substantially above its all-prior average (4.667), while Team A's recent-5 shots_on_target allowed (3.6) is below its all-prior average allowed (4.524). The joint condition of both shot volume AND on-target accuracy being simultaneously elevated in recent form — compared to each team's long-run baseline — may predict a higher combined shots-on-target total in the fixture than either team's long-run average alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single-observable mirror or a single observable with one coarse band. It requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for the same team, conditioning on both being simultaneously elevated in recent form — a two-observable joint signal that cannot be reduced to any single-observable comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (1) Team B's venue-split asymmetry in goals scored (home vs away all-prior), (2) Team B's recent-5 goals FOR exceeding both venue-split baselines, and (3) Team A's half-level split showing second-half goals conceded substantially exceeding first-half goals conceded. The joint condition of Team B playing away with a recent-form surge AND Team A having a structurally elevated second-half goals-against rate creates a cross-observable, cross-team asymmetric signal for second-half goal scoring.

It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band — it requires the joint conditioning on venue asymmetry, recent-form regime shift, and within-match half-level structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's home corner production being substantially above its away production (a venue asymmetry), while Team B's corners-against rate is below competition baseline. The mechanism tests whether the home team's venue-driven corner surplus is suppressed or amplified when the away opponent has a structurally low corners-against rate — requiring both the home/away production split and the opponent's defensive corner profile to be considered together.

The joint relationship between Team A's home corner production advantage and Team B's below-average corners-against rate creates a cross-team, two-observable asymmetric signal: one team's venue-driven production surplus interacts with the opponent's defensive corner suppression tendency.

It requires the joint interaction of Team A's venue-split asymmetry in corner production with Team B's corners-against rate relative to competition baseline — two distinct observables (home production split and opponent's defensive corner rate) conditioning each other, which is not reducible to one observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (1) Team B's cards_2h FOR and AGAINST both exceeding competition baseline, (2) Team A's recent-5 fouls FOR being below its all-prior average, and (3) Team A's recent-5 yellow_cards FOR declining below its all-prior average. The mechanism tests whether the combination of one team's structural second-half card elevation and the other team's recent foul/card reduction produces a net second-half card total that diverges from what either team's single-observable baseline predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team has structurally elevated second-half card rates on both sides while the opposing team shows a recent decline in fouls and yellow cards, the combined second-half card total is pulled in opposing directions — the net total is lower than Team B's baseline alone would predict but higher than Team A's recent form alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half cards (cards_2h FOR: 1.556, AGAINST: 1.571) are near the competition average (1.49), while Team B's second-half cards (FOR: 1.755, AGAINST: 1.765) are notably above the competition average. The joint condition of one team (Team B) having elevated second-half card rates on both sides of the ledger — while Team A's fouls committed are declining in recent form (12.6 recent-5 vs 13.127 all-prior) — creates an asymmetric cross-team signal: Team B's structural second-half card elevation interacts with Team A's recent foul reduction to produce a non-trivial joint prediction about second-half disciplinary volume.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint interaction of three distinct observables (cards_2h, fouls, yellow_cards) across two teams, with a within-match period split (second half) and a recent-vs-long-run regime comparison. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's recent-5 possession being above both its all-prior and home-venue averages, while Team B's recent-5 offsides FOR are below both its all-prior and away-venue averages. The mechanism tests whether the combination of home-team possession surge and away-team offside suppression co-occur systematically — requiring two distinct observables (possession and offsides) from two different teams to be evaluated jointly.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the home team's recent possession rises above its own home baseline, the away team's offsides FOR rate is suppressed below its own away baseline — the two observables move in opposing directions jointly, and this joint pattern is more informative than either observable measured independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession in recent form (53.2% recent-5) has risen above its all-prior average (49.873%) and above its home average (52.219%), while Team B's offsides FOR in recent form (1.0 recent-5) have dropped below their all-prior average (1.542) and their away average (1.761). The joint relationship between Team A's recent possession surge and Team B's recent offside suppression — where higher possession by the home team typically compresses the space for away-team high-line runs — tests whether possession dominance and opponent offside rate are jointly linked in a non-trivial way that neither observable captures alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and offsides) across two teams, conditioning on both a recent-vs-long-run regime shift and a venue split simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's shots-for is above the competition mean AND Team B's fouls-against is above the competition mean simultaneously. Measure Team A's corner-kicks-for in those jointly-conditioned matches versus the baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's corner-kick production rises when both Team A's shot volume is elevated and Team B's foul rate is elevated, more than either condition alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume is high but its conversion to shots-on-target is relatively modest, while Team B concedes a high volume of fouls (suggesting defensive pressure). The joint relationship between Team A's shots-for and Team B's fouls-against — two distinct observables from opposite sides — may predict corner-kick generation beyond what either observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint conditioning on two distinct observables from two different teams simultaneously (Team A shots-for AND Team B fouls-against), which is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the possession-holding team (Team A role) holds possession above a threshold AND the defending team (Team B role) commits fouls above a threshold. Measure cards_2h for the defending team in those jointly-conditioned matches.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The defending team's second-half card accumulation rises as the joint combination of opponent possession dominance and own foul rate increases, beyond what either variable alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A dominates possession (all-prior ~58%, recent ~58%) while Team B commits fouls at a high rate (all-prior ~13.5, against ~15.8 — well above competition mean ~12.9). The joint relationship between Team A's possession advantage and Team B's foul rate may produce an asymmetric card-loading pattern in the second half, where Team B accumulates cards-2h at a rate above what either team's individual card profile predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship: one team's possession level combined with the opposing team's foul rate predicting the opposing team's card outcome — two distinct observables from different sides, not a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split goals by half for both teams simultaneously. Measure the interaction between Team A's 2H-vs-1H goal-for ratio and Team B's 1H-vs-2H goals-against ratio to identify whether the half in which goals are most likely to occur is jointly determined by both teams' half-level profiles.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's second-half goal-scoring rate exceeds its first-half rate AND Team B's first-half goals-conceded rate exceeds its second-half rate, the match's goal distribution across halves is more skewed toward the second half than competition baseline, but the asymmetry between the two teams' half profiles creates a non-additive joint pattern.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A scores goals at a markedly higher rate in the second half than the first half (1H: ~0.755, 2H: ~1.108), while Team B concedes goals at a markedly higher rate in the first half than the second half (1H: ~0.676, 2H: ~0.490). This asymmetric half-level goal-scoring profile across the two teams — Team A back-loaded, Team B front-loaded in conceding — creates a joint within-match state structure that is not captured by full-match goal averages alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct half-level splits from two different teams (Team A's 2H goal-for vs 1H goal-for AND Team B's 1H goals-against vs 2H goals-against), which is a within-match state interaction across two observables from different sides — not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the attacking team's shots-on-target-to-shots ratio is above a threshold AND the defending team's fouls-against rate is above a threshold. Measure the attacking team's goals-for in those jointly-conditioned matches versus matches where only one condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals-for rises more steeply when both shot quality (SOT/shots ratio) is high AND the opponent's foul rate is high, compared to when only one condition holds — suggesting a super-additive or threshold interaction between the two observables.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots-on-target conversion rate (shots_on_target / shots) is relatively high (SOT ~5.4 vs shots ~13.75, all-prior), while Team B's shots-on-target rate is lower (SOT ~4.27 vs shots ~11.62). Meanwhile, Team B concedes fouls at a high rate (~15.8 against, well above competition ~12.9). The joint relationship between Team A's shot quality (shots-on-target as a share of shots) and Team B's defensive foul rate may predict Team A's goal output beyond what either observable alone captures — specifically, whether high shot quality combined with a high-fouling opponent produces a non-linear uplift in goals.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship between two distinct observables (shot quality ratio and opponent foul rate) from different sides, requiring simultaneous conditioning on both — not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Identify matches where a team's recent-5 yellow-card rate is substantially below its all-prior rate (suppressed regime) AND the opponent's fouls-against rate is above the competition mean. Measure cards_2h for both teams in those jointly-conditioned matches versus the baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team is in a suppressed recent yellow-card regime but faces an opponent that draws fouls at an elevated rate, second-half card accumulation reverts toward or exceeds the longer-run mean rather than continuing the suppressed trend — a regime-reversion pattern conditioned on the opponent's foul-drawing profile.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's yellow cards have dropped sharply in recent matches (recent-5: ~0.6 vs all-prior: ~1.98), while Team B's fouls-against (fouls conceded by opponents of Team B) are high (~15.8 all-prior). The divergence between Team A's recent disciplinary trend and its longer-run profile, combined with Team B's persistent high-foul-drawing tendency, creates a cross-observable regime structure: when a team's recent card rate is in a suppressed regime relative to its own history AND the opponent draws fouls at an elevated rate, the second-half card accumulation pattern may differ from what either team's standalone card profile predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a sequencing/regime structure (recent vs all-prior card rate divergence) combined with a cross-team observable (opponent foul-drawing rate), jointly conditioning on two distinct dimensions from different observables and different teams — not reducible to a single observable with one band or a simple recent-vs-long-run comparison alone.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where both teams hold below-competition-average possession (competition mean ~50%), then examine whether the team with higher shot volume relative to its possession share generates corners at a rate above what its raw possession alone would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kick production rises with shot volume even when possession is suppressed, and the relationship between shots and corners is steeper for the lower-possession side than for higher-possession sides.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When a low-possession team (Team A, ~42% possession) faces an opponent that also operates with low possession (~39%), the combined possession-deficit context suppresses corner kick production for both sides relative to the competition norm, but the team that generates more shots despite low possession (Team A: ~11.7 shots FOR vs Team B: ~10.8 shots FOR) may disproportionately convert shot volume into corners. The joint relationship between a team's own possession share and its shot volume in determining corner kick output is the mechanism to test.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession AND shots) for the same team, not a single observable against one coarse band. It tests a non-linear interaction between possession share and shot volume in producing corners, which is not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the defending team (Team B role) simultaneously allows above-competition-average shots AND holds below-competition-average possession, then measure corner kicks allowed in those matches versus matches where only one condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kicks allowed are elevated when both high shots-against and low possession co-occur, with the joint condition producing a higher corner rate than either condition alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B concedes a structurally high volume of shots (ALL_PRIOR ~16.9, RECENT_5 ~17.4) while also holding low possession (~39.5%). The joint condition of high shots-against AND low possession-for defines a defensive posture where the opponent (Team A) is likely to generate corners at an elevated rate. Test whether the combination of opponent high shots-against rate and own low possession jointly predicts elevated corner kicks allowed, beyond what either variable alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine two-observable joint conditioning (shots-against AND possession-for) on the same team, not a single observable with one coarse band. The interaction between these two dimensions is the novel structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where a team's red card rate exceeds the competition average AND the team concedes above-average shot volumes. Within those matches, compare the ratio of second-half cards to full-match yellow cards against the baseline ratio in matches where only one condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second-half card rate rises disproportionately (relative to full-match yellow cards) when both elevated red card propensity and high shots-against co-occur, indicating a non-additive escalation in the second half.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B carries a notably elevated red card rate (ALL_PRIOR ~0.375 per match, away ~0.5) relative to the competition norm (~0.137). When a team with a high red card rate also concedes high shot volumes (Team B: ~16.9 shots against), test whether the co-occurrence of elevated red card propensity and high shots-against is associated with a disproportionate increase in second-half cards (cards_2h) relative to full-match yellow cards, suggesting a within-match escalation pattern driven by the joint pressure of numerical disadvantage risk and shot volume.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct observables (red card rate AND shots-against) and examines a within-match temporal asymmetry (second-half cards vs full-match cards), combining a two-observable joint condition with a half-level split. Neither element alone is covered.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on match-ups where Team A's cards_2h FOR exceeds its cards_2h AGAINST, AND Team B's cards_2h AGAINST exceeds its cards_2h FOR (i.e., both asymmetries align to inflate second-half cards). Within those match-ups, also examine whether foul rates (Team A fouls FOR ~10.75, Team B fouls AGAINST ~12.96) reinforce the card escalation pattern.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total second-half cards are elevated when both teams' individual second-half card asymmetries (FOR vs AGAINST) point toward higher card production, and this joint alignment produces a higher second-half card total than either team's individual rate alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A generates more second-half cards (FOR: 1.375) than it concedes (AGAINST: 0.875) in the second half, while Team B concedes more second-half cards (AGAINST: 1.625) than it produces (FOR: 1.125). Test whether the asymmetry between a team's own second-half card production and its opponent's second-half card allowance — when both point in the same direction — jointly predicts an elevated total second-half card count, beyond what each team's individual card rate would suggest in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team relationship: it jointly uses Team A's FOR/AGAINST second-half card asymmetry AND Team B's FOR/AGAINST second-half card asymmetry as two distinct dimensions, then adds fouls as a third observable. This is not reducible to a single observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on match-ups where one team improves defensively in the second half (lower goals-against in 2H vs 1H) while the opponent improves offensively in the second half (higher goals-for in 2H vs 1H). Examine whether the net within-match goal distribution (1H vs 2H total goals) is systematically shifted relative to competition baseline, and whether shots_on_target half-level splits reinforce or contradict the goal-timing pattern.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's second-half defensive improvement and the opponent's second-half offensive improvement co-occur, the within-match goal distribution shifts toward the second half, and this shift is amplified relative to what either team's individual half-level goal rate alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A scores more goals in the second half (FOR 2H: 0.583) than the first half (FOR 1H: 0.583 — equal), while conceding more in the first half (AGAINST 1H: 0.875) than the second half (AGAINST 2H: 0.75). Team B scores more in the second half (FOR 2H: 0.708) than the first half (FOR 1H: 0.542), and concedes more in the first half (AGAINST 1H: 0.5) than the second half (AGAINST 2H: 0.792 — reversed). Test whether the joint half-level goal-scoring and goal-conceding profiles of both teams — specifically the interaction between Team A's defensive improvement in the second half and Team B's offensive improvement in the second half — predicts a distinctive within-match goal-timing pattern (more goals in one half than the other) that differs from what each team's individual half-level rates would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct half-level observables (goals FOR by half AND goals AGAINST by half) for both teams simultaneously, testing a cross-team interaction across two within-match periods. It is not reducible to a single observable's recent vs long-run level, a single half-level split, or a single-band conditioning.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where a team's recent shots FOR (RECENT_5) exceeds its ALL_PRIOR shots FOR by a meaningful margin, while its recent shots_on_target FOR (RECENT_5) does not keep pace (i.e., on-target ratio falls). Measure whether corner_kicks FOR is elevated in those same matches, since off-target shots frequently produce corners. Apply jointly to both TEAM_A and TEAM_B.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kick volume rises when shot volume is high but on-target ratio is suppressed, relative to matches where both shot volume and on-target ratio move together.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has surged in recent matches (RECENT_5) relative to its long-run average, while its shots-on-target rate (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR) has simultaneously declined in recent matches versus its long-run rate. The joint relationship between a rising shot count and a falling on-target conversion ratio — measured together across both teams — may predict corner kick volume differently than either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) and a third outcome (corners), not a single observable against one band. The ratio of shots_on_target to shots is a derived cross-observable quantity, and conditioning on its divergence from trend is not reducible to any single-observable split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where a team's RECENT_5 shots FOR is substantially above ALL_PRIOR shots FOR, while RECENT_5 goals FOR is substantially below ALL_PRIOR goals FOR. Within those matches, measure whether the opponent's shots_on_target AGAINST is also elevated, creating a joint two-team cross-observable state. Test whether total goals in such matches diverges from what either team's goal rate alone predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total match goals are suppressed relative to combined shot volume when one team's recent shot-to-goal conversion rate has collapsed, even as shot counts rise — the joint signal of high shots and low goals FOR is associated with continued goal underperformance.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's recent (RECENT_5) shots FOR have surged well above its ALL_PRIOR average, yet its goals FOR have collapsed in the same window. This divergence between shot volume and goal output — a joint cross-observable signal — may indicate that Team B's recent attacking output is generating volume without conversion, which interacts with Team A's defensive structure (shots_on_target AGAINST) to shape total match goal volume differently than either team's goal rate alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship across two distinct observables (shots and goals) for the same team, compared across two time windows, and then interacted with the opponent's defensive observable. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition simultaneously on: (1) Team A playing at home (where its corner FOR average is higher than away), and (2) Team B's second-half corners AGAINST being elevated relative to its first-half corners AGAINST. Measure whether the combination of these two dimensions — venue for Team A and half-level split for Team B — produces a compounding effect on second-half corner volume that exceeds what either dimension predicts independently.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half corner volume for Team A rises when both Team A's home corner advantage and Team B's second-half corner concession tendency are jointly present, more than either factor alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A generates substantially more corners at home than away, while Team B concedes more corners in the second half than the first half. The joint conditioning on Team A's home venue advantage in corner production AND Team B's second-half corner concession tendency — two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions — may predict second-half corner volume for Team A beyond what either dimension alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously: venue (home/away) and within-match half-level state (first half vs. second half corners allowed). The engine covers venue alone or half alone, but not their joint interaction across the two teams.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where: (1) the possession-holding team (Team A) also commits fouls at an above-average rate (home fouls FOR > away fouls FOR), and (2) the lower-possession team (Team B) has a recent fouls FOR above its all-prior average. Measure whether yellow card volume is elevated in this joint state — high possession asymmetry combined with elevated foul rates on both sides — relative to matches where only one of these conditions holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Yellow card volume rises when high possession asymmetry is jointly present with elevated foul rates for both teams, more than either observable predicts in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession advantage (both all-prior and recent) is paired with a fouls-committed rate that is higher at home than away, while Team B's recent fouls FOR have also risen above their all-prior average. The joint state of high possession for Team A AND elevated foul rates for both teams — two distinct observables interacting — may predict yellow card volume differently than possession or fouls alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship among three distinct observables (possession, fouls, yellow_cards) across both teams, with asymmetric roles (possession-holder vs. lower-possession team). It cannot be reduced to any single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where: (1) the away team (Team B) has a cards_2h FOR rate above the competition context second-half cards average, and (2) the home team (Team A) has a cards_2h AGAINST rate above the competition context average. This is an asymmetric cross-team pairing of two different observable perspectives (FOR for one team, AGAINST for the other) on the same metric, jointly conditioned. Also examine whether elevated fouls FOR for Team B in recent matches amplifies this second-half card tendency.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half total cards rise when the away team's cards_2h FOR tendency and the home team's cards_2h AGAINST tendency are jointly elevated above competition context, with the effect amplified when the away team's recent fouls FOR is also above its all-prior average.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half cards (cards_2h FOR) are above the competition context average, while Team A's cards_2h AGAINST are also above the competition context average. The asymmetric pairing — Team B tends to accumulate second-half cards, and Team A tends to draw second-half cards from opponents — jointly predicts second-half card volume beyond what either team's individual card rate or the competition baseline alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves an asymmetric cross-team pairing of FOR and AGAINST perspectives on the same metric (cards_2h), jointly conditioned against a competition baseline, and further interacted with a second observable (fouls). This is not reducible to a single observable with one band — it requires the joint state of both teams' asymmetric card tendencies plus a second observable.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where a team's recent-5 shots-for is elevated above its all-prior average while its recent-5 goals-for is simultaneously depressed below its all-prior average. Measure how often this joint divergence (high shots, low goals) co-occurs with a similarly divergent shots-on-target-to-shots ratio in the same window.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When recent shots-for rises above long-run average while recent goals-for falls below long-run average, the shots-on-target rate (shots_on_target / shots) is suppressed relative to the long-run ratio, indicating a conversion-quality deficit that is not visible from either observable in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has risen sharply in recent matches while its goals-for has fallen sharply in the same window, suggesting a joint divergence between shot production and conversion efficiency. The relationship between Team A's recent shots-for and recent goals-for, measured jointly against their long-run averages, may reveal a suppressed conversion rate that is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and goals) simultaneously diverging from their own baselines in opposite directions, then cross-referencing a third observable (shots_on_target). No single-observable mirror or single-band split captures this three-way joint state.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Pair Team A's shots_on_target FOR (recent-5 vs all-prior) against Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST (recent-5 vs all-prior), and simultaneously pair Team A's shots FOR against Team B's shots AGAINST. The conditioning is on the joint recent-form state of both teams across two distinct observables simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's recent shots-on-target-for is elevated relative to its long-run level and Team B's recent shots-on-target-against is simultaneously depressed relative to its long-run level, the cross-team alignment is doubly favorable for Team A's attacking output — a reinforcing joint signal not present when only one side's observable is considered.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-on-target allowed has declined sharply in recent matches while its shots allowed has also declined, but the ratio of shots-on-target-against to shots-against may have shifted. Jointly measuring Team A's shots-on-target-for against Team B's shots-on-target-against (an asymmetric cross-team pairing of different observables) tests whether the attacking quality Team A generates aligns with or diverges from the defensive quality Team B concedes.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team pairing: Team A's attacking observable is matched against Team B's defensive observable for the same metric, then both are simultaneously conditioned on their own recent-vs-long-run divergence. This is not a same-observable mirror (which uses one team's production vs the opponent's allowance at a single point in time without the joint recent-form conditioning across both).

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the half-level split jointly for both teams: compare Team A's corners-for in the first half vs second half against Team B's corners-against in the first half vs second half. The mechanism requires both the within-match half dimension and the cross-team asymmetry to be evaluated together.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: If Team A generates a disproportionately larger share of its corners in the second half while Team B concedes a disproportionately larger share of its corners in the second half, the corner advantage for Team A is amplified in the second half relative to what a full-match average would suggest — a half-level concentration effect not visible from full-match totals alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production is split asymmetrically across halves (first-half vs second-half), and Team B's corner-kick allowance is similarly split across halves. The joint within-match half-level profile of corner production for one team against corner allowance for the other — across both halves simultaneously — tests whether the corner advantage concentrates in a specific half rather than being uniform across the match.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two dimensions: (1) within-match half (first vs second), and (2) the cross-team pairing of Team A's production against Team B's allowance at the half level. Neither a single-observable full-match mirror nor a single half-level split for one team alone captures this joint structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (1) Team B's goals-for split by half (first-half rate vs second-half rate relative to full-match rate), and (2) Team A's goals-against split by half (first-half rate vs second-half rate relative to full-match rate). The mechanism fires when both halves align — i.e., Team B front-loads its scoring and Team A front-loads its conceding in the same half.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's first-half goals-for rate is elevated relative to its second-half rate, and Team A's first-half goals-against rate is simultaneously elevated relative to its second-half rate, the first half represents a compounded vulnerability window — a joint half-level asymmetry that is suppressed or invisible in full-match averages.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Goals are split asymmetrically across halves for both teams. Team B scores a disproportionate share of its goals in the first half (goals-for first-half vs second-half), while Team A concedes a disproportionate share of its goals in the first half (goals-against first-half vs second-half). The joint half-level goal-scoring profile of Team B's attack against Team A's defensive half-level vulnerability tests whether a specific half represents a compounded risk window.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint evaluation of two distinct half-level splits across two teams for the same observable, where the direction of the asymmetry must align. A single team's half-level split, or a full-match mirror, does not capture this compounded within-match state.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the venue-specific joint state: use Team A's home possession-for and home fouls-for together, and Team B's away possession-for and away fouls-for together. The mechanism tests the cross-observable relationship (possession vs fouls) for each team in their venue role, then compares the two teams' joint profiles against each other.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the team with lower venue-specific possession (Team B away) also has a higher venue-specific foul rate relative to the team with higher possession (Team A home), the foul-count asymmetry between the two teams is positively associated with the possession asymmetry — a joint two-observable, two-team relationship that is not reducible to either observable's mirror alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession advantage (home) is paired with its fouls-for rate (home vs away), and Team B's possession level (away) is paired with its fouls-for rate (away). The joint relationship between possession share and foul rate — measured simultaneously across both teams in the venue-specific context — tests whether the team with lower possession commits more fouls, and whether this asymmetry is amplified or reversed at this specific venue configuration.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and fouls) evaluated simultaneously for both teams in their respective venue roles, then cross-compared. No single-observable mirror or single-band split captures the cross-observable, cross-team, venue-conditioned joint structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on both Team A's recent-5 shots FOR and shots AGAINST each being elevated above their respective ALL_PRIOR means, AND Team B's recent-5 shots FOR also being elevated above its ALL_PRIOR mean. This is a joint three-directional condition across two teams and two perspectives, not a single observable with one band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams simultaneously show recent-form shot elevation (FOR and AGAINST), total match shots rise above what either team's long-run average alone would predict — a super-additive joint effect.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume surge in recent matches (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) coincides with a simultaneous surge in shots conceded, suggesting a joint high-tempo open-play regime rather than a one-sided dominance shift.
