mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires within-match half-level resolution for both teams simultaneously and conditions on a cross-team half-level differential — a within-match state structure. It is not reducible to a single team's corner average with one coarse band; it requires the joint half-split profiles of both sides.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint recent-versus-long-run drift for both teams simultaneously: measure the gap between RECENT_5 and ALL_PRIOR for yellow_cards AGAINST Team B, and the gap between RECENT_5 and ALL_PRIOR for yellow_cards FOR Team A. When both gaps move in opposite directions (Team B attracting more cards against, Team A committing fewer), test whether total match yellow cards and the distribution between teams differs from the baseline expectation set by long-run averages.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's recent yellow-cards-against rate has risen above its long-run rate while Team A's recent yellow-cards-for rate has fallen below its long-run rate, the disciplinary asymmetry (more cards on Team B's side) is amplified relative to what long-run averages predict; total yellow cards in the match are associated with this joint drift pattern.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's yellow card rate against it has spiked sharply in recent matches (AGAINST RECENT_5: 3.6 vs ALL_PRIOR: 1.955), while Team A's yellow card rate FOR has declined (FOR RECENT_5: 0.6 vs ALL_PRIOR: 0.8). This divergence in recent-versus-long-run trajectories for yellow cards on opposing sides — Team B attracting more cards against it recently while Team A is committing fewer fouls recently — represents a regime shift in the disciplinary asymmetry between the two teams that is not captured by either team's long-run average alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-team, two-direction regime-drift mechanism: it requires simultaneously conditioning on the recent-vs-long-run trajectory of yellow cards for both teams in opposite directions. It is not reducible to one team's recent level versus its long-run level (which is already covered); the novelty is the cross-team joint drift in opposing directions as a combined signal.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute each team's shots-on-target-to-shots ratio (FOR) from historical averages. Then condition goals output on whether a team's ratio is below vs. at/above the competition context baseline. The mechanism tests whether a low conversion ratio (many shots, few on target) for Team B co-occurs with suppressed goals FOR, while Team A's tighter ratio co-occurs with maintained goals FOR — a joint two-team asymmetric relationship.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's shots-on-target-to-shots ratio is materially lower than the competition baseline while the opponent's ratio is at or above baseline, the low-ratio team's goals FOR is suppressed relative to its raw shot volume, and the match's total goals rises less than raw shot counts would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot volume is structurally higher than its shots-on-target conversion rate, while Team A's shots and shots-on-target are more tightly coupled. The joint relationship between shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR across both teams — measured as the ratio of shots_on_target to shots — differs asymmetrically between the two sides, and this asymmetry may condition total goals in the match.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly comparing two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for both teams simultaneously, then relating that joint ratio asymmetry to a third observable (goals). It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band — it requires a cross-observable ratio and a cross-team asymmetry check.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each historical match, jointly evaluate Team B's possession FOR relative to competition baseline AND its shots_on_target FOR relative to competition baseline. Condition on matches where possession is below baseline: test whether shots_on_target FOR is maintained at or above baseline in those matches, versus matches where possession is at/above baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's possession is persistently below the competition baseline, its shots_on_target FOR does not scale proportionally with possession — the relationship between possession and shots_on_target saturates or decouples, indicating a counter-attacking profile where shot quality is maintained despite low ball share.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B habitually operates with low possession (all-prior mean ~42%, away mean ~41%) while facing opponents who dominate the ball (~58% possession against). The joint relationship between Team B's possession FOR and its shots_on_target FOR — both measured against the competition baseline — tests whether a low-possession team can maintain above-baseline shots-on-target output, and whether this combination predicts a counter-attacking shot profile distinct from a possession-led shot profile.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable relationship (possession AND shots_on_target) tested against a continuous possession threshold relative to baseline — not a single observable with one coarse band. It also involves an asymmetric cross-team comparison (Team B's low possession vs. Team A's high possession) to identify a structural regime difference.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly evaluate the sign and magnitude of each team's recent-5 vs. all-prior corner kicks FOR deviation from the competition baseline. The mechanism tests matches where Team A's recent trend is above its own long-run mean AND above competition baseline, while simultaneously Team B's recent trend is below its own long-run mean AND below competition baseline — a two-team, two-window joint condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's corner kicks FOR trend is rising above both its own long-run mean and the competition baseline while the opponent's trend is falling below both, the corner differential between the two teams is amplified beyond what either team's individual trend predicts in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner kicks FOR show a notable divergence between its all-prior mean (~4.8) and its recent-5 mean (6.6), while Team B's corner kicks FOR show the opposite divergence (all-prior ~5.0, recent-5 only 3.8). The joint condition of one team's corners trending sharply upward while the opponent's trend sharply downward — both deviating from the competition baseline (~5.3) in opposite directions — may condition the total corner differential in the match beyond what either team's individual trend alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two teams' recent-vs-long-run deviations for the same observable — a joint two-team, two-window regime condition. It is not reducible to a single team's recent vs. long-run split, nor to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compute the ratio of cards_2h FOR to fouls FOR from historical averages. Then jointly condition on whether both teams' ratios are above or below the competition baseline ratio. Test whether matches where one team's foul-to-card ratio is high (many fouls per card) differ in second-half card totals from matches where the ratio is low (cards accumulate quickly relative to fouls).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's historical cards_2h FOR is elevated relative to its fouls FOR (high card-per-foul rate), second-half cards in the match rise with fouls at a steeper rate than for teams with a low card-per-foul ratio — suggesting a non-linear or threshold escalation in card accumulation beyond a foul-rate baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half cards (cards_2h FOR: ~1.30) are notably higher than Team B's second-half cards (cards_2h FOR: ~0.94), and both differ from the competition context second-half cards mean (~1.19). The joint relationship between a team's fouls FOR and its cards_2h FOR — tested across both teams simultaneously — may reveal whether high-fouling teams accumulate second-half cards at a rate disproportionate to their foul volume, indicating a threshold or escalation effect in card accumulation as a function of foul rate.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable relationship (fouls and cards_2h) requiring a ratio computed across both, then tested for non-linear escalation. It is not a single observable with one band, and it involves a within-match period split (second half) combined with a cross-observable ratio condition.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly evaluate the sign and magnitude of each team's recent-5 vs. all-prior offsides FOR deviation from the competition baseline. Condition on matches where Team A's recent offsides trend is well above its long-run mean AND above competition baseline, while Team B's recent trend is well below its long-run mean AND below competition baseline. Then test whether this joint regime is associated with a specific pattern in possession and shots distribution.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's offsides FOR trend is rising sharply above its own long-run mean while the opponent's is falling sharply below, the total offsides in the match is amplified beyond what either team's individual trend predicts, and the high-offsides team's possession and shots FOR are also elevated — consistent with a high-line pressing regime that generates both more offsides and more attacking volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides FOR show a sharp recent spike (recent-5 mean: 2.6 vs. all-prior mean: 1.28), while Team B's offsides FOR show a sharp recent drop (recent-5 mean: 0.5 vs. all-prior mean: 1.43). The joint condition of one team's offsides trending sharply upward (suggesting a more aggressive high-line attacking approach) while the opponent's offsides trend sharply downward (suggesting a more cautious or deeper attacking line) — both deviating from the competition baseline (~1.46) in opposite directions — may condition the total offsides in the match and relate to the attacking line depth asymmetry between the two sides.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two teams' recent-vs-long-run deviations for offsides simultaneously, then relating that joint regime to a second observable (possession/shots) to test for a structural attacking-line asymmetry. It is not reducible to a single observable with one band or a simple recent-vs-long-run split for one team.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's shots FOR vs AGAINST differential AND Team B's goals FOR relative to shots FOR (conversion ratio). The mechanism asks whether the cross-team asymmetry — high shot generator (Team A) facing a low-conversion attacker (Team B) — produces a systematically different goals total than either team's shot or goal averages alone would imply.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total goals rises with shot volume only when conversion efficiency (goals per shot) is also elevated; when one side has high shots but low conversion, total goals is suppressed relative to what shot counts alone predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume dominance (high shots FOR, low shots AGAINST) jointly with Team B's poor conversion efficiency (goals FOR relative to shots FOR) conditions the total goals outcome: when one side generates many shots but the opposing side converts at a low rate, total goals may not rise proportionally with shot volume.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship across two distinct observables (shots and goals) for two different sides simultaneously. It cannot be reduced to a single observable mirror or a single observable with one coarse band — it requires measuring the interaction between Team A's shot generation and Team B's conversion rate as a joint conditioning structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's shots_on_target FOR (high, above competition context) and Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST (also above competition context). The mechanism tests whether the co-occurrence of both conditions — attacker generates many shots on target AND defender concedes many shots on target — produces a multiplicative rather than additive effect on goals scored.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals FOR for the attacking team rises more steeply when both the attacker's shots_on_target FOR and the defender's shots_on_target AGAINST are simultaneously elevated, compared to when only one condition holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots-on-target FOR versus Team B's shots-on-target AGAINST jointly determine whether Team A's high goal-scoring rate is sustained: when a high-volume attacking team faces a side that concedes many shots on target, the attacking team's goals FOR should be elevated beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots_on_target and goals) across two sides. It is not a single-observable mirror (shots_on_target FOR vs AGAINST for the same team) nor a single observable with one coarse band — it requires the simultaneous conditioning on both Team A's attacking output and Team B's defensive concession of shots on target.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's possession FOR (well above 50%) and Team B's fouls AGAINST (i.e., fouls committed by Team B, which is the fouls AGAINST perspective for Team B's opponents). The mechanism tests whether possession dominance combined with opponent foul pressure jointly drives corner kick generation above what either variable alone implies.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kicks FOR the possession-dominant team rise when both possession dominance and opponent foul rate are simultaneously elevated, with the joint effect exceeding what either variable alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession dominance jointly with Team B's elevated foul rate AGAINST (fouls committed) conditions corner kick generation: when a possession-dominant team faces a side that commits many fouls, corner kicks FOR the dominant team should be elevated beyond what possession or fouls alone predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship across two distinct observables (possession and fouls) conditioning a third (corner_kicks). It is not reducible to a single-observable mirror or a single coarse band — it requires measuring the interaction between Team A's possession share and Team B's foul-committing tendency as a joint structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the cross-team asymmetry between Team A's goals FOR in the first half and Team B's goals AGAINST in the first half, then test whether this asymmetry (one side likely leading at half-time) is associated with elevated cards_2h for the trailing side in the second half. This uses half-level goal splits to infer match state, then links that state to second-half card accumulation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Cards in the second half rise when the first-half goal asymmetry between the two sides is large, as the trailing team increases foul rate under pressure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetry between Team A's first-half goal rate FOR and Team B's first-half goal rate AGAINST conditions whether the second-half card rate (cards_2h) is elevated: matches where one side scores heavily in the first half may produce a trailing team that commits more fouls and receives more cards in the second half.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state dependence: it uses first-half goal splits (a half-level observable) to condition second-half card outcomes. It is not a single-observable comparison — it requires jointly reading first-half goals FOR one side and AGAINST the other to infer match state, then linking that state to a different observable (cards_2h) in the second half.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's offsides FOR AWAY (elevated relative to home) and Team A's possession FOR (dominant). The mechanism tests whether the combination of Team B's away-specific high-offside tendency (indicating a stretched attacking line) and Team A's possession dominance jointly suppresses Team B's shots and goals below what either variable alone predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's shots FOR and goals FOR are suppressed when Team B's away offsides rate is elevated and Team A's possession is simultaneously dominant, compared to matches where only one condition holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's offsides FOR away versus home split, combined with Team A's possession dominance, conditions Team B's effective attacking threat: when a lower-possession team plays away and generates high offsides, it signals a high-line pressing or counter-attacking style that may be suppressed by a possession-dominant home side, reducing Team B's shots and goals.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously: Team B's venue-split offside tendency (away vs home) and Team A's possession dominance. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band — it requires the joint conditioning on both Team B's away-specific attacking pattern and Team A's possession share.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR for each team under ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5 windows. Condition on the joint state where one team's ratio is rising (RECENT_5 > ALL_PRIOR) and the other's is falling, creating an asymmetric shot-quality regime between the two sides.

The joint divergence of both teams' shot-quality ratios in opposite directions conditions the expected on-target volume in this fixture beyond what either team's raw shot count alone would imply.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship across two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for both teams simultaneously, comparing ratio trajectories across two time windows in an asymmetric cross-team structure. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where a team's goals FOR RECENT_5 substantially exceeds its ALL_PRIOR mean AND its shots AGAINST RECENT_5 substantially undercuts its ALL_PRIOR mean. This dual-observable regime (hot attack + stingy defence in recent form) is the conditioning structure.

The joint condition of elevated scoring output alongside a compressed shots-conceded profile suggests a regime shift in Team B's attacking and defensive posture simultaneously, which jointly conditions total goals in the fixture differently than either observable alone.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's possession RECENT_5 is below its ALL_PRIOR AND Team B's possession RECENT_5 is above its ALL_PRIOR, and cross-validate that corner kick FOR trends move in the same direction as possession trends for each team. The mechanism is the joint cross-team co-movement of possession and corners.

The joint cross-team possession regime shift — where one team is losing possession dominance while the other is gaining it — conditions corner kick production asymmetrically: Team A's corners FOR have also dropped in recent form (3.8 RECENT_5 vs 6.05 ALL_PRIOR) while Team B's corners FOR have risen (5.6 RECENT_5 vs 4.49 ALL_PRIOR). The joint possession-corner relationship across both teams simultaneously is the mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship across two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) for both teams simultaneously, with the conditioning requiring both teams' recent-vs-season divergence to be in opposite directions. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on both teams' first-half vs second-half goal FOR and AGAINST splits. The mechanism activates when Team A concedes more in the first half than the second AND Team B scores more in the second half than the first, creating a half-level asymmetry in expected goal timing.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's first-half goals conceded rate exceeds its second-half rate AND Team B's second-half goals scored rate exceeds its first-half rate, the second half carries a disproportionate share of total match goals relative to the competition context's half-level distribution.

Team B mirrors this with more goals conceded in the second half (1.123) than the first (0.864), and more goals scored in the second half (0.802) than the first (0.630). The joint half-level goal distribution profiles of both teams — where Team A is more vulnerable in the first half and Team B is more productive in the second half — creates a within-match state structure that conditions which half carries more goal activity.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires half-level resolution and a joint conditioning on both teams' half-split profiles simultaneously (two teams, two halves, FOR and AGAINST perspectives). It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band, and it uses within-match state (half) as a genuine conditioning dimension.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (1) Team A's yellow_cards FOR RECENT_5 being below its ALL_PRIOR, (2) Team B's yellow_cards AGAINST RECENT_5 being above its ALL_PRIOR, and (3) Team A's fouls FOR RECENT_5 declining. The joint three-observable conditioning across both teams' disciplinary profiles is the mechanism.

The joint cross-team asymmetry — one team committing fewer fouls/cards while the opponent is drawing more — conditions the second-half cards total (cards_2h) differently than either team's individual card rate alone. This is further conditioned by Team A's fouls FOR also declining in recent form (9.6 RECENT_5 vs 10.762 ALL_PRIOR), suggesting a genuine disciplinary regime divergence.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship across three distinct observables (yellow_cards, fouls, cards_2h) and requires cross-team asymmetric conditioning (Team A's FOR declining, Team B's AGAINST rising). It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Measure the joint relationship between the cross-team possession differential (Team B FOR minus Team A FOR) and the cross-team shot differential (Team B shots FOR minus Team A shots FOR), conditioning simultaneously on both teams' possession levels rather than a single team's possession band. The mechanism asks whether the shot differential scales with the possession differential in a non-linear or threshold manner.

mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint, cross-team relationship between two distinct observables (possession and shots) measured simultaneously for both sides. It is not reducible to one team's possession against one band, nor to one team's shots against one band — it requires the interaction of both differentials at once.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on both teams' shots-on-target FOR and goals FOR to measure whether the ratio of goals to shots-on-target differs systematically between the two teams when their shot volumes are at their observed levels. The conditioning uses both teams' observables simultaneously, not a single team's observable against a band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's goals-per-shot-on-target rises relative to Team A's as Team B's shot-on-target volume advantage widens; the relationship is asymmetric across the two teams rather than symmetric.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's conversion efficiency (goals relative to shots on target) is asymmetrically higher than Team A's when both teams' shot-on-target volumes are jointly considered: Team B generates more shots on target and concedes fewer, while Team A's shots-on-target FOR and AGAINST are nearly symmetric. This asymmetry in the shots-on-target differential versus goals differential across both teams jointly signals a structural difference in conversion that is not captured by either team's own shot or goal rate alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a cross-team, two-observable joint relationship (shots_on_target and goals for both sides simultaneously). It cannot be reduced to one team's shots-on-target against one opponent band, nor to one team's goal rate in isolation.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the within-match half split for both teams simultaneously: compare Team A's first-half corner FOR rate versus second-half corner FOR rate, and Team B's first-half corner FOR rate versus second-half corner FOR rate, to test whether the two teams' intra-match corner distributions diverge from each other and from the competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's corner production is more front-loaded (higher first-half share) while Team B's is more back-loaded or uniform; the cross-team divergence in half-level corner distribution is greater than the competition baseline would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production exhibits a within-match half-level asymmetry (first half vs second half) that diverges from Team B's half-level corner profile. Specifically, Team A generates more corners in the first half relative to the second half, while Team B's corner production is more evenly distributed or second-half weighted. This cross-team, within-match half-split asymmetry in corner production is a joint two-observable (half-level corner FOR for each team) relationship.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split applied jointly to both teams' corner production, comparing the intra-match distribution shape across two teams simultaneously. It is not reducible to one team's corners against one opponent band, nor to a simple home/away split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's recent foul FOR rate and Team B's recent offsides AGAINST rate (offsides caught against opponents by Team B's defensive structure). Test whether matches where Team A's foul rate is elevated AND Team B's offsides-against rate is elevated jointly produce a different cards and set-piece environment than either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's foul rate is elevated and Team B's offsides-against rate is simultaneously elevated, the combined disciplinary pressure (yellow cards, cards_2h) rises above what either team's individual foul or offside rate would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's foul rate has risen sharply in recent matches (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) while Team B's foul rate has also risen recently, but Team B concedes fewer fouls than Team A produces. The joint relationship between Team A's elevated recent foul production and Team B's elevated recent offsides-against (opponent offsides caused by Team B's defensive line) suggests a combined pressing/foul-and-offside-trap interaction: when one team fouls more and the other team's defensive line catches more offsides, the match's disciplinary and set-piece environment is jointly shaped by both observables together.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint two-observable mechanism (fouls FOR for one team and offsides AGAINST for the other team) that requires both dimensions simultaneously. It is not reducible to one team's fouls against one opponent band, nor to one team's offsides in isolation.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (1) the cross-team second-half card differential (Team A cards_2h FOR minus Team B cards_2h FOR), and (2) Team A's foul rate regime (recent RECENT_5 vs long-run ALL_PRIOR). Test whether the second-half card asymmetry is amplified when Team A's foul rate is in its elevated recent regime versus its long-run baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second-half card differential favouring Team A (more cards received) is amplified when Team A's recent foul rate is elevated above its long-run mean; the relationship is asymmetric across the two teams and depends on the foul-rate regime, not just a single observable.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The second-half cards environment is jointly shaped by both teams' second-half card rates and their full-match foul differentials. Team A receives more cards in the second half than Team B (cards_2h FOR vs Team B cards_2h FOR), while Team A also commits more fouls overall. The joint relationship between Team A's foul-rate elevation (recent vs long-run) and the cross-team second-half card asymmetry tests whether the second-half disciplinary environment is predictably skewed toward Team A when their foul rate is in an elevated regime.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on a within-match period split (second half), a cross-team asymmetry in cards, and a regime comparison (recent vs long-run foul rate) for one team — three structural dimensions simultaneously. It is not reducible to one observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's shots FOR is elevated relative to its own long-run mean (recent-5 vs ALL_PRIOR divergence) while corner_kicks FOR is simultaneously depressed relative to its own long-run mean. Measure whether shots_on_target FOR rises or falls in this joint state compared to the baseline where both observables move together.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shot volume rises but corner production falls simultaneously, shots-on-target rate rises relative to the baseline where both observables are at their long-run levels — suggesting a more direct, central attacking mode rather than wide/set-piece-driven pressure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has risen sharply in recent matches while its conversion efficiency (shots-on-target rate) has also improved, but its corner-kick production has simultaneously declined. The joint relationship between shot volume, shots-on-target, and corner-kick production — specifically whether a team generating more shots but fewer corners is operating in a qualitatively different attacking mode — is worth measuring across historical match observations.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint conditioning on two distinct observables (shots and corner_kicks) simultaneously diverging from their own baselines in opposite directions, then measuring a third observable (shots_on_target). No single-observable mirror or single-band split covers this three-variable joint relationship.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where a team's shots_on_target FOR (recent-5) diverges upward from its ALL_PRIOR mean while shots_on_target AGAINST (recent-5) diverges downward from its ALL_PRIOR mean. Measure whether possession FOR is also elevated in this joint state, or whether the asymmetric shots-on-target pattern occurs independently of possession share.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shots_on_target FOR rises and shots_on_target AGAINST falls simultaneously, possession FOR rises with this joint state — but the relationship saturates or reverses when possession is already near or above 50%, suggesting diminishing returns to possession-driven shot suppression.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-on-target FOR has surged in recent matches (6.0 vs 3.971 long-run) while its shots_on_target AGAINST has dropped (2.8 vs 3.956 long-run), creating an asymmetric divergence across the two sides of the same observable. The joint relationship between a team's own shots-on-target production trend and the shots-on-target it concedes — specifically whether these two dimensions move independently or co-vary — is worth measuring to understand whether recent form reflects genuine two-way improvement or a sample artifact.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves an asymmetric joint relationship across two distinct perspectives (FOR vs AGAINST) of the same observable, further conditioned on a second observable (possession). It cannot be reduced to a single observable's own-vs-allowed mirror or a single coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on match-level observations where the attacking team's offsides FOR is elevated (above its own long-run mean) while the defending team's offsides AGAINST is simultaneously low (below its own long-run mean). Measure whether corner_kicks FOR and shots FOR are suppressed in this joint state relative to matches where both offside rates are near their respective means.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When an attacking team's offside rate is high and the defending team's offside-concession rate is low simultaneously, the attacking team's corner_kicks and shots are suppressed — indicating that a high-line, well-organized defense neutralizes forward runs and reduces attacking volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A concedes substantially more offsides than it generates (2.264 against vs 1.708 for, ALL_PRIOR), while Team B generates more offsides than it concedes (1.926 for vs 0.926 against). The joint relationship between one team's offside-generation tendency and the opponent's offside-concession tendency — specifically whether high offside-generation by one side against a low-offside-conceding opponent suppresses corner and shot production — is worth measuring as a two-observable, two-team interaction.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (offsides FOR for one team, offsides AGAINST for the opponent) from two different teams simultaneously, then measuring a third observable. This is a two-team, two-observable interaction not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where a team's fouls FOR (full match) is elevated above its own long-run mean. Within those matches, measure whether cards_2h FOR is disproportionately elevated relative to yellow_cards FOR (full match), testing whether foul-heavy teams accumulate cards non-linearly in the second half versus the first half.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's full-match foul rate is elevated above its long-run mean, its second-half card accumulation rises disproportionately relative to its full-match yellow card rate — suggesting a threshold or acceleration effect where foul accumulation in the first half leads to heightened card risk in the second half.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A generates substantially more cards in the second half than it concedes (1.603 FOR vs 1.123 AGAINST, cards_2h), while Team B's second-half card rates are nearly symmetric (1.324 FOR vs 1.397 AGAINST). The joint relationship between a team's second-half foul rate and its second-half card accumulation — specifically whether elevated foul production in the full match predicts asymmetric second-half card accumulation — is worth measuring as a within-match state interaction across two observables.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a within-match state split (second half vs full match) jointly conditioned on a second distinct observable (fouls), testing a non-linear threshold relationship. It is not reducible to a single observable's half-level split alone or a single coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where a team's second-half corner_kicks FOR exceeds its first-half corner_kicks FOR by more than its long-run half-differential. Measure whether goals FOR in the second half are also elevated relative to the first half in those same matches, versus matches where the corner-kick half-differential is near zero or reversed.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's second-half corner production exceeds its first-half corner production by more than its historical norm, its second-half goal production also rises relative to its first-half goal production — suggesting that corner-kick momentum within a match is a leading indicator of second-half scoring uplift.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production is split across halves (2.169 first half vs 2.815 second half FOR, ALL_PRIOR), and its goals are similarly back-loaded (0.589 first half vs 0.877 second half FOR). Team B shows a similar half-level pattern for goals (0.574 first half vs 0.838 second half FOR). The joint relationship between a team's corner-kick half-level distribution and its goal-scoring half-level distribution — specifically whether teams that generate disproportionately more corners in the second half also score disproportionately more goals in the second half — is worth measuring as a two-observable, within-match sequencing interaction.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on the within-match half-level differential of one observable (corner_kicks) to predict the within-match half-level differential of a second distinct observable (goals). It involves two observables and a within-match sequencing structure, not reducible to any single-observable half split or single-band conditioning.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where one team's recent foul rate (RECENT_5) diverges substantially upward from its ALL_PRIOR mean, while the opposing team's fouls-against rate is simultaneously below competition baseline. Measure second-half card outcomes (cards_2h) under this joint condition versus matches where neither divergence is present.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half cards rise when one team's recent foul rate is elevated AND the opponent's foul-concession rate is suppressed relative to competition baseline, compared to matches where only one or neither condition holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's foul production has surged sharply in recent matches relative to its season-long average, while Team A concedes fewer fouls than average. The joint relationship between Team B's elevated recent foul rate and Team A's historically low foul-concession rate may jointly suppress or amplify second-half card accumulation beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables from two different teams simultaneously (Team B's recent fouls FOR vs. Team A's fouls AGAINST), neither of which is a simple mirror of the same observable. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint within-match state where Team A's second-half goals FOR rate exceeds its first-half rate AND Team B's second-half goals AGAINST rate exceeds its first-half rate. Compare second-half goal totals in such matches against matches where this asymmetric half-level alignment is absent.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goals are elevated when both teams simultaneously exhibit a second-half-skewed goal profile (one scoring more in H2, the other conceding more in H2), compared to matches where the profiles are symmetric or misaligned.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A produces goals at a markedly higher rate in the second half than the first half, while Team B concedes goals at a higher rate in the second half than the first half. The asymmetric within-match goal-timing profiles of the two teams — one scoring more in the second half, the other conceding more in the second half — may jointly predict elevated second-half goal volume beyond what full-match averages suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match half-level split that jointly conditions on two distinct team-side observables (Team A goals FOR by half, Team B goals AGAINST by half) simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one coarse band, and it requires half-level resolution.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where the defending team's (Team A's) recent shots-against rate diverges upward from its season average AND the attacking team's (Team B's) recent shots-on-target rate also diverges upward. Measure goals scored by Team B under this joint condition versus when only one or neither divergence is present.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals scored by the attacking team rise when both the defending team's shots-against divergence and the attacking team's shots-on-target divergence are simultaneously elevated in recent form, compared to when only one or neither is elevated.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots-against rate has risen sharply in recent matches (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) while its shots-on-target-against rate has remained relatively stable, suggesting a divergence between shot volume allowed and shot quality allowed. Jointly measuring Team A's shots-against divergence alongside Team B's shots-on-target FOR rate (which has also risen recently) may reveal whether the combination of high shot volume and improved shot quality from Team B is associated with elevated goal-scoring outcomes beyond what either observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots-against divergence for one team, shots-on-target-for divergence for the other), requiring cross-team asymmetric conditioning on two different metrics simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable mirror or a single coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's recent corners-against diverges sharply upward from its season mean AND Team B's recent corners-against diverges sharply downward from its season mean simultaneously. Measure the resulting corner differential (Team B corners FOR minus Team A corners FOR) under this joint divergence condition versus matches where both teams' recent corners-against are close to their season averages.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The corner differential favoring Team B rises when Team A's recent corners-against is elevated AND Team B's recent corners-against is suppressed simultaneously, compared to matches where both teams' recent and season-long corner-against rates are aligned.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kicks-against rate has surged dramatically in recent matches (RECENT_5 = 7.8 vs ALL_PRIOR = 4.77) while Team B's corner-kicks-against rate has dropped sharply (RECENT_5 = 2.6 vs ALL_PRIOR = 5.22). This creates a strongly asymmetric recent corner profile between the two teams. The joint condition of one team's corners-against spiking while the opponent's corners-against collapses may be associated with a skewed corner distribution in the fixture that differs from what either team's season-long average would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This conditions on two distinct recent-vs-season divergences for two different teams simultaneously on the same observable, creating a joint two-team regime condition. It is not a single observable with one coarse band, and the divergence direction is opposite for the two teams, making it an asymmetric cross-team joint condition.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's recent offsides FOR rate diverges sharply downward from its season mean AND Team B's recent offsides AGAINST rate diverges upward from its season mean. Measure Team A's goal and shot outcomes under this joint condition versus matches where both rates are near their season averages.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's attacking output (goals, shots) is associated with a non-linear relationship to the joint offsides profile: when Team A's own offsides rate collapses while the opponent's offsides-against rate rises, the relationship between possession and attacking output changes direction or saturates compared to when both rates are near their season norms.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides FOR rate has dropped sharply in recent matches (RECENT_5 = 0.6 vs ALL_PRIOR = 1.76) while Team B's offsides AGAINST rate has risen (RECENT_5 = 1.4 vs ALL_PRIOR = 1.01). The joint condition of the attacking team running fewer offsides recently while the defending team is conceding more offsides recently may reflect a structural change in the attacking team's line-breaking behavior relative to the defensive line, which could be associated with changes in goal-scoring or shot-creation outcomes beyond what possession or shots alone capture.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint cross-team asymmetric conditioning on two distinct observables (Team A offsides FOR divergence and Team B offsides AGAINST divergence) simultaneously, and tests a non-linear/threshold relationship between the joint offsides regime and attacking output. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on (a) Team A's shots FOR vs Team B's shots AGAINST, and (b) Team B's shots FOR vs Team A's shots AGAINST, treating both asymmetric pairs together. Team A produces ~13.3 shots/game and Team B concedes ~14.5 shots/game (both well above the competition mean of ~12.4), while Team B produces only ~9.0 shots/game and Team A concedes only ~9.6 shots/game. The mechanism asks: when one side has a large shot-production surplus AND the opponent has a large shot-concession surplus, while the other side has a shot-production deficit AND the opponent has a shot-concession deficit, does the aggregate shot total and the within-match shot asymmetry between the two teams diverge from what either single-team mirror would predict?
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Aggregate shots in the fixture rise above competition baseline, and the within-match shot split is asymmetric (Team A producing disproportionately more shots than Team B), with the asymmetry larger than either team's own FOR/AGAINST mirror alone would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume advantage over Team B is structurally large (Team A FOR shots vs Team B FOR shots), but Team B concedes shots at a much higher rate than Team A concedes shots. The joint relationship between each team's shot production and the opponent's shot-concession rate — considered simultaneously rather than as two separate mirrors — determines whether the aggregate shot environment in this fixture is elevated, suppressed, or asymmetric relative to competition norms.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single-observable mirror. It requires jointly conditioning on two distinct asymmetric observable pairs (Team A shots FOR × Team B shots AGAINST, and Team B shots FOR × Team A shots AGAINST) simultaneously, which cannot be reduced to one observable with one band. The structural asymmetry between the two sides — one team dominant in shot production, the other suppressed — is the joint signal.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on the direction and magnitude of the recent-vs-long-run shift for BOTH teams simultaneously: Team B shots FOR (RECENT_5 ~13.8 vs ALL_PRIOR ~9.0, a large upward shift) combined with Team A shots AGAINST (RECENT_5 ~12.6 vs ALL_PRIOR ~9.6, also an upward shift). The mechanism tests whether the co-occurrence of both teams showing the same directional recent shift in the same observable produces a compounding effect on the fixture-level total beyond what either shift alone predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams simultaneously show an upward recent-form shift in the same observable (shots), the fixture-level total for that observable rises above what either team's individual recent-vs-long-run adjustment would predict additively.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots FOR in recent matches (RECENT_5: ~13.8) has surged dramatically relative to its season-long average (~9.0), while Team A's shots AGAINST in recent matches (~12.6) has also risen relative to its season average (~9.6). The joint recent-form trajectory of both teams' shot-related observables — not just one team's recent vs long-run — may signal a regime shift in the fixture's shot environment that neither team's individual recent-vs-long-run comparison captures alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: A single team's recent vs long-run is already covered. This mechanism requires the joint conditioning on both teams' recent-vs-long-run shifts in the same observable at the same time — a two-team, two-window interaction that is not reducible to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A corners FOR by half (1H vs 2H) and Team B corners AGAINST by half (1H vs 2H), and (b) Team B corners FOR by half (1H vs 2H) and Team A corners AGAINST by half (1H vs 2H). This is a within-match state (half-level) conditioning applied simultaneously to both teams' production and concession profiles — four half-level series interacting, not a single observable with one band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second half produces a higher share of total match corners than the first half, driven by the joint second-half elevation in both Team B's corner concession rate and Team A's corner concession rate, with the half-level imbalance larger than either team's individual half-split would suggest in isolation.

Simultaneously, Team B produces very few corners in the first half (FOR 1H: ~1.97) but more in the second half (FOR 2H: ~2.22), while Team A concedes more corners in the second half (AGAINST 2H: ~2.32 vs AGAINST 1H: ~1.97). The joint half-level asymmetry across both teams' corner production and concession profiles — conditioning on both the half dimension and the team-role dimension simultaneously — determines whether the corner distribution within the match is front-loaded, back-loaded, or asymmetric between the two teams across halves.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on the half-level split (within-match state) for two distinct team-role pairs (Team A FOR vs Team B AGAINST, and Team B FOR vs Team A AGAINST). It is not a single observable with one band; it is a joint four-series half-level interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A goals FOR by half and Team B goals AGAINST by half, and (b) Team B goals FOR by half and Team A goals AGAINST by half. The mechanism tests whether the joint half-level interaction of both teams' scoring and conceding profiles produces a within-match goal-timing distribution (more goals in one half vs the other) that differs from what either team's individual half-split predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The first half produces a disproportionate share of Team A's goal threat (relative to Team B's goal threat), while the second half is where Team B's goal threat is concentrated; the joint half-level asymmetry means the two halves have structurally different goal-scoring dynamics between the two teams, with the first half more one-sided and the second half more balanced.

Simultaneously, Team B scores almost exclusively in the second half (FOR 1H: ~0.34 vs FOR 2H: ~0.64), while Team A concedes more in the second half (AGAINST 1H: ~0.41 vs AGAINST 2H: ~0.56). The joint half-level goal-scoring and concession profiles of both teams interact to create a within-match goal-timing structure that is asymmetric: Team A's threat is relatively more front-loaded while Team B's threat is back-loaded, and this joint asymmetry cannot be captured by either team's half-split alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on the half-level split (within-match state) for two distinct asymmetric team-role pairs simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one band; it is a joint four-series half-level interaction across two teams' scoring and conceding profiles.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) both teams' recent-form foul rates (RECENT_5) being simultaneously elevated above their respective season averages and above competition baseline, and (b) the asymmetry between Team B's yellow-card FOR rate and Team A's yellow-card FOR rate. The mechanism tests whether the joint elevation of fouls across both teams in recent form, combined with the asymmetry in yellow-card propensity between the two teams, predicts an elevated second-half card environment beyond what either team's foul or card rate alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism involves three distinct observables (fouls, yellow_cards, cards_2h) jointly, conditions on both teams' recent-form shifts simultaneously, and incorporates a within-match period (second half) for the outcome variable. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one band; it requires the joint interaction of two teams' foul trajectories and their card-rate asymmetry.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's shots-for is above competition average but shots-on-target-for is below competition average (i.e. low conversion ratio), AND Team A's shots-on-target-against recent-5 is below its all-prior average. Both conditions must hold simultaneously.

The joint relationship between Team B's shots-for vs shots-on-target ratio and Team A's shots-on-target-against ratio conditions the expected quality of Team B's attacking threat beyond what either observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship across two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for two different teams simultaneously, and compares a ratio (shots vs shots-on-target) against a cross-team defensive suppression signal. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band.

The asymmetry between Team B's defensive exposure and Team A's offensive output is the conditioning structure.

mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B concedes a high volume of shots (well above competition average, and rising sharply in recent matches), while Team A produces shots at a level close to competition average but with a stable shots-on-target rate. The asymmetric relationship — Team B allows many shots while Team A's shot production is modest but consistent — jointly determines the expected shots-on-target volume for Team A in this fixture, in a way that differs from reading either team's observable in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team relationship between two different observables (Team A shots-for vs Team B shots-against), not a same-observable mirror. It requires jointly conditioning on both teams' values and comparing them to a competition baseline, which is structurally richer than any single-observable split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's fouls-for recent-5 is elevated above its season average AND above competition average, while Team A's corner-kicks-against recent-5 is below its season average. Measure whether this joint state predicts elevated second-half cards (cards_2h) relative to competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's recent foul rate is elevated and Team A's corner-kicks-against is suppressed, second-half card volume rises above competition average, because foul-prone teams under defensive pressure generate more disciplinary events in the second half.

The joint relationship between Team B's recent foul elevation and Team A's corner-kick-against suppression conditions the expected second-half card volume, since elevated fouls in a team that already concedes corners at a high rate historically co-occur with increased second-half card accumulation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a genuine joint relationship across three distinct observables (fouls, corner_kicks, cards_2h) and requires conditioning on two different team-level signals simultaneously — not reducible to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's offsides-for recent-5 is substantially above its season average, AND Team A's offsides-against recent-5 is below its season average. Within this joint state, examine whether Team B's possession and corner-kick production are suppressed relative to their season averages.
