mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's offsides-for has surged sharply in recent matches (recent-5 nearly double its season average), while Team A's offsides-against has declined in recent matches. The joint divergence between Team B's recent offside rate and Team A's recent offside-against rate — both moving in opposite directions from their season averages — signals a structural mismatch in attacking line management that conditions corner-kick and possession outcomes.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (offsides-for and offsides-against) for two different teams, and then examining a third observable (possession/corners) as the outcome. The two-team, two-observable conditioning structure is not reducible to any single-observable split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint within-match state: both teams show higher goal rates in the second half than the first half (half-level split), AND Team A's recent defensive form is sharply improved while Team B's is not. Measure whether the second-half goal rate is disproportionately elevated relative to the first half when both teams share this back-loaded pattern and defensive form diverges.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams individually show a back-loaded goal pattern (second-half rate exceeds first-half rate) and Team A's recent defensive form is improved while Team B's is not, the second half is expected to concentrate a disproportionate share of total match goals relative to competition average half-distribution.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals-for first-half rate is substantially below its second-half rate (0.492 vs 0.785 per match), while Team B's goals-against first-half rate is also below its second-half rate (0.797 vs 0.984). The joint within-match half-level asymmetry — both teams showing a back-loaded goal pattern — conditions the expected half-by-half goal distribution in a way that is not captured by full-match goal averages alone. Additionally, Team A's recent goals-against has dropped sharply (recent-5: 0.4 vs season: 1.554), while Team B's recent goals-against remains elevated (recent-5: 1.8 vs season: 1.781), creating a cross-team asymmetry in defensive form that further conditions the half-level goal distribution.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (first half vs second half goals) jointly conditioned on both teams' half-level patterns simultaneously, plus a cross-team asymmetry in recent defensive form. It is not reducible to a single observable with one band — it requires half-resolution data and a two-team joint conditioning structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on both teams' shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR (all-prior and recent-5 windows) to derive each team's on-target conversion ratio, then assess whether the cross-team asymmetry in that ratio (Team A high-volume/lower-conversion vs Team B lower-volume/higher-conversion in recent form) predicts aggregate shots_on_target relative to competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's recent shots-on-target rate (shots_on_target FOR RECENT_5 / shots FOR RECENT_5) diverges downward from its all-prior rate while Team B's recent rate diverges upward, aggregate match shots_on_target is suppressed relative to the sum of each team's standalone shots_on_target averages.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume advantage over Team B (shots FOR vs shots AGAINST) jointly interacts with Team B's shots-on-target conversion rate (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR) to shape the total shots-on-target environment. When one side generates many shots but converts few to on-target, and the other generates fewer shots but converts a higher share, the aggregate on-target volume is not predictable from either team's single-observable shot or shots-on-target average alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly relating two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for both sides simultaneously, and comparing recent-window conversion ratios against all-prior ratios in an asymmetric cross-team structure. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on both teams' goals FOR and AGAINST split by FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF. Specifically: Team B goals FOR FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF (all-prior), and Team A goals AGAINST FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF (all-prior), to assess whether the combined second-half goal concentration exceeds what the full-match averages would imply.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's second-half goal rate substantially exceeds its first-half rate AND Team A concedes more in the second half than the first, the proportion of total match goals falling in the second half rises above the competition baseline second-half share.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's goals are heavily back-loaded within matches (second-half goals FOR substantially exceed first-half goals FOR, while Team A concedes more in the second half than the first). This within-match temporal asymmetry between the two teams' goal-scoring and goal-conceding half-profiles jointly determines whether total goals are concentrated in the second half, which is a structurally different question from either team's full-match goal average.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) split applied jointly across two distinct team-direction pairs (Team B FOR and Team A AGAINST), creating a two-dimensional half-profile interaction. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on each team's possession FOR (all-prior and recent-5) and corner_kicks FOR (all-prior and recent-5, including first-half and second-half splits) to compute a possession-to-corner conversion ratio for each team. Assess whether the cross-team divergence in this ratio (Team A high corners per possession unit vs Team B low corners per possession unit) predicts total match corners relative to competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's corner yield per possession unit substantially exceeds Team B's, total match corners rise above what the simple sum of each team's standalone corner averages would predict, and the corner imbalance between teams is amplified beyond the possession imbalance.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between possession dominance and corner-kick generation is asymmetric across the two teams: Team A holds more possession and generates substantially more corners than Team B, while Team B generates fewer corners despite comparable possession levels. This asymmetry between possession share and corner yield (corners per unit possession) for each team jointly determines the total corner environment beyond what either team's standalone corner or possession average predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly relating two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) for both sides, computing a ratio that is not itself a single observable, and comparing the cross-team asymmetry in that ratio. It is not reducible to one observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A cards_2h FOR (second-half) and Team B cards_2h AGAINST (second-half), and symmetrically Team B cards_2h FOR and Team A cards_2h AGAINST, to assess whether the combined second-half card environment is elevated when both the card-drawing tendency of one team and the card-conceding tendency of the opponent are simultaneously above competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's cards_2h FOR and Team B's cards_2h AGAINST are both above competition baseline simultaneously, total second-half cards in the match rise above what either team's standalone second-half card average would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The second-half card environment is jointly shaped by both teams' second-half card production (cards_2h FOR) and the opponent's second-half card allowance (cards_2h AGAINST). Team B concedes more second-half cards against it (cards_2h AGAINST) than Team A does, while Team A produces more second-half cards than Team B. This cross-team asymmetry in second-half card profiles — one team as a high card-drawer and the other as a high card-receiver — jointly determines whether total second-half cards exceed the competition baseline, beyond what either team's standalone second-half card average implies.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric joint relationship across two different team-direction pairs for the same observable (cards_2h FOR for one team paired with cards_2h AGAINST for the other), requiring simultaneous conditioning on both dimensions. It is not a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on the direction and magnitude of each team's recent-5 vs all-prior possession shift (Team A rising, Team B falling) alongside each team's fouls FOR recent-5 vs all-prior shift, to assess whether matches where one team's possession drops sharply in recent form while the opponent's rises are associated with elevated total fouls relative to competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's recent possession share falls below its all-prior level while Team A's rises, and Team B's recent fouls FOR also rise, total match fouls are elevated above the competition baseline and above what either team's standalone foul average predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's recent-form possession share has dropped substantially relative to its all-prior average (recent-5 possession FOR is notably lower than all-prior), while Team A's recent possession share has risen. This regime shift in possession balance — where both teams' recent windows move in opposite directions simultaneously — jointly interacts with each team's fouls FOR (which also show recent-form changes) to determine whether the match foul environment is elevated, since lower-possession teams tend to foul more. The joint conditioning on possession-regime shift for both teams and each team's foul rate is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly relating two distinct observables (possession and fouls) for both teams, conditioning on the direction of recent-vs-all-prior regime shifts for both simultaneously. It is a two-observable, two-team, regime-shift interaction that cannot be reduced to one observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly examine Team B's FOR perspective across ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5 windows: compute the shots-to-shots_on_target ratio and the shots_on_target-to-goals ratio in each window to determine whether the recent goal decline is a shot-quality problem or a finishing problem.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shots_on_target FOR declines proportionally more than shots FOR in the recent window relative to the season baseline, goals FOR should decline in tandem (shot-quality-driven drought); when shots_on_target holds but goals fall, the drought is finishing-driven and may be more transient.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot-volume-to-goals conversion efficiency diverges sharply between its season-long history and its recent 5-match window: shots FOR have declined recently while goals FOR have also declined, but the ratio of shots_on_target FOR to goals FOR across the two windows reveals whether Team B's recent goal drought is driven by a deterioration in shot quality (shots_on_target declining faster than shots) or by a conversion failure at constant shot quality. This joint relationship between shots, shots_on_target, and goals across two time windows is structurally richer than any single observable comparison.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint three-observable relationship (shots × shots_on_target × goals) evaluated across two time windows simultaneously. No single observable with one conditioning band captures the interaction between shot quality and finishing efficiency, nor the cross-window comparison of their ratio.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For Team A FOR perspective, compare the shots_on_target-to-goals ratio in RECENT_5 versus ALL_PRIOR. Test whether the ratio of goals per shot_on_target is stable, rising, or falling as shot_on_target volume increases.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shots_on_target FOR rises substantially above the season baseline, the goals-per-shot-on-target ratio may saturate or compress, meaning goals do not rise proportionally with shot-on-target volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent surge in shots_on_target FOR (7.6 in RECENT_5 vs 5.117 season average) is not matched by a proportional surge in goals FOR (2.8 vs 1.909), suggesting a divergence between shot-on-target volume and conversion rate. Jointly measuring shots_on_target FOR against goals FOR across the two windows tests whether high shot-on-target volume translates to goals at a stable rate or whether conversion efficiency is suppressed when shot-on-target volume is elevated.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable (shots_on_target × goals) cross-window ratio test, not a single observable compared against a band. The saturation/non-linearity of conversion rate as volume rises is not captured by any single-observable baseline comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly examine Team B's possession FOR, corner_kicks FOR, and shots FOR across ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5 windows. Test whether the ratio of attacking outputs (corners, shots) per unit of possession is stable or declining as possession compresses toward 50%.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's possession advantage over the opponent compresses toward parity, corner_kicks FOR and shots FOR should decline at a rate greater than the possession decline alone would predict, indicating a non-linear relationship between possession margin and attacking output.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B holds structurally higher possession (55.9% season average, 51.8% recent) than Team A (50.8% season, 50.6% recent), yet Team B's corner_kicks FOR (6.0 season, 5.2 recent) and shots FOR (15.1 season, 13.2 recent) are both declining in the recent window. This tests whether possession dominance translates into attacking output (corners, shots) at a stable rate, or whether possession advantage decouples from attacking output when possession levels compress toward parity.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint three-observable relationship (possession × corner_kicks × shots) tested across two time windows. It is not reducible to any single observable with one conditioning band, and it tests a non-linear (decoupling) relationship rather than a simple level comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on both teams' cards_2h FOR and AGAINST in the SECOND_HALF. The mechanism fires when Team A's cards_2h AGAINST exceeds its cards_2h FOR AND Team B's cards_2h FOR exceeds its cards_2h AGAINST — i.e., both asymmetries point in the same direction (Team A receives more cards, Team B earns more cards). Also cross-reference with fouls FOR/AGAINST to test whether the card asymmetry is foul-driven.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's second-half card-conceded rate exceeds its card-earned rate AND Team B's second-half card-earned rate exceeds its card-conceded rate, the total second-half cards in the match should rise above the competition baseline, driven by an asymmetric disciplinary dynamic.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetry between Team A's second-half cards conceded (1.195 per match) versus Team A's second-half cards earned (0.909) and Team B's second-half cards earned (1.247) versus Team B's second-half cards conceded (1.039) creates a joint cross-team second-half card asymmetry. Specifically, Team A concedes more second-half cards than it earns, while Team B earns more second-half cards than it concedes. Testing whether this asymmetric pattern — one team systematically receiving more second-half discipline than it imposes, while the opponent does the reverse — is associated with a directional second-half foul/card dynamic in the match.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint cross-team asymmetric comparison of two different perspectives (FOR vs AGAINST) of the same observable (cards_2h) for both teams simultaneously, combined with a second observable (fouls) to test the mechanism. It is not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on both teams' goals split by half (FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF), comparing Team A goals FOR by half against Team B goals AGAINST by half. The mechanism tests whether the half in which Team A is most productive offensively (H2) coincides with the half in which Team B is most vulnerable defensively (H2 for goals against).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's goals FOR are more concentrated in the second half AND Team B's goals AGAINST are also more concentrated in the second half, second-half goal production in the match should rise above what a simple full-match average would predict, reflecting a complementary timing alignment.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's goals AGAINST are heavily concentrated in the first half (0.753 per match in H1 vs 0.896 in H2 season-wide), while Team A's goals FOR are more evenly distributed (0.831 H1 vs 1.078 H2). This creates an asymmetric half-level goal-timing profile: Team A scores more in the second half while Team B concedes more in the first half. Jointly testing Team A's goals FOR by half against Team B's goals AGAINST by half reveals whether the half-timing profiles are complementary (Team A's second-half scoring strength aligns with Team B's second-half defensive vulnerability) or misaligned.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint cross-team, cross-perspective, within-match half-level comparison of the same observable (goals) for two different teams. It requires simultaneously conditioning on half-period AND the asymmetric FOR/AGAINST perspectives of both teams, which is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A playing at home (where its corner production is materially higher than away) AND simultaneously condition on Team B's corners-against being elevated in recent matches relative to its season average. Both dimensions must be active together; neither alone captures the joint amplification.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total match corners rises when Team A's home corner advantage and Team B's elevated corners-conceded rate are jointly present, beyond what either team's unconditional average predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production is strongly asymmetric by venue (home vs away), and when combined with Team B's elevated recent corners-against (well above its season average), the joint corner supply from both sides in this home fixture may be structurally higher than either team's single-observable average alone would suggest. The mechanism tests whether the joint condition of Team A's home corner advantage AND Team B's high corners-conceded rate produces a corner total that exceeds what either team's full-match average predicts independently.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single-observable mirror or a single coarse band. It requires jointly conditioning on two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions at once: Team A's venue-split corner production AND Team B's recent-vs-season corners-against divergence. The engine's covered class handles each split separately but not their joint interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner production and concession by half for both teams. Condition on whether Team A's second-half corner rate exceeds its first-half rate AND whether Team B concedes more corners in the second half than the first. Test the joint half-level asymmetry.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half corner volume is disproportionately higher than first-half corner volume when both Team A's second-half corner production bias and Team B's second-half corners-against bias are simultaneously present.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner production splits markedly across halves (first half vs second half), and Team B's corners-against also splits across halves. The mechanism tests whether the within-match half-level corner imbalance for Team A (second half heavier than first) is amplified or suppressed by Team B's own half-level corners-against profile, producing a non-uniform within-match corner distribution that differs from the full-match average.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires within-match state resolution (half-level split) combined with a joint two-team asymmetry across different observables (Team A FOR vs Team B AGAINST), neither of which is reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's foul rate being above competition average AND Team B's shots-on-target-against rate being elevated. Test whether this two-observable joint condition (high fouling team facing a high-pressure opponent) is associated with elevated card volume relative to the competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Yellow card and total card volume rises when a high-fouling team (Team A) faces an opponent that generates elevated shots on target (Team B), beyond what either team's card or foul average alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A commits substantially more fouls than the competition average and more than Team B, while Team B's shots-on-target-against rate is elevated (both season and recent). The mechanism tests whether Team A's high foul rate jointly with Team B's high shots-on-target-against rate produces an elevated cards volume, specifically by examining whether the combination of one team's foul production and the opponent's attacking pressure (shots on target) is associated with higher yellow-card or total-card outcomes beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship across two distinct observables (fouls and shots_on_target) for two different sides, not a single-observable mirror or a single coarse band. The engine covers fouls alone or cards alone against a band, but not the cross-observable joint condition.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's recent possession being elevated above its season average (possession regime shift) AND Team B's recent shots-on-target FOR being below its season average. Test whether this joint two-observable, two-team condition suppresses Team B's goal output.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's goals FOR is suppressed when Team A's possession is in an elevated recent regime AND Team B's shots-on-target FOR is simultaneously in a declining recent regime, relative to what Team B's season goal average would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession has shifted markedly in recent matches (recent average well above its season average and above 50%), while Team B's shots-on-target FOR rate has declined recently relative to its season average. The mechanism tests whether a joint condition of Team A gaining possession dominance AND Team B's attacking output declining simultaneously is associated with a suppression of Team B's goal-scoring relative to its season average, beyond what either team's goal average alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship across two distinct observables (possession and shots_on_target) for two different sides, combined with a recent-vs-season regime comparison for both simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one band or a simple recent-vs-long-run comparison for one team.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split goals FOR and AGAINST by half for both teams. Condition on Team A's second-half goal rate exceeding its first-half rate AND Team B conceding more goals in the second half than the first. Test whether the joint half-level asymmetry from both sides concentrates goals in the second half.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goal volume is disproportionately higher than first-half goal volume when Team A's second-half scoring bias and Team B's second-half conceding bias are jointly present.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals split asymmetrically across halves (first half vs second half), and Team B also concedes more goals in the second half than the first. The mechanism tests whether the joint within-match half-level goal-scoring asymmetry — Team A scoring more in the second half AND Team B conceding more in the second half — produces a non-uniform intra-match goal distribution that is structurally skewed toward the second half beyond what the full-match goal averages imply.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires within-match half-level resolution combined with a joint two-team asymmetry (Team A FOR and Team B AGAINST across halves). The engine covers a single observable by half for one team, but not the joint half-level interaction between one team's scoring profile and the opponent's conceding profile.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Measure the joint ratio of shots_on_target FOR to shots FOR (on-target rate) for each team in RECENT_5 versus ALL_PRIOR, and cross-reference with goals FOR in the same windows. The mechanism fires when one team's recent on-target rate rises while the other's stagnates or falls, creating an asymmetric conversion environment not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent shots-on-target-to-shots ratio rises above its long-run rate while the opponent's ratio stays flat or falls, that team's goals FOR rises disproportionately relative to the opponent's goals FOR in the same window.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot-volume surge in recent matches (shots FOR) co-occurs with a simultaneous improvement in shots-on-target conversion rate (shots_on_target FOR), while Team A's recent shots FOR has declined and shots_on_target FOR has remained flat. The joint relationship between shot volume and on-target accuracy across both sides — rather than either observable alone — conditions the expected goal-scoring environment.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) computed as a ratio and compared across two teams simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band; it involves an asymmetric cross-team comparison of a derived two-variable quantity.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's shots AGAINST RECENT_5 versus ALL_PRIOR and Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST RECENT_5 versus ALL_PRIOR. The mechanism is active when these two defensive observables move in opposite directions across the two teams, creating a structural asymmetry in defensive quality that is not captured by either team's defensive shots or defensive shots-on-target in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's shots conceded recently exceeds its long-run rate while Team B's shots-on-target conceded recently is below its long-run rate, the total goals in the match are suppressed relative to what either team's individual defensive observable alone would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A concedes substantially more shots AGAINST in recent matches than its long-run average, while Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST has recently declined. The asymmetric divergence between one team's defensive shot-volume concession and the other team's defensive on-target concession — measured jointly — conditions whether the attacking team's volume translates into goals.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct defensive observables (shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST) for two different teams, with each moving in a different direction. This is a two-observable, two-team asymmetric joint relationship, not a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute each team's first-half share of total goals FOR (goals_1H / goals_full) and AGAINST (goals_1H_against / goals_full_against) from ALL_PRIOR half-level data. Jointly condition on both teams' half-level goal profiles to identify whether the match has a structural first-half or second-half goal concentration that differs from the competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's goals FOR are concentrated in the second half and the opponent's goals FOR are concentrated in the first half, the match exhibits a cross-half asymmetry where total first-half goals are suppressed relative to total second-half goals beyond what either team's half-level profile alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals are distributed more heavily in the second half than the first half (0.563 first half vs 0.873 second half FOR), while Team B's goals are distributed more heavily in the first half than Team A's (0.746 first half vs 1.099 second half FOR). The joint within-match half-level goal distribution profiles of both teams — measured simultaneously — conditions the expected timing of goals in the fixture.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on half-level splits for both teams simultaneously and comparing the resulting cross-team asymmetry. It is not a single observable with one band; it uses within-match state (half) for both teams jointly, and the mechanism depends on the interaction between the two teams' half-level profiles.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute each team's first-half and second-half corner kick shares FOR and AGAINST from ALL_PRIOR half-level data. Jointly condition on both teams' half-level corner profiles to identify structural half-level concentration patterns that differ from the competition baseline and from what either team's full-match corner average alone would suggest.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's corners FOR are concentrated in the first half and the opponent concedes more corners in the second half, the match's corner distribution across halves diverges from a uniform split, with the second half showing elevated corner volume relative to the first half.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner kicks are distributed across halves (2.385 first half, 2.646 second half FOR), while Team B's corner kicks show a first-half bias (2.812 first half, 2.493 second half FOR) and Team B concedes more corners in the second half (3.101) than the first (2.739). The joint half-level corner distribution profiles of both teams — combined with the within-match state — conditions whether corner volume is front-loaded or back-loaded in the fixture.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on half-level splits for corners for both teams simultaneously (four half-level observables: Team A FOR/AGAINST by half, Team B FOR/AGAINST by half). This is a within-match state (half) joint two-team mechanism, not a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on each team's possession FOR (as a continuous measure relative to the 50% baseline) and offsides FOR. The mechanism tests whether the joint state of below-average possession AND above-average offsides FOR (a two-observable combination) is associated with a distinct attacking pattern compared to either observable alone. Apply this jointly across both teams and compare long-run versus recent windows.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's possession is persistently below the competition average and its offsides FOR is above the competition average, that team exhibits a counter-attacking profile; when both teams simultaneously shift toward this joint state in recent matches, the match's total offsides rises above what either team's individual offside average would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A operates with a persistent below-competition-average possession share (45.2% FOR vs 50% competition baseline) while Team B operates near or above the competition average (51.0% FOR). The joint relationship between Team A's low possession and its elevated offsides FOR (1.812 vs competition 1.4) suggests a counter-attacking profile where low possession co-occurs with high offside exposure — a two-observable joint pattern. Simultaneously, Team B's recent possession has dropped to 45.8% (from 51.0% long-run) while its offsides FOR has risen to 2.25 (from 1.779), suggesting a similar recent shift toward a counter-attacking posture for Team B.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and offsides) that cannot be reduced to either observable alone or to a single observable with one conditioning band. The mechanism depends on the interaction between possession level and offside frequency, and is applied asymmetrically across both teams and across long-run versus recent windows.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the attacking team (Team A) exhibits a high shots-FOR but low shots_on_target-FOR ratio (low conversion accuracy), while the defending team (Team B) allows a relatively low shots_on_target AGAINST rate. In such joint conditions, measure Team A's corner_kicks FOR.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A corner_kicks FOR rises when Team A's shot accuracy is low (many shots, few on target) and Team B suppresses on-target shots, as off-target attempts and blocked shots are more likely to produce corners than goals
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR) is jointly considered alongside Team B's defensive suppression of shots_on_target AGAINST, to test whether the combined low-accuracy / high-volume-allowed pairing produces a different corner-kick yield than either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for Team A and a separate observable (shots_on_target AGAINST) for Team B simultaneously — not reducible to any single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B holds above-average possession (FOR) and simultaneously generates above-average corners FOR. Measure whether Team A's corners AGAINST co-varies with Team B's possession level across this joint distribution, or whether corner generation is decoupled from possession for Team B.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's corner_kicks FOR rises with possession FOR up to a threshold, but the relationship saturates or decouples at high possession levels, suggesting a non-linear rather than proportional link between possession dominance and corner generation
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetry between Team B's corner_kicks FOR (high, rising in recent form) and Team A's corner_kicks AGAINST (also elevated) is tested jointly against Team B's possession FOR, to determine whether Team B's corner dominance is possession-driven or possession-independent.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This tests a non-linear / threshold relationship between two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) for the same team, not a simple single-observable band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A holds below-average possession (FOR below competition mean of 50). Within those matches, compare Team A's goals FOR in the first half versus second half. Team A scores markedly more in the second half (0.767) than first half (0.279) overall; test whether this half-skew is amplified or suppressed when possession deficit is larger.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's second-half goals FOR rises relative to first-half goals FOR as Team A's possession deficit deepens, suggesting a counter-attacking or late-game pattern that is more pronounced when possession is ceded
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals FOR split by half (first half vs second half) is tested jointly against Team A's possession deficit (Team A possession FOR is below 50, opponent possession is above 50), to determine whether Team A's scoring pattern is concentrated in a specific half when playing as the lower-possession side.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state split (half-level) conditioned simultaneously on a continuous possession-deficit dimension — requiring both half resolution and a joint second observable, not covered by any single-observable or single-band baseline.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B commits above-average fouls FOR. Within those matches, compare Team B's goals FOR in the first half versus second half, and also measure yellow_cards FOR. Test whether the high-foul regime is associated with a front-loaded goal pattern and elevated card accumulation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: In matches where Team B's fouls FOR is elevated, Team B's first-half goals FOR is disproportionately higher relative to second half, and yellow_cards FOR is also elevated — suggesting a joint aggressive-early-dominance regime
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's goals FOR split by half (first half vs second half) is tested jointly against Team B's fouls FOR, to determine whether Team B's strong first-half scoring (0.806 per match) is associated with a high-foul, physically aggressive style that also generates yellow cards, and whether this joint pattern shifts across halves.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a three-observable joint relationship (goals by half, fouls, yellow_cards) with a within-match half-level split conditioned on a continuous foul-rate dimension — not reducible to any single observable or single band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where both Team A's fouls FOR and Team B's fouls AGAINST are simultaneously above the competition mean. Within that joint high-foul context, measure cards_2h FOR and AGAINST for both teams. Compare to the baseline cards_2h rate in matches where only one side's foul rate is elevated.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: cards_2h (for both teams combined) rises when both Team A fouls FOR and Team B fouls AGAINST are jointly elevated above competition mean, with the joint condition producing a greater second-half card rate than either team's individual foul elevation alone
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between Team A's fouls FOR and Team B's fouls AGAINST (both elevated relative to competition context) is tested against second-half cards (cards_2h) for both teams, to determine whether a high-mutual-foul-rate match context produces a disproportionate second-half card escalation beyond what each team's individual card rate would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint condition on two distinct observables (fouls FOR for Team A and fouls AGAINST for Team B) simultaneously, tested against a within-match-period outcome (second-half cards) — involving two opponent-descriptor dimensions and a half-level split, not covered by any single-observable baseline.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A's own shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR ratio (all-prior and recent-5) jointly with Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST rate. The mechanism asks whether the combination of a low on-target conversion rate (Team A) meeting a low shots-on-target concession rate (Team B) produces a jointly suppressed on-target output beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's shots-to-shots-on-target ratio is low (many shots, few on target) AND the opponent suppresses shots-on-target at a below-average rate, the combined on-target output is suppressed more than either factor alone would suggest — a joint multiplicative suppression rather than additive.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR) is jointly compared against Team B's defensive suppression of shots-on-target allowed, to test whether a team that generates many shots but converts few on target faces a structurally tighter defensive filter than its raw shot volume implies.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly relating two distinct observables (shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR for one team, shots_on_target AGAINST for the other) simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band; it is an asymmetric cross-team, cross-observable joint relationship.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on whether Team B's recent-5 possession exceeds its all-prior possession AND its recent-5 shots FOR exceeds its all-prior shots FOR simultaneously. The joint co-movement of both observables in the same direction (upward) defines a 'regime shift' condition distinct from either observable drifting alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both possession and shot volume rise together in recent matches relative to the long-run baseline, the team's shots_on_target FOR also rises — the joint upward regime in two observables is associated with a compounding rather than additive improvement in on-target output.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession dominance (FOR all-prior vs recent-5 showing an upward trend) is jointly related to its shot volume surge (shots FOR recent-5 well above all-prior), testing whether possession expansion and shot-volume expansion co-occur as a reinforcing regime shift rather than independently.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable regime structure (possession AND shots both trending up simultaneously) rather than a single observable's recent vs long-run comparison. The engine covers each observable's recent vs long-run split individually but not their joint co-movement as a regime condition.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A's goals FOR first-half vs second-half split simultaneously with Team B's goals AGAINST first-half vs second-half split. The mechanism tests the cross-team, cross-half asymmetry: Team A scores more in H1 (0.674 vs 0.581) while Team B concedes more in H2 (0.548 vs 0.411). The joint pattern — attacker peaks early, defender leaks late — is the conditioning structure.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the attacking team's goal production is front-loaded (higher H1 than H2) but the defending team's concession rate is back-loaded (higher H2 than H1), the within-match goal distribution is more uniform than either half-split alone implies — the mismatch partially cancels rather than compounds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetry between Team A's first-half goal production and second-half goal production (FOR) is jointly tested against Team B's first-half vs second-half goal concession asymmetry (AGAINST), to identify whether a team that scores more in the first half meets a defence that concedes more in the second half — creating a half-period mismatch in when goals are most likely.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct half-level splits from two different teams on different observables (Team A goals FOR by half, Team B goals AGAINST by half). It is an asymmetric cross-team within-match state relationship, not a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A's corners FOR H1 vs H2 (1.973 vs 2.432 — back-loaded) jointly with Team B's corners AGAINST H1 vs H2 (2.284 vs 2.985 — also back-loaded). The joint back-loading of both attacker production and defender concession in the same half defines a compounding second-half corner pressure condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both the attacking team's corner production and the defending team's corner concession are back-loaded into the second half, total corner volume in the second half rises above what either team's individual half-split would predict in isolation — a compounding rather than independent effect.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between Team A's corner-kick production split by half (FOR first-half vs second-half) and Team B's corner-kick concession split by half (AGAINST first-half vs second-half) tests whether the within-match corner distribution for Team A aligns or misaligns with the half in which Team B is most vulnerable to conceding corners.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct half-level splits from two different teams on the same observable (corners), creating a cross-team within-match state structure. The engine covers each team's corner rate individually and by venue, but not the joint half-period alignment between attacker production and defender concession.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A's fouls FOR recent-5 being substantially below its all-prior average (8.2 vs 12.86) simultaneously with Team B's yellow_cards FOR recent-5 being substantially above its all-prior average (2.8 vs 1.562). The joint condition — one team in a low-foul regime, the other in a high-card regime — is the cross-team, cross-observable conditioning structure tested against cards_2h outcomes.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the home team is in a low-foul regime and the away team is in a high-card-accumulation regime simultaneously, second-half card volume (cards_2h) is asymmetrically distributed toward the away team rather than being symmetric around the competition baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent-5 foul rate (FOR) has dropped sharply below its all-prior average while Team B's yellow-card rate (FOR) has risen sharply in recent matches. The joint relationship between one team's foul-rate regime shift and the opponent's card-accumulation regime shift tests whether a disciplinary asymmetry — one team fouling less while the other is being carded more — is associated with a divergence in second-half card volume (cards_2h).
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) from two different teams, both in regime-shift states (recent vs long-run divergence), and relates them to a third observable (cards_2h) at half resolution. It is not reducible to any single observable's recent vs long-run comparison or a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on each team's possession share and shot production simultaneously, computing shots-per-possession-unit for each side and comparing the cross-team asymmetry. This is not a single-observable mirror but a ratio relationship across two distinct observables for two sides.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's shots-per-possession-unit rises relative to Team B's as Team B's possession advantage widens; i.e., the side with lower possession produces disproportionately more shots per possession unit held
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B holds substantially higher possession than Team A across all windows, yet both teams produce similar shot volumes. The joint relationship between possession dominance and shot conversion efficiency (shots per unit possession) differs asymmetrically between the two sides, suggesting that Team A generates shots at a higher rate relative to its possession share than Team B does relative to its possession share.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly relating two distinct observables (possession and shots) across both sides simultaneously; cannot be reduced to one observable with one conditioning band or a simple home/away split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on each team's possession share and corner kick production/concession simultaneously, examining whether the team with lower possession generates corners at a rate inconsistent with its possession deficit. Compare all-prior vs recent-5 windows to detect a regime shift.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kick generation by the lower-possession team rises relative to its possession share as the possession gap widens; the relationship between possession and corners is non-proportional and asymmetric across the two sides
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B dominates possession yet Team A generates more corners per match in recent form than its season average, while Team B's corners against have dropped in recent matches. The joint relationship between possession share and corner generation differs asymmetrically: the lower-possession side (Team A) earns corners at a rate disproportionate to its possession share, while the higher-possession side (Team B) concedes fewer corners recently despite allowing more possession to opponents historically.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Involves a joint two-observable relationship (possession × corners) across both sides with an asymmetric cross-team structure, plus a regime-shift comparison between all-prior and recent-5 windows — not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's foul production and Team B's foul production simultaneously, then examine how the cross-team foul differential relates to second-half card totals for each side. The conditioning uses two opponent-descriptor dimensions (each team's foul rate) together with the second-half period split.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half cards for the higher-fouling side rise as the cross-team foul differential widens; the relationship between foul differential and second-half cards is stronger in the second half than the full-match card rate would imply
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A commits substantially more fouls than the competition average and more than Team B, while also accumulating more second-half cards than Team B. The joint relationship between a team's foul rate and its second-half card accumulation — conditioned on the opponent's foul rate — captures whether high-fouling teams facing lower-fouling opponents see a disproportionate escalation in second-half disciplinary events.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly relating two distinct observables (fouls and cards_2h) conditioned on both teams' foul rates simultaneously, with a within-match period split (second half). This is a two-observable joint relationship with a half-level resolution — not a single-observable mirror.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on each team's shots-on-target production and goals scored simultaneously, computing the conversion ratio (goals per shot on target) for each side across all-prior and recent-5 windows. Compare whether the conversion gap between sides persists or narrows in recent form.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The team with higher goals-per-shot-on-target maintains that conversion advantage even when shots-on-target volumes converge; the conversion ratio is a persistent asymmetric property not explained by shot volume alone
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B scores goals at a markedly higher rate than Team A (1.882 vs 1.342 per match all-prior) despite both teams producing similar shot and shots-on-target volumes. The joint relationship between shots-on-target production and goals scored — i.e., the shots-on-target-to-goals conversion ratio — differs substantially between the two sides, and this asymmetry is not captured by examining either observable in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly relating two distinct observables (shots_on_target and goals) for both sides simultaneously to compute a ratio; the cross-team asymmetry in conversion is not captured by either observable's mirror comparison alone.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's possession share and its offsides-against rate across the all-prior vs recent-5 windows simultaneously, testing whether the surge in offsides-against co-occurs with the possession increase as a joint regime shift rather than independent trends.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Offsides-against for the high-possession team rises as possession share increases beyond a threshold level, suggesting a non-linear or threshold relationship between possession dominance and defensive line exposure to offside traps
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's offsides conceded (opponents caught offside against Team B) has surged dramatically in recent matches (3.8 recent-5 vs 1.895 all-prior), coinciding with Team B's possession share also rising in recent form (65.8 recent-5 vs 59.5 all-prior). This joint regime shift across two observables — possession and offsides-against — suggests a structural change in Team B's defensive line behavior as possession dominance increases, which is not captured by examining either observable's recent-vs-all-prior trend in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Involves a joint two-observable relationship (possession × offsides) with a regime-shift structure across ordered time windows (all-prior vs recent-5), and tests a threshold/non-linear dependence rather than a simple recent-vs-long-run comparison of a single observable.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly examine Team B's shots FOR at home vs. away AND Team B's shots_on_target FOR at home vs. away, cross-referenced against Team A's shots FOR at home vs. away. The mechanism tests whether the venue-driven collapse in Team B's shot volume is accompanied by a disproportionate collapse in shot accuracy (shots_on_target / shots ratio), while Team A shows no such asymmetry — requiring two observables (shots and shots_on_target) evaluated simultaneously across two teams.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's shots_on_target rate (shots_on_target / shots) away is suppressed relative to home to a greater degree than Team A's equivalent home/away differential; the joint divergence between the two teams' venue-conditioned shot quality rises with the away-venue penalty on Team B
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot volume and shots-on-target production are jointly conditioned by venue: away from home, both metrics collapse substantially relative to home performance, while Team A's shot-generation is venue-stable. The joint cross-team asymmetry in how venue affects shot volume versus shot accuracy (shots-on-target ratio) for each side cannot be captured by any single-observable venue split.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single-observable venue split: it requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for each team simultaneously, and then compares the asymmetric venue effect across the two teams — a two-observable, two-team asymmetric structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on both Team A's yellow_cards FOR at home vs. away AND Team B's yellow_cards FOR at home vs. away simultaneously. Cross-reference with each team's foul rates by venue to test whether the joint home-venue disciplinary restraint of both teams compounds (i.e., the combined yellow card total is lower than what either team's individual venue adjustment would predict independently).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The joint total of yellow cards in matches where Team A is home and Team B is away is suppressed relative to the sum of each team's all-venue yellow card averages; the suppression is greater than either team's individual venue adjustment alone
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A accumulates yellow cards at a substantially higher rate away than at home, while Team B's yellow card production is higher at home than away. When Team A plays at home (this fixture), the joint interaction of Team A's home disciplinary restraint and Team B's away disciplinary restraint produces a combined yellow card environment that is jointly lower than either team's all-venue average — a two-team, two-dimension joint suppression not reducible to one team's venue split alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions (Team A's home disciplinary profile AND Team B's away disciplinary profile) and examining their joint interaction — not a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compute the ratio of corner_kicks FOR to possession FOR, split by home and away venue. Test whether Team B's possession-to-corners conversion rate collapses away from home (where both possession and corners drop) more than Team A's equivalent ratio changes by venue. The mechanism requires jointly tracking two observables (possession and corners) across two teams and two venue conditions.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's corners-per-possession-unit away is suppressed relative to home to a greater degree than Team A's equivalent home/away differential; the cross-team asymmetry in possession-to-corners conversion rises with the away-venue penalty on Team B
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner kick production shows a strong venue asymmetry (home vs. away), while Team A's corner production is venue-stable. The joint relationship between possession differential and corner kick differential — specifically whether the team with the larger possession share generates a disproportionately higher corner share — differs between the two teams and is conditioned on venue. This tests whether possession-to-corners conversion efficiency is asymmetric across teams and venue.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable relationship (possession and corner_kicks) evaluated asymmetrically across two teams and two venue conditions — not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the within-match half split: compare Team A's cards_2h FOR (second half) against the competition context baseline, and simultaneously compare Team A's goals AGAINST in the second half versus the first half. Test whether the combination of above-average second-half card accumulation and elevated second-half goals-against (relative to first-half goals-against) co-occur more than either signal alone would predict — requiring joint second-half state conditioning on two observables.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Teams with above-competition-average second-half card accumulation also show a higher ratio of second-half to first-half goals conceded; the joint elevation of both signals rises together rather than independently
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half card accumulation (cards_2h FOR) is elevated relative to the competition context, while Team A's goals conceded are skewed toward the second half relative to the first half. The joint relationship between second-half disciplinary load and second-half defensive vulnerability — whether teams that accumulate more second-half cards also concede more second-half goals — represents a within-match state interaction across two distinct observables.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (second half) jointly applied to two distinct observables (cards_2h and goals) and cross-referenced against the competition baseline — not a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's offsides FOR at home AND Team B's offsides FOR away, cross-referenced with each team's possession profile by venue. Test whether the combined offside count in this venue configuration is higher than the sum of each team's all-venue offside averages, and whether the possession differential mediates the joint offside elevation (i.e., the team with more possession generates more offsides in an attacking-dominant role).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The joint offside total rises when both teams' venue-specific offside tendencies align in the same direction (both elevated in their respective venue roles); possession differential moderates which team's offside contribution dominates
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides FOR show a notable home/away asymmetry (higher at home than away), while Team B's offsides FOR show the opposite pattern (higher away than at home). The joint interaction of both teams' offside tendencies in this specific venue configuration (Team A at home, Team B away) produces a combined offside environment that differs from what either team's individual venue adjustment would predict — testing whether the two teams' offside profiles reinforce or offset each other when their respective venue tendencies align in the same direction.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions (Team A's home offside profile AND Team B's away offside profile) and cross-referencing with possession — a two-team, two-observable, two-venue-dimension joint structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the possession differential between the two sides (Team B's all-prior possession FOR vs. Team A's all-prior possession FOR, and their respective RECENT_5 trends showing Team B rising to 61.4% and Team A falling to 40.4%). Within that possession-differential regime, measure whether the joint relationship between possession share and shots (and shots-on-target) for the dominant-possession side exceeds what the single-observable baselines would predict independently.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: As the possession differential between the two sides widens, the dominant-possession team's shots and shots-on-target rise jointly, while the lower-possession team's shot output is suppressed — a non-additive joint effect across both observables and both sides simultaneously.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When Team B (away) holds dominant possession, their shot and shots-on-target production rises disproportionately relative to their corner-kick generation, suggesting a joint possession–shot-conversion efficiency relationship that differs from Team A's lower-possession profile. The interaction between Team B's possession dominance and their shot volume (and on-target rate) should be tested jointly against Team A's possession-deficit and suppressed shot output.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single-observable mirror or a single-band split. It requires jointly conditioning on possession differential AND measuring the co-movement of shots and shots-on-target across both teams simultaneously — an asymmetric two-observable cross-team relationship not reducible to any single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on venue (Team A home, Team B away). Measure the joint ratio of shots-on-target to shots (on-target rate) and shots-on-target to goals (conversion rate) for each team in their respective venue roles, then test whether the away-venue suppression of Team B's shot volume also suppresses their goals proportionally or whether conversion rate compensates.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's goals FOR in away matches are suppressed relative to their home output by more than their shot volume alone would predict, suggesting a non-linear (saturation or threshold) relationship between shot volume and goals that differs by venue — the conversion rate does not fully compensate for the volume drop.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot-to-goal conversion efficiency (shots and shots-on-target FOR vs. goals FOR) is structurally different from Team A's, and this asymmetry is further conditioned by venue: Team B's home shot volume (15.47 shots, 5.59 on target) far exceeds their away output (10.58 shots, 3.58 on target), while Team A's home shot advantage is more modest. The joint relationship between shot volume, shots-on-target, and goals FOR — measured separately for each team and conditioned on venue — tests whether the shot-to-goal conversion rate saturates or diverges across the two teams in this specific venue configuration (Team A at home, Team B away).
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two observables (shots and shots-on-target) to derive a conversion-rate relationship, then further conditioning on venue for both teams simultaneously. It is not a single-observable home/away split; it is a three-observable joint relationship with venue as a second conditioning dimension.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split by half (first vs. second). Jointly condition on Team A's goals-against by half and Team B's goals-for by half. Additionally, condition on second-half card accumulation (cards_2h) for both teams, since elevated second-half card rates may reflect the same late-game intensity that drives second-half goals.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second half produces more goals than the first half in matches involving these two teams, and this effect is associated with elevated second-half card counts — both observables (goals and cards_2h) rise together in the second half, indicating a within-match state shift rather than a uniform distribution across halves.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half goal-concession rate exceeds its first-half rate (0.5 vs. 0.538 against in 2H vs. 0.538 in 1H — roughly balanced), while Team B scores more goals in the second half than the first (0.759 FOR in 2H vs. 0.655 in 1H). The joint within-match half-level asymmetry — Team A's defensive vulnerability by half combined with Team B's scoring timing by half — tests whether the second half is structurally more productive for goals than the first half in this specific matchup configuration.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match half-level split that jointly conditions on two distinct observables (goals by half and cards_2h) across both teams simultaneously. It is not a single observable split by one coarse band; it requires half-resolution data and a joint two-observable relationship.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint recent-5 trend for both fouls and yellow cards FOR each team, compared against their respective all-prior averages and the competition context baseline. The mechanism tests whether the co-elevation of both fouls and yellow cards in recent matches (a two-observable joint trend) predicts a high-card match environment beyond what either observable's recent trend alone would suggest.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both fouls and yellow cards are jointly elevated in recent matches for a team (relative to their own all-prior average and the competition norm), the total card count in the upcoming match rises — a joint threshold effect across two observables, not reducible to either foul rate or card rate alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent-5 yellow card rate (3.6 FOR) has surged well above its all-prior average (2.577 FOR) and above the competition norm (2.623), while Team A's recent-5 fouls committed (12.4) also exceed both its all-prior average (10.577) and the competition norm (11.158). The joint escalation of fouls and yellow cards in Team A's recent matches — conditioned on the fact that Team B's recent yellow card rate (3.0) has also risen above its all-prior average (2.345) — tests whether a high-foul, high-card regime is emerging for this fixture that exceeds what either observable alone would indicate.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (fouls and yellow cards) and their co-movement across two time windows (recent-5 vs. all-prior) for both teams, then comparing against the competition baseline. It is not a single-observable recent-vs-long-run comparison; the joint co-elevation of both observables is the signal.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's offsides FOR (recent surge) and Team B's offsides AGAINST (recent decline), treating these as two distinct dimensions of the same tactical interaction. The mechanism tests whether the divergence between Team A's rising offside rate and Team B's falling offside-concession rate represents a structural mismatch — Team A pushing higher lines against a team that has recently tightened its defensive shape — rather than a simple single-team offside average.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's offsides FOR are rising (indicating a higher attacking line) while the opponent's offsides AGAINST are falling (indicating a tighter defensive line), the actual offsides count in the match is suppressed relative to what Team A's recent offensive offside rate alone would predict — a cross-team asymmetric interaction effect.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides FOR have surged in recent matches (3.2 in RECENT_5 vs. 1.923 all-prior), while Team B's offsides AGAINST have declined (1.6 in RECENT_5 vs. 2.621 all-prior). This creates an asymmetric cross-team relationship: Team A's recent attacking line positioning (as proxied by offsides) is rising sharply, while Team B's defensive line is conceding fewer offsides recently. The joint interaction between Team A's offsides-FOR trend and Team B's offsides-AGAINST trend — two distinct observables for two different sides — tests whether the defensive line depth of Team B suppresses Team A's attacking runs in a way that neither observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team relationship involving the same observable (offsides) measured in opposite directions (FOR one team, AGAINST the other) with diverging recent trends. It requires jointly conditioning on both the FOR and AGAINST dimensions across two teams simultaneously, which is not reducible to a single-observable mirror or a single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on both teams' shots FOR, shots_on_target FOR, and goals FOR (all-prior full-match). Compute the implicit shot-to-goal and shots-on-target-to-goal ratios for each team and test whether the gap between Team A's ratio and Team B's ratio is associated with a directional difference in goals scored in the match, beyond what either team's raw shot volume alone would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Matches where Team A's shots-on-target-to-goals ratio is higher than Team B's are associated with Team A scoring more goals relative to Team B than the raw shot volumes would suggest; the joint ratio gap rises with the goal differential between the two sides.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot-volume-to-goals conversion asymmetry: Team B generates shots at a rate comparable to the competition average but converts them into goals at a markedly lower rate than Team A, suggesting that when two teams with divergent shot-to-goal ratios meet, the team with the higher conversion efficiency (Team A) produces more goals relative to its shot count than the team with the lower conversion efficiency (Team B), even when raw shot volumes are similar.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly relating three distinct observables (shots, shots_on_target, goals) for both teams simultaneously to form a cross-team ratio comparison. It cannot be reduced to a single observable mirrored against what the opponent allows, nor to one observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's possession FOR (all-prior and recent-5), Team B's fouls FOR (all-prior and recent-5), and Team B's yellow_cards FOR (all-prior and recent-5). Test whether the joint state of below-competition-average possession AND above-competition-average fouls is associated with elevated yellow card counts relative to what either variable alone predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's possession is below the competition mean and its foul rate is above the competition mean simultaneously, its yellow card rate rises above what either variable in isolation would predict; the joint deficit-plus-foul condition amplifies card accumulation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession-deficit combined with high foul rate: Team B habitually operates with below-average possession (well below 50%) while simultaneously committing fouls at a rate above the competition average, especially in recent matches. When a low-possession team also has a high foul rate, the joint combination is associated with elevated yellow card and total card volumes for that team, beyond what either possession or fouls alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and fouls) as co-predictors of a third (yellow_cards). It is not reducible to any single observable mirrored against opponent allowance, nor to one observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's shots_on_target AGAINST (all-prior) and Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST (all-prior and recent-5), and cross-reference with each team's goals AGAINST. Test whether the gap between Team B's shots-on-target allowed and Team A's shots-on-target allowed is associated with a directional asymmetry in goals conceded across the two teams in the same match.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The team that allows more shots-on-target (Team B) concedes more goals than the team that allows fewer shots-on-target (Team A); the asymmetry in shots-on-target allowed between the two teams rises with the asymmetry in goals conceded.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Cross-team asymmetric shots-on-target allowed: Team A allows shots-on-target at a rate close to the competition average, while Team B allows shots-on-target at a rate substantially above the competition average. When the defending team (Team B) allows markedly more shots-on-target than the attacking team (Team A) allows, the total goals conceded by the higher-allowing side rises disproportionately relative to the lower-allowing side, creating an asymmetric goals-against pattern between the two teams.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team relationship involving two different observables (shots_on_target AGAINST and goals AGAINST) for both sides simultaneously. It is not a single observable mirrored against what the opponent allows; it requires comparing the two teams' defensive profiles jointly.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's possession FOR HOME, Team B's fouls FOR AWAY versus HOME split, and Team B's yellow_cards FOR AWAY versus HOME split. Test whether the combination of Team A's home possession dominance and Team B's away-reduced foul rate produces a different total foul and card environment than the all-venue averages for either team would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the home team holds high possession and the away team's foul rate is suppressed away from home relative to its home rate, total match fouls and cards are lower than the sum of each team's all-venue averages would suggest; the venue-conditioned joint interaction suppresses the card environment.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's venue-conditioned foul rate interacts with Team A's possession dominance: Team B commits substantially more fouls at home than away, while Team A maintains high possession both home and away. When a high-possession team (Team A, playing at home) faces a side whose foul rate is elevated specifically in home contexts (Team B, playing away), the joint interaction of Team A's possession dominance and Team B's away-suppressed foul rate may alter the card and foul environment relative to what each team's overall averages suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions (venue split for fouls/cards AND possession level), and involves a cross-team joint relationship. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band or a simple home/away split of one observable.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's goals FOR FIRST_HALF and SECOND_HALF (all-prior) and Team B's goals FOR FIRST_HALF and SECOND_HALF (all-prior), as well as Team B's goals AGAINST FIRST_HALF and SECOND_HALF. Test whether the within-match half-level distribution of goals differs directionally between the two teams — specifically whether Team A's first-half goal rate exceeds Team B's first-half goal rate by more than the second-half comparison, and whether this half-level asymmetry is associated with the match's half-level goal split.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's goals are front-loaded (first half rate higher relative to Team B's first-half rate), while Team B's goals are back-loaded; the half-level asymmetry between the two teams rises with the difference in their first-half versus second-half goal rates, and this pattern is detectable at the half level rather than only at full-match resolution.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's recent shots FOR (RECENT_5) is substantially below its season average AND Team B's recent shots_on_target FOR (RECENT_5) is also below season average, while simultaneously Team A's recent shots_on_target FOR (RECENT_5) is above its season average. mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A (home) has a historically lower possession share at home than Team B typically commands in any venue, and measure whether Team A's corner_kicks FOR at home and Team B's corner_kicks AGAINST (recent) jointly reflect a possession-to-corners conversion asymmetry. Measuring how corner kick production for both teams responds to this specific cross-team possession asymmetry — where one team's possession is venue-sensitive and the other's is not — tests a joint two-observable, two-team mechanism.

mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two observables (fouls and yellow_cards) across two teams with asymmetric recent trajectories. It is not reducible to a single observable against one band.

Measure whether second-half goal totals in matches involving both teams exceed what the full-match average divided by two would predict, specifically when both teams show a second-half skew in the same direction.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the attacking team's goal production is skewed toward the second half and the defending team's goals conceded are also skewed toward the second half, second-half goal totals in the match are elevated relative to a naive half-match split of the full-match average.
