mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on the within-match half-level distributions of two distinct teams' goal observables (Team A FOR and Team B AGAINST), using half-resolution data. It is not a single observable against one band, and it requires half-level data resolution rather than full-match.

It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band, nor to a simple home/away or opponent-descriptor split.

It is not reducible to a single observable or a single coarse band; it requires computing a derived ratio and a cross-team joint trend.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on (1) Team A's home corner FOR being elevated relative to its away corner FOR, and (2) Team B's corner FOR ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5 being above the competition neutral mean. mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions at once: Team A's venue-conditioned corner production AND Team B's corner-generating tendency. The engine covers venue split for one team's own observable, but not the joint interaction of one team's venue asymmetry with the opposing team's own production level.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Use half-level corner data for both teams. Condition on Team A's corner FOR SECOND_HALF > FIRST_HALF and Team B's corner FOR SECOND_HALF > FIRST_HALF simultaneously. Evaluate whether the combined second-half corner volume exceeds what a uniform within-match distribution would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half corner volume is elevated relative to first-half corner volume when both teams individually show a second-half corner bias, and this joint back-loading is greater than either team's individual half-split would suggest in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Corner kick production is asymmetrically distributed across halves for both teams: Team A generates more corners in the second half than the first, while Team B also generates more corners in the second half. The joint within-match half-level distribution of corners — where both teams' second-half corner rates exceed their first-half rates — is associated with a back-loaded corner profile that differs from what full-match averages alone imply.

The engine covers a single observable's half-level split for one team, but not the joint interaction of both teams' half-level distributions producing a combined within-match regime.

Measure whether this asymmetric configuration — where one team is a high-card accumulator and the other is not — produces a second-half card total (cards_2h) that is elevated beyond what the competition baseline or either team's individual card rate predicts, particularly given that second-half card rates are already above the per-half average in this competition.

The joint relationship between one team's foul production and the other team's card accumulation — measured as an asymmetric cross-team pairing — may predict second-half card totals differently than either observable alone.

Measure whether this joint configuration (low possession + high offsides) is associated with a suppression of Team A's corner and shot production relative to what its all-prior rates would predict, and whether Team B's corner and shot production rises correspondingly.

The joint relationship between a team's possession deficit and its rising offside rate — two distinct observables moving in opposite directions — may indicate a structural shift toward a counter-attacking regime that affects shots, corners, and goals in a non-linear way.

The joint relationship between one team's shot-generation trend and the opponent's shot-suppression trend — measured across both observables simultaneously for both sides — captures a structural mismatch not reducible to either observable alone.

The asymmetric divergence pattern (one team's FOR rising, opponent's AGAINST also rising) is a two-observable, two-perspective joint structure.

Evaluate whether possession dominance combined with elevated offside rate co-occurs systematically.

Team B's offsides FOR have spiked recently (recent 3.2 vs all-prior 1.8), suggesting that high-possession, high-tempo forward play generates elevated offside counts. The joint relationship between possession dominance and offside frequency — across both teams — is a two-observable mechanism.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's fouls FOR exceeds Team B's fouls FOR, AND Team B's cards_2h AGAINST exceeds Team A's cards_2h AGAINST. Measure whether the team that commits more fouls against a high-card-conceding opponent generates elevated second-half cards for that opponent.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the fouling rate of one team (FOR) is elevated relative to the opponent's fouling rate, and the opponent's cards_2h AGAINST rate is also elevated, total second-half cards rise above competition context baseline
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A commits more fouls FOR (all-prior 12.9, away 13.0) than Team B (all-prior 12.1), while Team B concedes more fouls AGAINST (all-prior 13.5) than Team A concedes AGAINST (all-prior 10.6). Simultaneously, Team A's cards_2h FOR (1.32) exceeds Team B's cards_2h FOR (1.23), and Team B's cards_2h AGAINST (1.53) exceeds Team A's cards_2h AGAINST (1.08). The joint relationship between the foul-committing rate of one team and the second-half card rate of the opponent — across both observables and both perspectives — is an asymmetric cross-team mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team joint mechanism: it requires simultaneously reading one team's fouls FOR against the other team's cards_2h AGAINST — two distinct observables across two different team perspectives. This cannot be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the within-match half split of corner_kicks FOR and AGAINST for both teams simultaneously. Specifically, evaluate whether the team whose corner production is back-loaded (higher 2H than 1H rate) faces an opponent whose corner-conceding rate is also back-loaded, amplifying second-half corner totals relative to first-half corner totals.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams show a back-loaded corner profile (higher 2H than 1H rates for corners FOR and/or AGAINST), second-half corner totals exceed first-half corner totals by more than the competition baseline half-split would predict
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A generates corners more heavily in the second half (FOR 2H: 2.19 vs 1H: 1.79) while Team B generates corners more heavily in the first half (FOR 1H: 2.27 vs 2H: 2.56, but AGAINST 1H: 1.60 vs 2H: 2.08). The within-match half-level distribution of corner production differs structurally between the two teams, creating an asymmetric half-by-half corner profile that cannot be captured by full-match totals alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (1H vs 2H) applied jointly to both teams' FOR and AGAINST corner profiles simultaneously — a two-half, two-perspective joint structure. It is not reducible to a single observable at full-match level with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) the within-match half split of goals FOR and AGAINST for both teams, and (b) the possession dominance level of the attacking team. Evaluate whether teams with possession above a threshold show a different 1H-vs-2H goal distribution than teams with balanced or below-average possession.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team holds possession materially above competition baseline, its second-half goals FOR rate rises relative to its first-half goals FOR rate, and this half-skew is more pronounced than for teams with balanced possession
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B scores more goals in the second half (FOR 2H: 0.91) than the first half (FOR 1H: 0.67), while Team A concedes more in the first half (AGAINST 1H: 0.67) than the second half (AGAINST 2H: 0.76) — but Team B holds dominant possession (recent ~62%). The joint relationship between possession dominance and the within-match half-level goal distribution — specifically whether high-possession teams convert their dominance into goals more in one half than the other — is a two-observable, within-match-state mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on possession level (a continuous observable) and the within-match half-level split of goals — two distinct observables with a within-match state dimension. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on both teams' possession share and shots volume in the same match sample. The relationship is evaluated as a cross-team asymmetry: Team A's possession-to-shots ratio versus Team B's possession-to-shots ratio, using all-prior and recent-5 windows for both teams.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team holds a dominant possession share, its shots volume rises disproportionately relative to the possession-to-shots ratio of the lower-possession team; the gap between the two ratios widens as the possession differential grows.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A holds a large possession advantage over Team B, but the joint relationship between each team's possession share and their shots volume reveals an asymmetric conversion: Team A's recent possession surge (67.6%) co-occurs with a shots surge (16.6 recent vs 13.1 all-prior), while Team B's possession deficit (37.8% recent) co-occurs with a shots contraction (9.4 recent vs 10.2 all-prior). The mechanism tests whether the joint possession-shots ratio differs systematically across the two sides beyond what each observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single-observable mirror or a single-observable with one band. It requires jointly tracking two distinct observables (possession AND shots) for both sides simultaneously and testing whether their ratio relationship is asymmetric across teams — a two-observable, cross-team joint structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on both teams' possession share jointly with their shots and shots-on-target counts. Evaluate whether the shots-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio is higher for the possession-dominant team across historical match samples where a similar possession differential existed.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The possession-dominant team's shots-on-target per shot rises relative to the possession-deficient team's ratio; the asymmetry in conversion quality grows with the size of the possession differential.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots-on-target production (5.6 recent, 4.7 all-prior) is elevated relative to its shots volume, while Team B's shots-on-target rate (3.8 recent, 2.9 all-prior) is low relative to its shots volume. The joint relationship between possession dominance and shots-on-target conversion rate differs across the two teams: the dominant-possession team converts a higher share of shots to shots-on-target than the low-possession team.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires three observables jointly (possession, shots, shots_on_target) and a cross-team ratio comparison. Not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the half (first vs second) jointly for both teams' scoring and conceding rates. Specifically, test the joint pattern: Team A's first-half goals-for rate paired with Team B's first-half goals-against rate, versus Team A's second-half goals-for rate paired with Team B's second-half goals-against rate. This is a two-dimensional half × team-role interaction.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The combined first-half goal environment (Team A scoring + Team B conceding in H1) differs directionally from the combined second-half goal environment, with the second half showing a higher joint conceding exposure for Team B relative to the first half.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A scores more goals in the first half (0.684) than the second half (0.750), a relatively balanced split, while Team B scores heavily in the first half (0.382) relative to its second half (0.342), and concedes more in the second half (0.855) than the first (0.566). The joint within-match half-level goal distribution for both teams simultaneously — Team A's first-half scoring rate against Team B's second-half conceding rate, and vice versa — creates a cross-half, cross-team interaction that is not captured by either team's half-level split alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match half-level split applied jointly across both teams' FOR and AGAINST perspectives simultaneously — a two-dimensional conditioning (half × team-side) that cannot be reduced to a single team's half split or a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on half (H1 vs H2) and both teams' FOR and AGAINST corner rates simultaneously. Test whether the combined second-half corner total (Team A FOR + Team B FOR, or equivalently Team A AGAINST + Team B AGAINST) is systematically higher than the first-half combined total when both teams individually show second-half corner concentration.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams independently show higher second-half corner rates (FOR and AGAINST), the combined second-half corner environment rises above the first-half environment by more than either team's individual half-split would suggest in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Both teams show a second-half corner kick concentration: Team A generates 2.233 corners in H2 vs 1.959 in H1 (FOR), and concedes 2.808 in H2 vs 2.397 in H1 (AGAINST). Team B generates 2.276 in H2 vs 2.039 in H1 (FOR) and concedes 2.987 in H2 vs 2.697 in H1 (AGAINST). The joint half-level corner distribution across both teams' FOR and AGAINST perspectives tests whether the second-half corner environment is amplified when both teams simultaneously exhibit second-half corner concentration tendencies.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on half AND both teams' FOR/AGAINST corner rates simultaneously — a two-dimensional (half × dual-team) interaction not reducible to a single team's half split or a single-observable band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on a team's full-match foul rate (as a continuous variable) and test whether the second-half card rate (cards_2h) shows a threshold or non-linear relationship — specifically, whether teams above a foul-rate threshold accumulate cards_2h at an accelerating rate relative to teams below that threshold, rather than a simple linear scaling.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: cards_2h rises with fouls rate but shows a threshold or saturation pattern: below a foul-rate threshold the relationship is weak, but above it cards_2h escalates disproportionately; both teams in this fixture operate above the competition foul baseline, suggesting they sit in the elevated-escalation regime.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A commits high fouls (14.2 all-prior, 15.0 recent) and concedes high fouls (13.7 all-prior, 16.6 recent), while Team B commits fewer fouls (12.4 all-prior, 12.6 recent). The joint relationship between a team's foul-committing rate and its second-half card accumulation (cards_2h) tests whether high-foul teams face a non-linear escalation in second-half card exposure — i.e., whether the cards_2h rate saturates or accelerates beyond a foul-rate threshold, rather than scaling linearly. Team A's cards_2h FOR (1.316) and AGAINST (1.421) are both elevated relative to Team B's (1.211 FOR, 1.368 AGAINST), and the competition context cards_2h is 0.75, suggesting both teams operate above the competition norm.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable (fouls × cards_2h) threshold/non-linear relationship, not a single-observable mirror or a simple band split. It requires testing the shape of the fouls-to-cards_2h relationship across the continuous foul-rate distribution, which is structurally richer than any covered single-observable comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR (all-prior and recent-5) alongside Team B's shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST (all-prior and recent-5). The ratio of shots_on_target/shots for each team's attack versus the opponent's defensive filtering ratio forms a two-dimensional joint relationship.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's shot accuracy (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR) is low and the opponent's defensive filtering (shots_on_target AGAINST / shots AGAINST) is high, the resulting on-target volume is suppressed beyond what either observable alone would predict; the joint product of the two ratios falls below the competition baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shot accuracy) jointly with Team B's shots-against-to-shots-on-target-against ratio (defensive filtering) determines the asymmetric on-target threat differential in this match. Team A produces low shots and low shots-on-target both all-time and recently, while Team B concedes fewer shots but at a higher on-target rate recently, creating a cross-observable asymmetry between attacking accuracy and defensive filtering that is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly computing two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for both sides simultaneously and forming a cross-team ratio product. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band; it is an asymmetric cross-observable relationship between Team A's attacking accuracy and Team B's defensive filtering.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the simultaneous direction of drift (recent-5 vs all-prior) across all three observables for Team A in the AGAINST/FOR perspective. The mechanism fires when possession FOR drifts down while shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST both drift up — a three-way co-movement pattern.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's possession FOR recent drift is downward and its shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST recent drifts are both upward, the team's defensive exposure (shots_on_target conceded) rises more than the individual drifts would suggest in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent possession collapse (all-prior ~42.5% dropping to recent-5 ~36.2%) co-occurs with a simultaneous rise in shots conceded (all-prior ~12.3 rising to recent-5 ~15.4) and shots-on-target conceded (all-prior ~4.7 rising to recent-5 ~6.2). The joint drift across three observables — possession lost, shots conceded up, shots-on-target conceded up — signals a compounding defensive exposure regime that is structurally richer than any single observable's recent-vs-all-prior comparison.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves three distinct observables drifting jointly in consistent directions, not a single observable's recent vs long-run comparison. The joint co-movement condition across possession, shots, and shots_on_target is not reducible to any single-observable recent-vs-all-prior split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner_kicks FOR and AGAINST by FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF for both teams. Condition on the asymmetry: Team A's FOR corners grow modestly from 1H to 2H while its AGAINST corners grow more steeply from 1H to 2H; compare this within-match half-level asymmetry against Team B's own 1H-to-2H corner growth pattern.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's AGAINST corner growth from first to second half exceeds its FOR corner growth from first to second half, and Team B's FOR corner growth from first to second half is also positive, second-half total corners in the match rise above the first-half total, with Team A being the net conceder of the second-half corner surplus.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner kicks exhibit a pronounced first-half vs second-half split (1H all-prior ~2.01 FOR vs 2H ~2.27 FOR) while Team B's corners show the opposite pattern (1H ~2.16 FOR vs 2H ~2.43 FOR), and Team A concedes more corners in the second half (~2.94) than first half (~2.70). The within-match half-level distribution of corner kicks differs asymmetrically between the two teams, with both teams generating more corners in the second half but Team A conceding disproportionately more in the second half relative to its own production.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This uses within-match half-level splits (FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF) for both teams simultaneously and compares the asymmetric growth rates across perspectives (FOR vs AGAINST) within each half. It is not a single observable with one coarse band; it requires the joint half×perspective×team structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's offsides FOR recent-5 vs all-prior drift AND Team A's offsides AGAINST recent-5 vs all-prior drift. The mechanism requires both drifts to be upward simultaneously — a two-team, two-perspective co-movement condition on the same observable.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's offsides FOR recent drift is strongly upward and Team A's offsides AGAINST recent drift is also strongly upward, the match-level offsides total rises above competition baseline, and the joint signal is stronger than either team's individual drift would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's offsides FOR have spiked sharply in recent matches (all-prior ~1.72 vs recent-5 ~3.80) while Team A's offsides AGAINST have also risen recently (all-prior ~2.52 vs recent-5 ~4.00). This joint upward drift in both Team B's attacking line depth (offsides FOR) and Team A's defensive line positioning (offsides AGAINST) suggests a two-sided structural shift: Team B is pushing its line higher recently while Team A is also playing a higher defensive line, creating a compounding offside-trap dynamic that neither observable captures alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint co-movement of the same observable (offsides) across two teams in opposite perspectives (Team B FOR, Team A AGAINST) simultaneously. It is not a single team's observable vs a single band; it is a cross-team, cross-perspective joint drift condition.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (1) both teams' cards_2h FOR rates exceeding competition baseline, (2) Team B's fouls FOR being elevated both all-prior and in recent-5, and (3) Team A's yellow_cards FOR recent-5 being elevated above its own all-prior rate. All three conditions must hold simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams' second-half card rates exceed competition baseline AND the higher-fouling team's foul rate is rising in recent matches AND the opponent's yellow card rate is also rising recently, second-half total cards in the match rise above what either team's individual card rate or foul rate alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half cards (cards_2h FOR ~1.23, AGAINST ~1.34) and Team B's second-half cards (cards_2h FOR ~1.34, AGAINST ~1.22) jointly exceed the competition second-half cards baseline (~1.04 per team side). The cross-team joint second-half card accumulation — where both teams' FOR and AGAINST second-half card rates sit above the competition norm — interacts with Team B's elevated foul rate (FOR all-prior ~13.5, recent-5 ~14.8) and Team A's elevated yellow card rate recently (FOR recent-5 ~2.6 vs all-prior ~1.72). The joint condition of high second-half card rates on both sides combined with Team B's foul volume and Team A's recent yellow card escalation creates a compounding disciplinary pressure signal.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine three-observable joint condition (cards_2h, fouls, yellow_cards) across both teams simultaneously, with a within-match period split (second half) combined with a recent-vs-all-prior drift condition on a second observable. It cannot be reduced to any single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's RECENT_5 shots FOR exceeds its ALL_PRIOR shots FOR by a meaningful margin, AND Team B's RECENT_5 shots AGAINST is also elevated above its ALL_PRIOR shots AGAINST. Measure whether goals per shot in such joint-elevated-volume matchups differs from the baseline conversion rate implied by each team's individual shot and goal averages.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both attacking volume (Team A shots FOR RECENT_5 elevated) and defensive exposure (Team B shots AGAINST RECENT_5 elevated) are simultaneously high, goals per shot may saturate or be suppressed relative to the product of individual averages — i.e., volume and conversion do not scale linearly together.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent surge in shots and shots-on-target (RECENT_5) relative to its long-run average co-occurs with a simultaneous compression in Team B's recent shots allowed (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR). The joint condition — one team's attack volume rising while the opponent's defensive solidity is also rising — may suppress the conversion rate (goals per shot) relative to what either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (shots FOR for Team A and shots AGAINST for Team B) simultaneously, and examining a derived ratio (goals per shot) rather than either observable in isolation. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's shots_on_target FOR RECENT_5 is elevated above ALL_PRIOR AND Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST RECENT_5 is elevated above ALL_PRIOR. Within this joint condition, test whether corner_kicks FOR (Team A) and AGAINST (Team B) are elevated relative to competition context norms.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams' recent on-target shot profiles are elevated simultaneously, corner kick volume rises above competition context baseline — reflecting sustained attacking pressure that does not convert cleanly.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots-on-target FOR has risen sharply in RECENT_5 relative to ALL_PRIOR, while Team B's shots-on-target AGAINST has also risen in RECENT_5. The asymmetric relationship between one team's on-target accuracy trend and the opponent's recent defensive on-target concession trend — measured jointly — may predict whether corner kicks (a proxy for sustained attacking pressure without conversion) are elevated above competition norms.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (shots_on_target FOR for Team A and shots_on_target AGAINST for Team B) and relating their joint state to a third observable (corner_kicks). Not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's offsides FOR RECENT_5 being elevated above ALL_PRIOR AND Team B's offsides AGAINST RECENT_5 being elevated above ALL_PRIOR. Within this joint condition, compare the ratio of first-half goals to second-half goals for both teams against their unconditional first-half/second-half goal splits.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams' recent offside profiles are jointly elevated, the share of goals scored in the first half rises relative to the unconditional first-half/second-half goal split — reflecting high-line pressing dynamics that produce earlier scoring opportunities.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides FOR has risen sharply in RECENT_5 relative to ALL_PRIOR (and relative to its home vs away split), while Team B's offsides AGAINST has also risen in RECENT_5. The joint condition of both teams' offside profiles shifting simultaneously — one team pressing higher lines, the other conceding more offsides — may be associated with a distinct pattern in first-half versus second-half goal distribution, as high-line pressing tends to produce early goals but also fatigue-related second-half exposure.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (offsides FOR for Team A and offsides AGAINST for Team B) and relating their joint state to a within-match temporal split (first-half vs second-half goals). This combines a two-observable joint condition with a half-level resolution, neither of which is covered individually.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team B's corner kicks FOR showing a large home-vs-away gap (home ALL_PRIOR >> away ALL_PRIOR), AND (b) Team B's RECENT_5 corners FOR being below their away ALL_PRIOR. Test whether the combined match corner total is suppressed relative to the naive sum of Team A FOR ALL_PRIOR and Team B FOR ALL_PRIOR averages.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's corner production is both venue-asymmetric (much higher at home) and in a recent downward regime, the combined match corner total is suppressed below the naive sum of both teams' unconditional averages — the venue asymmetry and recent regime interact non-additively.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner kicks FOR show a pronounced home/away asymmetry (home ALL_PRIOR substantially higher than away ALL_PRIOR), while their RECENT_5 corners FOR has dropped sharply below both their ALL_PRIOR and their away average. Simultaneously, Team A's corner kicks FOR is stable across home/away. The joint condition — one team's corner production being venue-asymmetric AND in a recent downward regime — may predict whether the combined corner total in this match is suppressed relative to the sum of each team's individual ALL_PRIOR averages.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct dimensions for Team B (venue asymmetry as a ratio of home vs away averages, AND recent-vs-long-run regime shift), and relating their joint state to the combined total. A single observable with one coarse band cannot capture this two-dimensional conditioning.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A's possession FOR RECENT_5 being elevated above its ALL_PRIOR AND above its home ALL_PRIOR baseline, AND (b) Team B's possession FOR RECENT_5 being below its ALL_PRIOR. Within this joint diverging-possession condition, test whether Team B's fouls FOR and cards_2h FOR are elevated relative to their unconditional averages and competition context norms.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When possession trends diverge asymmetrically — one team rising, the other falling in RECENT_5 — the possession-losing team's foul rate and second-half card rate rise above their unconditional averages, with the relationship being stronger than what either team's possession level alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession FOR has risen sharply in RECENT_5 relative to ALL_PRIOR (and relative to its home average), while Team B's possession FOR has dropped in RECENT_5 below its ALL_PRIOR. This creates an asymmetric possession regime shift where one team is trending toward dominance and the other toward submission. The joint condition of diverging possession trends — rather than either team's possession level alone — may be associated with elevated fouls AGAINST for the possession-losing team (Team B committing more fouls as they chase the ball), and consequently elevated cards_2h for Team B in the second half.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession FOR for Team A trending up AND possession FOR for Team B trending down) and relating their joint divergence to a third observable (fouls/cards) for the possession-losing side. This is an asymmetric cross-team two-observable joint condition, not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint ratio of shots-for to shots-on-target for each team simultaneously (not just one team's mirror), comparing Team A's all-prior ratio against its recent-5 ratio, and Team B's all-prior ratio against its recent-5 ratio, to detect whether a divergence in shot quality (shots-on-target per shot) between the two sides is associated with a differential in goals-for relative to shots-on-target.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's shots-on-target-per-shot ratio is substantially lower than the opponent's, goals-for relative to shots-on-target is suppressed for the lower-ratio team, even as raw shot volume rises.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A generates a high volume of shots and shots on target but converts at a rate that, when jointly examined with Team B's low shots-for but improving recent shots-for trend, reveals an asymmetric shot-volume-to-on-target ratio relationship between the two sides. Specifically, the joint pattern of Team A's shots-for versus shots-on-target ratio (both all-prior and recent) compared against Team B's equivalent ratio tests whether high shot volume without proportional on-target accuracy is associated with suppressed goal output relative to shot count.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship across three observables (shots, shots_on_target, goals) for both teams simultaneously, comparing ratios across two time windows. It is not reducible to a single observable mirror or a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on both teams' possession levels and shots-for levels simultaneously. Specifically, test whether the team with lower possession (Team B, ~46%) but a recent surge in shots-for (9.6 all-prior to 14.2 recent) achieves a shots-on-target rate per possession unit that rises relative to the possession-dominant team (Team A, ~54-60% possession).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The team with lower possession but a rising shots-for trend generates shots-on-target per possession unit at a rate that rises relative to the possession-dominant team, indicating a non-linear relationship between possession share and shot quality.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A holds substantially more possession than Team B (both all-prior and recent), while Team B's recent shots-for has surged relative to its all-prior average despite lower possession. This joint relationship between possession dominance and shot generation tests whether a team that cedes possession but increases shot volume (a counter-attacking profile) generates shots-on-target at a disproportionately higher rate per unit of possession than the possession-dominant team.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship across two distinct observables (possession and shots/shots_on_target) for both teams simultaneously, not a single observable mirror or a single observable with one coarse band. The cross-team asymmetry in possession vs. shot-volume trends is the key structural feature.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on both the half-period (first vs second) and the team role (Team A scoring, Team B conceding), examining the cross-product of Team A's half-split goals-for with Team B's half-split goals-against. This is a two-dimensional conditioning: half-period × team-role asymmetry, not a single team's half split in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The combination of Team A's second-half scoring surge and Team B's first-half defensive weakness produces a within-match goal distribution that is skewed differently than either team's individual half-split would predict in isolation — specifically, the first half may see more Team B vulnerability while the second half sees more Team A dominance.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A scores more goals in the second half than the first half (0.831 first half vs 1.169 second half), while Team B concedes more in the first half than the second half (0.75 first half vs 0.594 second half). This cross-team, cross-half asymmetry in goal timing tests whether the joint pattern of Team A's second-half scoring tendency and Team B's first-half defensive vulnerability produces a non-uniform within-match goal distribution that differs from what either team's full-match average alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct dimensions: the half-period split AND the cross-team asymmetry between Team A's scoring half-distribution and Team B's conceding half-distribution. It is not a single observable's half split for one team.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on both teams' foul rates and Team A's recent yellow card surge, examining whether the combination of Team B's foul-committing tendency (11.656 all-prior, 9.8 recent) and Team A's elevated recent yellow card rate (3.0 recent vs 1.815 all-prior) is associated with elevated second-half card counts (cards_2h) beyond the competition context baseline of 1.167.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's own recent yellow card rate has surged AND the opponent commits fouls at an above-average rate, second-half card accumulation (cards_2h) rises above what either team's individual card or foul rate alone would predict — a joint amplification effect.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's yellow cards have surged in recent matches (1.815 all-prior to 3.0 recent) while Team B commits more fouls per match than Team A allows (11.656 vs 10.769). mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and shots/shots_on_target) with a non-linear divergence condition, not a single observable vs one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on (a) Team B holding possession above its own long-run average AND (b) Team A's recent foul rate being elevated above its long-run average. Measure whether Team B's shots_on_target and Team A's yellow_cards jointly deviate from their standalone baselines in this combined state.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a possession-dominant team faces an opponent whose recent foul rate has risen above its long-run level, the possession-dominant team's shots_on_target is suppressed relative to its standalone rate, while the high-fouling team's yellow card rate rises above its standalone rate — an asymmetric cross-observable relationship.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B consistently holds more possession than its opponents (52.7% all-prior, 55.4% recent) while Team A consistently cedes possession (46.4% all-prior, 42.6% recent). When the possession-dominant team (Team B) faces a team that both cedes possession AND has recently increased its foul rate (Team A: 12.4 fouls recent vs 10.5 all-prior), the joint interaction of possession dominance and elevated opponent fouling may suppress the possession-dominant team's shot conversion by increasing interruptions, while simultaneously elevating cards for the lower-possession team.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves an asymmetric relationship across different observables for the two sides (Team B's shots_on_target vs Team A's fouls/yellow_cards), conditioned on two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (possession dominance and foul-rate drift). Not reducible to any single-observable mirror or one-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on the half-level goal rates FOR and AGAINST for both teams simultaneously. Specifically, identify matches where Team B's H1 FOR rate exceeds its H2 FOR rate AND Team A's H2 FOR rate exceeds its H1 FOR rate. Measure whether the combined H1 vs H2 goal distribution in such matchups differs from the additive expectation of each team's standalone half-split.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the away team scores disproportionately in the first half and the home team scores disproportionately in the second half, the match-level goal distribution across halves is more balanced than either team's standalone half-split predicts, and the second half sees a higher home-team goal share than the away team's defensive H2 rate alone would imply.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's goals are heavily front-loaded in the first half (0.845 FOR H1 vs 0.930 FOR H2, and 0.563 AGAINST H1 vs 0.704 AGAINST H2), while Team A's goals are back-loaded (0.718 FOR H1 vs 1.000 FOR H2, and 0.535 AGAINST H1 vs 0.761 AGAINST H2). The joint within-match half-level goal distribution across both teams — where one team scores more in H1 and the other scores more in H2 — creates a non-additive half-level goal timing structure. Specifically, the interaction of Team B's H1 scoring tendency with Team A's H2 scoring tendency may produce a match where goals are distributed more evenly across halves than either team's standalone half-split would suggest, or where the H2 goal rate is disproportionately driven by Team A.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match half-level split conditioned on the joint state of both teams' half-level goal distributions simultaneously — a two-team, two-half, cross-observable structure that cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band or a simple home/away split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the possession gap between the two sides (Team B FOR minus Team A FOR) exceeds a threshold derived from the long-run averages. Within those matches, measure whether Team B's shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR co-move upward while Team A's shots FOR remains suppressed.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: As the cross-team possession gap widens in favour of Team B, Team B's shots and shots_on_target rise above their long-run means while Team A's shots remain at or below their long-run mean — a joint asymmetric co-movement across both observables and both teams simultaneously.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When Team B holds a large possession advantage over Team A (as seen in recent matches where Team B averaged ~63% possession vs Team A's ~41%), Team B's shot volume rises sharply relative to its long-run average, while Team A's shots-against also rises sharply. The joint relationship between the possession imbalance across both teams and the resulting shot differential is not captured by either team's possession or shots in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession and shots) measured for two different teams simultaneously, and testing an asymmetric cross-team relationship. It cannot be reduced to one team's possession vs one band, nor to one team's shots vs one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: In matches where Team A's fouls FOR (committed) is above a threshold, measure whether Team B's ratio of shots_on_target to shots is lower than in matches where Team A's fouls are below that threshold, controlling for Team B's raw shot volume.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's shots_on_target-to-shots ratio is suppressed in matches where Team A's foul rate is elevated, even when Team B's total shot count remains high — a non-linear joint relationship across two distinct observables from two different teams.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shot quality / accuracy) co-varies with Team A's defensive foul rate. When Team A commits more fouls (disrupting Team B's build-up), Team B's shots_on_target as a share of total shots may be suppressed even when raw shot volume is high. This joint relationship between Team A's fouls-committed and Team B's shots vs shots_on_target ratio is structurally richer than either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship between one team's fouls (Team A FOR) and the other team's shots vs shots_on_target ratio (Team B), which is an asymmetric cross-team, two-observable interaction not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split matches into first-half and second-half corner counts for both teams. Condition on Team A's historical tendency to concede more corners in the second half (AGAINST SECOND_HALF vs FIRST_HALF). Within those matches, test whether Team B's second-half corner count rises disproportionately relative to its first-half count compared to matches against teams that do not show this pattern.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's second-half corner count rises above its first-half count more sharply when facing opponents (like Team A) who structurally concede more corners in the second half — a within-match half-level interaction between two teams' corner tendencies across halves.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B generates substantially more corners in the second half than the first half (long-run 2H mean ~3.08 vs 1H mean ~2.52), while Team A generates fewer corners overall and concedes more corners recently. The joint within-match half-level split of corner production for Team B, conditioned on Team A's corner-conceding tendency, tests whether Team B's second-half corner surge is amplified when facing a team that structurally concedes more corners in the second half.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (first half vs second half) jointly conditioned on both teams' half-specific corner tendencies. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band; it requires two half-period observations and a cross-team conditioning dimension simultaneously.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Identify historical match contexts where the attacking team's recent-5 shots, shots_on_target, and possession all simultaneously exceed their long-run means, while the defending team's recent-5 shots-against, shots_on_target-against all simultaneously exceed their long-run means. Measure whether goals FOR the attacking team in such jointly-aligned contexts are elevated relative to contexts where only one or two of these observables are co-aligned.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals scored by the attacking team rise as the number of simultaneously co-aligned attacking/defensive observable pairs increases — a threshold or saturation effect where joint multi-observable alignment produces a stronger signal than any single observable's recent deviation alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent form shows a simultaneous deterioration across multiple defensive observables (shots against rising from ~14.9 to ~21.0, shots_on_target against rising from ~5.4 to ~6.6, goals against rising from ~1.79 to ~2.0, possession dropping from ~47% to ~40.8%) while Team B's recent form shows simultaneous improvement across multiple attacking observables (shots rising from ~14.5 to ~23.6, shots_on_target rising from ~5.7 to ~7.2, possession rising from ~53% to ~63.4%). The joint co-movement of multiple observables in the same direction for both teams simultaneously — one deteriorating defensively, one improving offensively — is a multi-observable regime signal not captured by any single observable's recent vs long-run comparison.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism requires joint conditioning on three or more distinct observables (shots, shots_on_target, possession) for both teams simultaneously, testing a threshold/saturation structure. It is not reducible to any single observable's recent vs long-run comparison or any single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: In historical matches where the home team's goals-against second-half rate exceeds its first-half rate AND the away team's goals-for second-half rate exceeds its first-half rate, measure whether the total second-half goal count (and cards_2h as a proxy for match intensity/state) is elevated relative to matches where only one or neither of these half-asymmetries holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goals and cards_2h are jointly elevated when both teams simultaneously exhibit a second-half concentration in goals-against (home) and goals-for (away) — a compounding within-match half-state interaction that saturates beyond what either team's half-split alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half goals-against rate (long-run ~1.056 per match) substantially exceeds its first-half goals-against rate (~0.732), while Team B's second-half goals-for rate (~1.239) substantially exceeds its first-half goals-for rate (~0.662). The joint within-match half-level asymmetry — where one team's defensive vulnerability is concentrated in the second half and the other team's attacking output is also concentrated in the second half — creates a compounding within-match state interaction. This is distinct from either team's half-split in isolation and requires conditioning on both simultaneously.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two teams' half-level splits for two different observables (goals and cards_2h), testing a compounding within-match state interaction. It is not reducible to a single observable's half split or a single-band conditioning.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on both teams' shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR (all-prior and recent-5 windows) alongside each team's goals FOR rate, to measure whether the cross-team ratio of on-target accuracy (shots_on_target / shots) for the attacking side versus the defensive side's shots_on_target conceded rate produces a joint signal distinct from either observable alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total goals rise when both teams simultaneously show high shots_on_target-to-shots ratios FOR; total goals are suppressed when one or both teams show a low on-target ratio despite high shot volume, with the suppression stronger when the defending team also concedes few shots_on_target.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot-to-goal conversion efficiency (goals FOR relative to shots FOR) interacts with Team A's shots-on-target conceded rate: when one side generates high shot volume but the opponent suppresses on-target shots, the joint ratio of shots-on-target FOR versus shots FOR across both sides jointly predicts whether total goals rise or are suppressed relative to the competition baseline.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship across three distinct observables (shots, shots_on_target, goals) for both teams simultaneously. It cannot be reduced to a single observable mirror or a single observable with one coarse band — it is a cross-team, cross-observable ratio interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the cross-team possession differential (Team B all-prior minus recent-5 vs Team A all-prior minus recent-5) and jointly measure whether the team gaining recent possession also gains corners and shots proportionally, or whether those observables lag the possession shift.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent possession rises relative to its own long-run baseline while the opponent's falls, that team's corners FOR and shots FOR rise in tandem; the relationship is asymmetric — the possession-losing team's corners and shots fall more than the possession-gaining team's rise.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession profile has diverged sharply between its all-prior average (55.4% FOR) and its recent-5 average (46.6% FOR), while Team A's possession has moved in the opposite direction (48.5% all-prior vs 50.6% recent-5). The joint possession regime shift — where one team's recent possession drops while the opponent's rises — interacts with each team's corner-kick and shots production to determine whether the attacking output of the possession-gaining team rises proportionally or whether corners and shots remain anchored to the longer-run possession baseline.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship across three distinct observables (possession, corners, shots) and requires comparing two distinct time windows (all-prior vs recent-5) for both teams simultaneously, creating a cross-team, cross-window, cross-observable interaction not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on each team's first-half versus second-half corner FOR and AGAINST averages jointly, measuring whether the cross-team half-level corner differential (Team A's second-half corner surplus vs Team B's flat half-distribution) predicts a back-loaded total corner distribution in the match.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team shows a pronounced second-half corner surplus relative to its first-half rate and the opponent shows a flat half-distribution, total corners in the second half rise relative to the first half at a rate exceeding what either team's individual half-split would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production splits asymmetrically across halves (2.36 first half vs 2.57 second half FOR all-prior), while Team B's corner production is nearly equal across halves (2.24 first half vs 2.33 second half FOR all-prior). The within-match half-level corner distribution for each team, when considered jointly, tests whether the team with a stronger second-half corner tendency (Team A) compounds against the opponent's relatively flat half-distribution, producing a non-linear total-corners profile across the two halves of the match.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match half-level split applied jointly across both teams' corner FOR and AGAINST profiles simultaneously. It requires half-resolution data and a cross-team joint conditioning, not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's home fouls FOR and Team B's away fouls FOR, alongside Team A's home yellow cards FOR and Team B's away yellow cards FOR, to measure whether the cross-team venue-specific foul-to-card conversion ratio differs from the all-venue baseline for both teams simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the home team's foul rate is suppressed at home relative to its away rate, and the away team's foul rate is venue-neutral, the joint foul environment is lower than the all-venue average for both teams combined; yellow cards are suppressed in tandem, but the away team's card rate relative to its foul rate rises asymmetrically compared to the home team's.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's fouls committed are notably higher away (13.32) than at home (11.85), while Team B's fouls are nearly venue-neutral (11.74 away, 11.50 home). In this fixture Team A is home and Team B is away. The joint interaction of Team A's home foul suppression with Team B's venue-neutral foul rate — alongside each team's yellow-card rates by venue — tests whether the combined foul environment in this specific venue configuration produces a card total that diverges from what either team's all-venue foul or card average would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (fouls and yellow cards) across two different venue-specific splits for two different teams simultaneously, creating an asymmetric cross-team, cross-observable, cross-venue interaction not reducible to a single observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on each team's cards_2h FOR (second-half cards) and each team's goals FOR split by half (first-half vs second-half), measuring whether the team with a stronger second-half goal-scoring tendency also accumulates more second-half cards, and whether this relationship is asymmetric across the two teams.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The team with a higher second-half goal-scoring rate relative to its first-half rate accumulates more second-half cards; when both teams show second-half goal surpluses, total second-half cards rise above the competition baseline, with the effect stronger for the team whose second-half goal surplus is larger.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half cards (cards_2h FOR: 1.43) are notably higher than Team A's (cards_2h FOR: 1.13), while Team A's second-half cards conceded (1.27) are close to Team B's (1.28). The asymmetry between the two teams' second-half card accumulation rates — when jointly conditioned on each team's goals FOR split by half (Team B scores more in the first half: 0.71 vs 0.79 second half; Team A scores more in the second half: 0.56 first vs 0.85 second) — tests whether the team that tends to score more in the second half also accumulates more second-half cards as a function of match state pressure.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship across two distinct observables (cards_2h and goals) split by half for both teams simultaneously, with an asymmetric cross-team comparison. It requires half-resolution data and cannot be reduced to a single observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's recent-5 fouls FOR (16.8) substantially exceeds its all-prior average (13.457), while Team A's recent-5 fouls FOR (8.2) substantially undershoots its all-prior average (11.044). Measure whether this divergent joint foul-rate regime is associated with elevated second-half cards relative to competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half card volume rises when one side's foul rate is trending sharply upward while the opponent's is trending sharply downward, compared to matches where both sides' foul rates are near their long-run averages.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's foul rate has surged sharply in recent matches relative to its long-run average, while Team A's foul rate has dropped. The joint interaction of one team's rising foul production and the opponent's declining foul production — measured simultaneously — may predict elevated second-half card volume beyond what either team's card rate alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (fouls FOR for each team) simultaneously diverging in opposite directions from their own baselines — a two-observable, asymmetric cross-team interaction. It cannot be reduced to a single observable against one opponent-descriptor band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team B simultaneously exhibiting high fouls FOR (all-prior 13.457, recent 16.8) and low possession FOR (all-prior 43.786, recent 47.2, away 41.971) relative to competition baseline possession of 50. Measure whether the combination of high foul rate and low possession is associated with higher yellow card accumulation than high foul rate alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Yellow cards for a team rise more steeply when that team jointly exhibits both elevated foul rate and below-average possession, compared to when only one of those conditions holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B commits fouls at a high rate (all-prior and recent) while also operating with below-average possession. The joint relationship between a team's foul rate and its possession deficit — both measured for the same team — may predict elevated yellow cards for that team, beyond what either observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint two-observable relationship (fouls × possession) for the same team, not a single observable split by one band. The interaction between foul rate and possession share is structurally richer than any single-observable mirror or band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's home goals FOR substantially exceeds its away goals FOR, AND Team B's away goals FOR exceeds its home goals FOR. This is a two-team, two-venue-dimension interaction: both teams' venue asymmetries point in the same direction (favouring Team A at home, Team B as visitor). Measure whether this joint asymmetry pattern is associated with higher combined goal output than the competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Combined goals in a match rise when the home team has a pronounced home-scoring advantage AND the away team has a pronounced away-scoring advantage, compared to matches where venue asymmetries are weak or misaligned.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals FOR split strongly between home (2.314) and away (1.028), while Team B's goals FOR split shows the opposite pattern — slightly higher away (1.412) than home (1.250). The asymmetric venue-scoring profiles of the two teams, measured jointly, may predict a different combined goal environment than either team's overall average would suggest when they meet at Team A's home ground.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct teams' venue-scoring asymmetries — a two-team, two-observable-dimension interaction. It is not reducible to one team's home/away split in isolation, nor to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's recent offsides FOR is substantially below its all-prior average (0.8 vs 1.924), AND Team B's recent shots FOR (15.4) and shots-on-target FOR (5.2) substantially exceed their all-prior averages (11.943 and 4.429). Measure whether this cross-team divergence in attacking intensity indicators is associated with Team B generating more corners and shots against Team A than the long-run averages would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's corner and shot volume against Team A rises when Team A's offside trap activity is declining while Team B's shot volume is simultaneously trending upward, compared to matches where both are near their long-run averages.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides FOR has dropped sharply in recent matches (recent-5: 0.8 vs all-prior: 1.924) while Team B's shots and shots-on-target have surged in recent matches. The joint pattern of one team's attacking line becoming more conservative (fewer offsides) while the opponent's shot volume is rising may indicate a structural shift in the match's attacking balance, measurable through the cross-team interaction of offsides and shots.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship between two distinct observables (Team A offsides FOR and Team B shots FOR), neither of which is a mirror of the other. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A's second-half goals FOR being substantially higher than its first-half goals FOR, and (b) Team B's second-half goals FOR also exceeding its first-half goals FOR. Additionally, both teams' corner kicks show a second-half lean (Team A: 2H 2.586 vs 1H 2.229; Team B: 2H 2.493 vs 1H 2.174). Measure whether this joint second-half attacking intensification across both teams is associated with a higher proportion of total match goals occurring in the second half.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The share of match goals occurring in the second half rises when both teams simultaneously exhibit a structural second-half goal-scoring lean relative to their first-half rates, compared to matches where only one team or neither team shows this pattern.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals split strongly between first half (0.606) and second half (1.056), while Team B's goals also split between first half (0.543) and second half (0.786). The within-match temporal distribution of goals — specifically whether both teams' second-half goal rates jointly exceed their first-half rates — may predict a back-loaded goal distribution in the match, measurable at half resolution.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two teams' within-match half-level goal distributions simultaneously, and combining that with a second observable (corners) also showing a half-level split. It is a two-team, two-observable, within-match state interaction — not reducible to a single observable's half split for one team.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Measure the joint relationship between (shots FOR, shots_on_target FOR) as a pair across historical matches for Team A, conditioning on whether the ratio shots_on_target/shots is above or below its own long-run average, and test whether goals FOR co-varies with that ratio rather than with raw shot volume alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals FOR rises with the shots_on_target-to-shots ratio rather than with raw shots volume; when shot volume rises but the ratio falls, goal output is suppressed relative to what shot volume alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has risen sharply in recent matches while its shots-on-target rate has not kept pace, suggesting a divergence between shot quantity and shot quality that jointly conditions goal output differently from either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint two-observable relationship (shots AND shots_on_target together as a ratio) to condition goal output — not a single observable against one band. The engine's covered class handles each observable independently against opponent descriptors or venue, not the interaction between two distinct attacking-quality observables.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For Team B, measure the joint distribution of (shots FOR, shots_on_target FOR, goals FOR) across historical matches. Test whether matches where shots_on_target FOR is elevated relative to shots FOR (high on-target ratio) still produce suppressed goals, indicating a conversion-rate floor independent of volume.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's goals FOR is suppressed even when shots_on_target FOR is elevated, indicating a conversion inefficiency that persists across different shot-quality regimes and is not explained by either shots or shots_on_target alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots and shots_on_target have both risen markedly in recent matches while its long-run goals-for rate is low, suggesting a persistent conversion inefficiency that is jointly captured only by examining shots, shots_on_target, and goals together — not any single observable.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (shots_on_target and shots) to isolate conversion rate as a third dimension — not reducible to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Measure the joint relationship between Team B's fouls FOR (which generate free-kicks and pressure situations) and Team A's corner_kicks FOR across historical match pairs where both Team B foul rate is above its long-run mean AND Team A corner rate is above its long-run mean simultaneously, versus matches where only one condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total corner_kicks FOR Team A rises more when Team B's fouls FOR is simultaneously elevated than when either condition holds alone, indicating a super-additive joint effect on set-piece volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's foul rate has surged in recent matches while its corners-against rate has remained stable, but Team A's corner-generation rate has also surged recently — the joint interaction of Team B's high foul rate and Team A's elevated corner production may compound set-piece volume beyond what either observable predicts alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine two-observable joint conditioning across two different teams' metrics (Team B fouls × Team A corners), not a single observable split by one opponent band. The engine covers each observable against an opponent descriptor band, but not the interaction of two distinct observables from opposite sides.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team separately, compute the ratio of goals FOR in the second half versus first half across historical matches. Then test whether, in matches where Team A's second-half goal rate is above its own long-run first-half rate AND Team B's second-half goal rate is below its own long-run first-half rate simultaneously, the second half produces disproportionately more total goals than the first half.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total goals in the second half are elevated relative to the first half when Team A's structural second-half scoring uplift and Team B's structural second-half scoring suppression are both present — an asymmetric cross-team half-level interaction not visible in full-match totals.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half goal rate substantially exceeds its first-half goal rate, while Team B's second-half goal rate is lower than its first-half rate — this asymmetric within-match goal-timing profile across the two sides jointly conditions the half-level goal distribution in a way not captured by full-match averages.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires half-level resolution AND a cross-team asymmetric comparison of two different teams' within-match goal-timing profiles simultaneously. It is not a single observable split by venue or opponent band; it is a joint two-team, two-period conditioning.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Across historical matches, condition on the joint state where Team A possession FOR exceeds a threshold (above its own long-run mean) AND Team B fouls FOR exceeds a threshold (above its own long-run mean), and measure the resulting corner_kicks differential (Team A FOR minus Team B FOR) versus matches where only one or neither condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The corner_kicks differential in favour of Team A is amplified when Team A's possession dominance and Team B's elevated foul rate co-occur, compared to when either condition holds in isolation — a non-additive joint effect across three observables.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession dominance is structurally high (both long-run and recent), while Team B structurally operates with low possession — the joint interaction of Team A's high possession and Team B's elevated foul rate (recent surge) may jointly suppress Team B's corner generation while amplifying Team A's, creating an asymmetric corner differential that is not captured by either possession or fouls alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves three distinct observables (possession, fouls, corner_kicks) with a joint two-dimensional conditioning (possession threshold × foul-rate threshold), which is structurally richer than any single-observable split by one band. The asymmetric cross-team framing (Team A possession × Team B fouls → corner differential) is not covered by the engine's existing two-way splits.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compare Team A's ratio of shots_on_target FOR to shots FOR under ALL_PRIOR versus RECENT_5 windows. Team A's shots FOR rises from ~12.1 (ALL_PRIOR) to ~14.0 (RECENT_5) while shots_on_target FOR stays flat at ~4.0, implying the conversion ratio compresses as volume increases. Test whether this decoupling (rising shots, flat on-target) is a persistent joint pattern across historical matches.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: As Team A's shot volume rises above its season baseline, shots_on_target rises less than proportionally — the on-target ratio is suppressed when shot volume is elevated.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When Team A's shot volume rises in recent matches relative to its season average, its shots-on-target rate (shots_on_target / shots) does not rise proportionally, suggesting a saturation or decoupling between shot volume and shot quality that is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly tracking two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) and their ratio across two time windows; it cannot be reduced to either observable measured alone against a single band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Team A concedes 0.667 goals in the first half and 0.889 in the second half (ALL_PRIOR), a second-half uplift of ~33%. Simultaneously, shots against Team A have risen sharply in RECENT_5 (16.4 vs 12.5 season average). Condition on whether elevated shots-against co-occurs with the second-half goal-concession uplift being larger than the competition's own first-half/second-half split, using half-level goal data.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's shots-against volume is elevated above its season baseline, its second-half goal concession rate rises more than its first-half rate — the second-half defensive vulnerability is amplified jointly with shot-volume pressure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half goal concession rate is disproportionately higher than its first-half concession rate relative to the competition norm, and this asymmetry co-occurs with Team A conceding more shots in recent matches — suggesting a joint relationship between defensive shot-volume allowed and second-half goal vulnerability.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This combines two distinct observables (shots against and goals against) across two within-match periods (first half vs second half), requiring a joint cross-observable, cross-period conditioning that is not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Team B's yellow_cards FOR rises from ~2.19 (ALL_PRIOR) to ~3.0 (RECENT_5) while fouls FOR stays near its season average (~12.4 ALL_PRIOR vs ~12.0 RECENT_5). Simultaneously, Team A commits more fouls away (~14.1) than at home (~12.8). Jointly condition on both teams' foul rates and the card-per-foul conversion ratio to test whether elevated card rates emerge from foul volume, foul-to-card conversion, or their interaction.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's card-per-foul conversion rate rises in recent matches independently of foul volume, and this elevated conversion co-occurs with Team A's higher away-foul tendency — jointly predicting elevated total match card volume beyond what either team's foul rate alone would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's yellow card production has spiked sharply in recent matches relative to its season average, while its foul rate has not risen proportionally — suggesting a joint relationship between foul volume and card conversion rate (cards per foul) that may interact with Team A's elevated foul production away from home.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) for two different teams simultaneously, with a cross-team asymmetry (Team A away foul rate vs Team B card conversion), not reducible to either observable alone with a single band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Team B's possession FOR drops ~5 percentage points away vs home, while Team A's possession is stable across venues. Simultaneously, Team A's corners FOR are stable across venues (~4.78 home vs ~4.78 away) but Team B's corners FOR are also stable (~4.83 home vs ~4.77 away). Test whether the joint condition of Team B playing away (possession-suppressed) combined with Team A's corner production creates a measurable asymmetry in total corner volume relative to when Team B plays at home.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B plays away, its possession suppression is not accompanied by a proportional corner suppression, suggesting the possession-to-corner conversion relationship is non-linear and venue-asymmetric across the two teams jointly.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession advantage at home versus away is asymmetric: it holds ~51.6% at home but only ~46.2% away, while Team A's possession is nearly venue-invariant (~48.4% home, ~48.3% away). This creates a joint possession-venue interaction where the two teams' combined possession profiles shift substantially depending on which team is at home — and this possession shift may jointly co-vary with corner kick production differences across venues.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) across two teams simultaneously, with venue as a dimension that affects the two observables differently for each team — not reducible to one observable with one venue band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's goals FOR split by half (first vs second) and Team A's goals AGAINST split by half (first vs second). Both point in the same direction: second half favors Team B's attack and disfavors Team A's defense. Test whether this joint half-level alignment (attacker's second-half uplift meeting defender's second-half vulnerability) is a persistent pattern historically across matches with similar half-level profiles.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When an attacking team's second-half goal rate exceeds its first-half rate AND the defending team's second-half concession rate exceeds its first-half concession rate, total second-half goals in the match rise above what either team's individual half-level average would predict independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half goal scoring rate exceeds its first-half rate (~0.786 vs ~0.600), while Team A's second-half defensive record is weaker than its first-half record (~0.889 conceded vs ~0.667). This creates a joint cross-team, cross-half asymmetry: Team B's scoring profile peaks in the half where Team A's defensive profile is weakest — a structural alignment that is not captured by either team's half-level data in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two teams' goal observables simultaneously across two within-match periods, creating a cross-team, cross-half interaction that cannot be reduced to one team's observable with a single half-level band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning: Team A's possession FOR (recent vs. all-prior) crossed with Team B's shots AGAINST (recent vs. all-prior). Both dimensions must shift in the same direction (possession down for A, shots-allowed up for B) to activate the mechanism. Neither dimension alone constitutes the full condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's shot production rises relative to its possession-adjusted baseline when Team B's recent defensive permissiveness (shots allowed) is elevated above its season mean, even as Team A's own possession is suppressed — suggesting a non-linear interaction between possession share and opponent defensive openness on shot volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume (FOR) is jointly conditioned by its own possession share and the opponent's (Team B's) defensive shot-allowance rate. When Team A operates below its long-run possession average AND faces an opponent whose shots-allowed rate is elevated in recent matches relative to its season baseline, Team A's shot production diverges from what either observable alone would predict.
