mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct observables from two different teams (Team A possession FOR vs. Team B shots AGAINST), each compared across two time windows. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band, nor to a simple home/away or same-competition split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning on Team B's shots FOR (recent vs. all-prior uplift) AND Team A's shots_on_target AGAINST (recent vs. all-prior uplift). The mechanism activates when both observables show concurrent recent elevation — an asymmetric cross-team joint condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's recent shot volume is elevated above its season mean AND Team A's recent shots-on-target conceded is elevated above its season mean, Team B's shots-on-target FOR rises disproportionately relative to either team's standalone baseline — indicating a multiplicative rather than additive relationship between the two observables.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-on-target conversion efficiency (shots_on_target FOR relative to shots FOR) is asymmetrically related to Team A's shots-on-target concession rate. When Team B's recent shot volume has risen sharply above its season baseline while Team A's shots-on-target conceded has also risen recently, the joint signal on on-target quality diverges from what each team's individual baseline implies.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires a joint cross-team condition on two distinct observables (Team B shots FOR and Team A shots_on_target AGAINST), each evaluated across two time windows. Not reducible to a single observable mirror or a single coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning on Team B's fouls FOR (recent vs. all-prior: 15.4 vs. 12.6) AND Team A's fouls AGAINST (all-prior: 11.2, below competition mean of 12.8). The mechanism tests whether the asymmetry between one team's elevated foul-committing rate and the opponent's below-average foul-drawing rate predicts yellow card volume differently than either team's card baseline alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the committing team's recent foul rate is elevated above its season mean AND the receiving team's foul-drawing rate is below competition average, yellow card volume (and second-half card accumulation) rises above what either team's standalone card baseline would predict — reflecting a non-linear foul-rate-to-card conversion under asymmetric foul pressure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's foul rate (FOR) has risen sharply in recent matches above its season baseline, while Team A's fouls-against (conceded) rate is below the competition average. The joint relationship between Team B's elevated recent foul production and Team A's below-average foul-drawing rate creates a cross-observable condition on yellow card accumulation that neither team's card baseline alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (fouls FOR for one team, fouls AGAINST for the other) across two different teams, then linking to a third observable (yellow_cards / cards_2h). This is a three-observable cross-team joint relationship, not a single-observable mirror or band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning on: (a) Team A's corner_kicks FOR first-half vs. second-half split (2.48 vs. 2.14) and AGAINST first-half vs. second-half split (2.36 vs. 3.03); (b) Team B's corner_kicks FOR first-half vs. second-half split (2.48 vs. 2.41) and AGAINST first-half vs. second-half split (2.63 vs. 2.51). The mechanism tests whether the within-match temporal distribution of corners — specifically whether a team generates more corners in the second half than the first — interacts with the cross-team corner differential to predict total match corner volume beyond what full-match averages imply.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's corner production is back-loaded (second half > first half) and the opponent's corner concession is also back-loaded, total match corners rise above the sum of full-match averages — indicating a second-half amplification effect that is only visible when both the half-level split and the cross-team differential are considered jointly.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The within-match half-level split of corner kicks for both teams jointly reveals whether corner production is front-loaded (first half) or back-loaded (second half), and this intra-match distribution pattern interacts with each team's full-match corner differential (FOR minus AGAINST) to predict total corner volume in a way that the full-match average alone does not.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism requires simultaneously using half-level resolution (first vs. second half splits) for both teams' FOR and AGAINST corner rates, then crossing those four half-level values. It is not reducible to a single full-match observable with one coarse band, and the half-level split is a within-match state dimension not covered by the engine's existing two-way splits.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning on: Team A's goals FOR first-half vs. second-half (0.68 vs. 0.83) and AGAINST first-half vs. second-half (0.72 vs. 0.65); Team B's goals FOR first-half vs. second-half (0.57 vs. 0.80) and AGAINST first-half vs. second-half (0.62 vs. 0.78). The mechanism tests whether the alignment or misalignment of both teams' half-level goal-rate gradients (i.e., both teams scoring more in the second half) predicts second-half goal volume above what full-match averages imply.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams exhibit a positive first-to-second-half goal-rate gradient (more goals in second half than first) on both the FOR and AGAINST dimensions, second-half goal volume rises above the competition baseline and above what full-match averages would predict — a within-match state amplification visible only through the joint half-level split across both teams.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goal-scoring is asymmetrically distributed across halves (0.68 first half vs. 0.83 second half FOR; 0.72 first half vs. 0.65 second half AGAINST), while Team B's goal concession is also asymmetrically distributed (0.62 first half vs. 0.78 second half AGAINST). The joint cross-team half-level goal distribution — where both teams' second-half goal rates diverge from their first-half rates in the same direction — creates a within-match state condition on total goals that full-match averages obscure.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires simultaneously using half-level resolution for both teams' FOR and AGAINST goal rates (four half-level values), then testing their joint directional alignment. This is a within-match state condition crossed with a cross-team asymmetry — not reducible to a single full-match observable, a single coarse band, or the engine's existing two-way splits.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A holds below-average possession (consistent with their away-venue profile and Team B's possession dominance) AND Team A's foul rate is at or above competition average. Measure Team A yellow cards in that joint cell versus the marginal baselines.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A yellow cards rise when possession deficit and foul rate are jointly elevated, beyond the additive expectation from each observable separately.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession dominance (structurally higher than Team A and above competition baseline) combined with Team A's elevated foul rate against opponents jointly predicts a higher yellow-card accumulation for Team A, beyond what either observable alone would suggest. When a lower-possession team commits fouls at an above-average rate against a possession-dominant opponent, disciplinary pressure compounds.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint two-observable conditioning (possession deficit × foul rate) for Team A simultaneously, not a single observable against one coarse band. Neither possession alone nor fouls alone captures the compounding disciplinary mechanism.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Within matches, condition on Team A's full-match foul rate being above competition average AND measure whether cards_2h FOR Team A is disproportionately elevated relative to competition baseline cards_2h. The half-level split on cards_2h combined with full-match foul rate creates a within-match state dependency.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A second-half cards rise with higher full-match foul accumulation in a non-linear (threshold-like) fashion, with the relationship stronger for Team A than Team B given their asymmetric card profiles.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half card rate (cards_2h FOR) is structurally elevated relative to Team B's, and Team A concedes more fouls against them in recent matches. The joint relationship between Team A's first-half foul accumulation and their second-half card rate — conditioning on both observables simultaneously — tests whether early foul load predicts a non-linear escalation in second-half disciplinary events.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This combines a within-match period split (second-half cards) with a full-match continuous observable (fouls) for the same team, and tests an asymmetric cross-team comparison — not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B concedes a high shots volume (above their ALL_PRIOR mean) and measure whether corner kicks FOR Team A co-vary with that shots-against surge. The joint conditioning on shots-against volume AND shots-on-target-against ratio distinguishes volume-driven from quality-driven defensive pressure.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's shots-against volume is elevated relative to their shots-on-target-against (i.e., high volume but lower conversion to on-target), Team A's corner kick generation rises with shots volume but the relationship saturates as shots-on-target-against increases — indicating a non-linear joint dependency.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-against have surged sharply in recent matches (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) while their goals-against have also risen, yet their shots-on-target-against remain relatively stable. This divergence between shots-against volume and shots-on-target-against — a joint relationship between two distinct defensive observables — tests whether Team B's recent defensive deterioration is driven by volume conceded or by quality conceded, with implications for corner kick generation by Team A.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship between two distinct opponent-side defensive observables (shots-against and shots-on-target-against) and a third attacking observable (corners), not a single observable against one band. The recent-vs-prior divergence for Team B adds a regime-shift dimension.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint half-level profiles: Team A scores disproportionately in the second half (second-half goals FOR > first-half goals FOR) AND Team B concedes at a relatively even or slightly second-half-weighted rate. Measure whether total second-half goals in such matchups exceed the competition baseline second-half goal rate.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goal volume rises when a team with a strong second-half scoring skew (Team A) faces an opponent whose defensive half-split does not compensate — the joint half-level asymmetry compounds toward elevated second-half scoring.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals-for show a pronounced first-half vs second-half asymmetry (0.493 vs 0.920 per match), while Team B's goals-against show a first-half vs second-half asymmetry in the opposite direction (0.613 vs 0.653). The joint within-match half-level split across both teams' goal-timing profiles — conditioning on both simultaneously — tests whether the match's goal distribution is skewed toward the second half beyond what either team's individual half-split would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on both teams' within-match half-level goal splits — a two-dimensional within-match state dependency — not a single observable with one coarse band. The asymmetry is cross-team and cross-half, not reducible to either team's half-split alone.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B holds above-average possession (above competition baseline of 50%) AND measure Team A's offsides-for rate. Compare this joint cell against Team A's unconditional offside rate and against matches where possession is more balanced. The venue dimension (home) interacts with possession level as a second conditioning dimension.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's offside rate is suppressed when facing a possession-dominant opponent at home, with the suppression deepening as opponent possession rises above a threshold — a non-linear relationship between opponent possession level and the attacking team's offside frequency.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides-for are structurally lower at home than away (1.027 vs 1.559), while Team B's possession dominance (52.6% overall, 56.2% recent) suggests they will control territory. The joint relationship between Team B's possession level and Team A's offside rate — conditioning on both simultaneously — tests whether high-possession opponents suppress the attacking team's offside-triggering runs (a proxy for high-line attacking intent) in a non-linear way, with Team A's home offside rate already below their away rate suggesting a venue-possession interaction.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint conditioning on two distinct observables (opponent possession level as a continuous variable and Team A's offside production) with a non-linear/threshold dependence on possession, plus a venue interaction — not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint relationship: Team B's own shots-to-shots-on-target ratio (FOR) combined with Team A's shots-allowed-to-shots-on-target-allowed ratio (AGAINST). Both ratios must be computed simultaneously — neither alone captures the cross-team accuracy-suppression interaction.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the attacking team (B) has a low shots-on-target-per-shot ratio FOR and the defending team (A) allows a high shots volume but low shots-on-target AGAINST, the match-level shots_on_target FOR Team B is suppressed relative to what either team's individual shot or on-target baseline would predict independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot-volume-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR) is jointly considered alongside Team A's defensive shot-suppression profile (shots AGAINST vs shots_on_target AGAINST), to test whether a low-accuracy attacking side facing a team that concedes high shot volumes but few on-target shots produces a jointly suppressed on-target output relative to either team's individual baseline.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for two different sides simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable mirror or a single observable with one coarse band — it is an asymmetric cross-team ratio interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the half-level split for both teams simultaneously: Team A goals FOR first-half vs second-half, Team A goals AGAINST first-half vs second-half, Team B goals FOR first-half vs second-half, and Team B goals AGAINST first-half vs second-half. The interaction of both teams' half-level profiles — not either team's profile alone — determines which half is more goal-active.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A scores more in the second half and concedes more in the first half, while Team B concedes more in the second half, the second half is expected to carry a disproportionately higher share of combined goals relative to the first half, beyond what either team's individual half-split would suggest in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A exhibits a structural within-match goal-timing asymmetry (more goals FOR in the second half than first half, more goals AGAINST in the first half than second half), while Team B shows the opposite pattern (more goals AGAINST in the second half). The joint half-level goal-timing profiles of both teams interact to shape which half carries elevated combined goal activity.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) split applied jointly across both teams' FOR and AGAINST profiles simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one coarse band — it requires four half-level averages across two teams to be evaluated together as a joint structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (1) Team B's structural low-possession profile (FOR all-prior and recent) combined with (2) Team A's recent possession uplift relative to its own long-run average, and (3) each team's corner-kick FOR and AGAINST rates. The mechanism tests whether the possession-asymmetry regime predicts a corner-kick imbalance beyond what each team's corner baseline alone captures.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team (B) structurally cedes possession and the other (A) is in a recent possession-gaining regime, the corner-kick differential (A FOR minus B FOR) rises above what either team's standalone corner average would predict, because territorial dominance compounds across both dimensions simultaneously.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B operates with a persistent low-possession identity (well below 50% both all-prior and recent), while Team A has recently shifted toward above-50% possession after a long-run below-50% average. The joint condition of one team structurally ceding possession and the other team in a possession-gaining regime interacts with corner-kick production, since corners are partly driven by territorial dominance.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) across both teams. It is not a single observable mirror or a single observable with one band — it requires the possession-regime interaction to be evaluated alongside corner production for both sides.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (1) Team A's recent yellow-card FOR uplift vs its long-run average, (2) Team B's away yellow-card FOR rate vs its home rate, and (3) the competition's second-half cards_2h baseline. The mechanism tests whether the combination of both teams' elevated card propensity predicts above-baseline second-half card volume beyond what either team's individual card rate or the competition baseline alone would indicate.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams simultaneously exhibit elevated yellow-card propensity (one via recent uplift, the other via away-venue elevation), second-half card volume rises above the competition baseline in a manner that is amplified relative to either team's individual card rate considered in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent (last 5) yellow-card rate FOR has risen sharply above its long-run average, while Team B's yellow-card rate FOR (away) is also elevated relative to its home rate. The joint condition of both teams showing elevated recent card propensity — combined with the competition's second-half card context (cards_2h) — tests whether the second-half card volume is amplified when both teams enter with elevated disciplinary pressure simultaneously.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (yellow_cards and cards_2h) across both teams and a within-match period (second half), while also incorporating the recent-vs-long-run regime shift for one team and the venue-split for the other. No single observable with one band captures this three-way interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the half-level split for both teams simultaneously: Team A corners FOR first-half vs second-half, and Team B corners AGAINST first-half vs second-half. The mechanism tests whether the alignment of Team A's second-half corner surge with Team B's second-half corner-concession tendency produces a compounded second-half corner imbalance.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the home team (A) generates more corners in the second half than the first, and the away team (B) concedes more corners in the second half than the first, the second half carries a disproportionately higher share of total match corners relative to the first half — beyond what either team's individual half-split would predict alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production has a pronounced half-level asymmetry (more corners FOR in the second half than first half), while Team B's corner-kick concession also has a half-level asymmetry (more corners AGAINST in the second half). The joint half-level corner profiles of both teams interact to determine whether the second half carries a disproportionate share of total corner volume in this fixture.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) split applied jointly across both teams' FOR and AGAINST corner profiles. It is not a single observable with one coarse band — it requires the half-level asymmetries of both teams to be evaluated together as a joint structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where the away team (Team B) holds possession above the competition neutral mean AND the home team (Team A) produces shots below the competition neutral mean. Measure Team A's corner-kick output in matches satisfying both conditions simultaneously, versus matches where only one or neither condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A corner-kick output is suppressed when Team B possession is elevated AND Team A shots are simultaneously below the competition baseline, relative to matches where only one of these conditions is met.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession dominance (structurally above 50%) combined with Team A's below-average shots-for rate jointly predicts a suppressed corner-kick output for Team A, because high-possession opponents limit Team A's attacking sequences that generate corners, while Team A's own low shot volume reflects constrained attacking access.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint intersection of two distinct observables (possession for Team B and shots for Team A) to define the conditioning state. Neither observable alone, nor each split independently against a single band, captures the interaction. The engine's covered class handles each observable with at most one simple band, not the cross-observable joint condition.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's shots-on-target FOR exceeds the competition neutral mean AND Team A's shots-on-target AGAINST exceeds Team A's own all-prior average. Measure Team B corner-kick output under this joint condition versus when only one condition is met.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B corner-kick output rises when Team B's shots-on-target production is simultaneously elevated and Team A's shots-on-target concession rate is also elevated, compared to matches where only one of these conditions holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetric relationship between Team B's shots-on-target production and Team A's shots-on-target concession jointly determines the corner-kick differential in the match. Team B generates shots-on-target well above the competition mean while Team A concedes shots-on-target well above its own average, suggesting that when both sides' shot-quality asymmetry is simultaneously elevated, corner-kick volume for Team B rises disproportionately.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team relationship: it uses Team B's offensive observable (shots-on-target FOR) jointly with Team A's defensive observable (shots-on-target AGAINST) to condition corner output. This cross-team, cross-perspective joint condition is not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compare Team A's first-half corner-kick average against Team A's second-half corner-kick average, and simultaneously compare Team B's first-half corner-kick average against Team B's second-half corner-kick average. Identify matches where Team A's first-half corner share is above its own half-split norm while Team B's second-half corner share is above its own half-split norm, and measure total corner output in those matches.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total match corner volume is higher in matches where Team A's first-half corner share and Team B's second-half corner share are both elevated relative to their respective half-split norms, compared to matches where the half-level distributions are more uniform.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's first-half corner-kick production relative to its second-half corner-kick production reveals a within-match distributional shift: Team A generates more corners in the first half than the second half on average, while Team B generates more corners in the second half than the first half. This half-level asymmetry between the two teams' corner-kick timing profiles is a within-match state structure that conditions total corner output differently across halves.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism requires simultaneously conditioning on within-match half-level splits for both teams on the same observable, comparing the half-level distributional asymmetry across the two sides. The covered class handles a single observable's recent vs. long-run level or a single half split for one team, not the joint half-level profile comparison across both teams.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's fouls FOR exceeds the competition neutral mean AND Team B's yellow cards FOR exceeds the competition neutral mean. Measure the combined second-half cards (cards_2h FOR + cards_2h AGAINST for Team A, equivalently Team B's cards_2h) under this joint condition versus when only one condition is met.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half card volume rises when both Team A's foul production and Team B's yellow-card accumulation are simultaneously above the competition baseline, compared to matches where only one of these conditions holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between Team A's foul rate and Team B's yellow-card accumulation rate captures a disciplinary interaction: Team A commits fouls at an above-competition-average rate (especially away, where it is highest), while Team B accumulates yellow cards at a rate above the competition mean. When a high-fouling team faces a high-card-accumulating opponent, the second-half card volume (cards_2h) for both teams is jointly elevated beyond what either team's individual card rate would predict alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint intersection of two distinct observables (fouls for one team and yellow cards for the other) to condition a third observable (cards_2h). No single-observable-with-one-band split captures this cross-observable, cross-team interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compare Team B's first-half goals-for average against Team B's second-half goals-for average, and simultaneously compare Team A's first-half goals-against average against Team A's second-half goals-against average. Identify matches where Team B's first-half goal share is above its own half-split norm while Team A's second-half concession share is above its own half-split norm, and measure the half-level goal distribution in those matches.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The proportion of total match goals occurring in the first half is higher when Team B's first-half scoring share is elevated and Team A's second-half concession share is also elevated simultaneously, compared to matches where the half-level profiles are more uniform.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals-against first-half rate relative to its goals-against second-half rate, combined with Team B's goals-for first-half rate relative to its goals-for second-half rate, reveals a within-match scoring timing asymmetry. Team B scores more goals in the first half than the second half on average, while Team A concedes more in the second half than the first half. The joint half-level mismatch between Team B's scoring timing profile and Team A's concession timing profile conditions when goals are most likely to occur within the match.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism requires jointly conditioning on within-match half-level splits for both teams on the same observable (goals), comparing the half-level distributional asymmetry across the two sides' offensive and defensive profiles. The covered class handles a single observable's half split for one team, not the joint half-level profile comparison across both teams' offensive and defensive perspectives.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint relationship between Team A's shots FOR (recent-5 vs all-prior) and goals FOR (recent-5 vs all-prior), cross-referenced with shots_on_target FOR (recent-5 vs all-prior). The mechanism asks whether a large positive divergence in shots is accompanied by a proportional divergence in goals and shots_on_target, or whether the shot surge is decoupled from on-target and scoring output.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shots FOR rises sharply in recent matches relative to the long-run mean, goals FOR and shots_on_target FOR are expected to rise proportionally; if shots rise but shots_on_target and goals do not, the shot surge is suppressed in quality — a non-linear joint relationship between volume and quality observables.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has surged in recent matches while its conversion rate (goals per shot) has not kept pace, suggesting a divergence between shot production and scoring efficiency. Jointly tracking Team A's shots FOR and goals FOR across the all-prior versus recent-5 windows reveals whether elevated shot counts translate into goals or represent a low-conversion regime.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly comparing two distinct observables (shots and goals, with shots_on_target as a third) across two time windows simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band; it tests the joint co-movement (or divergence) of multiple observables across windows.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's shots_on_target FOR (recent-5) is below its all-prior mean AND Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST (recent-5) is above its all-prior mean, while simultaneously Team A is playing at home (where its shots_on_target FOR is higher than away). The mechanism tests whether this asymmetric cross-team, cross-observable configuration is associated with a widened shots_on_target differential.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's recent shots_on_target FOR declines and shots_on_target AGAINST rises simultaneously, and Team A holds a home shots_on_target advantage, the combined shots_on_target differential in Team A's favour is expected to be wider than either team's individual observable alone would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B exhibits a divergence between its shots_on_target FOR (declining in recent matches) and shots_on_target AGAINST (rising in recent matches), while its goals FOR has also declined recently. Jointly, this asymmetric cross-observable pattern — Team B generating fewer quality chances while conceding more — may interact with Team A's home shot advantage to produce a structurally skewed shot-on-target differential.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves an asymmetric joint relationship across different observables for the two sides (Team A's home shots_on_target FOR vs Team B's recent shots_on_target FOR and AGAINST), which cannot be reduced to a single observable mirror or a single team's observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A's possession FOR being structurally below 50% (both all-prior and recent-5), while simultaneously measuring whether Team A's corner_kicks FOR and shots FOR meet or exceed competition-context norms. The mechanism tests the joint relationship: does low possession suppress corner and shot production, or are they decoupled?
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: For teams with chronic possession deficits, corner_kicks FOR and shots FOR are expected to be suppressed relative to competition norms; if they are not suppressed (or are elevated), this represents a decoupling — a non-linear joint relationship where possession level does not predict attacking volume observables in the usual direction.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A operates in a low-possession regime (chronically below 50%) but generates corners and shots at or above competition-context norms. This joint pattern — low possession combined with above-average attacking set-piece and shot production — tests whether possession deficit is decoupled from corner and shot output for this team, representing a non-standard joint relationship between a control observable and volume observables.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly comparing two distinct observables (possession and corners/shots) against a competition baseline simultaneously. It is not a single-observable mirror or a single observable with one band; it tests whether the joint state of two observables diverges from the expected co-movement.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint within-match state: Team A's goals AGAINST in the second half exceeds goals AGAINST in the first half (all-prior), AND Team B's goals FOR in the second half is at or above goals FOR in the first half (all-prior). The mechanism tests whether this aligned half-level asymmetry across both teams predicts a second-half-skewed goal distribution.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A concedes more in the second half and Team B scores more in the second half, the second half is expected to be more goal-productive than the first half for this fixture, representing a within-match state dependence that rises with the second-half period.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals conceded split between first and second halves reveals a back-loaded defensive vulnerability (more goals conceded in the second half than the first), while Team B's goals scored split shows a similar back-loading (more goals scored in the second half). The joint within-match state — both teams' half-level goal patterns aligning in the same direction — tests whether the second half is structurally more goal-productive for this fixture configuration.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a half-level split (within-match state) jointly across both teams' goal observables (Team A AGAINST and Team B FOR), which is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band. It combines two distinct team-role perspectives at half resolution.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state: Team A's fouls FOR exceeds fouls AGAINST (all-prior and recent-5), Team A's possession FOR is structurally below 50%, and Team B's possession is near-neutral. The mechanism tests whether the combination of high foul-committing and low possession (a two-dimensional conditioning) is associated with elevated second-half card accumulation, beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team commits more fouls than it receives AND operates in a low-possession regime, its second-half card rate is expected to rise relative to competition norms, with the joint condition producing a stronger association than either foul rate or possession deficit alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Cards in the second half (cards_2h) can be jointly examined against the fouls FOR and possession patterns of both teams. Team A commits more fouls than it receives (higher fouls FOR than fouls AGAINST), while Team B also commits fouls at a moderate rate. The joint relationship between a team's foul-committing tendency and its second-half card accumulation — conditioned on the possession imbalance (Team A low possession, Team B near-neutral) — tests whether foul volume under possession deficit predicts elevated second-half card rates.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (foul-committing tendency AND possession level) to condition the second-half card outcome. It is not reducible to a single observable with one band; it tests a two-dimensional joint conditioning on cards_2h.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute Team A's shots_on_target:FOR / shots:FOR (shot accuracy FOR) and Team B's shots_on_target:AGAINST / shots:AGAINST (shot accuracy AGAINST), then jointly condition on both ratios simultaneously — not either ratio alone — to assess combined on-target volume. Team A's recent shot accuracy (shots_on_target:FOR:RECENT_5 = 2.6 vs ALL_PRIOR = 3.706 on 8.0 shots vs 9.594) signals a deteriorating conversion rate, while Team B allows shots_on_target:AGAINST near its long-run mean (5.0 recent vs 4.871 all-prior). The joint cross-team accuracy interaction is the conditioning logic.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's shot accuracy ratio is suppressed relative to its long-run level AND Team B's shots-on-target-allowed ratio is stable, combined match shots_on_target rises less than the sum of individual team baselines would suggest — i.e. the joint ratio product is lower than the product of independent baselines.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shot accuracy) jointly with Team B's shots-against-to-shots-on-target-against ratio (defensive shot quality allowed) determines the combined on-target shot volume in the match. When one side produces many shots but few on target while the opponent allows a high proportion of shots on target, the joint interaction produces a different on-target total than either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly combining two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) across two different team perspectives (Team A FOR and Team B AGAINST) as a ratio-of-ratios interaction. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band; it is a cross-team, cross-observable joint relationship.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Team A's possession:FOR all-prior is 44.5% (recent 38%), meaning it structurally cedes possession at home. Team B's shots:FOR:HOME = 12.278 vs shots:FOR:AWAY = 9.5 — a meaningful home-venue uplift for Team B even as the away team. Condition jointly on (a) Team A's possession deficit relative to competition baseline (50%) and (b) Team B's home-vs-away shot volume asymmetry to assess whether corner_kicks:AGAINST for Team A rises beyond what either variable alone predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's possession is suppressed below competition baseline AND Team B's shot volume is elevated relative to its own away average, Team A's corners conceded rises above what Team A's corners-against baseline or Team B's corners-for baseline individually imply — the joint condition amplifies corner concession.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession deficit (structurally low possession FOR, high possession AGAINST) combined with Team B's asymmetric venue-split in shots (much higher shots at home than away) jointly shapes the corner-kick imbalance. When a low-possession team hosts a side that generates significantly more shots at home than away, the corner-kick differential is driven by the interaction of possession dominance and venue-conditioned shot volume — not by either dimension alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves three distinct observables (possession, shots, corner_kicks) and two simultaneous conditioning dimensions (possession deficit AND venue-split shot asymmetry). It is not reducible to a single observable with one band, nor to a simple home/away split of one observable.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Team A concedes 0.435 goals in the first half and 0.826 in the second half (all-prior), a ratio of approximately 1:1.9 — heavily back-loaded. Team B scores 0.629 in the first half and 0.786 in the second half. Condition jointly on both teams' half-level splits simultaneously: when Team A's second-half concession rate is disproportionately elevated relative to its first-half rate AND Team B's second-half scoring rate exceeds its first-half rate, the second half is structurally more dangerous than full-match averages indicate.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's goals-against second-half rate substantially exceeds its first-half rate AND Team B's goals-for second-half rate exceeds its first-half rate, goals in the second half of this fixture rise relative to what the full-match average and competition baseline would predict — the two half-splits interact to amplify second-half goal volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The within-match half-level goal distribution asymmetry — specifically whether Team A's second-half goal concession rate is disproportionately higher than its first-half rate relative to Team B's own half-level goal-scoring split — identifies a structural second-half vulnerability that is not captured by full-match goal averages alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) split applied jointly across two teams' asymmetric half distributions for the same observable. It requires simultaneously conditioning on both Team A's half-split concession asymmetry and Team B's half-split scoring asymmetry — not a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint recent-vs-all-prior drift of two observables simultaneously for Team A: possession:FOR:RECENT_5 (38.0) vs ALL_PRIOR (44.5) AND corner_kicks:FOR:RECENT_5 (1.2) vs ALL_PRIOR (3.826). Both observables have drifted downward together in the recent window. Test whether this co-suppression regime predicts further suppression of Team A's attacking output (corners, shots) beyond what either single-observable recent drift would indicate.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both Team A's possession and corner-kick production are jointly suppressed in the recent window relative to their long-run levels, Team A's attacking output metrics (corners, shots) in the target match are further suppressed than either single-observable recent drift alone would predict — the joint co-movement amplifies the signal.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent-form possession collapse (recent-5 possession FOR = 38% vs all-prior 44.5%) combined with its simultaneous recent-form corner-kick production collapse (recent-5 corners FOR = 1.2 vs all-prior 3.826) represents a joint regime shift across two observables. The co-movement of both possession and corners into suppressed territory in recent matches — beyond what either trend alone signals — identifies a structural attacking output deterioration.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint two-observable recent-vs-long-run drift comparison (possession AND corners simultaneously), not a single observable's recent level versus its longer-run level. The co-movement of two distinct observables into the same suppressed regime is the novel structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Team A: fouls:FOR all-prior = 13.188, yellow_cards:FOR all-prior = 1.696 (ratio ~7.8 fouls/card). Team B: fouls:FOR all-prior = 11.574, yellow_cards:FOR all-prior = 1.543 (ratio ~7.5 fouls/card). Both teams have cards_2h:FOR around 1.1-1.25, meaning cards concentrate in the second half. Condition jointly on (a) the cross-team asymmetry in foul-to-card ratios and (b) the second-half card concentration for both teams to assess whether total yellow cards and second-half cards are jointly elevated when fouls are high but first-half card issuance is suppressed.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams exhibit high foul rates relative to their yellow card rates (high foul-to-card ratio) AND both teams show cards_2h concentration above competition baseline, total yellow cards and second-half cards rise together — the joint foul-volume and half-concentration interaction predicts a back-loaded disciplinary match beyond what either observable alone signals.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetric foul-to-yellow-card conversion relationship between the two teams — where Team A commits more fouls per yellow card than Team B — combined with the second-half cards concentration (cards_2h) identifies whether the match's disciplinary volume is driven by a high-foul/low-card regime in the first half followed by a card-concentrated second half, rather than a uniform distribution across the match.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly combining three distinct observables (fouls, yellow_cards, cards_2h) across both teams, with a within-match half-level conditioning on cards_2h. It is not reducible to any single observable with one band, and the foul-to-card ratio is an asymmetric cross-observable relationship not covered by the engine's existing class.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Measure matches where the home team holds possession above a continuous threshold (not a coarse band) and jointly examine how corner differential behaves as possession rises — specifically whether corner differential saturates or continues to rise linearly with possession share, using Team A's possession FOR and Team B's corners AGAINST as the two dimensions simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner differential in favour of Team A rises with possession advantage up to a threshold, then saturates — i.e. a non-linear (threshold/saturation) relationship between possession share and corner differential rather than a simple linear one.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A dominates possession and generates corners at a high rate, while Team B concedes corners at a high rate and holds low possession. The joint relationship between Team A's possession advantage and the combined corner differential (Team A FOR minus Team B FOR) may be structurally different from what either observable alone predicts, because possession dominance and corner generation are distinct processes that can reinforce or decouple depending on how a low-possession team defends.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly modelling two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) across both teams simultaneously, and tests for a non-linear/saturation shape in the relationship — neither of which is covered by any single-observable mirror, single-band split, or simple home/away contrast.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner data by half for both teams simultaneously: measure Team A corners FOR in H1 vs H2 jointly with Team B corners AGAINST in H1 vs H2. The conditioning is on half (H1 vs H2) applied to both sides at once, not just one team's single observable.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second-half corner differential (Team A FOR minus Team B FOR) is higher than the first-half corner differential, and this asymmetric half-level shift is larger than what either team's individual half split would suggest in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A generates more corners in the second half than the first half (2.059 vs 2.338), while Team B concedes more corners in the second half than the first half (2.761 vs 3.284). The joint within-match half-level profile of corner generation FOR Team A and corner concession AGAINST Team B — measured simultaneously across both halves — may reveal a compounding second-half corner pressure that is not captured by full-match averages alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) split applied jointly to two teams' asymmetric observables simultaneously — not a single observable with one coarse band. The joint half-profile across both sides is structurally richer than any single-team half split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on both the shots volume and the shots-on-target volume for each team, comparing the all-prior ratio against the recent-5 ratio. The mechanism tests whether the regime shift (recent vs all-prior) in shots-on-target fraction is asymmetric across the two teams — rising for Team A and falling for Team B simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent shots volume rises while shots-on-target fraction also rises (Team A), and the opponent's recent shots volume falls while shots-on-target fraction also falls (Team B), the combined on-target shot differential is amplified beyond what either team's individual recent trend would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent shot volume has surged (10.7 all-prior to 13.2 recent) while its shots-on-target rate has also risen, yet Team B's recent shot volume has dropped sharply (9.6 all-prior to 7.4 recent) with shots-on-target also declining. The joint relationship between each team's shots-to-shots-on-target ratio (a conversion quality proxy) and the direction of recent regime shift — rising for Team A, falling for Team B — represents an asymmetric cross-team pattern across two distinct observables.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) jointly, applied asymmetrically across both teams, and tests a regime-shift pattern (recent vs all-prior) in the ratio of the two — not a single observable with one band or a simple recent-vs-long-run comparison of one metric.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on full-match foul rate and second-half card rate for each team. Measure whether the ratio of second-half cards to full-match fouls differs systematically between the higher-fouling team (Team B) and the lower-fouling team (Team A), and whether this ratio is stable or shifts in the recent window.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The team with the higher foul rate (Team B) accumulates second-half cards at a disproportionately higher rate relative to its foul volume than the lower-fouling team (Team A), and this joint foul-to-card ratio is not captured by either observable's individual trend.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A commits fouls at a rate that has dropped recently (12.9 all-prior to 12.2 recent) while Team B commits fouls at a stable high rate (13.25 all-prior, 13.2 recent). Both teams have second-half card data available. The joint relationship between a team's foul rate and its second-half card accumulation — measured across both teams simultaneously — tests whether the team with the higher foul rate (Team B) disproportionately accumulates second-half cards relative to its foul volume compared to Team A.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and cards_2h/yellow_cards) applied asymmetrically across both teams, testing a ratio relationship — not a single observable with one band or a simple mirror comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on possession FOR and offsides FOR for each team, and also on offsides AGAINST for Team A. Measure whether, in matches where one team holds possession well above its opponent, the lower-possession team's offside count rises non-linearly — and whether Team B's recent possession drop (from 44.6 to 34.8) corresponds to a shift in its offside generation pattern.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: As the possession gap between teams widens (Team A increasingly dominant), the lower-possession team's (Team B's) offside count rises — reflecting increased desperation in forward runs — while the higher-possession team's offside count remains suppressed; this joint cross-team relationship is non-linear with respect to the possession gap.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A holds high possession (~57% all-prior, 60% recent) and generates very few offsides (1.6 FOR), while Team B plays with low possession (~45% all-prior, 35% recent) and generates more offsides (2.67 FOR all-prior). Simultaneously, Team A concedes many offsides against it (4.79 AGAINST), suggesting opponents run high-line traps against Team A. The joint relationship between possession share and offside generation — across both teams simultaneously — tests whether the low-possession team (Team B) is more exposed to an offside trap when facing a high-possession opponent, and whether Team B's recent possession collapse amplifies this exposure.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (possession and offsides) applied jointly and asymmetrically across both teams, with a non-linear/threshold dependence on the possession gap — not reducible to any single-observable mirror, single-band split, or simple recent-vs-long-run comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's RECENT_5 shots FOR is elevated relative to its ALL_PRIOR shots FOR, AND Team B's ALL_PRIOR shots AGAINST exceeds the competition context shots mean. Within that joint condition, measure whether Team A's shots_on_target FOR rate (shots_on_target / shots) is higher than its unconditional long-run rate.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's shots-on-target conversion rate rises when its own recent shot volume is elevated AND the opponent structurally concedes above-average shots
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent surge in shots (FOR, RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) combined with Team B's structural inability to suppress shots allowed (AGAINST, ALL_PRIOR vs competition context) jointly predict whether Team A's shots-on-target rate (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR) rises above its own long-run conversion rate. The joint condition — one team's recent volume uplift meeting the other team's chronic defensive permissiveness — is richer than either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint condition across two distinct observables (shots volume trend for Team A AND shots-allowed level for Team B relative to competition context), which cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band. It also combines a recent-vs-long-run regime signal for one team with a cross-team opponent-descriptor dimension.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's RECENT_5 goals FOR and shots_on_target FOR are both above their ALL_PRIOR means, while simultaneously Team A's RECENT_5 goals AGAINST is below its ALL_PRIOR mean. Measure whether total match goals in this joint regime differs from the unconditional competition-context mean.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total match goals are suppressed relative to the competition context mean when Team A's recent defensive tightening and Team B's recent attacking uplift are simultaneously present, because the two forces partially offset each other — the relationship is non-additive and asymmetric across the two teams
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's recent offensive uplift (goals FOR and shots_on_target FOR both elevated in RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) interacts asymmetrically with Team A's defensive record: Team A concedes fewer goals recently (AGAINST RECENT_5 below ALL_PRIOR) while Team B's goals-against has risen recently. This asymmetric cross-observable divergence — one team's attack trending up while the other's defence is also trending tighter — jointly shapes the expected goals environment beyond what either team's single-observable trend captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct observables (goals and shots_on_target) across two teams in opposing directions — an asymmetric cross-team joint condition that cannot be expressed as a single observable with one band or a simple home/away split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each historical match, compute each team's corners-per-possession-unit ratio. Condition on matches where Team A's ratio is in an elevated regime (RECENT_5 corners FOR elevated vs ALL_PRIOR, possession stable) while Team B's ratio is in a suppressed regime (RECENT_5 corners FOR below ALL_PRIOR). Measure whether total match corners deviates from the competition context mean under this joint cross-team condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total match corners rises above the competition context mean when one team's corners-per-possession ratio is in an elevated regime and the opponent's is simultaneously in a suppressed regime, because the dominant team's set-piece generation is not offset by the opponent
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between a team's possession share and its corner-kick production is tested across both teams simultaneously: Team A holds above-average possession (FOR ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5 both above 50) and its corner-kick FOR RECENT_5 is markedly elevated above its ALL_PRIOR, while Team B's corner-kick FOR RECENT_5 is markedly below its ALL_PRIOR despite similar possession levels. This cross-team divergence in the possession-to-corners conversion ratio — not just each team's corners in isolation — is the mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable (possession AND corner_kicks) relationship measured simultaneously across both teams, requiring a ratio construct and a cross-team asymmetric conditioning — not reducible to either team's corners alone with a single band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state of: (a) both teams' fouls FOR ALL_PRIOR relative to competition context fouls mean, and (b) each team's first-half vs second-half goals FOR split (whether a team is a second-half scoring team). Measure whether cards_2h FOR each team is elevated above the competition context cards_2h mean when fouls are above average AND the team is chasing a second-half deficit (goals AGAINST 1H > goals AGAINST 2H pattern).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half cards rise above the competition context mean when both teams commit fouls at above-average rates AND the within-match half-level goal distribution creates a second-half chasing dynamic for at least one team
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Second-half card accumulation (cards_2h) is jointly shaped by both teams' foul-committing tendencies AND the within-match half-level goal distribution. Team A concedes more goals in the first half than the second half (goals AGAINST: 0.563 1H vs 0.690 2H reversed — actually Team A concedes more in 2H), while Team B scores more in the second half (goals FOR: 0.648 2H vs 0.648 1H equal, but goals AGAINST 2H 0.535 vs 1H 0.676). The joint condition of foul rates for both teams combined with the half-level goal-scoring asymmetry determines whether second-half cards are elevated above the competition context cards_2h mean.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (fouls and goals) AND a within-match half-level split on goals — a three-dimensional conditioning structure (fouls level × half-level goal asymmetry × cards_2h) that is not reducible to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's offsides FOR RECENT_5 is substantially above both its ALL_PRIOR and the competition context mean, while Team A's offsides AGAINST RECENT_5 is below its ALL_PRIOR (indicating Team A's defence is successfully catching Team B's runs). Within this joint condition, measure whether Team B's shots_on_target FOR is suppressed relative to its RECENT_5 uplift, despite elevated possession.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's shots_on_target FOR is suppressed relative to its recent uplift when its offsides FOR is in an elevated regime AND the opponent's offsides AGAINST is simultaneously in a declining regime — the two signals jointly indicate a structural mismatch that limits attacking efficiency beyond what either observable alone predicts
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's offsides FOR has surged in RECENT_5 (3.8) well above its ALL_PRIOR mean (2.074) and above the competition context (1.931), while Team A's offsides AGAINST has declined in RECENT_5 (1.4) below its ALL_PRIOR (2.1). This cross-observable, cross-team divergence — one team's attacking line pushing higher (more offsides) while the opponent's defensive line is conceding fewer offsides — jointly determines whether Team B's shots and shots_on_target FOR are suppressed relative to their recent uplift, because a high-line attack caught offside repeatedly does not convert possession into shots.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires a joint condition across two distinct observables (offsides and shots_on_target) measured asymmetrically across both teams, combined with a recent-vs-long-run regime comparison for both — a four-dimensional structure not reducible to any single observable with one band or a simple venue/competition split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A's recent-5 shots FOR vs. its all-prior shots FOR, (b) Team A's recent-5 shots AGAINST vs. its all-prior shots AGAINST, (c) Team B's recent-5 shots FOR vs. its all-prior shots FOR, and (d) Team B's recent-5 shots AGAINST vs. its all-prior shots AGAINST — all four drift directions evaluated simultaneously rather than any single observable in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams simultaneously show a recent-form drift where one team's attack is declining and the other's is rising, total shots and shots-on-target in the match are suppressed relative to the sum of season averages, because the attacking surge of one side is offset by the defensive deterioration of the other — the net effect is non-additive and depends on the joint configuration.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has declined sharply in recent matches while shots conceded have risen, and simultaneously Team B's shot volume has surged recently while shots conceded have also risen — the joint recent-form divergence across both teams' attacking and defensive shot profiles interacts to shape the total shots environment beyond what either team's season average alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires evaluating four distinct recent-vs-season drift signals across two teams and two perspectives (FOR/AGAINST) simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band; it is a joint four-dimensional drift interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's fouls FOR (both all-prior and recent-5) substantially exceed the competition average, while Team B's fouls AGAINST (all-prior and recent-5) are well below the competition average — i.e., one team is a high fouler meeting an opponent that structurally avoids drawing fouls. Evaluate how this asymmetric cross-team foul pairing relates to second-half card totals.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a high-fouling team (Team A) faces an opponent that structurally draws few fouls (Team B), the second-half card volume rises relative to the competition baseline, because the fouling team's discipline deteriorates under accumulated pressure without the natural foul-drawing friction that would otherwise distribute cards more evenly across both sides.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's foul rate is structurally high (both season-long and recent) while Team B concedes very few fouls against it — the asymmetric foul-production profile across the two sides jointly conditions the second-half card environment, because high-fouling teams facing low-foul-conceding opponents generate a specific disciplinary pattern that differs from the symmetric case.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team relationship between two distinct observables (fouls FOR for one team, fouls AGAINST for the other) jointly conditioning a third observable (cards_2h). It cannot be reduced to a single observable mirror or a single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A's goals FOR split by first vs. second half, (b) Team A's goals AGAINST split by first vs. second half, (c) Team B's goals FOR split by first vs. second half, and (d) Team B's goals AGAINST split by first vs. second half — specifically testing whether both teams' half-level profiles align in the same temporal direction (both back-loaded or both front-loaded).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams' attacking and defensive goal-timing profiles are jointly back-loaded (second half > first half for both FOR and AGAINST), second-half goal totals rise relative to first-half totals beyond the competition baseline, and this effect is stronger than either team's half-split considered in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's goal-scoring is heavily back-loaded (second-half goals substantially exceed first-half goals across its season history), while Team A's goals conceded are also back-loaded — the joint half-level goal-timing profiles of both teams interact to shape whether total goals are concentrated in the second half, beyond what full-match averages reveal.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on four half-level splits across two teams and two perspectives — a genuine joint within-match state interaction. It is not a single observable with one coarse band; it is a four-way half-level profile alignment test.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where both Team A's possession FOR (all-prior, home, recent-5) and Team B's possession FOR (all-prior, away, recent-5) are simultaneously below the 50% competition baseline — a dual low-possession configuration. Test how this joint configuration relates to total corner-kick volume relative to the competition average.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams are structurally low-possession sides meeting each other, total corner kicks are suppressed relative to the competition average, because neither team sustains the prolonged attacking territorial pressure that generates corners — the suppression is non-additive and saturates as both teams' possession deficits deepen.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession is structurally below 50% (both season-long and at home) while Team B also operates below 50% possession in all contexts — when both teams are structurally low-possession sides, the joint possession deficit interacts with corner-kick production in a non-linear way, because neither team dominates territory, which suppresses the corner-kick volume below what either team's corner average alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable (possession + corners), two-team relationship with a non-linear (saturation) structure. It requires simultaneously conditioning on both teams' possession profiles relative to a threshold (50%), which is not reducible to a single observable mirror or a single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) the ratio of Team A's recent-5 shots FOR to its all-prior shots FOR (volume maintenance), (b) the ratio of Team A's recent-5 goals FOR to its all-prior goals FOR (conversion collapse), and (c) Team A's recent-5 goals AGAINST vs. all-prior goals AGAINST (defensive deterioration) — testing whether the combination of maintained shot volume with collapsed conversion and worsening defense is a distinct regime from the season average.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team maintains shot volume but shows a sharp recent decline in goals FOR while simultaneously conceding more goals, the match-level shots-to-goals ratio rises (more shots per goal), indicating a conversion-efficiency regime shift that is not captured by either shots or goals averages alone — and this regime is associated with higher total shots but not proportionally higher goals.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots-to-goals conversion efficiency (shots FOR vs. goals FOR, both season-long and recent) has deteriorated in recent matches while goals conceded have surged — the joint relationship between Team A's shot-volume maintenance and its conversion collapse, combined with Team B's defensive deterioration (goals AGAINST rising recently), creates a specific match state where high shot counts do not translate to goals at the expected rate, and this divergence between shot volume and goal output is structurally different from the season baseline.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism involves a joint three-observable relationship (shots, shots_on_target, goals) across two temporal windows (recent vs. season) for the same team, testing a non-linear ratio/threshold structure (conversion efficiency regime). It is not reducible to any single observable mirror, single-band split, or simple recent-vs-season comparison of one metric.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team B's recent-5 window versus all-prior window simultaneously for both shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR, then relate the joint recent decline in both observables to Team B's recent goals FOR versus season goals FOR.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both shot volume and shot accuracy decline together in the recent window relative to the season baseline, goals FOR is suppressed more than when only one of the two declines.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot volume (shots FOR) has declined sharply in recent matches relative to its season-long average, while simultaneously its shots-on-target conversion rate (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR) has also dropped in recent matches. The joint deterioration of both volume and accuracy — rather than either alone — may be associated with a suppressed goal-scoring output in recent fixtures compared to the season baseline.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship across two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) in the same window comparison — not a single observable against one band. The engine does not already measure the interaction between simultaneous declines in two separate production metrics.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team B's recent-5 versus all-prior window for both shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST simultaneously, then relate the joint increase in both to goals AGAINST in the same window.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both shot volume allowed and shot accuracy allowed rise together in the recent window, goals conceded rises disproportionately relative to the season baseline — a joint amplification effect rather than an additive one.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's defensive exposure has worsened in recent matches: both shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST have risen sharply in the recent-5 window relative to the season baseline, while goals AGAINST has also spiked. The joint relationship between rising shot volume allowed and rising shot accuracy allowed — measured together — may be associated with a non-linear amplification of goals conceded beyond what either metric alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires a joint two-observable relationship (shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST) rather than a single observable with one conditioning band. The interaction between volume and accuracy allowed is not captured by any single-observable mirror or recent-vs-baseline split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on the asymmetry between Team B's fouls FOR (high, stable) and Team A's possession FOR (rising in recent window), then test whether this cross-team asymmetry — high fouler facing a possession-dominant opponent — is associated with elevated yellow cards and second-half cards for Team B.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's foul rate is elevated and its opponent's possession is simultaneously elevated (recent window), the high-fouling team's yellow card and second-half card accumulation rises relative to matches where only one of these conditions holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B commits substantially more fouls than Team A (both season-long and recently), while Team A's recent possession has risen above its season average and above Team B's recent possession. The joint condition of high foul-committing by one side and elevated possession by the other side may be associated with elevated yellow cards for the high-fouling team, particularly in the second half where card accumulation is tracked.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship involving two distinct observables from different teams (Team B fouls FOR vs Team A possession FOR), which cannot be reduced to a single observable mirror or a single-observable split by one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's corners FOR recent-5 versus all-prior AND Team B's corners AGAINST recent-5 versus all-prior simultaneously. Test whether the joint elevation of both (attacker generating more, defender conceding more) is associated with a total corner count that exceeds the sum of individual baselines.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the attacking team's recent corner generation and the defending team's recent corner concession are both elevated above their respective season baselines simultaneously, total match corners rise more than when only one side shows elevation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner kick production has risen sharply in the recent-5 window relative to its season average, while Team B concedes corners at a rate that has also risen recently. The joint condition — Team A's elevated corner generation meeting Team B's elevated corner concession — may be associated with a non-additive amplification of total corner volume in the match, beyond what either team's individual baseline would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint two-team, two-window relationship on the same observable (corners FOR for Team A and corners AGAINST for Team B, both in recent vs all-prior), which is structurally richer than a single-observable mirror or a single team's recent-vs-baseline split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's goals FOR split by half (first vs second) and Team B's goals AGAINST split by half (first vs second), both from all-prior season data. Test whether the combination of Team A's second-half scoring tendency and Team B's second-half defensive weakness is associated with a higher second-half share of total goals than the competition context baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the home team scores proportionally more in the second half and the away team concedes proportionally more in the second half, the share of total match goals occurring in the second half rises above the competition context baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals are distributed more heavily in the second half than the first half (season-long), while Team B concedes more in the second half than the first half. The joint within-match temporal asymmetry — Team A's second-half goal production tendency meeting Team B's second-half defensive vulnerability — may be associated with a disproportionate share of total match goals occurring in the second half when these two teams meet, beyond what the competition context baseline would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) joint relationship across two teams and two perspectives (Team A goals FOR by half, Team B goals AGAINST by half), requiring half-resolution data and a cross-team asymmetric combination. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's FOR shots and FOR shots_on_target (both all-prior and recent-5 windows) alongside Team B's AGAINST shots and AGAINST shots_on_target. The mechanism requires the joint relationship between volume and accuracy across both sides simultaneously — not either observable alone against a single band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent shots_on_target FOR rate declines relative to its all-prior rate while the opponent's shots_on_target AGAINST rate is also below competition baseline, the match-level shots_on_target total is suppressed relative to what either team's individual baseline would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR) is jointly compared against Team B's defensive suppression of both shots and shots_on_target allowed, to test whether a high-volume but recently declining accuracy attacker facing a low-shots-allowed defence produces a jointly suppressed shots_on_target outcome relative to each team's individual baselines.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint product of two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) across both FOR and AGAINST perspectives simultaneously. It cannot be reduced to one observable mirrored against its opponent-allowed counterpart, nor to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the cross-team asymmetry: Team A FOR fouls (low, ~11) vs Team A AGAINST fouls (high, ~14.4, spiking to 16 recently) combined with Team B AGAINST fouls (low all-prior ~12.7, spiking to 16 recently). The joint signal is the simultaneous divergence of both teams' recent AGAINST-fouls from their all-prior baselines, not either team's foul rate alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams show a recent spike in fouls-AGAINST relative to their all-prior baselines, total match fouls and yellow cards rise above what either team's individual all-prior foul rate would predict, with the asymmetry (one team draws fouls, the other commits them) amplifying card accumulation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's asymmetric foul-production profile (low fouls FOR, high fouls AGAINST) is jointly conditioned with Team B's recent spike in fouls AGAINST to test whether a match where one side commits few fouls but draws many, facing an opponent whose opponents have recently fouled them more, produces an elevated total-fouls and yellow-cards outcome beyond what either team's individual foul rate predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) across two teams' FOR and AGAINST perspectives simultaneously, plus a recent-vs-all-prior divergence on both sides at once.
