It is not reducible to one observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A FOR possession (all-prior ~54, home ~55) and Team B FOR possession away (~47 vs home ~51), alongside both teams' corner FOR and AGAINST rates split by half (first-half vs second-half). The mechanism requires the joint interaction of possession asymmetry and its half-level translation into corners — two distinct observables across two venue-split dimensions simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A holds a structural possession advantage that is amplified by Team B's away-venue possession drop, Team A's corner-kick generation rises above its all-prior average, and the corner differential between the two teams widens beyond what either team's individual corner rate or possession rate alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between Team A's possession dominance (FOR possession well above 50) and Team B's away possession deficit (away possession notably below home possession) is tested against corner-kick generation: specifically whether Team A's possession advantage, when compounded by Team B's structural away-possession drop, produces a corner-kick differential that exceeds what either team's individual corner baseline predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) where the conditioning involves two opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (venue-split possession for both teams) and a half-level resolution for corners. It cannot be reduced to one observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint recent-vs-all-prior divergence for both teams simultaneously: Team A FOR goals (recent-5 ~1.0 vs all-prior ~1.9) and Team B AGAINST goals (recent-5 ~2.2 vs all-prior ~1.56), combined with Team A AGAINST goals (recent-5 ~2.2 vs all-prior ~1.31) and Team B FOR goals (recent-5 ~0.8 vs all-prior ~1.47). The mechanism tests whether the cross-product of these four divergences — two teams each showing recent-form shifts in both attack and defence — produces a non-additive total-goals signal.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams simultaneously show a recent-form divergence from their all-prior goal rates (one team's attack declining while both teams' defences are conceding more recently), the total goals outcome diverges from the competition baseline in a direction that is not predictable from any single team's recent or all-prior rate alone, suggesting a threshold or regime shift in the joint recent-form signal.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent-form goal-scoring collapse (FOR goals recent-5 well below all-prior) is jointly conditioned with Team B's recent defensive deterioration (AGAINST goals recent-5 above all-prior) to test whether the simultaneous divergence of both teams' recent goal rates from their long-run baselines — in opposite directions — produces a goals total that is non-linearly different from what either team's all-prior rate or the competition baseline would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint conditioning on four recent-vs-all-prior divergences across both teams' FOR and AGAINST goal rates simultaneously. It is not a single observable with a recent-vs-long-run split, nor a single observable with one opponent band — it requires the cross-product of both teams' simultaneous form divergences.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team B FOR red_cards away (~0.216) vs home (~0.125), Team A AGAINST red_cards recent-5 (~0.4 vs all-prior ~0.182), and both teams' cards_2h rates (second-half card accumulation). The mechanism requires the joint interaction of two distinct observables (red_cards and cards_2h) across two venue-split and temporal dimensions simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's away red-card rate is structurally elevated above its home rate, and Team A's recent AGAINST red-card rate has spiked above its all-prior level, the second-half card total (cards_2h) rises above competition baseline, with the joint signal being stronger than either team's individual card rate would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between Team B's elevated away red-card rate (away red cards FOR notably above home) and Team A's elevated red-cards-AGAINST rate (recent-5 spiking above all-prior), conditioned on second-half card accumulation rates for both teams, is tested to determine whether the combination of Team B's away disciplinary risk and Team A's recent tendency to provoke red cards produces a second-half cards total that exceeds competition baseline beyond what either team's individual card rate predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship between two distinct observables (red_cards and cards_2h) conditioned on two opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (venue split for Team B's red cards, and recent-vs-all-prior for Team A's AGAINST red cards), plus a within-match temporal split (second half). It is not reducible to one observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's shots FOR (recent vs. all-prior) AND shots_on_target FOR (recent vs. all-prior) simultaneously. Both observables must be evaluated together — a drop in shots combined with a drop in on-target ratio is a joint signal distinct from either alone. Compare resulting goal output against long-run goals FOR mean.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A goals FOR rises with the joint level of shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR; when both are simultaneously below long-run averages (as in recent-5 vs. all-prior here), goals FOR is suppressed relative to the long-run mean.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume (FOR) combined with its shots-on-target conversion rate (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR) jointly predicts whether Team A's goal output rises above its long-run mean, beyond what either observable alone captures. Specifically, when a team's recent shot volume is declining while its on-target ratio is also declining, goal output is expected to be suppressed relative to the long-run average.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single-observable mirror or a single observable with one band. It requires the joint relationship between two distinct offensive production observables (shots volume and on-target accuracy) and their combined effect on goals — neither observable alone captures the interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's shots_on_target FOR (recent vs. all-prior) AND Team A's shots_on_target AGAINST (recent vs. all-prior). Both are elevated in the recent window. Measure whether the joint elevation of both observables — one team's attacking quality and the opponent's defensive concession rate — is associated with higher total goals AGAINST for Team A than either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both Team B's shots_on_target FOR (recent) and Team A's shots_on_target AGAINST (recent) are simultaneously elevated above their respective long-run means, goals AGAINST for Team A rises above what either single observable predicts independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-on-target FOR (recent) has risen relative to its long-run mean, while its goals FOR (recent) has also risen. The joint relationship between Team B's shots-on-target FOR and Team A's shots-on-target AGAINST (both elevated in recent windows) creates a combined attacking-vs-defensive pressure signal that is richer than either team's individual observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship: it combines one team's attacking observable (Team B shots_on_target FOR) with the opponent's defensive observable (Team A shots_on_target AGAINST) simultaneously, which is not reducible to a single-observable mirror or a single band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner_kicks FOR and AGAINST for Team A by half (FIRST_HALF vs. SECOND_HALF). Jointly evaluate the FOR–AGAINST differential within each half. Test whether the net corner deficit (AGAINST minus FOR) is larger in one half than the other, and whether this half-level asymmetry is consistent across the historical sample.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's net corner deficit (corners AGAINST minus corners FOR) is larger in the first half than the second half, indicating a half-specific suppression of Team A's corner production that is not captured by full-match averages alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner kicks FOR exhibit a pronounced asymmetry between first-half and second-half production (FOR: 1H avg ~1.97, 2H avg ~2.19, all-prior), while Team A's corner kicks AGAINST are also split across halves (1H ~2.72, 2H ~2.69). The within-match half-level split of corner kicks FOR vs. AGAINST for Team A, conditioned jointly on both halves, reveals whether Team A's corner deficit (FOR vs. AGAINST) is concentrated in a specific half rather than uniformly distributed.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match state split (half-level) combined with a joint FOR vs. AGAINST differential within each half — two dimensions simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner_kicks FOR and AGAINST for Team B by half (FIRST_HALF vs. SECOND_HALF). Jointly evaluate the FOR–AGAINST differential within each half. Test whether Team B's net corner concession (AGAINST minus FOR) is concentrated in the second half.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's net corner concession (corners AGAINST minus corners FOR) is larger in the second half than the first half, indicating a second-half-specific vulnerability to opponent corners that is not visible in full-match averages.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner kicks AGAINST are split asymmetrically across halves (1H ~2.27, 2H ~2.87), while Team B's corner kicks FOR are more evenly split (1H ~2.35, 2H ~2.42). The joint half-level profile of Team B's corners FOR and AGAINST reveals that Team B concedes significantly more corners in the second half than the first, while generating corners more evenly. This half-level asymmetry in the FOR vs. AGAINST corner differential for Team B is a within-match structural pattern.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split combined with a joint FOR vs. AGAINST differential within each half for Team B — two dimensions simultaneously. Not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's fouls FOR (away venue, all-prior) as the foul-generation input, and Team A's cards_2h FOR and AGAINST (second-half, all-prior) as the disciplinary output. Also incorporate Team B's yellow_cards FOR (away vs. home split) to assess whether elevated away fouls translate into elevated second-half card accumulation when Team B plays away. Test the joint relationship across both observables simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's away foul rate is elevated above its home rate, second-half cards (cards_2h) in matches involving Team B away rise above the competition context baseline, and this relationship is stronger than what either foul rate or cards_2h alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's foul rate FOR is substantially higher away than at home (away ~12.19 vs. home ~10.11), while Team A's foul rate FOR shows minimal venue variation (home ~10.49, away ~10.88). The joint relationship between Team B's elevated away foul rate and Team A's cards_2h (second-half cards) — both teams' foul-generating tendencies combined with the second-half card accumulation pattern — creates a cross-observable, cross-team signal for second-half disciplinary activity that is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and cards_2h/yellow_cards) across two different teams, conditioned on venue, and evaluated within a specific match period (second half). It combines an asymmetric cross-team observable pairing with a within-match period split — not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on (a) Team A's possession FOR being above its own long-run mean and (b) Team B's corner_kicks AGAINST being above the competition context mean. Both conditions must hold simultaneously — neither alone is sufficient.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A corner_kicks FOR rises when both conditions are met, and the joint effect exceeds the sum of each single-condition effect.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production is jointly conditioned on both its own possession dominance and the opponent's (Team B's) corner-kick concession rate: when Team A holds elevated possession AND faces a side that concedes above-average corners, Team A's corner output rises beyond what either dimension alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) from two different teams to be evaluated jointly. It is not reducible to one observable with one coarse band — it is a genuine two-observable, cross-team interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compare Team A's corner_kicks FOR FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF split, conditioned on whether Team B's possession FOR is below the competition context mean (indicating Team B typically cedes possession). The within-match half-level split is the key structural element.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's possession FOR is suppressed relative to competition context, Team A's ratio of first-half corners to second-half corners rises (corners are less back-loaded) compared to matches where Team B holds more possession.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's first-half corner production relative to its second-half corner production shifts depending on Team B's possession tendency: when Team B typically concedes high possession (i.e., plays low-block), Team A's corner generation is more evenly distributed across halves rather than back-loaded.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match half-level split (first half vs second half corner distribution) conditioned on a cross-team possession dimension — requiring two distinct observables across two teams and a half-resolution split. Not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on (a) Team A's shots_on_target AGAINST being below competition context mean and (b) Team A's possession FOR being above competition context mean. Evaluate Team B's shots_on_target FOR under this joint condition versus either condition alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's shots_on_target FOR is more suppressed under the joint condition than under either single condition, indicating a compounding cross-observable interaction.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-on-target production is jointly suppressed when Team A's shots-on-target allowed is low AND Team A's possession dominance is high: the combination of a possession-heavy opponent that also concedes few shots on target creates a compounding suppression on Team B's attacking output.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires two distinct observables (shots_on_target and possession) evaluated jointly across both teams. Not a single-observable mirror or a single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on (a) Team B's fouls FOR being above competition context mean and (b) Team A's possession FOR being above competition context mean. Evaluate Team B's cards_2h FOR under this joint condition versus each single condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's cards_2h FOR rises more steeply under the joint condition (high fouls AND facing high-possession opponent) than under either condition alone, indicating a non-additive interaction between foul tendency and possession pressure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half card accumulation (cards_2h) is jointly related to both Team B's foul rate FOR and Team A's possession dominance: when Team B commits fouls at an elevated rate against a possession-heavy Team A, second-half card accumulation for Team B rises beyond what either foul rate or possession differential alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Involves three distinct observables (cards_2h, fouls, possession) across two teams, with a within-match period restriction (second half). Not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compare Team A's goals FOR FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF ratio, conditioned on whether Team B's fouls FOR is above the competition context mean. The within-match half-level split in goals is the key structural element, conditioned on an opponent's foul-rate dimension.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's fouls FOR exceeds the competition context mean, Team A's second-half goals FOR rises relative to first-half goals FOR — the ratio of second-half to first-half goals for Team A is higher in high-foul-opponent contexts than in low-foul-opponent contexts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goal scoring rate in the second half relative to the first half is asymmetrically related to Team B's defensive foul rate: when Team B commits fouls at a high rate (disrupting Team A's build-up), Team A's goals shift toward the second half rather than being evenly distributed, suggesting a threshold-like adaptation effect across halves.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires a within-match half-level split on goals conditioned on a cross-team foul-rate dimension — two distinct observables (goals and fouls) across two teams with half-resolution. Not a single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's recent shots FOR (RECENT_5) is meaningfully below its ALL_PRIOR shots FOR, while simultaneously examining whether shots_on_target FOR rate (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR) compensates. Measure this joint two-observable relationship against Team A's goals FOR output.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shot volume is suppressed relative to long-run average, goals FOR rises with shots_on_target conversion rate (shots_on_target / shots) rather than with raw shot volume — i.e., the conversion ratio becomes the dominant co-predictor of goals when volume is low.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume (shots FOR) and shot conversion efficiency (shots_on_target FOR as a share of shots FOR) jointly determine whether Team A's goal output rises above competition baseline, particularly when Team A's recent shot volume has dropped sharply relative to its long-run average. mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute each team's yellow_cards FOR / fouls FOR ratio (card-per-foul rate). When the two teams' card-per-foul ratios diverge substantially (one team is much more card-prone per foul than the other), test whether total cards_2h in the match is elevated relative to competition context.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total match cards_2h rises as the cross-team divergence in yellow_cards-per-foul ratio increases, reflecting that one team's structural card-proneness amplifies second-half card accumulation beyond what raw foul counts alone predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The cross-team asymmetry in yellow card accumulation versus foul rate — specifically, Team A's yellow cards FOR relative to its fouls FOR compared to Team B's yellow cards FOR relative to its fouls FOR — identifies whether one side is systematically more card-prone per foul committed, and whether this asymmetry is associated with elevated total second-half cards in the match.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a ratio of two observables (yellow_cards / fouls) computed for each team and then compared asymmetrically across teams — a cross-team, two-observable ratio structure. It is not reducible to a single observable mirror or a simple opponent-descriptor band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where one team's recent shots FOR (RECENT_5) substantially exceeds its all-prior average AND the opponent's shots AGAINST (ALL_PRIOR) substantially exceeds competition context, then examine whether the corner-kick FOR rate and shots-on-target FOR rate move together or diverge relative to the goals FOR rate.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent shot volume surges above its own baseline AND the opponent structurally allows many shots, corner-kick generation rises with shot volume but goals FOR rises less than proportionally, indicating a saturation or decoupling between shot volume and conversion in this joint condition.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume is jointly elevated in recent form (shots FOR rising sharply) while Team B concedes shots at a level well above competition context, but Team B's shots-on-target allowed has not risen proportionally in recent form — suggesting a divergence between raw shot volume and shot quality allowed that conditions how corner-kick generation relates to actual goal threat.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (shots and shots-on-target) across two teams simultaneously, then relating that joint state to a third observable (corner kicks) and a fourth (goals). It cannot be reduced to any single observable against one opponent-descriptor band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on each team's possession FOR (ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5) and their shots-on-target-to-shots ratio (derived from FOR observables), then examine the corner-kick FOR differential and goals FOR differential across matches where possession dominance and shot-quality ratio diverge between the two sides.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team holds higher possession but its shots-on-target-to-shots ratio is lower than the opponent's, its corner-kick generation rises relative to goals scored — the relationship between possession dominance and goal output is suppressed when shot quality is low.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The ratio of shots-on-target FOR to total shots FOR (conversion to on-target) differs asymmetrically between Team A and Team B, and this asymmetry interacts with each team's possession level to predict corner-kick differential — teams with higher possession but lower shot-quality ratios generate more corners without proportionally more goals.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires a joint relationship among three distinct observables (possession, shots, shots-on-target) for both teams simultaneously, forming a ratio and interacting it with a second observable dimension. Not reducible to any single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where one team's fouls FOR RECENT_5 diverges downward from its ALL_PRIOR baseline while the opponent's fouls FOR RECENT_5 diverges upward from its ALL_PRIOR baseline. Within this asymmetric regime, measure whether cards_2h FOR and AGAINST are elevated relative to competition context.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the two teams' recent foul trajectories diverge in opposite directions (one falling, one rising), second-half card volume rises above what either team's individual foul baseline predicts — the asymmetric divergence amplifies disciplinary outcomes in the second half.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's foul rate FOR has dropped sharply in recent form relative to its all-prior baseline, while Team B's foul rate FOR has risen in recent form — this asymmetric recent-vs-baseline divergence in fouls across the two teams jointly conditions the second-half card (cards_2h) volume, beyond what either team's foul rate alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint, asymmetric relationship across two distinct observables (fouls and cards_2h) for both teams simultaneously, conditioning on the direction of recent-vs-baseline divergence for each team independently and then combining them. It is not reducible to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Use first-half and second-half corner-kick FOR averages for each team alongside first-half and second-half goals AGAINST averages to identify whether the team that concentrates corners in the second half also concedes more goals in the second half, and whether this joint half-level pattern predicts total corner volume above competition context.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's second-half corner share is structurally higher than its first-half share AND the opponent concedes more goals in the second half than the first half, total match corner volume rises above competition context — the half-level concentration of attacking pressure compounds with defensive vulnerability timing.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The within-match half-level split of corner kicks (first-half vs second-half) differs structurally between Team A and Team B: Team A generates a higher share of corners in the second half relative to the first half, while Team B's corner distribution across halves is more balanced. This half-level asymmetry in corner timing interacts with each team's goals-against first-half vs second-half split to condition total match corner volume.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (first-half vs second-half) for two distinct observables (corners and goals) across both teams simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one band; it is a joint half-resolution relationship across two observables and two teams.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B holds higher possession FOR than Team A (both all-prior and recent) but also concedes more goals AGAINST than Team A. Within this joint condition, examine whether offsides AGAINST (opponent offsides caught) are elevated for the high-possession but high-conceding team, indicating a high defensive line that is both a source of possession and a vulnerability.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team holds higher possession than its opponent but concedes goals at a higher rate, its offsides AGAINST (trapping opponents offside) rises above competition context — the high defensive line that enables possession also creates more offside traps but does not fully suppress goals conceded, and this joint pattern is detectable across matches.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession FOR is structurally above competition context and above Team A's possession FOR, yet Team B's goals AGAINST (both all-prior and recent) are substantially higher than Team A's goals AGAINST — indicating that possession dominance does not suppress goals conceded for Team B. Jointly conditioning on possession differential and goals-against differential across both teams reveals whether high-possession teams that still concede heavily also generate elevated offside counts (as a proxy for high defensive lines being exploited).
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship among three distinct observables (possession, goals, offsides) across both teams, conditioning on two opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (possession differential and goals-against differential). It cannot be reduced to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the simultaneous state where Team B's recent-5 corners FOR (8.4) is substantially above its all-prior average (5.731) AND Team A's recent-5 corners AGAINST (5.2) is above its all-prior average (4.721). Measure total corner volume in matches where both conditions hold jointly, versus matches where only one or neither holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total corner volume rises when both the attacking team's recent corner surge and the defending team's recent corner-concession surge are present simultaneously, compared to when only one condition is present.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner-kick production shows a sharp upward shift in recent form relative to its long-run average, while Team A's corner-kick concession shows a corresponding upward shift in recent form. The joint condition — attacker's recent corner surge AND defender's recent corner-concession surge — may amplify total corner volume beyond what either single-observable baseline predicts alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint evaluation of two distinct observable streams (Team B corners FOR recent vs. long-run AND Team A corners AGAINST recent vs. long-run) interacting multiplicatively. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band — it is a two-dimensional recent-form interaction across two different team roles.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner production and concession by half. Condition on matches where Team B's first-half corner rate (FOR, H1) is above competition baseline AND Team A's second-half corner concession rate (AGAINST, H2) is above its own first-half concession rate. Measure whether the second half sees a disproportionate corner share relative to the first half in such configurations.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half corner volume is disproportionately elevated relative to first-half corner volume when the attacking team's first-half corner production is high and the defending team's second-half corner concession rate exceeds its first-half rate.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner production is asymmetrically split between halves: its first-half average (2.671) exceeds its second-half average (2.800 is close, but against Team A the second-half concession rate 2.367 is lower than first-half 2.291 — the asymmetry is cross-observable). Specifically, Team A concedes more corners in the second half than the first half, while Team B generates more corners in the first half. The joint half-level profile of attacker's first-half corner production versus defender's second-half corner concession creates a within-match distributional asymmetry that is not captured by full-match averages.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match half-level split conditioned on two distinct half-level observables from two different teams — it requires half resolution and a cross-team, cross-half joint condition, which is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the attacking team's shots FOR is elevated above its long-run average while its shots_on_target FOR does not rise proportionally (i.e., shots-to-on-target ratio declines), AND the defending team's shots_on_target AGAINST is below its long-run average. Measure whether goals FOR the attacking team are suppressed in this joint configuration relative to what shot volume alone would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals for the attacking team are suppressed when shot volume is high but the shots-to-on-target ratio is declining and the opponent's shot-on-target concession rate is simultaneously improving — indicating a non-linear decoupling between shot volume and goal output.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots volume has surged sharply in recent form (recent-5: 17.6 vs. all-prior: 13.105) while its shots-on-target rate has not kept pace (recent-5: 4.8 vs. all-prior: 4.698). Simultaneously, Team B's shots-on-target concession has improved in recent form (recent-5: 3.8 vs. all-prior: 4.821). The joint condition of high shot volume with low conversion-to-on-target ratio for the attacker, combined with improved shot-on-target suppression by the defender, may indicate a saturation or decoupling between shot volume and shot quality that is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for the attacker, combined with a third observable (shots_on_target AGAINST) for the defender — a three-variable cross-team interaction that cannot be reduced to any single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B is playing away AND Team B's away foul rate is above the competition foul baseline. Within that condition, measure whether the combined foul volume (both teams) correlates with second-half card volume above the competition second-half card baseline. This is a two-dimensional conditioning: venue-specific foul asymmetry for Team B crossed with the joint foul environment.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half card volume rises with the joint foul environment when Team B is playing away and its away foul rate is elevated above the competition baseline — with the relationship being stronger than what Team B's card rate alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B commits substantially more fouls away from home (12.0) than at home (9.949), while Team A's foul production is relatively stable across venues (home: 10.465, away: 10.907). When Team B plays away and its foul rate is elevated, the joint foul environment (Team B fouls FOR away + Team A fouls FOR home) may interact with the second-half card rate. Specifically, a high combined foul environment in a match where Team B is away may predict elevated second-half cards beyond what either team's card baseline alone suggests.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (fouls and cards_2h) across two teams, with a venue-specific asymmetry for one team (Team B away fouls vs. home fouls) that is not symmetric. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band — it requires the cross-observable foul-to-card relationship conditioned on venue-specific foul asymmetry.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where both teams' offsides FOR are simultaneously below their respective long-run averages (a joint offside suppression state). Within that joint condition, measure whether goals and shots are also suppressed relative to competition baseline — testing whether the joint offside decline is a leading indicator of a low-intensity attacking match state.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals and shots are suppressed when both teams' offsides FOR are simultaneously below their long-run averages, suggesting a joint tactical retreat that reduces attacking intensity beyond what either team's individual goal or shot baseline predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides FOR has dropped sharply in recent form (recent-5: 1.0 vs. all-prior: 1.904, and vs. home all-prior: 2.146), while Team B's offsides FOR has also declined recently (recent-5: 1.6 vs. all-prior: 2.377). A joint decline in offsides for both teams simultaneously may indicate a shared tactical shift toward deeper, more cautious attacking lines — which in turn may correlate with lower goal totals and lower shot volumes, independent of what either team's goal or shot baseline alone predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint condition across two distinct observables (offsides for both teams simultaneously) used to predict a third observable (goals/shots), requiring a two-team, two-observable joint conditioning that cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning on (a) Team B's long-run possession advantage over Team A (all-prior) AND (b) the direction of Team A's recent possession shift relative to its own baseline. Both dimensions must be active simultaneously — not one at a time.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total corner-kick volume rises when the possession differential between a structurally dominant-possession team and its opponent narrows in recent matches, relative to matches where the differential is stable or widening.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When a high-possession team (Team B, ~58% all-prior) faces a team whose recent possession share has shifted upward relative to its own long-run average (Team A: 48.3% all-prior vs 51.8% recent-5), the joint interaction between Team B's structural possession dominance and Team A's recent possession uplift conditions the total corner-kick volume differently than either team's corner rate alone would predict. Specifically, the combined corner production of both sides should be examined as a function of the possession differential between the two teams across the two time windows simultaneously.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession and corners) across two distinct time windows (all-prior vs recent-5) for two different teams simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band, nor to a simple home/away or competition split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) the attacking team's (Team B) ratio of second-half to first-half goals FOR, and (b) the defending team's (Team A) ratio of second-half to first-half goals AGAINST. Both half-level splits for both teams must be active simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goal volume rises when both the attacking team's second-half scoring uplift and the defending team's second-half defensive deterioration are jointly present, relative to matches where only one or neither condition holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B exhibits a pronounced asymmetry between its first-half and second-half goal-scoring rates (0.667 1H vs 0.901 2H FOR, all-prior), while Team A's goals-against are also split across halves (0.694 1H vs 0.778 2H). The joint relationship between Team B's half-level goal-scoring profile and Team A's half-level defensive concession profile — specifically whether Team B's second-half scoring uplift is amplified or suppressed when facing a team that concedes more in the second half — is a within-match, cross-team asymmetric mechanism not captured by any single-observable baseline.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) mechanism that is asymmetric across two different teams' observables (Team B FOR vs Team A AGAINST), requiring joint conditioning on two half-level splits from two sides. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team B's recent-5 foul rate relative to its own all-prior baseline (regime shift upward), AND (b) Team A's recent-5 fouls-against relative to its own all-prior baseline (regime shift upward). Both regime shifts must be jointly present and measured against each team's own baseline — not against a competition average.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half card volume rises when both the fouling team's recent foul rate and the fouled team's recent fouls-received rate are simultaneously elevated above their respective long-run baselines.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's foul rate has increased sharply in recent matches (10.6 recent-5 FOR vs 10.8 all-prior FOR, stable) while the fouls conceded against Team A have risen more markedly (14.4 recent-5 AGAINST vs 12.2 all-prior AGAINST). Team B's foul rate has also shifted dramatically in recent matches (14.0 recent-5 FOR vs 10.3 all-prior FOR). The joint interaction between Team B's recent foul-rate surge and Team A's recent increase in fouls received — both deviating from their own baselines in the same direction — conditions second-half card volume (cards_2h) in a way that neither team's foul rate alone predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (fouls and cards_2h), two teams' regime shifts measured against their own baselines simultaneously, and a within-match period (second half). It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) the direction of a team's recent possession shift relative to its own all-prior baseline (compression vs expansion), AND (b) the direction of its recent shots-volume shift relative to its own all-prior baseline. The interaction of these two regime directions — specifically the case where shots surge while possession compresses — is the conditioning event.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The shots-on-target share of total shots is suppressed when a team's shot volume surges in recent matches while its possession share simultaneously compresses relative to its own baseline, compared to matches where both move in the same direction.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B has a strong structural possession advantage (~58% all-prior FOR) but its recent possession share has compressed toward 53.2% (recent-5), while Team A's recent possession has risen to 51.8% (recent-5) from 48.3% (all-prior). Simultaneously, Team B's shots volume has surged in recent matches (19.4 recent-5 vs 14.5 all-prior FOR) while its shots-on-target conversion rate (shots_on_target / shots) can be computed across both windows. The joint relationship between a team's recent possession compression and its simultaneous shot-volume surge — i.e., whether increased shot volume without possession growth reflects a lower-quality shot profile — conditions the shots-to-shots-on-target ratio in a non-linear way.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship among three distinct observables (possession, shots, shots_on_target) with a non-linear/threshold structure (the divergence between possession and shot-volume regime directions). It cannot be reduced to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team B's recent-5 offside rate FOR relative to its own all-prior baseline (regime shift upward), AND (b) Team A's home vs away offside-drawn differential (AGAINST: HOME vs AWAY). Both dimensions — Team B's recent regime and Team A's venue-specific defensive line behavior — must be active simultaneously in a home fixture context.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's offsides FOR are amplified in matches where Team A's home defensive line draws significantly more offsides than its away line AND Team B's own recent offside rate is already elevated above its baseline, relative to matches where only one condition holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offside rate away from home (1.059 all-prior AWAY) is substantially lower than at home (1.882 all-prior HOME), while Team B's offside rate FOR is elevated in recent matches (3.0 recent-5 vs 1.835 all-prior). The asymmetric interaction between Team B's recent offside surge and Team A's venue-conditioned defensive line depth (proxied by offsides drawn AGAINST) — where Team A draws more offsides at home than away — jointly conditions whether Team B's recent offside surge is amplified or suppressed in this specific home context. This is an asymmetric cross-team mechanism involving two distinct observables (offsides FOR for Team B, offsides AGAINST for Team A) conditioned on venue simultaneously.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct teams' offside observables (Team B FOR and Team A AGAINST) conditioned simultaneously on two dimensions: Team B's recent regime shift and Team A's venue-specific differential. It is not a single observable with one band, and the asymmetry across teams' roles (attacker vs defender) makes it structurally richer than any mirror comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A's shots FOR being below competition baseline (10.12 vs 14.16 context mean) and (b) Team B's shots AGAINST in RECENT_5 being markedly elevated versus its ALL_PRIOR average (13.8 vs 11.1). Measure whether Team A's shots_on_target FOR rises toward or above its own ALL_PRIOR average when the opponent's recent defensive shot-allowance is in an elevated regime, despite Team A's own low shot production.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's shots_on_target FOR rises relative to its own baseline when the opponent's recent shots-allowed is elevated, even when Team A's total shot volume remains below the competition mean — i.e., a divergence between shot volume and on-target rate conditioned on opponent's recent defensive state.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume is structurally low relative to the competition baseline, yet its shots-on-target conversion rate (shots_on_target / shots) is comparable to Team B's, while Team B concedes shots at a rate well above its season average in recent matches. The joint relationship between one team's shot-generation deficit and the opponent's recent defensive shot-allowance surge conditions how shots-on-target volume for Team A is likely to behave — specifically, whether a low-volume attacker can sustain on-target output against a recently porous defence.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (shots FOR for Team A and shots AGAINST RECENT_5 for Team B) across two different teams simultaneously, and comparing the ratio shots_on_target/shots rather than either observable in isolation. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A's possession FOR being persistently below 50% (both all-prior and recent) and (b) Team B's corner kicks FOR AWAY being above the competition corner mean. Measure whether the combined possession-deficit of Team A and the corner-generation tendency of Team B away produces a total corner count above the competition baseline, and whether Team A's corner concession rate in RECENT_5 (6.0) represents a genuine elevated regime versus its all-prior (5.03).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total corner kicks in the match rise above competition baseline when one team has a structural possession deficit and the opponent has an above-average corner generation rate away from home — the joint signal is stronger than either observable's individual deviation from baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A operates with a persistent possession deficit (44.3% all-prior, 43.2% recent) while Team B also concedes possession (51.8% against all-prior). The joint interaction of both teams' possession profiles — specifically when the attacking team (Team B) holds above-average possession against a team that habitually cedes it — conditions corner kick generation asymmetrically. Team B's corner production away (4.56) versus Team A's corner concession rate (5.03 all-prior, 6.0 recent) creates a joint signal distinct from either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) across both teams simultaneously, and tests whether their interaction produces a non-additive effect on total corners. It is not a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint recent-vs-all-prior drift for Team A across two defensive observables simultaneously: goals AGAINST RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR and shots_on_target AGAINST RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR. Test whether matches where both observables are simultaneously elevated (coherent deterioration) are associated with a higher goals-against outcome than matches where only one is elevated (divergent signal).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both goals-against and shots-on-target-against are simultaneously elevated in recent matches relative to all-prior averages for the same team, the goals-against outcome is higher than when only one observable is elevated — the joint signal is more predictive than either drift alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals-against rate has spiked sharply in recent matches (2.6 RECENT_5 vs 1.65 all-prior) while Team B's shots-on-target AGAINST has also risen recently (5.0 RECENT_5 vs 3.84 all-prior). The joint condition of Team A's recent defensive deterioration across two distinct dimensions — goals conceded and shots on target allowed — tests whether the recent regime shift is coherent (both observables moving together) or divergent (one observable elevated without the other), which has different implications for whether the defensive deterioration is structural or noise.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (goals and shots_on_target) both in their RECENT vs ALL_PRIOR drift dimension for the same team, testing coherence of a multi-observable regime shift. It is not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team B's goals FOR SECOND_HALF vs FIRST_HALF split (0.882 vs 0.691) and (b) Team A's goals AGAINST SECOND_HALF vs FIRST_HALF split (0.868 vs 0.779). Test whether the second-half goal rate in matches where the away team has a positive second-half scoring skew AND the home team has a positive second-half conceding skew is higher than the competition second-half baseline, compared to matches where only one of these conditions holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goal rate rises above competition baseline when the away team has a positive second-half scoring skew and the home team has a positive second-half conceding skew simultaneously — the joint half-level asymmetry across both teams produces a stronger second-half goal signal than either team's half split alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B scores more goals in the second half than the first half (0.882 vs 0.691 all-prior), while Team A concedes more in the second half than the first half (0.868 vs 0.779 all-prior). The asymmetric half-level goal-scoring and goal-conceding profiles of the two teams — Team B front-loaded in the second half, Team A more vulnerable in the second half — creates a within-match state interaction: the second-half goal environment is jointly shaped by both teams' half-specific tendencies, not just one team's profile.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split conditioned jointly on two teams' asymmetric half profiles simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one band, and it uses half-resolution data in a joint cross-team conditioning structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A's yellow_cards FOR ALL_PRIOR being above competition baseline (2.43 vs 1.64) and (b) Team B's fouls AGAINST RECENT_5 being sharply below its ALL_PRIOR average (7.8 vs 11.65). Test whether the second-half card rate (cards_2h) is suppressed relative to Team A's own cards_2h baseline when the opponent is in a low-fouls-drawn recent regime, compared to matches where the opponent draws fouls at a normal rate.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half card accumulation for Team A is suppressed when the opponent's recent fouls-drawn rate is markedly below its own all-prior average, even when Team A's own card-accumulation tendency is persistently elevated — the joint signal across two distinct observables (cards and fouls) across both teams conditions the second-half card outcome.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A accumulates cards at a high rate (2.43 yellow all-prior, 1.63 cards_2h second-half) while Team B's fouls AGAINST in RECENT_5 have dropped sharply (7.8 vs 11.65 all-prior), suggesting Team B is recently drawing fewer fouls from opponents. The joint relationship between Team A's persistent card accumulation tendency and Team B's recent shift in fouls-drawn rate conditions the second-half card environment: when the team that typically commits fouls faces an opponent that is recently drawing fewer fouls, the second-half card rate may diverge from what either team's card profile alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct observables (yellow_cards/cards_2h and fouls) across both teams, using a within-match half-level split for cards and a recent-vs-all-prior drift for fouls. It is not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint relationship: Team A's own shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR (measuring attacking accuracy) crossed with Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST (measuring defensive on-target suppression). Both dimensions must be active simultaneously — not one observable with one band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's shot-to-on-target ratio is low (many shots, few on target) and the opponent allows a below-average rate of shots on target, the resulting shots_on_target FOR is suppressed further than either factor alone would suggest — a compounding, non-additive relationship.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR) is jointly considered alongside Team B's defensive suppression of shots on target allowed, to test whether a low-accuracy attacker facing a permissive shot-on-target defence produces a different shots_on_target total than either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint product of two distinct observables (shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR for Team A, plus shots_on_target AGAINST for Team B) — it cannot be reduced to a single observable mirrored against what the opponent allows, nor to one observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's recent fouls FOR (RECENT_5) is substantially elevated above its ALL_PRIOR baseline, while simultaneously Team A's yellow_cards AGAINST (ALL_PRIOR) is also elevated above competition context. Both conditions must hold together — a two-observable, regime-shift cross.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's foul rate has recently escalated into a high-foul regime AND the opponent historically draws elevated yellow cards from opponents, yellow_cards FOR (Team B) rises above what either team's standalone card or foul average would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's foul rate has diverged sharply between its all-prior average and its recent 5 matches (all-prior ~10.5 FOR, recent ~15.2 FOR), while Team A concedes fouls at a stable rate. The joint relationship between Team B's recent foul escalation and Team A's yellow-card-against rate tests whether a high-fouling visiting team facing a team that draws above-average yellow cards from opponents produces a non-linear spike in cards, beyond what either team's individual card or foul rate alone would indicate.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) across two teams, conditioned on a within-team recent-vs-prior regime shift in one observable — not reducible to a single observable with one band or a simple recent-vs-prior comparison of the same observable.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on half (first vs second) simultaneously for both Team A's corner production and Team B's corner concession. The mechanism requires the within-match half split for both sides at once — not just one team's half split in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second half produces a higher combined corner total than the first half, and this asymmetry is amplified when Team A's second-half corner production tendency is combined with Team B's elevated second-half corner concession tendency — the joint second-half corner rate rises above what either team's half-split alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner kicks show a meaningful first-half vs second-half split (1H ~1.92 FOR, 2H ~2.05 FOR all-prior), while Team B concedes corners at a higher rate in the second half than the first (1H ~2.52 AGAINST, 2H ~3.14 AGAINST all-prior). The joint within-match half-level asymmetry — Team A's corner production by half crossed with Team B's corner concession by half — tests whether the second half produces a disproportionately elevated corner total relative to the first half, beyond what full-match averages imply.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split applied jointly to both teams' corner observables simultaneously — it is not a single observable with one coarse band, and it is not a simple home/away or recent/prior split. The joint half-level asymmetry across both sides is the novel structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's yellow_cards FOR (RECENT_5) is in a declining regime relative to ALL_PRIOR, while Team B's fouls FOR (RECENT_5) is in an escalating regime relative to ALL_PRIOR. The asymmetry across teams and across observables (cards vs fouls) is the conditioning structure.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team is in a low-card recent regime and the opposing team is in a high-foul recent regime, the second-half cards (cards_2h) distribution becomes asymmetric — concentrated on the high-fouling team — rather than balanced, and the total cards_2h rises above competition context baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's yellow cards FOR have dropped sharply in recent matches (all-prior ~2.31, recent ~1.2) while Team B's fouls FOR have spiked (all-prior ~10.5, recent ~15.2). The asymmetric divergence between one team's disciplinary restraint trend and the other team's foul escalation trend — measured as a cross-team, cross-observable regime divergence — tests whether the cards_2h (second-half cards) total is elevated when one side is in a high-foul regime and the other is in a low-card regime, creating an asymmetric second-half card distribution.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves three distinct observables (yellow_cards, fouls, cards_2h) across two teams in opposing regime directions — a cross-team, cross-observable asymmetric divergence. It cannot be reduced to any single observable with one band, nor to a simple recent-vs-prior comparison of the same observable for one team.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (1) Team B's possession FOR being in a low-possession regime (below competition context of 50%) both all-prior and in recent matches, AND (2) Team A playing at home where their possession is highest. The joint possession-asymmetry across both teams simultaneously — not just one team's possession split — is the conditioning structure, and the outcome tested is whether shots and corners FOR (Team A) are elevated under this joint condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a home team with above-average home possession faces a visiting team with a structural low-possession profile, the home team's shots FOR and corner_kicks FOR rise above what either team's standalone possession or shot/corner averages would predict — possession asymmetry compounds attacking volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B operates with a persistent below-average possession share (all-prior ~44.8%, recent ~42.4%) while also conceding above-average possession to opponents (opponents hold ~55.2% against Team B). Team A, playing at home, holds slightly above-average possession at home (~50.8%) but below average away. The joint relationship between Team B's structural low-possession profile and Team A's home possession tendency tests whether a possession-asymmetric match (one team structurally dominant in possession) produces a different shots and corner kicks distribution than possession-balanced matches — specifically whether Team A's shots FOR and corners FOR are elevated beyond their own baseline when facing a team that structurally cedes possession.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship among three distinct observables (possession, shots, corner_kicks) conditioned on two opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (Team A's home possession tendency AND Team B's structural away low-possession profile). It cannot be reduced to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B's shots-against (recent-5: 17.4 vs season: 12.97) AND shots-on-target-against (recent-5: 8.0 vs season: 4.58) are simultaneously elevated above their respective season baselines. Measure whether goals-against also rises jointly, and whether the co-elevation of both shot observables is more predictive than either alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both shots-against and shots-on-target-against are simultaneously above season baseline, goals-against rises more than when only one is elevated — a super-additive joint relationship.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot-volume conceded has surged sharply in recent matches relative to its season-long average, while its shots-on-target conceded has surged even more dramatically in the same window. The joint condition of both shot-volume AND shot-quality conceded rising together — rather than either alone — may be associated with elevated goal-conceding outcomes for Team B, beyond what either observable alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint two-observable condition (shots-against AND shots-on-target-against both elevated simultaneously), not a single observable with one coarse band. The engine does not currently measure the interaction between two distinct shot-quality observables on the same side.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the attacking team (Team A role) has a home venue uplift in shots (home: 13.58 vs away: 10.84) AND the defending team (Team B role) is in a recent-form regime of elevated shots-on-target conceded. Measure whether corner kicks and goals for the attacking side are jointly elevated under this dual condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's home shot-production advantage is paired with Team B's recent elevated shots-on-target-against regime, corner kicks and goals for Team A rise together — a cross-team, cross-observable joint relationship.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A produces more shots at home than away, while Team B concedes far more shots-on-target in recent form than its season average. The asymmetric pairing of Team A's home shot-production uplift against Team B's recent defensive deterioration in shot quality allowed may jointly condition corner-kick and goal outcomes beyond what either team's single-observable baseline captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (shots and shots-on-target) across two different teams simultaneously, plus a venue dimension for one and a recent-form regime for the other. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B's possession is below the competition midpoint (50%) AND Team B's fouls are above the competition average (10.22). Measure whether yellow cards for Team B and corner kicks for Team A are jointly elevated under this two-dimensional condition, compared to when only one condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team simultaneously holds below-median possession and above-median fouls, its yellow cards rise and the opponent's corner kicks rise — a joint two-observable relationship that saturates or amplifies relative to either condition alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B operates in a persistent low-possession regime (season avg ~44%, recent ~45%) while also committing high fouls (season avg ~12.5, recent ~12.6). The joint condition of below-median possession AND above-median fouls for the same team may be associated with elevated yellow-card and corner-kick outcomes for the opposing team, as a two-dimensional defensive pressure profile.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires two distinct observables (possession AND fouls) to be jointly conditioned for the same team, which is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band. The engine does not currently measure the interaction between possession level and foul rate.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on fixtures where both the home team's cards_2h-against AND the away team's cards_2h-for are simultaneously above the competition second-half average. Measure whether total second-half cards in such fixtures is elevated beyond the sum of individual team baselines, indicating a non-additive joint effect.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams independently carry above-competition second-half card rates, total second-half cards in the fixture rises more than a simple additive combination of individual baselines — suggesting a threshold or amplification effect from the joint profile.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half cards conceded (1.816 per match) substantially exceed both its own first-half rate and the competition second-half average (0.972), while Team B's second-half cards are also above competition average (1.642 vs 0.972). The joint second-half card accumulation profile of both teams — each independently elevated above competition norms — may condition whether total second-half cards in this fixture saturates at a higher threshold than either team's individual profile alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This conditions on two distinct team-level observables simultaneously (Team A's cards_2h-against AND Team B's cards_2h-for) both exceeding a competition baseline, which is a two-team, two-perspective joint condition not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where a team's shots-for is above its season average while its offsides-for is simultaneously below its season average (divergent regime). Measure whether corner kicks and goals for that team are elevated in this joint regime compared to matches where both move in the same direction.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shot volume rises while offside rate falls simultaneously for the same team, corner kicks and goals for that team rise — the divergent joint regime is associated with more effective attacking penetration than either observable alone captures.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides-for has declined from its season average (2.38 all-prior, 2.81 at home) to a lower recent level (1.6 recent-5), while Team A's shots-for has increased in recent matches (14.0 recent-5 vs 12.21 season). This divergence — more shots but fewer offsides — may indicate a structural shift in Team A's attacking line positioning or build-up pattern. The joint condition of rising shot volume alongside falling offside rate for the same team may be associated with a different corner-kick and goal profile than either observable alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint two-observable condition (shots-for rising AND offsides-for falling simultaneously) for the same team, which is an asymmetric cross-observable relationship not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly examine Team B's RECENT_5 shots (17.6) versus ALL_PRIOR shots (11.673) alongside RECENT_5 shots_on_target (5.4) versus ALL_PRIOR shots_on_target (4.02). The mechanism tests whether the within-team ratio of shots_on_target to shots shifts when shot volume is in a high-surge regime (RECENT_5 substantially above ALL_PRIOR), and whether this ratio shift is directionally consistent across historical instances of similar surge magnitude.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent shot volume is elevated well above its long-run mean, the shots_on_target-to-shots ratio tends to compress (i.e., the marginal shots added in high-volume regimes are less likely to be on target), so shots_on_target rises less than proportionally with shots.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's recent shot volume surge (RECENT_5) relative to its long-run average is jointly associated with a divergence in shot-to-shots-on-target conversion efficiency: when a team's recent shots rise sharply but recent shots-on-target rise proportionally less, the ratio of on-target to total shots compresses, suggesting a qualitative change in shot quality or positioning that is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly tracking two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) and their ratio across two time windows simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band; the mechanism is about the joint non-linear relationship between volume and quality across windows.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's RECENT_5 shots (17.6) and shots_on_target (5.4) are both above their ALL_PRIOR means (11.673 and 4.02 respectively), while RECENT_5 goals (0.8) are below the ALL_PRIOR mean (1.235). Test whether this three-way dissociation — high shots, high on-target, low goals — is a historically identifiable regime with a distinct goals-against profile for the opponent.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team enters a match in a regime of elevated shot volume and on-target shots but suppressed goals relative to long-run averages, its goals-for in that match tends to remain suppressed relative to what shot volume alone would predict, indicating a conversion-rate depression that persists across the regime.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's recent goals-for (RECENT_5) has declined relative to its long-run average despite a concurrent surge in shots and shots_on_target, suggesting a joint dissociation between shot-volume production and goal conversion that is structurally different from either observable's baseline trend alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires three observables jointly (goals, shots, shots_on_target) and a cross-window comparison (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) for each. Not reducible to any single observable or single conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on (a) Team A's home corner_kicks-for being substantially above its away rate, and (b) Team B's RECENT_5 corner_kicks-against being substantially below its ALL_PRIOR rate. The mechanism tests whether, in historical matches where both conditions hold simultaneously — the home team is a strong home corner producer AND the away team is in a recent low-corners-conceded regime — the realized corner total is suppressed relative to what Team A's home production rate alone would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the home team's elevated home corner production meets an away team in a recent low-corners-conceded regime, the realized corner count for the home team is suppressed relative to the home team's home-venue baseline, indicating the away team's recent defensive corner suppression partially offsets the home venue advantage.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetric venue split in Team A's corner_kicks-for (HOME: 6.388 vs AWAY: 4.122) combined with Team B's asymmetric corner_kicks-against (ALL_PRIOR: 5.357, RECENT_5: 3.4) creates a joint cross-team, cross-observable condition: the home team's corner production advantage interacts with the away team's recent suppression of corners conceded, and this joint state is distinct from either team's single-observable venue or recent-form split.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a two-team, two-dimension joint condition: it simultaneously uses Team A's venue split and Team B's recent-form window for the same observable. The engine covers each split individually but not their joint interaction across teams.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's RECENT_5 offsides-for being substantially above its ALL_PRIOR and venue-split baselines, AND Team B's RECENT_5 offsides-against being substantially below its ALL_PRIOR baseline. Test whether this joint divergence — attacker increasingly caught offside while the opponent's defensive line is increasingly disciplined — is associated with a suppression of Team A's attacking output (shots, goals) relative to its own baselines.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the attacking team's recent offsides-for is elevated above its long-run mean while the defending team's recent offsides-against is depressed below its long-run mean, the attacking team's goals-for and shots-on-target tend to be suppressed relative to their own baselines, reflecting a structural mismatch in attacking line discipline versus defensive line management.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides-for has surged in RECENT_5 (3.0) relative to its ALL_PRIOR mean (1.792) and its home/away splits (HOME: 1.898, AWAY: 1.681), while Team B's offsides-against has declined in RECENT_5 (1.2) relative to its ALL_PRIOR mean (2.118). The joint state — one team's offside-trap exposure rising while the opponent's ability to trigger offsides against them is falling — represents a cross-team asymmetric divergence across two distinct observables (Team A offsides-for, Team B offsides-against) that cannot be captured by either team's single-observable recent-vs-prior comparison.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly tracking two teams' offsides observables (FOR for Team A, AGAINST for Team B) across two time windows each, and then linking this joint state to a third observable (goals/shots). Not reducible to a single observable or single conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly examine Team B's cards_2h-for (second-half, ALL_PRIOR) against its fouls-for (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) and yellow_cards-for (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR). The mechanism tests whether, in historical matches where a team's foul rate is in a low-recent regime but its second-half card rate remains at or above its long-run mean, the cards_2h outcome is better predicted by the cards_2h baseline than by the foul-rate baseline — i.e., the two observables decouple in this regime.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent foul rate drops sharply below its long-run mean but its second-half card rate remains near its long-run mean, the second-half cards outcome is not suppressed proportionally with fouls, indicating that cards_2h and fouls are not linearly coupled and that the cards_2h baseline retains predictive structure independent of the foul-rate regime.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half cards (cards_2h FOR: 1.367) are elevated relative to Team A's second-half cards (cards_2h FOR: 1.194) and the competition context (cards_2h NEUTRAL: 1.186), while Team B's fouls-for have dropped sharply in RECENT_5 (7.4) versus ALL_PRIOR (10.633). This joint state — historically higher second-half card rate combined with a recent sharp drop in foul rate — tests whether the second-half card rate is structurally decoupled from the foul rate for Team B, i.e., whether cards_2h is driven by a different mechanism (e.g., concentration of high-severity fouls) rather than foul volume.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly tracking two distinct observables (cards_2h and fouls) across two time windows for the same team, and testing for decoupling between them. This is a non-linear / threshold relationship between two observables, not a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on both teams showing a recent-vs-all-prior possession shift in the same direction (both TEAM_A and TEAM_B show elevated RECENT_5 possession FOR vs ALL_PRIOR FOR), then jointly examine whether shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR also shift upward in RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR for the same teams. This is a joint two-team, two-observable co-movement test, not a single observable mirror.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams simultaneously show a recent possession surge, their recent shot production rises jointly above their long-run averages — the co-movement is stronger than either possession or shots alone would predict independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When a team's recent possession share (RECENT_5) diverges sharply upward from its all-prior average, its shots and shots-on-target production in the same recent window also rises disproportionately relative to its all-prior shot rate — testing whether the joint possession-surge and shot-surge co-move across both teams simultaneously in the same fixture context.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship across two distinct observables (possession and shots) for both teams simultaneously. It cannot be reduced to one observable with one conditioning band; it tests whether the cross-observable co-movement is coherent across both sides at once.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compute the ratio of shots_on_target FOR to shots FOR (accuracy) from ALL_PRIOR data, and cross it against the opponent's shots_on_target AGAINST (allowed) rate. Condition on cases where one team's accuracy ratio is below the competition context baseline while the opponent's allowed shots_on_target is also below baseline — a two-dimensional joint suppression condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's own shot accuracy is below the competition baseline AND its opponent allows fewer shots on target than the competition baseline, the team's shots_on_target FOR is suppressed below what either dimension alone would predict — a non-additive joint suppression.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: A team's shots-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shot accuracy) interacts with its opponent's shots-on-target allowed rate: when one side has high shot volume but low on-target accuracy while the opponent allows few shots on target, the joint suppression of on-target output is greater than either observable alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for one team conditioned simultaneously on two opponent-descriptor dimensions (opponent's allowed shots_on_target and the team's own accuracy ratio). It is not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compute the ratio of corner_kicks FOR in FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF (both ALL_PRIOR). Similarly compute corner_kicks AGAINST in FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF. Condition on the case where one team's FOR corners are back-loaded (second half > first half) and the opponent's AGAINST corners are also back-loaded — a joint within-match half-level asymmetry across both teams.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams' half-level corner profiles are jointly back-loaded (team's own second-half FOR corners exceed first-half, and opponent's second-half AGAINST corners exceed first-half), total second-half corner volume rises above what the full-match average would imply — a non-linear within-match state dependence.
