mechanisms.mechanism_statement: A team's corner kick production splits asymmetrically across halves (first-half vs second-half FOR rates), and this within-match half-level asymmetry differs between the two teams — testing whether the team with a stronger second-half corner bias faces an opponent whose corner-allowed rate is also skewed toward the second half, producing a compounding second-half corner surge.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF) combined with a joint condition across both teams' FOR and AGAINST half-profiles simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one coarse band; it is a two-team, two-half asymmetry interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compute the direction of shift (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) for both yellow_cards FOR and fouls FOR. Condition on the case where one team shows a joint suppression in both yellow cards and fouls recently (both RECENT_5 below ALL_PRIOR) while the opponent shows a joint elevation in both — an asymmetric cross-team, cross-observable disciplinary regime divergence.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's recent yellow card and foul rates are jointly suppressed while the opponent's are jointly elevated, the match-level total cards and fouls are driven asymmetrically by the elevated team, and the suppressed team's contribution is below its long-run average — the asymmetry is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: A team's recent-window (RECENT_5) yellow card rate diverging from its all-prior average, when jointly considered with its recent foul rate divergence, tests whether the two disciplinary observables co-move in the same direction (both elevated or both suppressed recently) — and whether this joint recent disciplinary regime shift is asymmetric between the two teams (one team's regime shifting while the other's does not).
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric joint relationship across two distinct observables (yellow_cards and fouls) for two teams simultaneously, conditioned on the direction of recent-vs-all-prior regime shift for both observables at once. It cannot be reduced to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compare fouls FOR at HOME vs AWAY (venue split) and cross this against cards_2h FOR (second-half cards, ALL_PRIOR). Condition on the case where a team's away foul rate exceeds its home foul rate AND its second-half card rate (cards_2h) is above the competition context baseline — testing whether the venue-driven foul elevation translates into a second-half card elevation beyond what the full-match card average would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Teams whose away foul rate materially exceeds their home foul rate show a disproportionate elevation in second-half cards when playing away, above what their full-match yellow card average or the competition baseline would imply — a non-additive venue-by-foul-by-half interaction.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The second-half cards (cards_2h) rate for each team, when jointly conditioned on both teams' full-match foul rates and the venue split (home vs away foul tendencies), tests whether a team that commits more fouls away from home also accumulates disproportionately more second-half cards away — an interaction between venue-conditioned foul production and within-match second-half card accumulation that requires both the venue dimension and the foul observable simultaneously.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on venue (home vs away foul split), a second distinct observable (fouls), and a within-match half-level period (second half cards). It involves two distinct observables and two conditioning dimensions (venue and half), which is structurally richer than any single-observable, single-band covered case.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute the ratio of shots-FOR to possession-FOR for TEAM_A across ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5 windows; do the same for TEAM_B. Test whether the joint recent-vs-longrun shift in both observables simultaneously (possession up, shots up) reflects a stable or changing shots-per-possession rate, conditioning on both observables together rather than either alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent possession share rises substantially above its long-run mean, its shots-per-possession rate is expected to either rise with it (compounding effect) or saturate/decline (diminishing returns); the direction of this joint shift is what the engine should measure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent possession share has surged dramatically relative to its long-run average, while its recent shot volume has also risen sharply. The joint relationship between a team's possession-to-shots conversion efficiency (shots produced per unit of possession held) in recent form versus its long-run baseline reveals whether the recent possession gain is translating into proportionally more shots, or whether the conversion rate is saturating or diverging.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint ratio of two distinct observables (shots and possession) across two time windows simultaneously. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band — it is a cross-observable rate that must be computed jointly.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compute shots_on_target / shots across ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5 windows. Test whether the recent increase in shot volume (both teams show higher recent shots) is accompanied by a proportional, improving, or degrading on-target rate — conditioning on both observables jointly, not either in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: A team whose shot volume rises sharply in recent form is expected to show either a stable, rising, or declining on-target rate; the direction of this joint shift (volume × precision) is the testable relationship.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between a team's shots volume and its shots-on-target rate (shots_on_target / shots) captures shooting precision. When both teams show recent surges in shot volume, the team whose on-target rate holds up or improves under higher shot loads is structurally different from one whose precision degrades. This cross-observable joint relationship between shot volume and on-target conversion is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint ratio across two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) compared across time windows. Neither observable alone, nor either compared to a single opponent-descriptor band, captures the precision-under-volume dynamic.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on TEAM_A's first-half vs second-half goals-FOR and goals-AGAINST rates alongside TEAM_B's first-half vs second-half goals-FOR and goals-AGAINST rates. The interaction of TEAM_A's second-half scoring tendency with TEAM_B's first-half conceding tendency (and vice versa) is the joint conditioning, not either team's half-split alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team is structurally a second-half scorer and the opponent is structurally a first-half conceder, the combined match goal-timing distribution is expected to be more concentrated in specific halves than either team's individual half-split would suggest in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The two teams show asymmetric within-match goal-scoring distributions across halves. TEAM_A scores and concedes more in the second half than the first, while TEAM_B concedes more in the first half than the second. The joint conditioning on both teams' half-level goal distributions simultaneously — rather than either team's half split in isolation — reveals whether the match's goal-timing profile is structurally skewed by the interaction of these asymmetries.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions (each team's half-level goal distribution) and their interaction. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band, nor to a simple home/away or recent/longrun split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compute the ratio of cards_2h-FOR to fouls-FOR (all-prior). Then compare this ratio between the two teams and against the competition context. Test whether a team with a higher foul rate also shows a proportionally higher or disproportionately higher second-half card rate — i.e., whether the foul-to-card conversion in the second half is linear or exhibits a threshold/saturation pattern.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: A team with a higher foul rate is expected to show a rising second-half card rate, but the rate of increase in cards per foul may saturate or accelerate beyond a foul-rate threshold, rather than scaling linearly.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Second-half card accumulation (cards_2h) is jointly related to foul production rates. A team that commits many fouls overall but whose second-half card rate is disproportionately high relative to its foul rate suggests a non-linear threshold effect — card issuance per foul rises in the second half beyond what foul volume alone predicts. The joint relationship between fouls-FOR and cards_2h-FOR, compared across both teams, is the mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint cross-observable relationship (fouls × cards_2h) with a within-match period dimension (second half only for cards), requiring two distinct observables to be related to each other. It is not a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on each team's possession-FOR rate and the opponent's offsides-FOR rate (which equals the team's offsides-AGAINST). Test whether the team with higher possession (TEAM_B) is associated with fewer opponent offside attempts, and whether TEAM_A's higher offside rate co-occurs with lower possession — examining the cross-team asymmetry in this joint relationship.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: A team with higher possession is expected to suppress opponent offside attempts (opponent offsides-FOR falls as possession-AGAINST rises), while a lower-possession team pressing higher up the pitch is expected to generate more offsides; the asymmetry between the two teams in this joint possession-offside relationship is the testable direction.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: TEAM_A generates substantially more offsides than TEAM_B (both for and against), while TEAM_B holds more possession. The joint relationship between a team's possession share and the offsides it draws from the opponent (offsides-AGAINST) captures whether high-possession teams suppress opponent offside attempts — i.e., whether possession dominance and opponent offside rate are inversely related across these two teams in a way that is asymmetric between them.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (possession and offsides) measured asymmetrically across the two teams simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one band, and the cross-team asymmetric joint relationship is structurally richer than any covered class.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's RECENT_5 shots-for (9.8) is materially below its ALL_PRIOR shots-for (12.01) AND Team A's RECENT_5 shots-against (16.4) is materially above its ALL_PRIOR shots-against (10.897). Measure goals-for in matches where both conditions hold simultaneously versus matches where neither holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals-for rises with shot production and falls when shot production is simultaneously depressed and shots-conceded is simultaneously elevated — the joint deterioration suppresses scoring more than either condition alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has dropped sharply in recent matches while the shots allowed against them has risen sharply; jointly, when a team's own recent shot production falls below its long-run average AND its recent shots-conceded rises above its long-run average simultaneously, its goals-for output in that match is suppressed relative to its long-run goals-for average.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint intersection of two distinct observables (shots-for trend AND shots-against trend) both deviating from their long-run baselines in the same match window. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band; it is a two-observable joint condition.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the possession gap between the two sides (Team B possession-for minus Team A possession-for) exceeds a threshold derived from the historical distribution of possession gaps in this competition. Within those matches, measure the corner-kick differential (Team A corners-for minus Team B corners-for).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner-kick differential for Team A falls (becomes more negative) as the possession gap in favour of Team B widens — the relationship between possession dominance and corner generation is tested jointly across both teams rather than for either team in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession has declined sharply in recent matches (from a long-run average above 51% to a recent average of 42.2%) while Team B maintains a stable high possession profile (55.8% long-run, 55% recent). The joint possession imbalance between the two sides — measured as the gap between Team B's possession-for and Team A's possession-for in the same match — is associated with a shift in corner-kick differential, because Team A's corners-for has also dropped in recent matches (3.0 recent vs 5.95 long-run) while Team B's corners-for is stable.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (possession and corner kicks) measured asymmetrically across both teams simultaneously, and tests a threshold/non-linear relationship between the possession gap and the corner differential. It is not reducible to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's offsides-for is above its long-run mean AND Team B's offsides-against is above its long-run mean simultaneously. Within those matches, measure the ratio of Team A goals-for to Team A shots-on-target-for versus the same ratio in matches where neither condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's goals-per-shot-on-target is suppressed when both Team A's offside rate and Team B's offside-trap rate are jointly elevated, relative to matches where only one or neither condition holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's offsides-against (opponents caught offside against Team B) has spiked sharply in recent matches (4.2 recent vs 2.45 long-run), while Team A's offsides-for (Team A caught offside) has also risen recently (2.8 recent vs 1.86 long-run). The joint condition — Team A running more high-line attacking movements (more offsides) into a defence that is also catching more opponents offside — is associated with a suppression of Team A's shots-on-target conversion into goals, because high-offside-trap defences tend to compress the space in which shots-on-target are generated.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable, two-team condition (Team A offsides-for AND Team B offsides-against) tested against a third observable (goals relative to shots-on-target). It cannot be reduced to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where both Team A's fouls-against (fouls committed against Team A, i.e. by the opponent) and Team B's fouls-for (fouls committed by Team B) are simultaneously above their respective long-run means. Within those matches, measure total second-half cards (cards_2h) for both teams combined versus the competition context baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total second-half cards rise above the sum of each team's individual card-rate baseline when both teams' foul loads are jointly elevated — the joint condition produces a super-additive card outcome relative to either team's individual foul profile.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half card rate (cards_2h FOR: 1.283, AGAINST: 1.424) and Team B's second-half card rate (FOR: 1.323, AGAINST: 1.312) both sit above the competition second-half card context mean (1.167). The joint foul-load profile — Team A's recent fouls-against (12.6) rising above its long-run mean (11.08) while Team B's recent fouls-for (12.0) also rises above its long-run mean (10.87) — suggests a match where both teams' foul rates are simultaneously elevated. Test whether the joint elevation of both teams' foul rates is associated with a super-additive increase in second-half cards relative to what each team's individual card rate would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This tests a joint two-team, two-observable condition (Team A fouls-against AND Team B fouls-for simultaneously elevated) against a within-match state outcome (second-half cards). It requires both a half-level split and a two-team joint foul condition, which is not reducible to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the attacking team (Team B) has a higher goals-for rate in the second half than the first half AND the defending team (Team A) has a higher goals-against rate in the second half than the first half. Measure whether the combined second-half goal rate in such matches exceeds the first-half goal rate by more than either team's individual half-split would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second-half goal rate for Team B rises relative to the first half when Team B's own second-half attacking uplift and Team A's second-half defensive drop-off are jointly present — the asymmetric half-split combination across both teams produces a larger second-half goal differential than either team's individual half-split alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals-against is split asymmetrically across halves (first-half: 0.444, second-half: 0.646 long-run), while Team B's goals-against is split more evenly (first-half: 0.677, second-half: 0.688). Team A concedes more in the second half than the first, while Team B concedes roughly equally across halves. The joint half-by-half goal-scoring profile — Team B's goals-for in the second half (0.812) exceeds its first-half goals-for (0.635), and Team A's second-half goals-against (0.646) exceeds its first-half goals-against (0.444) — creates a testable asymmetric within-match state: whether the combination of Team B's second-half attacking uplift and Team A's second-half defensive vulnerability jointly produces a higher second-half goal rate than the first-half goal rate in this specific matchup configuration.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split conditioned jointly on both teams' asymmetric half-by-half goal profiles simultaneously — an asymmetric cross-team, within-match state condition. It is not reducible to a single team's half-split in isolation.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's shots FOR (all-prior and recent-5) alongside Team B's shots_on_target FOR (all-prior and recent-5), and cross with Team A's shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST (all-prior and recent-5). The mechanism is the joint ratio of shots-to-shots-on-target for Team B versus the corresponding ratio Team A typically allows, not either observable in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's recent shots volume rises sharply (recent-5 vs all-prior) while shots-on-target stays flat or declines, the on-target rate suppresses relative to raw shot volume; this divergence is amplified or dampened by Team A's own shots-allowed vs shots-on-target-allowed ratio, producing a joint interaction that rises or saturates non-linearly.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot volume is structurally high relative to its shots-on-target conversion, and this ratio interacts with Team A's defensive shot-suppression profile: when a team generates many shots but a lower fraction on target, the joint relationship between total shots allowed and shots-on-target allowed for Team A determines whether Team B's volume translates into meaningful on-target pressure beyond what either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for both teams simultaneously — not a single observable mirrored against its opponent-allowed counterpart. The engine's covered class handles each observable independently; this mechanism is the cross-ratio interaction between the two.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's offsides FOR (all-prior vs recent-5 drift) and Team B's offsides AGAINST (all-prior vs recent-5 drift). The mechanism fires when both drift in the same direction simultaneously, indicating a shared structural shift in line-depth interaction rather than independent team-level changes.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's offsides FOR recent-5 is substantially below its all-prior mean AND Team B's offsides AGAINST recent-5 is also below its all-prior mean, the joint suppression of offsides is greater than the sum of the two independent suppressions — a non-additive interaction between attacking line depth and defensive line positioning.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offside rate FOR has collapsed in recent matches relative to its all-prior average, while Team B's offside rate AGAINST has also declined recently. The joint condition of both teams' offside observables moving in the same direction simultaneously — Team A running fewer offside traps or attacking lines and Team B conceding fewer offsides — suggests a structural interaction between Team A's attacking line depth and Team B's defensive line positioning that is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single observable compared against its opponent-allowed mirror. It requires the joint drift of the same observable across both teams' perspectives simultaneously (Team A FOR drift × Team B AGAINST drift), which is a two-dimensional regime shift not reducible to one observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team B's corner_kicks FOR SECOND_HALF (all-prior) versus Team B's corner_kicks FOR FIRST_HALF (all-prior), and cross with Team A's corner_kicks AGAINST SECOND_HALF (all-prior) versus Team A's corner_kicks AGAINST FIRST_HALF (all-prior). The mechanism is the half-level asymmetry in corner dominance for both teams simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's corner production is more concentrated in the second half than the first half; Team A's corner concession is also more concentrated in the second half. When both half-level asymmetries align, the second-half corner imbalance between the teams rises beyond what the full-match averages would suggest, indicating a within-match state saturation effect.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner kick production is structurally higher than Team A's, and both teams show a within-match half-level asymmetry in corners (first half vs second half). The joint relationship between Team B's second-half corner dominance and Team A's second-half corner concession rate — both measured at half resolution — determines whether the corner imbalance is concentrated in the second half, which is a within-match state dependence not visible at full-match resolution.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires half-level resolution for both teams simultaneously and a joint comparison of first-half vs second-half splits across two teams — not a single observable at full-match level with one conditioning band. The within-match state dependence (half) combined with the cross-team joint condition makes this structurally richer.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's cards_2h FOR (second-half, all-prior) alongside Team B's yellow_cards FOR AWAY (all-prior) versus HOME (all-prior), and cross with Team A's cards_2h AGAINST (second-half, all-prior) and Team A's yellow_cards AGAINST (all-prior). The mechanism is the interaction between second-half card period and venue dimension for Team B, tested against Team A's second-half card-concession profile.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's second-half card rate is suppressed relative to its full-match away yellow card rate; when Team B plays away and the second-half period is isolated, the card accumulation for Team B rises toward its away yellow card baseline rather than its low cards_2h average — an asymmetric venue × half interaction that diverges from either observable's standalone level.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's cards_2h (second-half cards FOR) is substantially lower than Team A's cards_2h and the competition context, while Team B's yellow_cards FOR away is notably higher than at home. The asymmetric relationship between Team B's second-half card accumulation and its venue-conditioned yellow card rate — combined with Team A's second-half card concession rate — creates a two-dimensional conditioning structure: second-half period × venue, applied asymmetrically across the two teams' card observables.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (cards_2h and yellow_cards) jointly, conditioned on two dimensions simultaneously (second-half period AND venue), applied asymmetrically across the two teams. This is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's possession FOR (all-prior and recent-5) and Team A's fouls FOR (all-prior, recent-5, and venue split HOME vs AWAY). The mechanism tests whether Team A's foul rate co-varies with the degree of possession imbalance against them — a cross-observable joint relationship between two structurally distinct metrics across the two teams.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: As Team B's possession advantage over Team A grows (measured by the gap between Team B's possession FOR and Team A's possession FOR), Team A's foul rate rises — and this relationship is amplified when Team A plays at home (where their foul rate is lower on average) versus away, suggesting a threshold or saturation in foul response to possession pressure that differs by venue.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession dominance is structurally high (all-prior and recent-5), while Team A's fouls FOR away are elevated relative to home. The joint relationship between Team B's possession level and Team A's foul rate — where higher possession by Team B forces more defensive fouls from Team A — creates a cross-observable interaction: possession (Team B FOR) × fouls (Team A FOR), where the foul rate is expected to rise as a function of the possession imbalance, not independently of it.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and fouls) across the two teams, not a single observable mirrored. It also involves a threshold/saturation structure (foul response to possession imbalance) and a venue dimension interacting with the cross-observable relationship — three structural elements beyond the covered class.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A being the home side. Jointly examine: (a) Team A shots FOR all-prior vs recent-5, (b) Team A shots_on_target FOR all-prior vs recent-5, and (c) Team A goals FOR all-prior vs recent-5. The mechanism fires when shots volume is stable but shots_on_target and goals have diverged downward in the recent window relative to the long-run baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shots_on_target FOR recent-5 falls below shots_on_target FOR all-prior while shots FOR remains stable, goals FOR recent-5 is suppressed relative to goals FOR all-prior — i.e., conversion efficiency declines non-proportionally with the on-target rate drop.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume-to-goals conversion relationship: when Team A generates a high volume of shots (near its home average) but its recent shots-on-target rate has declined relative to its all-prior rate, its goals-for output is suppressed relative to its long-run average. The joint pattern of shots FOR, shots_on_target FOR, and goals FOR across the all-prior versus recent-5 windows captures a conversion-efficiency regime shift that is not visible from any single observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint three-observable relationship (shots, shots_on_target, goals) across two temporal windows simultaneously. It cannot be reduced to any single observable compared against a single band or baseline; the mechanism is about the cross-observable divergence pattern, not any one metric in isolation.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A as home side. Jointly examine: Team A shots AGAINST, shots_on_target AGAINST, goals AGAINST, and fouls AGAINST across all-prior vs recent-5 windows. The mechanism is identified when shots/goals allowed rise while fouls allowed fall in the same recent window.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shots AGAINST and goals AGAINST recent-5 are elevated above all-prior, but fouls AGAINST recent-5 is below all-prior, the defensive regime has shifted in a way that is not captured by any single observable — the combination of more shots allowed with fewer fouls suggests opponents are finding space without being fouled, a qualitatively distinct defensive state.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's defensive deterioration is asymmetric across observables: in the recent-5 window, shots conceded, shots_on_target conceded, and goals conceded have all risen sharply relative to all-prior averages, while fouls conceded has fallen. This joint pattern — more shots allowed but fewer fouls drawn — suggests a structural defensive-shape change rather than a simple form dip, and the cross-observable asymmetry (shots/goals up, fouls down) is the testable signal.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship across four distinct observables (shots, shots_on_target, goals, fouls) in the AGAINST perspective, requiring simultaneous cross-observable comparison. No single-observable baseline or band captures the asymmetric directional divergence across these metrics.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on: (a) Team A corners FOR recent-5 vs all-prior (declining), and (b) Team B corners AGAINST recent-5 vs all-prior (rising sharply). The mechanism tests whether the cross-team joint signal — one team's recent attacking corner production declining while the opponent's recent defensive corner concession is rising — produces a non-additive interaction in expected corner volume.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B corners AGAINST recent-5 is substantially elevated above its all-prior average AND Team A corners FOR recent-5 is below its all-prior average, the two signals partially offset each other; the net corner volume relationship is non-linear relative to what either team's individual trend would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner-kick concession rate has spiked sharply in recent matches relative to its all-prior average, while Team A's corner-kick production has declined in recent matches relative to its all-prior average. The joint cross-team divergence between Team B's corners AGAINST recent-5 and Team A's corners FOR recent-5 — both moving in the same direction (more corners for the attacking side) — creates a compounded corner-volume signal that neither team's individual trend alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct team-direction combinations of the same observable (Team A FOR recent vs all-prior, Team B AGAINST recent vs all-prior) and testing their joint interaction. This is not a single-observable single-band comparison; it is a cross-team, cross-window joint signal.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the second half as the within-match state. Jointly examine: (a) Team A goals FOR first-half vs second-half all-prior, and (b) Team B goals AGAINST first-half vs second-half all-prior. The mechanism fires when Team A's second-half scoring rate exceeds its first-half rate AND Team B's second-half concession rate exceeds its first-half concession rate.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's goals FOR second-half all-prior exceeds goals FOR first-half all-prior, and Team B's goals AGAINST second-half all-prior exceeds goals AGAINST first-half all-prior, the second half is expected to be disproportionately goal-rich relative to the first half — a compounded within-match-state signal not reducible to either team's half-split in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Both teams show a within-match half-level asymmetry in goals: Team A scores more in the second half than the first half (all-prior), while Team B concedes more in the second half than the first half (all-prior). The joint alignment of Team A's second-half goal-scoring tendency with Team B's second-half goal-conceding tendency — both pointing in the same direction — is a cross-team, within-match-state interaction that is richer than either team's half-split alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint cross-team within-match-state relationship: it requires simultaneously conditioning on the half (within-match state) and combining two distinct team-direction signals (Team A FOR, Team B AGAINST) for the same observable. Neither team's half-split alone, nor a simple home/away band, captures this joint alignment.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the second half as the within-match state. Jointly examine: (a) Team A cards_2h FOR and AGAINST vs competition context cards_2h, and (b) Team B cards_2h FOR and AGAINST vs competition context cards_2h. The mechanism tests whether both teams' second-half card rates sit on the same side of the competition norm (both elevated or both suppressed), producing a compounded signal.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both Team A's and Team B's second-half card rates (FOR and AGAINST) are jointly elevated above the competition-context second-half card baseline, second-half card volume rises with the joint elevation; when both are suppressed, it falls — the joint alignment amplifies the signal relative to either team's individual deviation from the norm.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The second-half cards (cards_2h) environment is jointly shaped by both teams' second-half card tendencies relative to the competition context. Team A's cards_2h FOR and AGAINST (second-half) and Team B's cards_2h FOR and AGAINST (second-half) can be jointly compared against the competition-context cards_2h baseline to identify whether both teams simultaneously sit above or below the competition norm — a two-team, two-direction joint signal against a shared reference that is not reducible to either team's individual card rate.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two teams' second-half card rates (both FOR and AGAINST perspectives) against a shared competition-context reference, within the second-half state. It is not a single-observable single-band comparison; it is a four-signal joint alignment test against a competition baseline.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on (a) Team B's recent-5 corner-kicks FOR vs. Team B's all-prior corner-kicks FOR, and (b) Team A's recent-5 corner-kicks FOR vs. Team A's all-prior corner-kicks FOR. The mechanism activates when one team's recent window diverges substantially from its long-run level while the other team's does not — creating an asymmetric regime rather than a symmetric shift.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's recent corner-kick production collapses relative to its long-run level while the opponent's remains stable, the combined (total) corner count is suppressed relative to the sum of the two teams' all-prior averages, and the corner-kick share skews toward the stable team.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner-kick production shows a sharp divergence between its all-prior average and its most-recent-5 average, while Team A's corner-kick production remains stable across those two windows. The joint pattern of one team's recent corner-kick collapse alongside a stable opponent's corner-kick output may predict a lopsided corner distribution in the fixture that is not captured by either team's single-observable mirror alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint, asymmetric comparison across two distinct observables (each team's own recent-vs-long-run divergence for the same metric), not a single observable against one band. The engine's covered class handles each team's recent vs. long-run level independently; it does not measure the interaction between the two teams' divergence directions simultaneously.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on (a) Team A's shots_on_target FOR at home vs. away, (b) Team A's shots FOR at home vs. away, and (c) Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST all-prior vs. competition context. The mechanism tests whether the combination of Team A's home-elevated shot accuracy and Team B's above-average defensive leakiness jointly predicts a higher-than-additive on-target volume for Team A.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's home shots-on-target rate (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR at home) is substantially higher than its away rate, and the opponent's shots_on_target AGAINST rate exceeds the competition baseline, the combined effect on Team A's on-target volume rises more than either factor alone would suggest — a super-additive joint relationship.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots-on-target FOR shows a notable divergence between home and away venues (home substantially higher than away), while Team B's shots-on-target AGAINST is elevated relative to the competition context. The joint relationship between Team A's venue-conditioned shot accuracy (shots_on_target / shots) and Team B's defensive shot-on-target concession rate may predict a non-linear interaction in on-target volume that neither team's single-observable mirror captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) jointly, plus two distinct conditioning dimensions (venue for one team, opponent defensive leakiness vs. competition baseline for the other). It is not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where both Team A's recent-5 fouls FOR and Team B's recent-5 fouls FOR exceed their respective all-prior averages, and both exceed the competition context foul mean. Then test whether cards_2h (second-half cards for each team) is elevated relative to competition context cards_2h when this bilateral foul-escalation condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams simultaneously show recent foul rates above their own long-run averages and above the competition baseline, second-half card volume rises above the competition context cards_2h baseline — and this joint bilateral condition predicts a larger elevation than either team's foul escalation alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Both teams show elevated foul rates (FOR) relative to the competition context, and both show a recent-5 foul rate that is higher than their all-prior average. The joint condition of both teams simultaneously trending upward in fouls — rather than just one — may predict a threshold-like escalation in second-half cards (cards_2h), since card accumulation in the second half is a downstream consequence of foul volume across both sides.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship across two distinct observables (fouls and cards_2h) and requires both teams' foul trends to be elevated simultaneously — a bilateral, cross-observable condition. The engine covers each team's fouls vs. competition baseline independently, but not the joint bilateral escalation interacting with second-half card outcomes.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on (a) Team B's recent-5 possession FOR vs. all-prior possession FOR (large upward shift), (b) Team A's possession FOR all-prior vs. competition context, and (c) each team's offsides FOR and AGAINST rates. The mechanism tests whether a team undergoing a possession-regime shift (from low to near-parity) shows a corresponding shift in its offside generation rate that is not predicted by its long-run offside average.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent possession level rises substantially toward parity from a historically low baseline, its offsides FOR rate rises above its long-run average — reflecting a transition from a counter-attacking to a more possession-based attacking shape — and this relationship is stronger than what either observable's own recent-vs-long-run comparison would suggest independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession FOR shows a large divergence between its all-prior average (substantially below 50) and its recent-5 average (near 50), while Team A's possession FOR is also below 50 all-prior but slightly higher in recent-5. The joint possession regime — where both teams historically concede possession but one is recently trending toward parity — may interact with each team's offside rate in a non-trivial way: as a low-possession team gains possession, its attacking line positioning changes, affecting offsides generated and conceded.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and offsides) where the possession regime shift for one team is used to condition the expected offside rate. It is not a single observable with one band, and it involves an asymmetric cross-observable interaction between the two teams' possession and offside profiles.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on (a) Team A's goals FOR first-half vs. second-half split, (b) Team B's goals AGAINST first-half vs. second-half split, and (c) Team B's goals FOR first-half vs. second-half split vs. Team A's goals AGAINST first-half vs. second-half split. The mechanism tests whether the bilateral alignment of back-loaded goal production and back-loaded defensive vulnerability produces a non-additive concentration of second-half goals.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both the attacking team's goal-scoring and the defending team's defensive vulnerability are disproportionately concentrated in the second half, the ratio of second-half goals to first-half goals in the match exceeds what either team's individual half-split ratio would predict — a super-additive second-half goal concentration.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals FOR splits strongly by half (first-half mean lower than second-half mean), and Team B's goals AGAINST also splits by half (first-half conceded lower than second-half conceded). The joint condition — where the attacking team's goal production is back-loaded AND the defending team's defensive vulnerability is also back-loaded — may produce a threshold-like concentration of goals in the second half that exceeds what either team's individual half-split would predict additively.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint, asymmetric comparison across both teams' half-level splits for the same observable (goals), combining FOR and AGAINST perspectives across two teams simultaneously. The engine covers each team's half-split independently, but not the bilateral alignment of both teams' half-splits interacting to produce a non-additive within-match state.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute the joint pairing of (Team B corners FOR) with (Team A corners AGAINST) and separately (Team A corners FOR) with (Team B corners AGAINST), then assess whether the combined cross-team corner imbalance signal — both dimensions simultaneously — predicts corner totals and corner winner beyond what either team's own mirror alone captures.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Matches where one team's FOR corners and the opponent's AGAINST corners are both extreme in the same direction (large imbalance on both dimensions simultaneously) should show a stronger skew in corner distribution toward the dominant team than matches where only one dimension is extreme.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner-kick dominance (high FOR, low AGAINST) interacts jointly with Team A's corner-kick deficit (low FOR, high AGAINST) to produce an asymmetric corner-kick imbalance that is structurally different from either team's single-observable mirror. The joint cross-team corner differential — Team B's FOR minus Team A's FOR, and Team A's AGAINST minus Team B's AGAINST — should be measured together as a two-observable, two-team joint signal.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: The engine covers each team's own FOR vs opponent's AGAINST as a same-observable mirror independently. This mechanism requires the joint evaluation of both teams' FOR and AGAINST corner rates simultaneously — a two-team, two-perspective joint relationship — which is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner production by half for both teams. Condition on whether Team B's first-half corner FOR rate substantially exceeds its second-half rate, and whether Team A's first-half corner AGAINST rate differs from its second-half AGAINST rate, to test whether the half-level imbalance is consistent or reverses across halves.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's first-half corner FOR rate is disproportionately higher than its second-half rate, and Team A's first-half corner AGAINST rate is also elevated, the first half should show a stronger corner skew toward Team B than the second half — i.e., the within-match half distribution of corners is non-uniform and directionally predictable.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner-kick production is heavily front-loaded into the first half (FOR first-half mean notably higher than second-half mean), while Team A concedes corners more evenly across halves. The joint within-match half-level distribution of corners — Team B's first-half corner FOR rate relative to its second-half rate, conditioned on Team A's half-level AGAINST rates — should be measured as a within-match state mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split of a single observable conditioned on both teams' half-level rates simultaneously — a within-match state dependence combining two teams' half-period observables. It is not a simple recent vs. long-run comparison or a single coarse band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on (a) the possession gap between the two teams being large (Team B FOR possession far above competition context mean of 50%) and (b) Team A's shots-on-target FOR rate relative to its shots FOR rate (on-target conversion ratio). Test whether the combination of extreme possession asymmetry and low shot quality for the possession-deficit team produces a suppression of goals FOR for Team A beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When possession asymmetry is large and the lower-possession team's shot-on-target ratio is also below the competition mean, goals FOR for the lower-possession team should be further suppressed relative to matches where only one of these conditions holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's high possession dominance (FOR ~69%) is jointly paired with Team A's low shot conversion efficiency (high shots AGAINST, low goals FOR relative to shots FOR). The relationship between Team B's possession advantage and Team A's shots-to-goals conversion ratio should be measured as a joint two-observable signal: whether extreme possession asymmetry co-occurs with suppressed shot quality for the lower-possession team (Team A), producing a non-linear interaction between possession share and shot conversion.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and shot quality ratio) for two different teams simultaneously. It cannot be reduced to a single observable mirror or a single coarse band split — it requires the interaction of possession asymmetry with shot conversion efficiency across teams.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's first-half goals FOR rate and Team A's second-half goals AGAINST rate. Test whether matches where Team B has a high first-half scoring rate AND Team A has a high second-half conceding rate produce a specific within-match goal timing pattern (goals concentrated in both halves but for different structural reasons) that differs from the competition context baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's first-half goals FOR rate is elevated above competition context and Team A's second-half goals AGAINST rate is also elevated, the within-match goal distribution should show a non-uniform half-level pattern — with Team B goals skewed earlier and Team A concessions skewed later — rather than the uniform distribution implied by treating each half independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's goals are heavily skewed toward the first half (FOR first-half mean ~1.21 vs second-half ~1.46 across 80 matches, but first-half rate is notably high relative to competition context goals mean of ~1.47 per match total), while Team A concedes more in the second half than the first half. The asymmetric within-match half-level goal distribution — Team B scoring more in the first half while Team A concedes more in the second half — should be measured as a joint cross-team half-level goal timing mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two teams' half-level goal rates simultaneously (Team B first-half FOR and Team A second-half AGAINST), which is a within-match state dependence across two distinct half-period observables for two teams. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on (a) Team A's recent-5 foul FOR rate being substantially below its all-prior rate AND (b) Team B's recent-5 foul FOR rate being substantially below its all-prior rate. Test whether this joint foul-rate regime shift (both teams trending lower simultaneously) is associated with suppressed second-half card volume relative to the competition context cards_2h baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams show a concurrent downward regime shift in foul rates (recent trend below long-run baseline for both), second-half card volume should be suppressed relative to the competition context mean — and this suppression should be stronger than when only one team shows a foul-rate decline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's foul rate has declined sharply in recent matches (FOR recent-5 mean ~9.2 vs all-prior ~12.0), while Team B's foul rate has also declined (FOR recent-5 ~8.6 vs all-prior ~9.5). The joint recent-trend trajectory of both teams' foul rates — both declining simultaneously — should be measured against the second-half cards rate (cards_2h), to test whether a joint foul-rate regime shift for both teams co-occurs with a suppression of second-half card volume relative to the competition context baseline.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism requires jointly conditioning on two teams' recent-vs-long-run foul rate trajectories simultaneously, then linking that joint regime shift to a different observable (cards_2h). It combines a sequencing/regime structure (recent vs. all-prior) for two teams with a cross-observable relationship (fouls to cards), which is not reducible to any single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the cross-team pairing: Team A's shots-FOR (16.0 all-prior, 14.6 recent) against Team B's shots-on-target-AGAINST (4.156 all-prior, 6.2 recent), AND Team B's shots-FOR (10.442 all-prior, 9.2 recent) against Team A's shots-on-target-AGAINST (3.312 all-prior, 3.8 recent). The asymmetry is that Team A produces far more shots but Team B allows more shots-on-target per match than Team A does. Measure whether the combined on-target output in matches where one side has a large shots-volume advantage but the other side has a higher shots-on-target-allowed rate diverges from the competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total match shots-on-target rises when the high-volume shooting team faces a high shots-on-target-allowed opponent, but the relationship is asymmetric: the high-volume side's on-target count rises more steeply than the low-volume side's, producing a skewed distribution of on-target activity between the two teams rather than a symmetric uplift.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A generates substantially more shots and shots-on-target than Team B, while Team B concedes shots-on-target at a higher rate than Team A concedes. The joint relationship between one team's shot-production volume and the opponent's shots-on-target-allowed rate — across both sides simultaneously — conditions the match's total on-target activity in a way that neither team's own shot mirror alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (shots volume FOR one team, shots-on-target AGAINST the other team) for both sides simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable mirror or a single observable with one coarse band; it is an asymmetric cross-team, cross-observable relationship.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's possession-FOR (~60%) and Team A's corners-FOR (6.36 all-prior, 5.2 recent) alongside Team B's possession-FOR (~53%) and Team B's corners-FOR (5.61 all-prior, 4.0 recent). The mechanism tests whether, in matches where one team holds a large possession advantage over the other (not just over a league baseline), the possession-to-corner conversion ratio for the dominant side is higher than for the subordinate side — i.e., whether the relationship between possession share and corner generation is non-linear or asymmetric across the two sides of the same match.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The team with the larger possession advantage in a given match generates corners at a disproportionately higher rate relative to its possession share than the lower-possession team, suggesting a non-linear or threshold relationship between possession dominance and corner production.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A holds dominant possession (~60%) and generates far more corners (6.36 all-prior) than Team B (5.61 all-prior), while Team B concedes fewer corners (4.60) than Team A concedes (3.90). The joint relationship between possession dominance and corner-kick generation — across both teams — tests whether the possession-to-corners conversion rate differs between the dominant-possession side and the lower-possession side in the same match.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) for both teams simultaneously, testing a cross-observable ratio relationship. It is not a single-observable mirror or a single-band split; it requires measuring the possession-to-corners conversion rate as a function of the possession gap between the two sides.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on each team's fouls-FOR and yellow_cards-FOR across all prior matches. Compute the yellow-cards-per-foul ratio for each team and test whether the team with the higher absolute foul rate (Team B) also has a disproportionately higher yellow-card-per-foul ratio, or whether the relationship saturates. Additionally, test whether the asymmetry in foul profiles (Team A low-foul, Team B high-foul) predicts a divergence in yellow card totals beyond what each team's yellow card average alone would suggest.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Yellow cards per foul rise with total foul volume in a non-linear (threshold/saturation) manner: teams committing more fouls accumulate yellow cards at a disproportionately higher rate per foul, and the asymmetry between the two teams' foul profiles amplifies the difference in their yellow card totals beyond a simple additive expectation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A commits far fewer fouls (9.17 all-prior) than Team B (13.69 all-prior), while Team B concedes fewer fouls (11.97) than Team A concedes (14.13). This creates a strongly asymmetric foul-committing profile between the two sides. The joint relationship between each team's foul rate and its yellow-card rate tests whether the team that commits fewer fouls (Team A, 1.62 YC/match) accumulates yellow cards at a lower rate per foul than the team that commits more fouls (Team B, 2.26 YC/match), and whether this ratio diverges from competition norms.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) and tests a ratio/non-linear relationship between them, not a simple mirror of either observable alone. The asymmetry across the two teams adds a second dimension that cannot be captured by a single-observable band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the within-match half split: compare each team's first-half corner rate to its second-half corner rate (both FOR and AGAINST), and test whether the match-level first-half share of total corners is elevated when Team A (first-half concentrated) hosts Team B (flat distribution). This requires half-level resolution and the joint conditioning on both halves' corner counts for both teams simultaneously — not just a single half's average.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a first-half-concentrated corner producer (Team A) faces a team with a flat half-distribution (Team B), the first half accounts for a larger share of total match corners than the competition baseline, with the concentration effect driven primarily by the home team's first-half production rather than a symmetric uplift across both halves.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A produces corners heavily in the first half (3.41 FH vs 2.93 SH all-prior) while Team B's corner production is more evenly split (2.83 FH vs 2.77 SH). The within-match half-level distribution of corner production differs between the two teams. This tests whether the team with a first-half corner concentration advantage (Team A) generates a disproportionate share of total match corners in the first half when facing a team with a flatter half-distribution (Team B), and whether this half-concentration pattern is stable or regresses.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires half-level data resolution and conditions on the within-match temporal distribution (first-half vs second-half ratio) of a single observable for both teams simultaneously. It is not a simple single-observable split by one coarse band; it tests a within-match sequencing/regime structure across two halves jointly for both sides.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on both teams' half-level goal-FOR and goal-AGAINST rates. Specifically: Team A's second-half scoring rate (1.14) combined with Team B's second-half conceding rate (0.77) versus Team A's first-half scoring rate (0.90) combined with Team B's first-half conceding rate (0.64). Test whether the second-half goal concentration is amplified when both the scoring team's second-half production advantage AND the conceding team's second-half defensive vulnerability align in the same direction — a two-dimensional half-level conditioning that cannot be reduced to either team's half split alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second-half share of total match goals is elevated beyond competition norms when the attacking team has a second-half scoring concentration AND the defending team has a second-half conceding concentration, with the effect stronger than either team's half-split pattern would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A scores more goals in the second half (1.14 SH vs 0.90 FH all-prior) while conceding more in the second half (0.53 SH vs 0.43 FH). Team B scores more in the first half relative to its second half (0.53 FH vs 0.69 SH all-prior) and concedes more in the second half (0.77 SH vs 0.64 FH). The cross-team asymmetry in half-level goal-scoring and goal-conceding profiles — where Team A is a second-half scorer facing a team that also concedes more in the second half — tests whether the combined second-half goal rate in this specific matchup exceeds the first-half rate by more than competition norms would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This conditions simultaneously on two teams' half-level goal profiles (FOR and AGAINST) across both halves, requiring half-level data resolution and a joint two-team, two-observable-period conditioning. It is not reducible to a single team's half split or a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A holds possession above a threshold (e.g. >65%) AND the opponent commits fouls above a threshold (e.g. >13/match). Measure Team A's corner_kicks FOR in those joint-condition matches versus the unconditional mean.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A corner_kicks FOR rises when both high possession dominance and high opponent foul rate are jointly present, beyond what either condition alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When Team A's dominant possession profile (historically ~69%) is paired against Team B's high foul rate (historically ~14 fouls/match away), the joint interaction between possession differential and foul volume should produce an elevated corner-kick yield for Team A beyond what either observable alone would predict. Specifically, Team A's corner production is jointly conditioned on both its own possession dominance and the opponent's foul-committing tendency.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires two distinct observables (possession AND fouls) to be jointly above thresholds simultaneously — it cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band. It is an asymmetric cross-observable interaction: Team A's possession production is paired with Team B's foul concession, not a mirror of the same observable.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the possession differential between the dominant team and the opponent exceeds a threshold (e.g. >30 percentage points). Measure the difference between the lower-possession team's cards_2h FOR and the higher-possession team's cards_2h FOR across those matches, and test whether this gap widens as possession asymmetry increases.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The gap between the lower-possession team's second-half cards and the higher-possession team's second-half cards rises with increasing possession asymmetry — a non-linear threshold relationship rather than a flat split.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half card accumulation (cards_2h FOR ~1.85/match) is structurally elevated relative to Team A's second-half card accumulation (cards_2h FOR ~1.15/match) and relative to the competition context (~1.57/match). The joint relationship between Team A's high possession dominance and Team B's elevated second-half card rate suggests that as possession imbalance persists into the second half, Team B's disciplinary pressure rises non-linearly — i.e., the gap between the two teams' second-half card rates is conditioned on the degree of possession asymmetry in the match.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and cards_2h) where the direction is asymmetric across the two sides. It is not a single observable with one band; it requires measuring how one observable (cards_2h differential) responds to the continuous level of another (possession differential), testing for threshold/saturation behavior.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's shots FOR exceeds a threshold AND the opponent's shots_on_target AGAINST (i.e., allowed) exceeds a threshold. Measure Team A's goals FOR in those joint-condition matches versus matches where only one condition holds, testing whether the joint condition produces a disproportionate uplift in goals.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A goals FOR is disproportionately elevated when both high shot volume and high opponent defensive permissiveness (shots_on_target allowed) are jointly present, suggesting a super-additive interaction rather than independent contributions.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-to-goal conversion efficiency (goals FOR relative to shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR) is jointly conditioned on both the volume of shots produced and the quality of opponent defensive pressure (opponent shots_on_target AGAINST allowed). Team B allows relatively more shots on target against (4.17/match) compared to the competition context (4.41/match), while Team A produces high shot volumes (16.87 shots FOR, 6.74 on target). The joint relationship between Team A's shot volume and Team B's defensive permissiveness across both shots and shots_on_target dimensions should be tested for a non-additive interaction.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves three distinct observables (shots, shots_on_target, goals) in a joint conditioning structure — specifically testing whether the relationship between shot volume and goals is moderated by a second observable (opponent defensive permissiveness). This is not reducible to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split by half. In the second half, jointly measure Team B's cards_2h FOR and goals AGAINST (second half). Test whether matches where Team B accumulates more second-half cards are also matches where Team B concedes more second-half goals — a within-match joint co-movement across two distinct observables in the second-half period.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's second-half goals conceded rises with Team B's second-half card accumulation — the two observables co-move within the second-half regime, suggesting a joint disciplinary-defensive breakdown pattern.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals are distributed asymmetrically across halves (1.19 FOR in first half vs 1.42 FOR in second half), while Team B's goals against are also asymmetrically distributed (0.47 AGAINST in first half vs 0.71 AGAINST in second half). The joint within-match state structure — where Team B concedes more in the second half — should be tested against Team B's own second-half card accumulation (cards_2h FOR ~1.85), to determine whether Team B's elevated second-half disciplinary burden is jointly associated with their elevated second-half goal concession, forming a within-match regime where both observables co-move in the second half.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match half-level split (requiring half resolution) combined with a joint relationship between two distinct observables (cards_2h and goals) for the same team in the same period. It is not a single observable with one band, and it requires half-level data resolution.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's offsides AGAINST (opponent offsides generated by Team A's defensive line) exceeds a threshold. Measure Team B's fouls FOR in those matches versus matches below the threshold. Test whether the two observables — opponent offsides generated and opponent fouls committed — are jointly elevated, indicating a tactical regime interaction.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's fouls FOR rises in matches where Team A generates more opponent offsides, suggesting the two observables are jointly elevated under a high-press/high-line tactical regime — a non-trivial cross-observable relationship.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's away foul rate (14.74/match away) is substantially higher than their home foul rate (12.54/match home) and higher than the competition context (12.93/match). Team A's offsides AGAINST (4.58/match all-prior, but dropping to 3.2 in recent 5) suggests Team A deploys a high defensive line that generates opponent offsides. The joint relationship between Team B's elevated away foul rate and Team A's high-line defensive structure (proxied by offsides AGAINST) should be tested: specifically, whether matches where Team A generates many opponent offsides are also matches where Team B commits more fouls, reflecting a joint tactical interaction between Team A's pressing/high-line and Team B's foul-committing response.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (offsides and fouls) from different perspectives (Team A's offsides AGAINST as a proxy for Team A's defensive structure, and Team B's fouls FOR as a response), forming an asymmetric cross-observable relationship. It is not a single observable with one band, and the conditioning is on a continuous observable (offsides AGAINST) rather than a coarse venue or competition band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute Team A's historical shots-FOR to shots_on_target-FOR ratio (all-prior) and Team B's shots-AGAINST to shots_on_target-AGAINST ratio (all-prior and recent-5). Condition on the joint cross-team pairing of these two ratios simultaneously — neither ratio alone, but their product/interaction — to assess whether the combined on-target volume rises or is suppressed relative to competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total match shots-on-target rises when both Team A's own conversion ratio and Team B's allowed conversion ratio are jointly elevated; suppressed when either ratio is jointly low — the joint product diverges from what either single-observable mirror would predict independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR) jointly with Team B's defensive shot-suppression ratio (shots AGAINST vs shots_on_target AGAINST) determines the combined on-target shot volume in the match. When one side produces many shots but a low fraction on target while the opponent allows many shots but a high fraction on target, the joint interaction — not either observable alone — shapes total shots-on-target.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for two different sides in an asymmetric cross-team pairing. It is not reducible to a single observable compared against what an opponent allows, nor to one observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner_kicks FOR into first-half and second-half averages for Team A; split corner_kicks AGAINST into first-half and second-half averages for Team B. Condition on the joint half-level pairing: whether both teams show a second-half-skewed corner profile simultaneously, versus a first-half-skewed or balanced profile.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half corner volume rises above the full-match per-half average when Team A's second-half corner production rate exceeds its first-half rate AND Team B's second-half corner concession rate exceeds its first-half rate jointly; the relationship is suppressed when the half-level profiles are misaligned.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetry between Team A's first-half corner production and second-half corner production (a within-match half-level split) interacts with Team B's corresponding half-level corner concession pattern to determine whether corner volume is front-loaded or back-loaded in this specific fixture. When Team A generates more corners in the second half than the first, and Team B concedes more corners in the second half than the first, the second-half corner total is jointly amplified beyond what full-match averages suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This uses within-match half-level resolution (first-half vs second-half splits) for two distinct observables (Team A FOR and Team B AGAINST) simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one coarse band, nor a simple home/away or recent/long-run split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's historical yellow_cards FOR rate and Team A's historical fouls AGAINST rate (fouls drawn). The mechanism activates when both are simultaneously elevated relative to competition baseline — a two-observable, two-team asymmetric joint condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B yellow cards rise when Team B's own yellow card rate and Team A's foul-drawing rate are jointly above competition baseline; the relationship is weaker when only one of the two conditions holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's yellow card accumulation rate (yellow_cards FOR) jointly with Team A's foul-drawing rate (fouls AGAINST — fouls committed against Team A, i.e. fouls drawn by Team A) determines the disciplinary pressure on Team B in this fixture. When Team B commits fouls at an elevated rate AND Team A draws fouls at an elevated rate, the joint interaction predicts elevated yellow card volume for Team B beyond what either observable alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-observable relationship: Team B's yellow cards are conditioned jointly on Team B's own foul tendency AND Team A's foul-drawing tendency — two distinct observables across two different teams. Not reducible to one observable mirrored against what an opponent allows.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on (a) the possession imbalance between Team A (home) and Team B (away) using both all-prior and recent-5 windows, and (b) the drift in Team A's corner production (recent-5 vs all-prior) alongside Team B's corner concession drift (recent-5 vs all-prior). The mechanism tests whether possession advantage reliably converts to corner advantage, or whether recent drift in corner rates decouples the two.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner volume for Team A rises with possession advantage when Team A's recent corner production rate has not declined relative to its long-run rate; when recent corner production has drifted downward despite stable possession, the possession-to-corner relationship saturates or decouples.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between possession differential (Team A possession FOR minus Team B possession FOR, i.e. the possession imbalance) and corner kick differential determines whether possession dominance translates into corner dominance. When Team A holds more possession at home but its corner production has recently declined (recent-5 vs all-prior), while Team B concedes more corners recently, the possession-to-corner translation efficiency is the joint mechanism of interest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) incorporating a regime/drift dimension (recent-5 vs all-prior window comparison) for both teams simultaneously. Not reducible to either observable alone with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split goals FOR into first-half and second-half averages for Team A; split goals AGAINST into first-half and second-half averages for Team B. Condition on the joint half-level pairing: whether Team A's second-half scoring rate exceeds its first-half rate AND Team B's second-half concession rate exceeds its first-half rate simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goal volume rises above the per-half average when Team A's second-half scoring rate is higher than its first-half rate AND Team B's second-half concession rate is higher than its first-half rate jointly; the effect is attenuated when the half-level profiles are misaligned between the two teams.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between Team A's goals-FOR half-level split (first-half vs second-half scoring rate) and Team B's goals-AGAINST half-level split (first-half vs second-half concession rate) determines whether goal-scoring is concentrated in a particular half. When Team A scores more in the second half than the first, and Team B concedes more in the second half than the first, the second-half goal volume is jointly amplified — an asymmetric cross-team, within-match state mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This uses within-match half-level resolution (first-half vs second-half splits) applied asymmetrically across two teams (Team A FOR and Team B AGAINST) simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one coarse band, nor a simple venue or recent/long-run split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on both teams simultaneously showing a recent-5 possession mean that is lower than their all-prior possession mean (both teams are in a low-possession recent regime). Within that joint condition, measure whether shots_on_target FOR is suppressed relative to all-prior for the possession-losing side, and shots_on_target AGAINST is elevated for the possession-conceding side.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams' recent possession is below their long-run average, the combined shots_on_target FOR across both teams is suppressed relative to the combined all-prior baseline, suggesting a jointly compressed attacking output regime.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When a team's recent possession share drops materially below its long-run average (indicating a regime shift toward a more defensive or reactive posture), its shots-on-target production also falls relative to its long-run average, while the opponent's shots-on-target allowed rises. The joint pattern of possession-drop and shots-on-target divergence across both teams simultaneously is the signal of interest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint condition across two distinct observables (possession AND shots_on_target) for both teams simultaneously. It is not reducible to one observable with one band — it requires the co-movement of possession and shots_on_target across both sides to be evaluated together.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compute the ratio of shots_on_target FOR to shots FOR across all-prior and recent-5 windows. Condition on the case where Team A's ratio is declining (recent < all-prior) while Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST is rising (recent > all-prior), and vice versa. Measure whether this asymmetric cross-team pattern is associated with a directional shift in goals FOR/AGAINST relative to baseline.
