mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's shot accuracy is declining while the opponent's defensive shots-on-target-allowed is rising, goals FOR for the accuracy-declining team are suppressed relative to what either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: A team's shots-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shot accuracy) interacts asymmetrically with the opponent's defensive solidity as measured by shots-on-target allowed. Specifically, when one team's shot accuracy (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR) is trending downward in recent matches while the opponent's shots_on_target AGAINST is trending upward, the joint signal differs from either observable read in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a ratio of two observables (shots_on_target / shots) for one team jointly conditioned against a different observable (shots_on_target AGAINST) for the opponent — a cross-team, cross-observable asymmetric relationship not reducible to any single-observable mirror or band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) both teams' fouls FOR all-prior being above the competition context fouls baseline, AND (b) the competition context cards_2h baseline. Measure whether the joint elevation of both teams' foul rates relative to competition context predicts cards_2h above the competition context cards_2h mean, beyond what a single-team foul rate comparison would capture.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams' foul rates exceed the competition baseline simultaneously, second-half cards rise above the competition context cards_2h mean, with the joint excess being greater than the sum of each team's individual foul-rate excess.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The second-half cards (cards_2h) rate for a match is jointly shaped by both teams' foul-production tendencies and the match's goal-scoring context. Specifically, when both teams have elevated foul rates relative to competition context AND the competition context shows a high second-half cards baseline, the combined cards_2h output rises non-linearly beyond what either team's foul rate or the competition baseline alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-team, two-observable relationship (fouls for both teams jointly conditioned against cards_2h) evaluated against a competition baseline. It is not a single observable against one band — it requires the interaction of both teams' foul tendencies together with the cards_2h outcome.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, condition on the joint state where possession FOR (recent-5) is above the competition context possession baseline, but shots FOR (recent-5) is below the team's own all-prior shots average. Within this joint condition, measure whether corner_kicks FOR is suppressed relative to the team's all-prior corner kick average.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team has above-average possession but below-average shots in recent matches, its corner kick production is suppressed relative to its long-run average, indicating that possession without penetration does not translate to corner volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Corner kick generation is jointly influenced by a team's possession share and its shots volume. When a team holds above-average possession but its shots volume is below its long-run average (suggesting possession without penetration), its corner kick production is suppressed relative to what possession alone would predict. This cross-observable interaction between possession, shots, and corners is the mechanism of interest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves three observables jointly (possession, shots, corner_kicks) with a cross-observable conditioning logic — possession above baseline AND shots below own average — which cannot be reduced to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A's goals FOR second half mean exceeds Team A's goals FOR first half mean (Team A is a second-half scorer), AND (b) Team B's goals AGAINST second half mean exceeds Team B's goals AGAINST first half mean (Team B concedes more in the second half). Measure whether the combined second-half goal environment exceeds the competition context full-match goal baseline proportionally more than the first-half environment.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's scoring is back-loaded and Team B's defensive vulnerability is also back-loaded, second-half goals in matches between such teams rise above what the full-match averages and competition context would predict, representing a non-linear amplification from the joint half-level alignment.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The within-match distribution of goals between first and second halves is asymmetric across the two teams in a way that depends on each team's half-specific goal rates jointly. When Team A scores a higher proportion of its goals in the second half (goals FOR second half > goals FOR first half) while Team B concedes a higher proportion in the second half (goals AGAINST second half > goals AGAINST first half), the second-half goal environment for Team A is amplified beyond what either team's full-match goal rate would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (first half vs. second half goals) evaluated jointly across both teams' FOR and AGAINST perspectives simultaneously — a two-team, two-half, asymmetric cross-observable structure not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint relationship between Team A's shots FOR (all-prior: 11.41, recent-5: 15.2) and goals FOR (all-prior: 1.18, recent-5: 2.2) alongside shots_on_target FOR (all-prior: 3.78, recent-5: 5.8). Measure whether the recent uplift in shots and shots_on_target co-moves proportionally with goals, or whether goals rise disproportionately relative to the shot increase — i.e., test the joint shots × shots_on_target × goals relationship rather than any single observable alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR rise together in the recent window relative to the long-run baseline, goals FOR rises more than proportionally to the shot increase (super-linear co-movement), rather than remaining flat or rising only in proportion.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has risen sharply in recent matches while its conversion rate (goals per shot) has not kept pace, suggesting a divergence between shot production and scoring efficiency. Jointly tracking Team A's shots FOR and goals FOR across the all-prior versus recent-5 windows reveals whether elevated shot counts translate into goals or represent a low-conversion regime.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship across three distinct observables (shots, shots_on_target, goals) comparing their co-movement across two time windows. It cannot be reduced to any single observable versus one band; it tests whether the ratio of goals to shots changes as shot volume changes — a non-linear, multi-observable structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's shots FOR vs AGAINST (all-prior: 11.41 vs 11.78; recent-5: 15.2 vs 11.8), shots_on_target FOR vs AGAINST (all-prior: 3.78 vs 4.25; recent-5: 5.8 vs 4.6), and goals FOR vs AGAINST (all-prior: 1.18 vs 1.59; recent-5: 2.2 vs 1.6). The mechanism tests whether the cross-side asymmetry in shot-to-goal conversion (Team A converting shots at a different rate than opponents do against Team A) is a stable or regime-dependent feature.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: In the recent window, Team A's goals FOR rises relative to shots FOR (improving conversion) while goals AGAINST remains stable despite shots AGAINST falling — indicating an asymmetric cross-side conversion pattern that diverges from the long-run baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A structurally concedes more shots and shots_on_target than it produces over its full history, yet its recent-5 goal output has risen while goals conceded remain stable. This asymmetry between Team A's offensive shot-to-goal conversion and its defensive shot-against-to-goal-against conversion — measured jointly — may indicate a regime where Team A scores more efficiently than it defends, despite being outshot.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-observable relationship across both sides simultaneously (FOR and AGAINST for shots, shots_on_target, and goals), requiring a joint four-variable structure. It cannot be reduced to a single observable's FOR vs AGAINST mirror or a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's possession FOR (all-prior vs recent-5 shift), Team B's possession FOR (stable high), and both teams' corner_kicks and fouls FOR/AGAINST. The mechanism asks: when Team A's possession approaches parity with Team B's (as in recent-5), does the corner-kick differential and foul differential between the two sides compress or diverge relative to what each team's individual possession baseline predicts?
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: As Team A's possession rises toward parity with Team B, the corner-kick differential between the two sides compresses (Team A corners FOR rises, Team B corners AGAINST rises), and the foul differential narrows — a joint non-linear response across three observables that is not captured by any single observable's own baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession share has shifted substantially in recent matches (all-prior: 40.3%, recent-5: 48.4%) while Team B consistently holds above-average possession (all-prior: 52.4%, recent-5: 55.2%). The joint possession profiles of both teams in the same match create a contested possession dynamic distinct from either team's individual baseline. This mechanism tests whether the joint possession balance between a low-possession team (Team A historically) and a high-possession team (Team B) is associated with a different corner-kick and foul distribution than either team's individual possession baseline would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly tracking possession FOR for both teams simultaneously alongside corner_kicks and fouls, testing a three-observable interaction. It is not reducible to one observable with one band; it tests how the balance of two teams' possession levels jointly predicts distributional outcomes in two other observables.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team B's goals FOR in the first half versus second half, and Team A's goals AGAINST in the first half versus second half. The mechanism requires half-level resolution for both teams simultaneously, testing whether the cross-team first-half goal rate is elevated relative to the second-half rate in a way that neither team's full-match average captures.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The joint first-half goal rate (Team B scoring + Team A conceding) is elevated relative to the second-half joint rate, and this half-level asymmetry is more pronounced than either team's individual full-match goal average would suggest — i.e., the first half is disproportionately goal-rich for this specific matchup structure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B scores heavily in the first half (goals FOR 1H: 0.897) relative to the second half (goals FOR 2H: 1.0 over full match minus 1H), while Team A concedes more in the first half (goals AGAINST 1H: 0.809) than the second half (goals AGAINST 2H: 0.779). Jointly, this creates a within-match half-level asymmetry where Team B's first-half goal production meets Team A's first-half defensive vulnerability — a cross-team, cross-half joint structure. The mechanism tests whether the joint first-half goal environment (Team B's 1H scoring rate combined with Team A's 1H concession rate) exceeds what either team's full-match baseline would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match half-level split applied jointly across both teams' asymmetric observables (Team B's 1H scoring profile combined with Team A's 1H defensive profile). It requires two-team, two-half conditioning simultaneously, which is not reducible to a single observable's half split or a single team's half-level average.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's fouls FOR (all-prior vs recent-5 decline) and Team B's fouls FOR (all-prior vs recent-5 rise), alongside both teams' yellow_cards FOR and cards_2h FOR. The mechanism tests whether the joint foul-rate regime (which team is currently the higher-fouling side) predicts the direction of yellow-card and second-half card asymmetry between the two teams.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's recent foul rate falls below Team B's recent foul rate (a crossover from the long-run baseline), Team A's yellow cards FOR and cards_2h FOR are suppressed relative to Team B's, and this asymmetry is more pronounced in the second half — a joint three-observable, two-team, within-match-period structure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's fouls FOR have dropped sharply in recent matches (all-prior: 12.28, recent-5: 9.2) while Team B's fouls FOR have risen slightly (all-prior: 10.19, recent-5: 11.0). Jointly, this creates a foul-rate regime shift where the historically higher-fouling team (Team A) is now fouling less than its opponent. The mechanism tests whether this joint foul-rate crossover — where Team A's recent foul rate falls below Team B's recent foul rate — is associated with a corresponding shift in yellow-card and second-half card distributions, given that cards_2h and yellow_cards are also tracked for both teams.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly tracking fouls, yellow_cards, and cards_2h across both teams simultaneously, conditioning on a regime crossover (which team is currently the higher-fouling side) rather than any single team's foul rate in isolation. It involves two distinct observables (fouls and cards) across two teams with a within-match period dimension (cards_2h), which is not reducible to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's recent shots_on_target FOR is elevated relative to its long-run mean AND Team B's recent shots AGAINST is elevated relative to its long-run mean. Measure whether the cross-product of these two deviations is associated with Team A goals FOR beyond what each deviation predicts independently.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A goals FOR rises more steeply when both Team A's shot quality (shots_on_target/shots ratio) is above its long-run level AND the opponent's shots-allowed is above its long-run level, compared to when only one condition holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has risen in recent matches while its shots-on-target conversion rate (shots_on_target / shots) has also improved recently, whereas Team B concedes markedly more shots in recent matches than its long-run average. The joint condition of one team's improving shot quality alongside the opponent's recent defensive deterioration in shot-volume-allowed may produce a non-additive relationship with goals scored that neither observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables from two different perspectives (Team A's own shot quality trend AND Team B's defensive shot-volume trend) simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band, nor to a simple home/away or recent-vs-long-run split on a single metric.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's possession FOR is below a threshold (e.g. below competition mean of 50%) AND Team B's possession FOR is also below its own long-run mean. Measure whether corner_kicks FOR Team A and shots FOR Team A jointly behave differently in this dual-low-possession regime versus when possession is more balanced.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams are simultaneously below their respective possession baselines, Team A's corner_kicks FOR and shots FOR show a different joint distribution than when possession is more one-sided, suggesting a non-linear interaction between the two teams' possession deficits.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A operates with a persistent below-average possession share (long-run ~44.8%, recent ~42.8%) while Team B has recently dropped below its own long-run possession average. When both teams are simultaneously in a low-possession regime, the joint possession deficit may be associated with a distinct corner-kick and shots pattern compared to matches where only one team is possession-deficient.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This conditions on two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (Team A's own possession level AND Team B's possession level), and examines the joint relationship with two output observables. It cannot be reduced to a single observable split by one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's offsides FOR is simultaneously elevated above its long-run mean AND Team B's offsides AGAINST is elevated above its long-run mean. Measure whether Team A's goals FOR is associated with this joint elevation differently than when only one offside dimension is elevated.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A goals FOR rises when both Team A's offsides FOR and Team B's offsides AGAINST are jointly above their respective long-run means, consistent with a high-line defensive regime by Team B that creates more behind-the-line opportunities alongside more offside traps.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides FOR has spiked sharply in recent matches (long-run ~1.48, recent ~3.2) while Team B's offsides AGAINST has also spiked recently (long-run ~1.10, recent ~2.6). The joint elevation of both Team A's offensive line-breaking attempts and Team B's defensive line exposure may interact with Team A's goals FOR in a non-additive way — high offsides on both sides simultaneously may indicate a high-line defensive setup by Team B that creates both more offsides traps and more goal opportunities.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables from asymmetric perspectives (Team A's offensive offsides production AND Team B's defensive offsides concession) and their combined association with a third observable (goals). It requires two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously and is not reducible to any single-observable split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the within-match half structure: compare first-half vs second-half goal production for Team A FOR against Team B's first-half vs second-half goals AGAINST. Measure whether the joint second-half skew of both Team A's attacking output and Team B's defensive vulnerability produces a compounding effect on second-half goals, and whether this is further associated with elevated second-half card activity (cards_2h).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goals in matches involving Team A (home) and Team B (away) are elevated relative to first-half goals, and this elevation is associated with higher cards_2h, consistent with a late-game intensity regime driven by the joint half-level asymmetry of both teams.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half goal production (long-run 0.586 per match) exceeds its first-half production (0.557), while Team B concedes more goals in the second half (0.757) than the first half (0.614). The asymmetry between Team A's half-level goal distribution FOR and Team B's half-level goal distribution AGAINST — both favouring the second half — may jointly amplify second-half goal activity beyond what either team's half-split alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This uses within-match half-level resolution for two teams simultaneously across two distinct observables (goals and cards_2h), conditioning on the joint half-skew of both Team A's attacking and Team B's defensive profiles. It is not a single observable split by one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's yellow_cards FOR is below its long-run mean AND Team B's yellow_cards FOR is above its long-run mean simultaneously. Within this asymmetric disciplinary regime, measure whether corner_kicks AGAINST Team A (i.e. FOR Team B) and second-half cards (cards_2h) are jointly elevated relative to matches where the disciplinary asymmetry is reversed or absent.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A is in a low-yellow-card regime and Team B is in a high-yellow-card regime simultaneously, corner_kicks FOR Team B and cards_2h are jointly elevated, consistent with Team B pressing more aggressively and generating both more set-piece opportunities and more disciplinary events.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's yellow cards FOR have declined sharply in recent matches (long-run ~2.36, recent ~1.6) while Team B's yellow cards FOR have risen recently (long-run ~2.34, recent ~2.6), and Team B's fouls FOR have declined recently (long-run ~12.39, recent ~10.6) while Team A's fouls AGAINST have also declined recently (long-run ~12.24, recent ~11.0). The joint divergence in disciplinary and foul profiles — one team becoming less aggressive while the other becomes more so — may interact with corner-kick production in the second half in a way not captured by either team's disciplinary profile alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This conditions on two distinct observables from asymmetric perspectives across both teams (Team A's yellow_cards FOR declining AND Team B's yellow_cards FOR rising) and examines their joint association with two further observables (corner_kicks and cards_2h). It requires simultaneous conditioning on two opponent-descriptor dimensions and involves an asymmetric cross-team relationship.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where both Team A's shots-for and shots_on_target-for are simultaneously above their respective long-run means (ALL_PRIOR). Within that joint condition, examine whether goals-for tracks proportionally or diverges — specifically comparing the recent-5 regime (shots 15.2, SOT 6.2, goals 1.6) against the long-run regime (shots 11.6, SOT 4.2, goals 1.4).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals-for rises with jointly elevated shot volume and shots-on-target, but at a diminishing rate relative to the shot-quality uplift — i.e., conversion efficiency saturates or lags when both volume and quality are simultaneously high.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has surged in recent matches while its shots-on-target conversion rate (shots_on_target / shots) has also risen, but its goals-for has not kept pace — suggesting a joint relationship between shot volume, shot quality, and goal output that diverges from the long-run average. The engine should measure whether, when both shot volume and shots-on-target are jointly elevated above long-run baselines, goals-for rises proportionally or lags (a conversion efficiency gap).
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint condition on two distinct observables (shots AND shots_on_target) simultaneously exceeding baselines, then measuring a third observable (goals). It cannot be reduced to a single observable vs. one band; it is a three-variable joint relationship.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on away matches for Team B where possession-for exceeds the competition neutral mean (50.0). Within those matches, examine whether shots_on_target-for and goals-for are jointly elevated relative to Team B's home baseline. Cross-reference against Team A's shots_on_target-against and goals-against rates to assess whether Team A's defensive profile amplifies Team B's away attacking output.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's goals-for away rises with jointly elevated away possession and shots-on-target-for, and this relationship is amplified when the opponent (Team A) has an above-average shots-on-target-against rate.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B produces more goals away than at home (1.917 away vs 1.541 home) while also carrying higher possession away (54.5) than the competition average (50.0), yet Team A concedes more goals than it scores and allows above-average shots-against in recent form. The engine should measure whether Team B's away goal output is jointly associated with both elevated away possession and elevated shots-on-target-for, forming an asymmetric cross-team mechanism: Team B's possession dominance away interacts with Team A's defensive shot-concession tendency.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team mechanism involving two distinct observables for Team B (possession + shots_on_target) jointly conditioned, then cross-referenced against a different observable for Team A (shots_on_target-against). It spans two teams and two observable dimensions simultaneously.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner_kicks by half (FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF) for both Team A and Team B simultaneously. Condition on matches where both teams show a second-half corner surplus over first-half. Measure whether the combined second-half corner total exceeds the combined first-half total by more than the competition-level half-split baseline would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams individually show a second-half corner surplus, the aggregate second-half corner total rises above what the competition baseline half-split would predict — a super-additive within-match temporal effect.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A generates substantially more second-half corners than first-half corners (2.616 vs 1.959), while Team B also generates more second-half corners than first-half (2.973 vs 2.479). The engine should measure whether the joint within-match corner distribution — specifically the ratio of second-half to first-half corners for both teams simultaneously — is associated with a higher total corner count in the second half relative to the first half, and whether this half-level split diverges from the competition context baseline.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (not just full-match) applied jointly to both teams simultaneously, then compared against a competition baseline. It combines a within-match state dimension with a joint two-team conditioning — not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's yellow_cards-for is below its long-run mean AND Team B's yellow_cards-for is at or above its long-run mean simultaneously. Within that joint condition, examine whether cards_2h is disproportionately concentrated on Team B's side (Team B cards_2h FOR: 1.753 vs Team A cards_2h FOR: 1.192), and whether this asymmetry is amplified relative to the competition context cards_2h baseline (1.356).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's yellow card rate is suppressed relative to its long-run mean while Team B's is elevated, second-half card concentration (cards_2h) skews asymmetrically toward Team B — the total cards_2h rises above competition baseline driven by one side rather than both.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's yellow cards-for have dropped sharply in recent form (0.8 recent-5 vs 1.918 long-run) while Team B's yellow cards-for remain elevated and stable (2.6 recent-5 vs 2.411 long-run). The engine should measure whether this asymmetric disciplinary divergence — one team trending toward fewer cards while the other trends toward more — is jointly associated with a higher total cards-in-match count driven primarily by one side, and whether the second-half card concentration (cards_2h) for Team B is elevated relative to Team A's second-half card rate.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint condition on two different observables (yellow_cards and cards_2h) across two teams with opposite directional trends, plus a within-match temporal split (second half). It is an asymmetric cross-team, cross-observable, within-match-period mechanism.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B's offsides-for exceeds the competition baseline AND Team A's offsides-against exceeds the competition baseline simultaneously. Within that joint condition, examine whether total match offsides are elevated above the competition context mean (1.907 per team). Additionally, condition on Team B's possession-for being above 50% (consistent with their 55.6 long-run average), as higher possession by Team B may drive more attacking runs and thus more offside traps against Team A's defensive line.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total match offsides rise above competition baseline when Team B's offsides-for tendency and Team A's offsides-against tendency are jointly elevated, and this effect is further amplified when Team B holds above-average possession — a three-variable joint relationship.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A has a markedly higher offsides-against rate (2.861 long-run, 3.4 recent-5) than Team B's offsides-against rate (1.0 long-run and recent-5), while Team B's offsides-for rate (2.0) substantially exceeds Team A's offsides-for rate (1.778 long-run, 1.4 recent-5). The engine should measure whether the joint combination of Team B's high offsides-for production and Team A's high offsides-against concession — an asymmetric offside-trap interaction — is associated with elevated total offsides in the match, and whether this joint signal predicts a higher-than-competition-baseline offside count.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (offsides and possession) across two teams with asymmetric profiles, then measuring a combined match-level outcome. It is not reducible to a single observable with one band; it involves an asymmetric cross-team interaction across two observable dimensions.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's shots FOR (long-run vs. recent-5) and Team A's shots_on_target FOR (long-run vs. recent-5) to compute a within-team shot-quality ratio, then cross it against Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST (long-run vs. recent-5). Both the ratio dimension and the opponent-allowed dimension must be active simultaneously — not one at a time.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent shots-on-target share falls well below its long-run share while its raw shot volume holds steady, its effective on-target output against a given opponent's allowed rate is suppressed relative to what raw shot volume alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume is substantially higher than Team B's shots-allowed rate, yet Team A's shots-on-target rate has dropped sharply in recent matches relative to its long-run average. The joint relationship between Team A's shot volume and its shots-on-target conversion rate (shots-on-target as a share of shots) — measured across both long-run and recent windows simultaneously — conditions how many on-target attempts Team A actually generates against Team B's defensive profile.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint ratio of two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for the same team, compared across two time windows simultaneously, then crossed against the opponent's allowed rate — three dimensions active at once. No single-observable mirror or single-band split covers this.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR against Team A's shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST. The mechanism is asymmetric: Team B's offensive ratio is compared against Team A's defensive ratio, not the same observable mirrored.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the attacking team's shots-on-target share exceeds the defending team's shots-on-target-allowed share, the on-target volume advantage rises faster than the raw shot volume gap alone would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B generates substantially more shots than Team A allows on average, yet Team B's shots-on-target FOR (long-run) is also higher than Team A's shots-on-target AGAINST (long-run). The asymmetric cross between Team B's offensive shot profile (shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR) and Team A's defensive shot-quality profile (shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST) — where the two observables are different for each side — determines whether Team B's volume advantage translates into a proportional on-target advantage.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross of two distinct observables across two sides simultaneously — not a single-observable mirror. It requires computing ratios for both teams on different observables and comparing them jointly.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's fouls FOR (long-run vs. recent-5 divergence) and Team B's fouls AGAINST (long-run vs. recent-5 divergence), then relate this joint foul-pressure signal to the combined corner-kick production of both teams (Team A corners FOR + Team B corners FOR). The two observables — fouls and corners — must be linked jointly, not independently.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the attacking team's recent foul rate falls while the defending team's recent foul-concession rate rises, the corner-kick volume is elevated relative to what each team's corner average alone would predict, because defensive pressure and set-piece frequency co-move with foul patterns.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A commits fouls at a high long-run rate but its recent-5 foul rate has dropped sharply, while Team B's fouls-against rate has risen recently. The joint relationship between Team A's foul production (FOR) and Team B's foul-concession rate (AGAINST) — each measured across both long-run and recent windows — conditions the expected corner-kick volume, since fouls near the box and defensive pressure are linked to corner generation. Specifically, when one team's foul rate diverges across windows while the opponent's foul-allowed rate diverges in the opposite direction, the corner-kick total is affected in a non-additive way.
