mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When both teams simultaneously carry high possession, Team B's corner-kick production advantage over Team A is amplified relative to when possession is more balanced. Both teams are high-possession sides, but Team B generates substantially more corners per match than Team A. The joint condition of two dominant-possession teams meeting — rather than either team's possession in isolation — shapes the corner differential in a way not captured by either team's corner rate alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession level for both teams simultaneously) and measuring a differential across a second observable (corners). It cannot be reduced to one observable with one coarse band — it requires a two-dimensional possession condition plus a cross-team corner comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner production by half for both teams. Measure whether Team B's first-half corner dominance over Team A (Team B FOR first-half corners vs Team A FOR first-half corners) is greater than Team B's second-half corner dominance, and whether this asymmetry is consistent across historical matches.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's corner advantage over Team A is concentrated in the first half rather than distributed evenly, because Team B's first-half corner rate is markedly higher than Team A's while second-half rates are closer.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner-kick production is asymmetrically split across halves (first-half mean substantially higher than second-half mean), while Team A's corner production is roughly balanced across halves. The joint half-level corner distribution for both teams — not just either team's full-match total — determines whether the corner advantage concentrates in the first or second half.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) split applied jointly to both teams' corner production, comparing the asymmetry of the differential across halves. It is not a single observable with one coarse band — it requires half-resolution data for both teams and a cross-team asymmetry comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For Team B, jointly condition on the relationship between (a) the ratio of recent-5 shots FOR to all-prior shots FOR, and (b) the ratio of recent-5 shots-on-target AGAINST to all-prior shots-on-target AGAINST. Measure whether matches where both ratios move in the favourable direction (shots up, shots-on-target conceded down) are associated with higher goal output than either signal alone would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's goals FOR rises more when both shot volume is elevated AND shots-on-target conceded is suppressed simultaneously, compared to when only one of these conditions holds — indicating a non-additive joint relationship between attacking volume and defensive solidity.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot volume has surged sharply in recent matches relative to its long-run average, while its shots-on-target allowed has simultaneously declined in recent matches. The joint condition of rising attacking shot volume and tightening defensive shot-on-target concession — two distinct observables moving in opposite directions for the same team — suggests a regime shift in Team B's attacking-defensive balance that is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots FOR and shots-on-target AGAINST) for the same team, comparing recent-regime values against long-run baselines for both simultaneously. It cannot be reduced to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split goals FOR and AGAINST by half for both teams. Measure whether the first-half goal differential (Team B FOR first-half goals minus Team A FOR first-half goals, adjusted for what each team concedes in the first half) is systematically larger than the second-half equivalent, and whether this asymmetry is stable across historical matches.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The goal differential in favour of Team B is concentrated in the first half rather than the second half, because Team B scores at a higher rate in the first half and Team A concedes more in the first half than the second half — a joint half-level asymmetry not visible from full-match totals.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's goals are asymmetrically distributed across halves (first-half mean markedly higher than second-half mean), while Team A concedes goals more evenly across halves. The interaction between Team B's first-half goal-scoring tendency and Team A's first-half defensive vulnerability — both measured at half resolution — produces a joint half-level goal-distribution pattern that differs from what either team's full-match goal rates would imply.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires half-resolution data for both teams' goals FOR and AGAINST, and a cross-team comparison of the half-level differential. It is not a single observable with one coarse band — it requires within-match state conditioning applied jointly across both teams.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on (a) the direction of Team A's recent foul-rate change (FOR fouls declining, AGAINST fouls rising) and (b) Team B's foul-rate allowed declining. Within this joint regime, measure whether second-half card totals (cards_2h) for Team A are elevated relative to Team A's long-run cards_2h average, testing whether the asymmetric foul differential predicts second-half card accumulation beyond what either team's card rate alone would suggest.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half cards for Team A rise when Team A is in a regime of conceding more fouls than it commits, especially when facing a team (Team B) that also draws fewer fouls — the asymmetric foul-differential jointly with the opponent's foul-drawing tendency predicts elevated second-half card exposure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's foul rate has declined in recent matches while the fouls it concedes has risen sharply, and Team B's foul rate allowed has also declined recently. The joint condition of Team A fouling less (fewer fouls FOR) while conceding more fouls (more fouls AGAINST) — combined with Team B allowing fewer fouls — creates an asymmetric foul-differential regime that interacts with second-half card accumulation (cards_2h) in a way not captured by either team's foul or card rate alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship among three distinct observables (fouls FOR, fouls AGAINST, cards_2h) across both teams, with a within-match state (second-half) conditioning and a cross-team asymmetric comparison. It cannot be reduced to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute shots_on_target / shots (conversion ratio) for both Team A FOR and Team B FOR using ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5 windows simultaneously. The mechanism activates when one team's ratio is trending upward (Team A: 4.739/12.101 all-prior vs 4.8/14.8 recent) while the other's is trending sharply downward (Team B: 2.794/10.176 all-prior vs 1.2/9.6 recent). The joint divergence — not either ratio alone — is the conditioning structure.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the cross-team gap in shot-conversion ratio widens (one team improving, the other deteriorating simultaneously), the team with the deteriorating ratio produces fewer goals than its shot volume alone would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot-volume-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR) has deteriorated sharply in recent matches relative to its season-long average, while Team A's conversion ratio has improved. The joint cross-team divergence in shot quality — measured as the ratio of shots_on_target to total shots for each side simultaneously — may predict a suppressed attacking output for Team B beyond what either observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for both teams simultaneously, and comparing their ratio trends across two time windows. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B goals FOR and shots_on_target FOR (both ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5) alongside Team A shots_on_target AGAINST (ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5). The mechanism tests whether the combination of Team B's low finishing rate and Team A's improving shot-suppression creates a compounding suppression effect on Team B's goal output.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's goals-per-shot-on-target ratio is declining in recent matches AND the opponent is conceding fewer shots on target recently, the team's goal output is suppressed beyond what either factor alone would indicate.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's goals FOR per shot on target (finishing efficiency) has collapsed in recent matches (0.4 goals / 1.2 shots_on_target recent vs 0.765 goals / 2.794 shots_on_target all-prior), while Team A's defensive shots_on_target allowed has also declined recently. The joint relationship between Team B's finishing efficiency and Team A's defensive shot-quality suppression may jointly determine whether Team B scores, beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly relating two distinct observables (goals and shots_on_target) across both teams' FOR and AGAINST perspectives simultaneously, with a cross-window (recent vs all-prior) comparison. Not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B possession FOR (ALL_PRIOR vs RECENT_5), Team B shots FOR (ALL_PRIOR vs RECENT_5), and Team B goals FOR (ALL_PRIOR vs RECENT_5). The mechanism tests whether a team that gains possession share without a corresponding increase in shots or goals exhibits a decoupling pattern — i.e., possession rise does not predict attacking output rise, and may even be inversely associated in this regime.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent possession share rises substantially above its season average but shots and goals do not rise proportionally (or decline), the possession-to-output relationship saturates or inverts, indicating a qualitatively different attacking regime.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession share has swung dramatically in recent matches (59.6% recent vs 49.7% all-prior FOR), while their offensive output (shots, shots_on_target, goals) has simultaneously declined. The joint relationship between possession gain and attacking output — specifically whether possession increases translate into shot/goal increases or decouple — is a non-linear, two-observable mechanism worth measuring.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint three-observable relationship (possession, shots, goals) testing for non-linear decoupling/saturation, not a single observable with one band. The saturation/inversion structure is explicitly not covered by the baseline.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A corner_kicks AGAINST (ALL_PRIOR vs RECENT_5) and Team B corner_kicks AGAINST (ALL_PRIOR vs RECENT_5) simultaneously. The mechanism is the asymmetric divergence: Team A is conceding more corners recently while Team B is conceding fewer. This cross-team asymmetry in the same observable from the AGAINST perspective for both sides is the conditioning structure.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's corners-conceded rate is rising while the opponent's corners-conceded rate is falling, the corner differential in the match shifts toward the team whose opponent is conceding more, and the total corner count is pulled in opposing directions that partially offset.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner kicks conceded have risen sharply in recent matches (5.6 recent vs 4.729 all-prior AGAINST) while Team B's corners conceded have fallen sharply (2.4 recent vs 3.912 all-prior AGAINST). The asymmetric cross-team divergence in corners-against — one team conceding more, the other conceding fewer — jointly conditions the expected corner differential in this match beyond what either team's own corner production or allowance alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on the AGAINST perspective of the same observable for both teams and measuring the asymmetric divergence between them across two time windows. It is not a single observable with one band — it is a cross-team asymmetric joint relationship.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B fouls FOR (ALL_PRIOR vs RECENT_5) and Team B yellow_cards FOR (ALL_PRIOR vs RECENT_5) to compute a foul-to-card conversion ratio and its recent trend. Simultaneously condition on Team A fouls FOR (ALL_PRIOR vs RECENT_5) and yellow_cards FOR. The mechanism tests whether the joint elevation of foul rates for both teams, combined with Team B's rising card-per-foul rate, predicts a non-linear increase in total cards beyond what either foul rate or card rate alone would suggest.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams' foul rates are elevated and one team's card-per-foul conversion rate is rising in recent matches, total yellow cards in the match rise non-linearly — the joint foul-volume and card-conversion-rate interaction produces more cards than either factor alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's foul rate has risen sharply in recent matches (14.8 FOR, 17.0 AGAINST recent vs ~14-15 all-prior), while their yellow cards have also risen (2.8 FOR and AGAINST recent vs ~2.1-2.2 all-prior). The joint relationship between foul volume and card conversion rate (yellow cards per foul) — measured across both teams simultaneously — may indicate a threshold effect where elevated foul rates translate non-linearly into card accumulation, particularly when the opponent (Team A) also has a high foul rate historically.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable relationship (fouls and yellow_cards) testing for a non-linear threshold/saturation in card conversion as foul volume rises, conditioned on both teams simultaneously. Not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute Team A's on-target rate (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR, all-prior) and Team B's defensive on-target-conceded rate (shots_on_target AGAINST / shots AGAINST, all-prior). Condition on the joint combination of both ratios simultaneously — not either ratio alone — to identify matches where both sides' shot quality profiles interact.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's on-target conversion rate is below the competition baseline AND Team B's defensive on-target-conceded rate is also below baseline, total match shots_on_target is suppressed relative to what either team's individual shot volume would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR) is jointly considered alongside Team B's defensive shot-suppression ratio (shots AGAINST vs shots_on_target AGAINST), to test whether a match where one side generates high shot volume but low on-target accuracy faces a defence that also leaks high shot volume but fewer on-target concessions produces a systematically different total shots-on-target environment than either ratio alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint product of two distinct within-team ratios (shots vs shots_on_target) across two different sides simultaneously. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band; it is an asymmetric cross-team interaction between two distinct observables.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the fouling team (Team B FOR fouls) exceeds the competition foul baseline AND the opposing team (Team A AGAINST fouls) is below the competition foul baseline — i.e. a high-foul-disparity match context. Within this joint condition, measure whether yellow_cards FOR Team B and cards_2h FOR Team B rise above their unconditional averages.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total yellow cards and second-half cards rise with the foul-disparity between the two sides; the relationship is stronger when the high-fouling team faces a low-foul-conceding opponent, suggesting the disparity itself (not just one team's foul rate) drives card accumulation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B commits substantially more fouls than Team A (and more than the competition average), while Team A concedes fewer fouls than average. The joint relationship between Team B's foul production and Team A's foul concession — both measured simultaneously — is tested against whether the resulting total-match yellow-card and cards_2h environment rises above what either team's individual card rate would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable, two-team interaction: Team B's foul production combined with Team A's foul-concession rate, tested against a third observable (cards). It is not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute Team A's ratio of second-half corners FOR to first-half corners FOR (all-prior), and Team B's ratio of second-half corners AGAINST to first-half corners AGAINST (all-prior). Condition on the joint combination of both half-level ratios simultaneously. Test whether matches where both ratios indicate back-loaded corner generation/concession produce a second-half corner surplus beyond what full-match averages imply.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A generates proportionally more corners in the second half AND Team B concedes proportionally more corners in the second half, the second-half corner total rises relative to the first-half corner total beyond what either team's full-match corner average would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner production is asymmetrically split between first and second halves (FOR first half vs FOR second half), while Team B's corner concession is similarly split (AGAINST first half vs AGAINST second half). The joint within-match half-level interaction between Team A's corner generation profile and Team B's corner-concession profile by half is tested against whether the second-half corner total is elevated or suppressed relative to the first-half total in a way that neither team's full-match corner average predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires half-level resolution and a joint two-team interaction on the same observable across two distinct periods. It is not a single observable with one coarse band; it is a within-match state (half) combined with a cross-team joint condition.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition simultaneously on: (1) Team A FOR possession below competition baseline (sub-50%), (2) Team B AGAINST possession above competition baseline (opponent dominates ball), and (3) Team A FOR offsides relative to competition baseline. Within this joint three-variable condition, test whether Team A's first-half vs second-half goal split differs from the unconditional split.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A operates with below-average possession against a ball-dominant opponent AND generates above-average offsides, Team A's goals are more concentrated in the second half relative to the first half, compared to low-possession teams with low offside rates.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession deficit (Team A FOR possession below 50, Team B AGAINST possession above 54) is tested jointly against Team A's offside rate (FOR offsides) to determine whether a low-possession team that also generates above-average offsides exhibits a structurally different goal-scoring pattern (goals FOR first half vs second half) compared to low-possession teams with low offside rates — capturing a potential high-line pressing vs deep-block distinction via observable proxies.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine three-observable joint relationship (possession, offsides, goals) with a within-match half-level split. It cannot be reduced to any single observable with one band, nor to the two-way splits already covered.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Identify matches where Team B's RECENT_5 shots FOR is elevated above ALL_PRIOR shots FOR, while simultaneously Team B's RECENT_5 shots_on_target FOR is below ALL_PRIOR shots_on_target FOR, AND Team B's RECENT_5 fouls AGAINST is sharply below ALL_PRIOR fouls AGAINST. Within this joint multi-observable recent-form condition, test whether Team B's RECENT_5 goals FOR diverges from what the all-prior shot-to-goal ratio would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's recent form shows rising shot volume but falling on-target accuracy alongside a sharp drop in fouls conceded (suggesting a changed opponent style), Team B's recent goal output is suppressed relative to what its all-prior shot volume and goal rate would predict — indicating a multi-observable efficiency regime shift.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's recent-form trajectory (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) across multiple observables simultaneously — specifically shots FOR rising while shots_on_target FOR is falling and fouls AGAINST falling sharply — is tested as a joint multi-observable regime shift against whether Team B's goals FOR in recent matches diverges from what its all-prior goal rate and shot volume would predict, capturing a potential efficiency-degradation regime not visible in any single observable's recent vs long-run comparison.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint combination of three distinct observables' recent-vs-long-run trajectories simultaneously (shots, shots_on_target, fouls), not any single observable's recent level vs long-run level. The mechanism is a multi-observable regime structure, not a single-observable recent-vs-prior comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Measure Team A's historical matches segmented by whether shots-on-target / shots falls below vs. above the sample median, then compare corner kick FOR averages across those segments. This requires jointly conditioning on two observables (shots volume and on-target fraction) rather than either alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A corner kicks FOR rise as the ratio of shots to shots_on_target increases (more off-target shots relative to total shots), reflecting that wide/blocked attempts generate corners
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume and shot-on-target conversion rate jointly condition corner kick generation: when a team produces high shots but a lower fraction land on target, more off-target attempts tend to produce corner-kick opportunities, so the ratio of shots to shots-on-target for Team A (high shots, moderate on-target rate) should co-vary with Team A's corner kick output beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) used together to condition a third (corner_kicks). It cannot be reduced to a single observable against one coarse band; it requires the interaction of both shooting observables simultaneously.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's possession FOR exceeds Team B's possession FOR by a threshold (i.e., large possession differential), then measure the resulting corner kick differential (Team A FOR minus Team B FOR). This uses two distinct observables across two sides simultaneously, not a single observable with one band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The corner kick differential in favour of Team A rises as the possession differential in favour of Team A increases, with the relationship being stronger than either team's marginal corner or possession average alone would suggest
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: An asymmetric cross-team relationship exists between Team A's possession dominance and Team B's corner kick concession rate: Team A structurally holds more possession (all-prior and recent) while Team B concedes corners at a high rate, suggesting that when possession differential is large, the corner-kick imbalance between the two sides is amplified beyond what each team's own corner averages imply independently.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint cross-team interaction between two different observables (possession and corner_kicks) across both sides, requiring a two-dimensional conditioning structure that is not reducible to one observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Segment Team B's historical matches by whether opponent shots AGAINST Team B exceed a threshold (high-pressure vs. low-pressure matches), then compare Team B's cards_2h FOR and yellow_cards FOR across those segments. This requires jointly conditioning on an opponent observable (shots) and a within-match temporal split (second half vs. full match).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's second-half card concentration (cards_2h relative to full-match yellow cards) rises when opponent shot volume is high, indicating non-linear escalation of disciplinary events under sustained attacking pressure
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's foul rate and yellow card accumulation interact asymmetrically with Team A's offensive pressure (shots FOR): when Team A generates high shot volumes against Team B, Team B's historically elevated foul rate (conceding fouls) and yellow card rate should jointly produce more cards, but the second-half card concentration (cards_2h) may be disproportionately elevated relative to the full-match card average, reflecting a non-linear escalation under sustained pressure.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism combines a within-match temporal split (second half cards vs. full match) with a cross-observable conditioning variable (opponent shots), requiring both a half-level resolution and a joint two-observable structure that is not covered by any single-observable baseline.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Identify historical matches where the home team's fouls FOR is above median AND the away team's offsides FOR is below median simultaneously. In those matches, measure the away team's shots FOR and corner_kicks FOR. This requires two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions (foul rate and offside rate) conditioning a third observable.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Away team shots FOR and corner_kicks FOR are suppressed when home team foul rate is high and away team offside rate is simultaneously low, compared to matches where only one condition holds
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between Team A's fouls committed and Team B's offsides generated reveals an asymmetric tactical interaction: Team A commits fouls at a high recent rate while Team B generates few offsides, suggesting Team B defends deep and does not press a high line. When Team A's foul rate is high AND Team B's offside rate is low, this jointly signals a match where Team B is sitting deep, which should suppress Team B's corner and shot production below what either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (fouls and offsides) to condition a third observable, which is explicitly richer than any single-observable with one coarse band and is not covered by the two already-supported two-way splits.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each historical match, compute Team A's first-half goal share (1H goals / total goals FOR) and Team B's second-half goal concession share (2H goals AGAINST / total goals AGAINST). Condition on matches where Team A's 1H goal share is above median AND Team B's 2H concession share is above median simultaneously, and test whether total match goals are concentrated in specific halves differently from the competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's historical first-half goal share is high and Team B's historical second-half concession share is high simultaneously, the within-match goal distribution is more spread across both halves than when only one condition holds, reflecting the opposing half-level tendencies of the two teams
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goal scoring exhibits a first-half vs. second-half temporal asymmetry that interacts with Team B's half-specific goal concession pattern: Team A scores more in the first half relative to the second half, while Team B concedes more in the second half than the first half. This cross-team, cross-half asymmetry in goal timing — where the two teams' half-level goal profiles point in opposite directions — should produce a detectable within-match goal-timing pattern that is not captured by either team's full-match goal averages.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism requires jointly conditioning on two distinct half-level splits across two different teams (Team A's 1H goal production timing and Team B's 2H goal concession timing), creating a cross-team, cross-half interaction that cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band or a single team's half-level split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the possession differential between the two sides exceeds a threshold (e.g., Team B holds >55% possession), then measure whether Team A's foul rate is elevated relative to its unconditional average. This is a joint two-observable interaction, not a single-observable band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's foul production rises as Team B's possession share increases beyond a threshold, reflecting a suppression-and-foul dynamic that saturates at high possession differentials.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's dominant possession profile (historically ~61%) combined with Team A's high foul rate (historically ~17.2 fouls/match, elevated away at ~18.3) creates a joint condition where Team A's foul production rises as a function of Team B's possession dominance — i.e., the interaction between one team's possession share and the opposing team's foul rate jointly predicts foul volume beyond what either observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables from two different teams simultaneously (Team B's possession AND Team A's foul rate), which cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band. It is an asymmetric cross-team interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B's possession exceeds a threshold (e.g., >55%), then measure the joint distribution of Team A corners conceded and Team B corners produced. Compare against each team's unconditional corner averages to test whether the possession-corner relationship is super-additive.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total corner volume rises with Team B's possession dominance, with Team A's corners-against and Team B's corners-for both elevated above their unconditional means when possession differential is large.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's high possession share jointly interacts with Team A's corner kick concession rate: when Team B dominates possession, Team A concedes significantly more corners than its unconditional average, while Team B's corner production is also elevated — creating a compounding corner-volume effect driven by the joint possession-corner relationship across both teams.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable, two-team interaction (possession differential AND corner production/concession for both sides simultaneously), not reducible to a single observable with one band. The super-additive structure requires measuring both observables together.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split goals by half for both teams simultaneously. Condition on the joint first-half vs. second-half goal rates for both Team A (FOR and AGAINST) and Team B (FOR and AGAINST) to test whether the second half produces a disproportionate share of total goals relative to competition context norms.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goal volume for both teams combined is elevated relative to first-half volume, and this asymmetry is more pronounced than the competition-context baseline implies.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B exhibits a pronounced within-match goal-scoring asymmetry: its second-half goal rate (~1.015/match) is substantially higher than its first-half rate (~0.662/match), while Team A's goals-against are also back-loaded (first-half ~0.667, second-half ~0.750). The joint half-level scoring profiles of both teams — measured simultaneously — test whether the second-half goal environment is structurally elevated beyond what full-match averages imply.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on half-level splits for both teams' FOR and AGAINST goal rates simultaneously, comparing the within-match state structure across both sides — not a single observable with one band. The half-level resolution and cross-team joint structure make it structurally richer.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on: (1) Team A's second-half card rate and foul rate, (2) Team B's second-half card rate and possession dominance, and (3) competition context second-half card norm. Test whether the combined second-half card environment when a high-fouling team faces a possession-dominant team exceeds what either team's individual card rate or the competition norm predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half total cards are elevated above competition context norms when a high-fouling team (Team A) faces a possession-dominant team (Team B), with the joint effect exceeding the sum of individual team deviations from the norm.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half card accumulation (cards_2h FOR ~1.723/match) combined with Team A's second-half card accumulation (cards_2h FOR ~2.389/match) — both measured against the competition context second-half card norm (~1.35/match) — tests whether the joint second-half disciplinary environment in this specific matchup is structurally elevated above competition norms, driven by the interaction of Team A's high foul rate and Team B's possession-dominant style creating late-match friction.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves three observables jointly (cards_2h, fouls, possession), two teams' second-half profiles simultaneously, and a within-match state (second half) — not reducible to any single observable with one band or a simple home/away split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute the ratio of shots_on_target to shots for Team B (FOR) and for Team A (AGAINST) separately, then jointly condition on whether Team B's shot-conversion-to-target ratio is suppressed when facing teams with Team A's defensive shot-filtering profile. Test whether the joint ratio structure predicts shots_on_target volume better than either team's raw shots or shots_on_target average alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's shots-on-target production is suppressed relative to its raw shot volume when facing a team (Team A) whose shots-on-target-against rate is below the competition norm, indicating a non-linear filtering effect that saturates as defensive quality improves.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots ~14.9, shots_on_target ~4.86, all-prior) versus Team A's shots-against-to-shots-on-target-against ratio (shots_against ~12.4, shots_on_target_against ~3.97) jointly characterize the shot quality / defensive filtering interaction: when Team B's volume shooting meets Team A's relatively efficient shot-suppression, the net shots-on-target environment may be suppressed relative to what Team B's raw shot volume alone implies. This tests a non-linear, ratio-based relationship between two observables across both teams.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a ratio/non-linear relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) measured asymmetrically across both teams — Team B's offensive conversion ratio interacting with Team A's defensive filtering ratio. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's shots FOR (all-prior and recent-5) alongside Team A's shots_on_target FOR (all-prior and recent-5), crossed with Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST (all-prior vs recent-5 divergence). The mechanism requires both the attacking conversion ratio and the opponent's recent defensive trajectory to be evaluated simultaneously — neither alone captures the joint signal.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent shots-to-shots-on-target ratio deteriorates (more shots, fewer on target) while the opponent's shots_on_target allowed has recently tightened relative to their long-run average, total shots_on_target in the match is suppressed relative to what either team's individual shot volume would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR) interacts with Team B's recent defensive suppression of shots on target allowed: when one team generates many shots but a low on-target fraction while the opponent has recently been conceding fewer shots on target than their long-run average, the joint signal on attacking quality vs defensive tightening differs from either observable read alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for one side, crossed with a divergence signal (recent vs all-prior) for the opponent's defensive version of the same pair — not reducible to any single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compare Team A shots FOR all-prior vs recent-5 and shots_on_target FOR all-prior vs recent-5, against Team B shots FOR all-prior vs recent-5 and shots_on_target FOR all-prior vs recent-5. The conditioning is on the cross-team divergence in the shots-to-shots_on_target trajectory, not on either observable in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's recent shots_on_target rate rises relative to their long-run level while the opponent's falls, the team with the improving on-target trajectory generates disproportionately more shots_on_target than raw shot volume alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: An asymmetric shots-volume vs shots-on-target relationship across the two sides: Team A produces shots at a higher rate than Team B (both all-prior and recent), but Team B's recent shots_on_target FOR has surged relative to their all-prior average while Team A's shots_on_target FOR has declined. This cross-team asymmetry in shot quality trajectories — one side improving on-target rate, the other declining — is a joint two-observable, two-team signal.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric, cross-team joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) evaluated simultaneously for both sides — not a single observable with one band, and not a simple home/away or recent/all-prior split of one metric.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's possession FOR (recent-5 vs all-prior divergence) and Team B's fouls FOR (recent-5 vs all-prior divergence). When possession rises sharply and fouls drop sharply together, this signals a style shift that affects both the foul count and the corner kick count (teams with more possession tend to generate more corners but commit fewer fouls). The joint two-observable conditioning is required.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent possession rises substantially above their long-run average while their recent fouls committed drop substantially below their long-run average, their corner kicks FOR rises and total match fouls are suppressed relative to what either observable's individual baseline would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession has recently surged well above their long-run average (and above the competition baseline) while their fouls committed have recently dropped sharply relative to their long-run average. This joint shift — more possession, fewer fouls — represents a regime change in Team B's playing style that jointly conditions corner kick and foul outcomes in a way neither observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a genuine joint relationship among two distinct observables (possession and fouls) as simultaneous conditioning variables predicting a third (corner_kicks / fouls total) — not reducible to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's fouls FOR (recent-5 vs all-prior divergence) and Team A's yellow_cards FOR (recent-5 vs all-prior divergence). The mechanism requires both observables to be elevated simultaneously — the joint signal is richer than either single observable's recent-vs-prior divergence alone. The outcome of interest is cards_2h FOR (second-half cards), which is also available for both teams.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent fouls committed and recent yellow cards both rise above their long-run averages simultaneously, their second-half card count (cards_2h) rises above what the long-run cards_2h average or either single observable's recent trend would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's fouls committed have recently surged well above their long-run average and above the competition baseline, while Team A's yellow cards FOR have also risen recently. Jointly, the combination of elevated recent fouls and elevated recent yellow cards FOR — both diverging from long-run levels simultaneously — signals a disciplinary regime that conditions second-half card outcomes (cards_2h) beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable (fouls and yellow_cards) conditioning on a third observable (cards_2h) with a within-match period split (second half), combining a multi-observable joint signal with a half-level resolution — not reducible to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's offsides AGAINST (all-prior and recent-5, relative to competition baseline) and Team B's offsides FOR (all-prior and recent-5, relative to competition baseline). When both are elevated simultaneously, it signals that Team B's attacking runs are frequently disrupted by Team A's high line, which jointly suppresses Team B's goal opportunities and corner kicks while potentially increasing Team A's transition-based corner and goal opportunities.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the defending team's offsides AGAINST rate is elevated above the competition baseline and the attacking team's offsides FOR rate is also elevated, the attacking team's goals FOR and corner_kicks FOR are suppressed relative to what their shot volume or possession share alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides AGAINST (opponents caught offside against Team A's defensive line) is substantially higher than the competition average and has risen further in recent matches, while Team B's offsides FOR (Team B caught offside) is also elevated relative to the competition average. The joint signal — Team A's high defensive line trapping opponents offside, combined with Team B's own tendency to be caught offside — creates a two-dimensional offside trap interaction that conditions corner kick and goal outcomes differently than either team's offside rate alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (Team A's defensive line behavior measured via offsides AGAINST, and Team B's attacking run behavior measured via offsides FOR), jointly conditioning a third observable (goals/corners) — not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where one team (Team A) produces markedly fewer shots than it concedes AND the opposing team (Team B) maintains a high shots-to-shots-on-target ratio FOR. Measure whether Team A's corner_kicks FOR is suppressed and Team B's corner_kicks FOR is elevated relative to competition context, specifically in this joint configuration rather than either dimension alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's shots FOR is substantially below its shots AGAINST AND the opponent's shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR ratio is elevated, that team's corner_kicks FOR is suppressed relative to competition baseline, while the opponent's corner_kicks FOR rises above baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume disadvantage (low shots FOR, high shots AGAINST) combined with Team B's high offensive shot conversion efficiency (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR ratio) jointly predict a suppressed corner-kick share for Team A relative to Team B, beyond what either team's corner average alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots imbalance and shot-quality ratio) across both teams simultaneously. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band — it involves an asymmetric cross-team pairing of two different observable dimensions.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compare each team's corner_kicks FOR in FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF (as a ratio to their full-match total) simultaneously. The mechanism is the cross-team asymmetry in half-level corner distribution — not either team's half split in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's corner_kicks FOR ratio (first half share of full-match total) is higher than Team B's equivalent ratio, meaning Team A's corner production is front-loaded while Team B's is more evenly spread or back-loaded; this asymmetry is detectable at the half level.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The within-match half-level distribution of corner kicks differs between the two teams: Team A generates a larger share of its corners in the first half relative to the second half, while Team B's corner production is more evenly distributed or second-half weighted. This asymmetric half-level corner distribution is a joint property of both teams' half-split profiles.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) split applied asymmetrically across two teams simultaneously. It requires half-resolution data and a cross-team comparison of distributional shape, not a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's fouls FOR (RECENT_5) is substantially above both its ALL_PRIOR average and the competition baseline, AND Team A's fouls AGAINST (RECENT_5) is also elevated. Measure whether yellow_cards FOR (Team B) and the match total yellow cards are elevated in this joint high-foul configuration.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent fouls FOR is elevated above its season average AND the opponent's fouls AGAINST is also above competition baseline, yellow cards FOR for the high-fouling team rise above that team's season yellow card average.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's recent foul rate (FOR) has surged sharply above its season average while Team A's foul rate conceded (AGAINST) is also elevated above competition baseline. The joint condition of high Team B fouls committed AND high Team A fouls suffered — both simultaneously above their respective baselines — predicts an elevated yellow_cards total for the match, beyond what either team's yellow card average alone would indicate.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and yellow cards) across both teams' perspectives simultaneously, with a recent-vs-season trend dimension layered in. It cannot be reduced to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition simultaneously on Team B's cards_2h AGAINST (second-half cards conceded by opponents in Team B's matches) being above competition baseline AND Team A's cards_2h FOR (second-half cards Team A receives) being above competition baseline. Measure whether the combined second-half card total exceeds competition context.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams independently show elevated second-half card profiles (one in cards_2h FOR, the other in cards_2h AGAINST), the match-level second-half card total rises above competition context — a super-additive joint effect not captured by either team's profile alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The second-half card concentration (cards_2h) is jointly predicted by both teams' second-half card profiles relative to their full-match card profiles. When Team B's cards_2h AGAINST is elevated (opponents receive more second-half cards against Team B) AND Team A's cards_2h FOR is also elevated, the match second-half card total is expected to be above competition baseline — a joint two-team, within-match-state mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match state (second half) split applied jointly across two teams' asymmetric perspectives (FOR vs AGAINST), combined with a cross-team joint condition. It is not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's offsides AGAINST (opponents caught offside in Team B's matches) is substantially above competition baseline AND Team A's offsides FOR is at or below competition baseline. Measure whether Team A's goals FOR per shot FOR is suppressed in this configuration relative to Team A's season average conversion.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the opponent (Team B) generates a high offsides AGAINST rate AND the attacking team (Team A) has a low offsides FOR rate, Team A's goals FOR per shots FOR ratio is suppressed relative to Team A's season average — suggesting Team B's defensive line disrupts Team A's attacking runs even when Team A is not habitually offside.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B generates a high volume of offsides AGAINST (opponents caught offside against Team B) while Team A's offsides FOR (Team A caught offside) is near or below competition baseline. This asymmetric cross-team offside profile — one team pressing a high defensive line causing opponent offsides, the other team not running offside traps — jointly predicts a suppressed goal-scoring rate for Team A relative to its shots volume, because Team A's attacking runs are being caught offside at an elevated rate when facing Team B's defensive structure.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team relationship between two distinct observables (offsides and goals/shots ratio) across different perspectives (Team B AGAINST vs Team A FOR). It requires the joint condition of both dimensions simultaneously and cannot be reduced to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the simultaneous state where Team A's recent shots FOR (RECENT_5) exceeds its ALL_PRIOR shots FOR, AND Team A's recent shots_on_target FOR (RECENT_5) exceeds its ALL_PRIOR shots_on_target FOR, AND Team B's recent shots AGAINST (RECENT_5) exceeds its ALL_PRIOR shots AGAINST. Measure corner_kicks and shots_on_target outcomes in matches satisfying all three conditions jointly.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When all three conditions hold simultaneously, Team A's corner_kicks FOR and shots_on_target FOR rise together relative to baseline — the joint uplift is larger than the sum of each single-observable uplift.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has risen sharply in recent matches while its shots-on-target conversion rate (shots on target as a share of total shots) has also improved recently, yet Team B concedes more shots in recent matches than its season average. The joint relationship between Team A's recent shot volume uplift AND its recent on-target accuracy uplift, set against Team B's recent defensive shot-concession trend, may jointly predict corner and on-target activity beyond what either observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the simultaneous joint state of three distinct observables across two teams — Team A's shot volume trend, Team A's accuracy trend, and Team B's defensive shot-concession trend — none of which can be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner_kicks FOR (Team A) and corner_kicks AGAINST (Team B) by half. Condition on the cross-team, cross-half joint state: compare Team A's first-half corner production rate against Team B's first-half corner concession rate, and separately Team A's second-half corner production rate against Team B's second-half corner concession rate. Test whether the half-level pairing reveals a divergent within-match trajectory.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's corner production relative to Team B's concession rate is lower in the first half and rises in the second half — the within-match trajectory is non-flat and the half-level joint pairing diverges from the full-match average pairing.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner_kicks FOR are split asymmetrically across halves (first-half mean notably lower than second-half mean), while Team B's corner_kicks AGAINST are also split across halves. The joint half-level corner production of Team A against Team B's half-level corner concession profile may reveal a within-match timing asymmetry in corner activity that a full-match view obscures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) split applied jointly across two teams' asymmetric observables — it requires both the half resolution and the cross-team pairing simultaneously, which is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint half-level state: Team A's goals AGAINST FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF split, paired with Team B's goals FOR FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF split. Test whether the half in which Team A is most vulnerable (first) aligns or misaligns with the half in which Team B is most productive (second), and measure how total goals in each half relate to this cross-team timing asymmetry.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The cross-team half-level pairing reveals a timing mismatch — Team A's defensive vulnerability peak (first half) does not coincide with Team B's attacking output peak (second half) — such that the joint half-level profile diverges from a flat within-match distribution implied by full-match averages alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A concedes goals heavily in the first half (high first-half goals AGAINST) relative to the second half, while Team B scores more goals in the second half than the first half. This cross-team, cross-half asymmetry in goal-scoring timing — where Team A's defensive vulnerability is concentrated in the first half but Team B's attacking output is concentrated in the second half — creates a joint within-match state that differs from what either team's full-match goal average implies.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two teams' half-level splits for the same observable (goals) in an asymmetric cross-team pairing — not reducible to one observable with one band, and requires half-level data resolution.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where both Team A's possession FOR and Team B's possession FOR are below 50% (both sides are sub-50% possession teams). Within this joint condition, measure fouls FOR/AGAINST and yellow_cards FOR/AGAINST and cards_2h, comparing against the competition context baseline and against matches where at least one team holds majority possession.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams are structurally sub-50% possession sides, fouls and yellow_cards are elevated relative to the competition context baseline, and cards_2h are also elevated — the joint low-possession pairing is associated with a more contested, card-prone match profile.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession is structurally below 50% (both all-prior and recent), while Team B also operates below 50% possession on average. When both teams in a match are sub-50% possession sides, the joint low-possession context may be associated with a distinct foul and card profile — specifically elevated fouls and cards — compared to matches where at least one team dominates possession. Team B concedes notably more fouls than the competition average, reinforcing this joint dynamic.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint condition of two distinct observables (possession for each team) both falling below a threshold simultaneously — a two-dimensional threshold condition across two teams — not reducible to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's shots_on_target FOR rate (shots_on_target / shots) is below competition average AND Team B's shots_on_target FOR rate is at or above competition average. Within this asymmetric joint condition, measure total shots_on_target in the match and compare against matches where both teams have similar shot-quality profiles.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A has a structurally lower shot-to-on-target conversion rate than Team B, the match-level shots_on_target distribution is asymmetric — Team B generates a disproportionately higher share of total match shots_on_target relative to its share of total shots, and this asymmetry is larger than what either team's individual shot-quality profile alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots FOR have a low conversion to shots_on_target (shots_on_target FOR as a share of shots FOR is well below competition average), while Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST are also below competition average. The joint relationship between Team A's low shot accuracy and Team B's low shot-on-target concession rate creates a compounded suppression of on-target activity that is asymmetric: Team B's own shots_on_target FOR are above competition average, meaning the two teams have opposing shot-quality profiles. This cross-team asymmetry in shot quality (accuracy FOR vs accuracy AGAINST) is a joint two-observable, two-team relationship.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint cross-team comparison of two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for both teams simultaneously, forming an asymmetric two-team, two-observable relationship — not reducible to one observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team B being a low-shots-conceded opponent (season mean shots-against well below competition context mean). Within that condition, examine whether Team A's shots-to-shots-on-target ratio and shots-on-target-to-goals ratio jointly differ from their unconditional season averages.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's shots-on-target rate and goals-per-shot-on-target are suppressed when facing a low-shots-conceding opponent, even as raw shot volume remains elevated — i.e., volume does not linearly predict on-target or goal output against such opponents.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume is high but its conversion to goals has declined in recent matches, while Team B concedes very few shots against. The joint relationship between Team A's shots-for and its shots-on-target-for, conditioned on Team B's shots-against suppression level, tests whether high shot volume translates to on-target output when facing a low-shots-conceding opponent.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint three-variable relationship (shots, shots_on_target, goals) conditioned simultaneously on the opponent's shots-against level. It is not reducible to any single observable mirrored against its opponent-allowed counterpart, nor to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on both teams having above-competition-average shots-for. Within this two-sided high-volume condition, examine whether shots-on-target and goals outcomes for each side differ from single-team baselines — specifically testing whether the interaction of two high-volume attacking teams compresses or amplifies on-target rates.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams produce above-average shot volumes, the shots-on-target rate per shot is suppressed relative to single-team baselines, reflecting defensive pressure from both sides; goals outcomes do not scale linearly with combined shot volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B produces a high shots volume relative to the competition context but concedes very few shots. The asymmetric relationship between Team B's shots-for and Team A's shots-against (both relative to competition baseline) tests whether a dominant-possession, high-shot-volume attacker facing a high-shot-volume opponent produces a different shots-on-target and goals outcome than when facing a low-shot-volume opponent.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint two-team, two-observable interaction (both teams' shots-for simultaneously above baseline) conditioned on a second observable (shots-on-target), which cannot be reduced to a single observable mirror or a single coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the within-match half split for both teams simultaneously: Team A's goals-against first-half vs second-half, and Team B's goals-for first-half vs second-half. Test whether the joint half-level distribution (both teams' tendencies combined) differs from what either team's individual half split would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second half is disproportionately goal-rich relative to the first half in this matchup, beyond what either team's individual half-split tendency would predict alone — i.e., the two half-level tendencies reinforce each other.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A concedes a high volume of goals in the first half relative to the second half, while Team B scores more in the second half than the first. The joint within-match half-level goal distribution for both teams tests whether the combination of Team A's first-half defensive vulnerability and Team B's second-half attacking tendency produces a distinctive half-level goals pattern in this matchup.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct within-match half-level splits for two different teams across an asymmetric observable (goals-against for Team A, goals-for for Team B), which is not reducible to a single observable's half split or a single team's half-level trend.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the within-match half split for both teams simultaneously: Team A's corners-for first-half vs second-half, and Team B's corners-for first-half vs second-half. Test whether the combined half-level corner distribution differs from what each team's individual half split predicts in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner production shifts across halves in opposing directions for the two teams — Team A dominates corners in the first half while Team B's corner share rises in the second half — producing a non-uniform intra-match corner timing pattern that is not captured by full-match corner totals alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A generates substantially more corners in the first half than the second half, while Team B generates more corners in the second half than the first. The joint within-match half-level corner distribution tests whether the two teams' opposing half-level corner tendencies produce a distinctive intra-match corner timing pattern — specifically whether the first half is corner-dominated by Team A and the second half by Team B.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two teams' within-match half-level splits for the same observable (corners), examining the interaction of opposing half-level tendencies. This is not reducible to a single observable's half split or a single team's half-level trend.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on both teams having above-competition-average possession (indicating a contested possession match). Within this condition, examine whether fouls-for and yellow-cards-for are elevated or suppressed relative to each team's unconditional averages, and whether second-half cards (cards_2h) are disproportionately elevated relative to full-match yellow cards.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: In contested high-possession matchups, fouls and second-half cards rise relative to each team's unconditional averages, and the second-half card share of total cards is elevated — reflecting increased contest intensity as both teams press for possession control in the closing stages.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession is substantially above competition average while Team B also holds above-average possession. The joint relationship between both teams' possession levels and their respective foul rates tests whether high-possession matchups (where both teams compete for ball control) produce a different fouls-per-match and cards-in-second-half pattern than matchups where possession is more asymmetric.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint four-variable relationship (possession, fouls, yellow_cards, cards_2h) conditioned on both teams simultaneously exceeding a possession threshold, and further examines the within-match temporal distribution (second-half cards vs full-match cards). This is not reducible to any single observable mirror or single-band conditioning.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute each team's shots-on-target ratio (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR) and cross-condition: when the dominant-possession team (Team A) maintains both high shot volume AND high on-target ratio while the opponent (Team B) has lower on-target ratio despite comparable shot volume, the aggregate match shots-on-target total is driven asymmetrically by the dominant side.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Match-level shots_on_target rises with Team A's shots-on-target ratio relative to Team B's, beyond what either team's raw shot volume alone would predict; the asymmetry between the two ratios is positively associated with the gap in shots_on_target totals.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's high shot volume is jointly paired with a markedly elevated shots-on-target rate (shots_on_target / shots), while Team B's shot-to-on-target conversion is substantially lower. The joint relationship between total shot volume and on-target accuracy across both sides — rather than either observable alone — conditions the total shots-on-target environment of the match.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for both teams simultaneously to derive a ratio-based asymmetry. It cannot be reduced to a single observable against one opponent-descriptor band; it is a cross-team, cross-observable joint relationship.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's possession FOR exceeds a high threshold AND Team B's possession AGAINST also exceeds a high threshold (both pointing to the same structural imbalance). Within this joint condition, measure whether Team A's corner_kicks FOR is elevated beyond what possession alone predicts, and whether Team B's corner_kicks AGAINST is also elevated, creating a compounding corner surplus for Team A.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's corner_kicks FOR rises with the joint possession-dominance condition (both Team A possession FOR high and Team B possession AGAINST high), and this joint condition is more predictive of corner surplus than either possession observable alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A dominates possession (season avg ~61%) while Team B concedes possession (season avg ~52% against) and has recently conceded even more (~58.6% against in last 5). When one team structurally holds high possession and the opponent structurally concedes it, corner kick generation is jointly shaped by both the possession differential and each team's corner-kick-per-possession efficiency. The interaction between possession dominance and corner generation rate — not possession alone — determines the corner environment.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) jointly, and requires conditioning on both Team A's possession production and Team B's possession concession simultaneously — a two-observable, two-team joint relationship not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split goals by half for both teams. Condition on the joint state: Team B's goals FOR in the second half versus first half (back-loading ratio), crossed with Team A's goals AGAINST split by half. Measure whether the second-half goal environment (combined goals in H2) is elevated relative to H1 in this specific structural pairing, beyond what the full-match averages suggest.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Combined second-half goals are elevated relative to first-half goals when Team B's back-loaded scoring profile meets Team A's relatively balanced concession profile across halves; the H2/H1 goal ratio for the match rises with Team B's own H2/H1 scoring ratio.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's goals are heavily back-loaded: their season average shows 0.682 goals FOR in the first half versus 1.091 in the second half, while Team A concedes more in the first half (1.091) than the second (1.136 — nearly equal). The joint half-level goal-scoring and goal-conceding profiles of both teams create an asymmetric within-match scoring-timing structure that differs from the full-match averages.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on half-level splits for both teams' goals (FOR and AGAINST) simultaneously — a within-match state (half) combined with a cross-team asymmetric observable relationship. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (1) Team B's fouls FOR AWAY being elevated above their fouls FOR HOME, and (2) Team A's yellow_cards AGAINST (drawn from opponents) relative to competition baseline. Measure whether the joint condition of high away-foul-rate opponent meeting a consistent foul-drawing home team produces elevated yellow card totals beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Yellow cards FOR Team B rise with the joint condition of Team B's elevated away foul rate and Team A's above-baseline foul-drawing rate; the interaction between these two observables is more predictive of yellow card volume than either foul rate or yellow card rate alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B commits substantially more fouls away (13.818) than at home (10.636), while Team A draws fouls at a consistent rate regardless of venue. The joint relationship between Team B's venue-conditioned foul rate (away vs home) and Team A's foul-drawing rate determines the yellow card environment: when a high-fouling away team faces a team that consistently draws fouls, the yellow card total is shaped by the interaction of these two distinct observables (fouls committed and yellow cards) across the venue dimension.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) conditioned simultaneously on venue and opponent foul-drawing behavior — two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions (venue and opponent foul profile) interacting with two observables. Not reducible to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's corner_kicks FOR split by half (H1 vs H2) and Team B's corner_kicks AGAINST split by half (H1 vs H2). Measure whether the second-half corner surplus for Team A (relative to H1) is amplified when Team B also concedes more corners in H2 than H1, creating a compounding within-match corner timing effect.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's second-half corner surplus (H2 corners minus H1 corners) is positively associated with Team B's second-half corner concession surplus; the joint H2 corner environment rises when both team's half-level profiles align toward second-half corner concentration.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corners are split markedly between halves (4.095 in H1 vs 4.762 in H2 FOR), while Team B's corners are more evenly split (3.105 H1 vs 3.105 H2 FOR) but Team B concedes more corners in the second half (3.474 AGAINST H2 vs 3.737 AGAINST H1 — nearly equal). The joint half-level corner profiles of both teams — Team A's corner generation by half crossed with Team B's corner concession by half — creates a within-match corner timing structure that differs from full-match totals and is not captured by either team's half-level corner rate alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on within-match half-level splits for both teams' corner observables simultaneously (Team A FOR by half and Team B AGAINST by half), which is a within-match state dependency combined with a cross-team joint observable relationship — not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.
